leaves.title: The blocked-terms list

leaves.title: The protection rule for imported people

leaves.title: Real names live only in the user's copy

leaves.title: Typed-in real names
leaves.criterion: No name list in content holds full names. Generators combine parts.

leaves.title: Source terms

leaves.title: Legal review before public release
leaves.criterion: The release record for any public build holds the dated answers.

leaves.title: Periods, intermissions, halftime
leaves.criterion: 1. A simulated regulation game has exactly four periods and one halftime, with period lengths read from the rule set. 2. Ball, down, distance, and line to gain are identical before and after the quarter 1 and quarter 3 breaks, mirrored for direction. 3. A tied score at the end of period 4 always hands control to B10.

leaves.title: Coin toss and choices
leaves.criterion: 1. Over 10,000 seeded tosses the visiting team wins between 49% and 51%. 2. For each of the four first-half choices, the second-half options offered match the rule. 3. Choosing "kick" rather than "defer" leaves the opponent with first choice in the second half.

leaves.title: Change of goals
leaves.criterion: Yards to the goal line and yards to the line to gain are unchanged across the break in 1,000 random states.

leaves.title: Starting on schedule
leaves.criterion: Both fouls exist in the foul catalogue (B8) with the yardage and spot above and can be triggered by a test hook.

leaves.title: Clock state machine
leaves.criterion: 1. The clock is in exactly one state at every tick. 2. The restart mark shown to the user matches the mode the engine then applies in every case of the B1.2.3 test table.

leaves.title: What stops the clock
leaves.criterion: Each of the ten reasons has a test play that stops the clock with the right code. A first down gained in bounds with no other condition leaves the clock running.

leaves.title: Restart: on the snap or on the ready signal
leaves.criterion: A table of at least 60 states (stop reason by period by time by possession change by foul side) returns the mode the rule text gives for each. The table lives in Q1 as rule-engine cases.

leaves.title: Choosing 40 or 25 seconds
leaves.criterion: Each trigger in rule 2 produces a 25-second clock that starts on the whistle event. All other dead balls produce a 40 that starts at the dead-ball tick.

leaves.title: Interrupted play clock and resets
leaves.criterion: One test per listed cause returns the listed value.

leaves.title: Delay of game
leaves.criterion: A play clock that reaches zero without a snap always produces the foul with a 5-yard enforcement from the succeeding spot.

leaves.title: Charged team timeouts
leaves.criterion: 1. No team can hold more than 3 timeouts in a half or 2 in a regular season overtime period. 2. A request while the ball is live never stops the down; it is granted at the dead-ball tick if still valid. 3. After a timeout the restart mode is snap and the play clock is 25.

leaves.title: Second and excess timeouts, freezing the kicker
leaves.criterion: The second timeout by one team in a dead-ball period produces the 5-yard foul. The defensive second timeout before a field goal produces unsportsmanlike conduct.

leaves.title: Referee's timeout
leaves.criterion: After a Referee's timeout the restart mode and play clock equal their values before it.

leaves.title: Two-minute warning
leaves.criterion: Exactly one warning occurs in each of periods 2 and 4 whenever a down ends at or after the clock reaches 2:00. The late-half flag is true from then until the half ends.

leaves.title: Injury timeout before the two-minute warning
leaves.criterion: An injured player with no exception is not on the field for the next down. With a charged timeout taken he may be.

leaves.title: Injury timeout after the two-minute warning
leaves.criterion: A decision table over (timeouts left, side, time in, exception) returns the charge, yardage, play clock, restart mode, and runoff option the notes give. The 8-second case ends the half.

leaves.title: The 10-second runoff
leaves.criterion: 1. Each act (a) to (f) by the offense with time in after the warning offers the runoff. 2. The three outcomes (runoff, timeout instead, declined) give the play clock and restart mode in rule 2. 3. A runoff with 10 seconds or fewer left ends the half.

leaves.title: Substitution violation after the two-minute warning
leaves.criterion: An offensive substitution foul with time in at 0:30 offers the runoff.

leaves.title: Defensive fouls or injuries in the last 40 seconds
leaves.criterion: Leading offense, 0:20 left, defensive offside with time in, defense out of timeouts: the offense is offered the end of the half.

leaves.title: Runoff after a replay reversal or a nullified foul
leaves.criterion: A reversal from incomplete to complete in bounds after the warning produces the runoff unless a timeout is spent.

leaves.title: Time expires with the ball in play
leaves.criterion: A down in progress at 0:00 always completes.

leaves.title: Extension by an untimed down
leaves.criterion: Each of cases (a) to (h), with each listed exception, has a rule-engine test that returns extend, no extend, or choice to the right team.

leaves.title: The overtime coin toss
leaves.criterion: The visiting captain always calls. The winner's menu matches the pregame menu.

leaves.title: Regular season overtime: one 10-minute period
leaves.criterion: Field goal, then field goal, then next score wins. Touchdown and extra point, then the second team scores a touchdown and makes a two-point try: second team wins. Opening drive uses 10:00 and ends in a field goal as time expires: first team wins. 10:00 expires tied: tie.

leaves.title: Postseason overtime: 15-minute periods until a winner
leaves.criterion: Opening drive lasts 15:00 and ends with a touchdown on the last play: the second team still gets its possession in the next period.

leaves.title: Opportunity to possess
leaves.criterion: Opening kickoff muffed and recovered by the kicking team, which then kicks a field goal: game over. First possession ends in an interception returned for a touchdown: game over, defense wins. First possession punt, second team field goal: game over.

leaves.title: Ending the game on a turnover
leaves.criterion: Second team trailing by 3 throws an interception, defender kneels: game over. Same play with defensive offside before the throw: the penalty is enforced and the possession continues.

leaves.title: What changes and what does not
leaves.criterion: In overtime a thrown challenge flag gets no review and costs a timeout (15 yards if none remain); the control is never disabled. A team that ended regulation with three unused timeouts starts regular season overtime with two.

leaves.title: Crew positions and what each watches
leaves.criterion: Every play has seven official positions. Each candidate foul location lies in at least one watch zone.

leaves.title: The Referee's authority
leaves.criterion: No user action other than a successful challenge changes a ruling.

leaves.title: Truth and called values for every ruling
leaves.criterion: For any play in a saved game, both values can be listed for every ruling. Replaying the same seed gives the same truth and the same calls.

leaves.title: Detection: which true fouls are called
leaves.criterion: With league-average teams and crews, 1,000 simulated games give per-game called counts within 10 percent of each target in B11.3.3 for the five most common fouls.

leaves.title: Errors: phantom calls and wrong rulings
leaves.criterion: No phantom foul exists without a recorded borderline event. Error frequency by aspect matches the J15 target once research supplies it.

leaves.title: Calibration targets for called fouls
leaves.criterion: J15 lists each row with its status and season range.

leaves.title: Crew tendencies
leaves.criterion: Across a season, crews' flags per game spread around the league mean with a standard deviation that J15 sets from data. The H2 crew page matches the save's actual counts.

leaves.title: Captains and who speaks to the officials
leaves.criterion: The captain list is limited to six and is locked 90 minutes before kickoff in game time.

leaves.title: League-office disqualification
leaves.criterion: A flagrant hit missed by the crew leads to ejection only if detected before the next snap.

leaves.title: Emergencies and extraordinarily unfair acts
leaves.criterion: A resumed game restores the exact saved situation.

leaves.title: The rule-set file
leaves.criterion: A scan of the engine source finds no numeric rule constant outside the rule-set loader. Loading `college_2026` changes the hash position, the catch test, and the overtime module with no code change. A missing required key stops the load with the key's name.

leaves.title: Key inventory and ownership
leaves.criterion: Every key has exactly one owning leaf. Every "Football facts used" value in B1 to B10 maps to a key or a table row.

leaves.title: Which rule set a game uses
leaves.criterion: A college game and a pro game simulated on the same day in one save use different rule sets. Re-opening a five-year-old game's film applies that year's rules.

leaves.title: Rules in future seasons
leaves.tag: v1 for frozen and patched, v2 for generated
leaves.criterion: A frozen career in its tenth season still uses the starting file. A following career picks up a newly installed file at the next rollover, not before.

leaves.title: The living rulebook
leaves.criterion: Over 30 simulated seasons the rule set changes several times, every change is in the candidate list, and each changed season's file loads and passes the rule test suite (B12.4.1).

leaves.title: The rules briefing
leaves.criterion: Changing one key in a test file produces exactly one briefing line with old and new values. A playbook formation made illegal by a change appears in the list.

leaves.title: The coach's voice in rule changes
leaves.criterion: 1. No proposal can pass that sets a key to a value the engine does not support. 2. Over 200 simulated offseasons the pass rate of proposals is inside the band set in config (starting band 20 to 50 percent, an Assumption). 3. The user's support alone never changes another club's vote by more than the L8 term.

leaves.title: Rule test suite and verification status
leaves.criterion: The suite exists, covers every acceptance criterion in area B, and runs on both shipped rule sets. The status report lists zero Unverified keys that affect scoring, possession, or the clock.

leaves.title: Switch table
leaves.criterion: 1. Loading the college rule set and dumping all keys reproduces the table above. 2. A search of engine code for the word "college" finds no rule logic, only rule-set loading.

leaves.title: Key naming rule and alias register
leaves.criterion: 1. A script search of the bible for `rules.` followed by a name with no second dot finds only this table, once every writer has converted. 2. The rule-set validator rejects any key not in the B12.1.2 inventory, for both level files. 3. Every alias in the table resolves to exactly one canonical key.

leaves.title: Hash marks
leaves.criterion: With the college rule set, a run that ends 5 yards from the left sideline is next snapped 60 feet from that sideline. With the pro set, 70.75 feet.

leaves.title: Jersey numbers and the offensive line
leaves.criterion: A college formation with four linemen numbered 50 to 79 is flagged illegal outside a scrimmage-kick formation.

leaves.title: Clock after a first down
leaves.criterion: College game, 1:30 left in the half, first down gained in bounds: the clock stops and restarts on the ready signal. At 5:00 it does not stop. Pro game: it never stops.

leaves.title: Out of bounds and the two-minute timeout
leaves.criterion: College, 8:00 left in the fourth, runner out of bounds: the clock restarts on the ready signal. At 1:00: on the snap.

leaves.title: Halftime
leaves.criterion: The halftime budget differs by level by the ratio of the two values.

leaves.title: Feigned injury charge
leaves.criterion: A late-showing injury with timeouts left reduces the count by one.

leaves.title: When the runner is down
leaves.criterion: College: an untouched receiver who dives and catches a pass is down at the catch spot. Pro: he may get up and run.

leaves.title: Feet in bounds on a catch
leaves.criterion: A catch with one foot in and the next step out is complete in college and incomplete in the pro set.

leaves.title: Pass interference
leaves.criterion: College: interference 40 yards downfield moves the ball 15 yards. Pro: 40.

leaves.title: Defensive holding and contact on receivers
leaves.criterion: A reroute 8 yards downfield before the throw, receiver not yet even with the defender, is legal in college and a foul in the pro set.

leaves.title: Ineligible receiver downfield
leaves.criterion: A lineman 2.5 yards downfield at the throw draws no foul in college and a foul in the pro set.

leaves.title: Intentional grounding
leaves.criterion: Grounding from 8 yards behind the line costs 8 yards and the down in college.

leaves.title: Kickoff
leaves.criterion: A college kickoff fair caught at the 8 is next snapped at the 25.

leaves.title: Missed field goal and the fair catch kick
leaves.criterion: A 45-yard miss snapped from the 28: the defense takes over at its 28 in college and at its 35 or 36 in the pro set.

leaves.title: The try
leaves.criterion: College tries snap at the 3 for both kinds.

leaves.title: Overtime procedure
leaves.criterion: 1. A college game never ends tied. 2. After a touchdown in the second period the kick may still be called, and a made kick scores nothing. 3. The third period consists of single plays from the 3.

leaves.title: Targeting
leaves.criterion: A third targeting foul in a season removes the player from the next game's active list.

leaves.title: Replay model
leaves.criterion: In a simulated college season, booth-initiated reviews outnumber coach challenges.

leaves.title: Radio, tablets, and headsets
leaves.criterion: The sideline tablet view offers video in a college game and stills in a pro game.

leaves.title: Rules briefing and quiz at a new level
leaves.criterion: The briefing is generated from the rule-set files and lists every key whose value differs between the two sets, with no hand-written list. The user's coach record has no rules familiarity field.

leaves.title: Blocking below the waist
leaves.criterion: A wide receiver's cut block on a perimeter run is flagged in college.

leaves.title: Blocking downfield on passes behind the line
leaves.criterion: A bubble screen caught 1 yard behind the line with receivers blocking 4 yards downfield draws no foul.

leaves.title: College values for keys named in I6 to I11
leaves.criterion: Every key named in the game-day handoff has a college row here or an explicit "Unverified" value.

leaves.title: Dimensions and zones
leaves.criterion: The constants file holds 360 ft, 160 ft, 30 ft end zone depth, 70 ft 9 in inbounds line offset, 8 in goal line width, each with its rule citation.

leaves.title: Yard lines, hash marks, numerals
leaves.criterion: Hash separation in the engine equals 18.5 ft within rounding. A formation saved with a receiver "at the bottom of the numbers" places him 12 yd from the sideline.

leaves.title: The goal
leaves.criterion: Goal constants match the rule. A kick crossing the plane 1 in inside the outer edge of a post is good.

leaves.title: Ball specification and supply
leaves.criterion: Ball constants are in config with the rule citation.

leaves.title: Eleven players
leaves.criterion: Twelve offensive players set for 3 seconds draws the dead-ball foul. Twelve defenders at the snap draws the live-ball foul and the offense gets the choice of the play or the penalty (B8).

leaves.title: Jersey numbers by position
leaves.criterion: No regular-season roster holds a number outside its position's range or a duplicate.

leaves.title: Reporting eligible or ineligible
leaves.criterion: A number 71 aligned as the end man on the line without reporting draws the foul. After reporting he may catch a pass legally. If he lines up at tackle the next play without one of the listed breaks, the foul is called: 5 yards, illegal substitution.

leaves.title: Legal substitution and becoming a player
leaves.criterion: A substitute who enters while the ball is live draws the 5-yard illegal substitution foul (rule 2). A replaced player still inside the field at the snap triggers B2.3.1 rule 3.

leaves.title: Offensive substitution limits
leaves.criterion: A substitute receiver set outside the numerals without having come inside them draws the 5-yard foul.

leaves.title: The defense's right to match
leaves.criterion: 1. With an offensive substitution, the snap never occurs before the defensive match completes or the cap is reached. 2. With no offensive substitution and no huddle, a defense that substitutes can be caught with 12 at the snap. 3. The offense's substitution at 6 s on the play clock with a defensive response produces delay of game on the offense.

leaves.title: Helmet radio
leaves.criterion: A call confirmed at 14 s on the play clock is never delivered by radio. Two radio helmets for one team are never on the field together.

leaves.title: Down, series, and line to gain
leaves.criterion: A series starting at the opponent's 7 has the goal line as line to gain. A 10-yard offensive penalty on first and 10 gives first and 20 with the line to gain unchanged.

leaves.title: Live ball
leaves.criterion: No snap tick precedes the ready tick.

leaves.title: Dead-ball conditions
leaves.criterion: 1. Each reason (a) to (s) has at least one golden play in Q1 that ends with that code. 2. A runner whose knee touches with no opponent contact before or at that tick is not ruled down. 3. A runner whose forward progress is stopped for the restraint threshold is ruled dead under (b).

leaves.title: Forward progress and the whistle
leaves.criterion: A runner who reaches the 30, is held, and is driven back to the 27 is spotted at the 30. A runner who retreats from the 30 to the 27 untouched and is tackled there is spotted at the 27.

leaves.title: Erroneous whistle and ball striking an object
leaves.criterion: A test hook that fires an erroneous whistle in each of the three ball states returns the option set in rules 1 to 3.

leaves.title: The forward point of the ball
leaves.criterion: With officiating error off, the recorded spot equals the ball's foremost x at the dead-ball tick in every golden play.

leaves.title: Out of bounds
leaves.criterion: A runner stepping on the sideline at the 34 with the ball's foremost point at the 34.6 is spotted at 34.6. A loose ball touching a player who is standing out of bounds is out.

leaves.title: The inbounds spot and the hash
leaves.criterion: A run ending 3 yd from the left sideline at the 40 gives a next snap on the left hash at the 40. An incompletion after a snap from the right hash snaps again from the right hash.

leaves.title: First down for the offense
leaves.criterion: Each case (a) to (e) has a rule-engine test. The double change of possession case returns first and 10 for the original offense.

leaves.title: First down for the opponent
leaves.criterion: Fourth and 2 at the 40, runner down at the 41: defense's ball, first and 10 at the 41 going the other way.

leaves.title: Line of scrimmage and neutral zone
leaves.criterion: With the ball spotted, the two planes are one ball length apart. No pre-snap foul can be recorded before the ready signal.

leaves.title: Who is on the line
leaves.criterion: A tackle whose helmet is behind the snapper's beltline plane by 0.5 yd is "neither" and triggers B4.2.2. A wide receiver on the ball with his helmet through the plane is on the line.

leaves.title: Seven on the line and eligible ends
leaves.criterion: Six on the line draws illegal formation. A number 72 on the end of the line without reporting draws illegal formation. A wide receiver covering the tight end is legal and makes the tight end ineligible.

leaves.title: The player neither on nor off the line
leaves.criterion: A slot receiver set 0.5 yd off the ball (the "neither" band) draws illegal formation. A quarterback under center does not.

leaves.title: Tight end box
leaves.criterion: The box is computed once per play at the snap and does not move with the ball.

leaves.title: The one-second set
leaves.criterion: A snap 0.8 s after the last player stops draws illegal shift. A snap 1.0 s after draws nothing.

leaves.title: Shifts
leaves.criterion: Two receivers trading sides at once is a shift and resets the count. One back motioning, stopping, then a second back motioning needs no new set. Two backs moving at once with a snap 0.5 s after they stop draws illegal shift.

leaves.title: Motion at the snap
leaves.criterion: A slot receiver in flat jet motion at the snap is legal. The same receiver angled 15 degrees toward the line at the snap draws illegal motion. Two players moving at the snap draws a flag.

leaves.title: False start
leaves.criterion: A guard in a three-point stance who lifts his down hand before the snap draws a false start and the play does not run. A tackle in a two-point stance who drops into a three-point stance and holds until the snap draws nothing. A shotgun quarterback clapping with no snap is legal unless the hands thrust forward.

leaves.title: Shift converts to false start late in a half
leaves.criterion: Clock running at 0:40 of the fourth quarter, snap with a receiver still moving to his spot: dead ball, false start, runoff offered. Same snap with the clock stopped: live-ball illegal shift.

leaves.title: Encroachment
leaves.criterion: A defensive tackle who touches the guard before the snap: dead ball, 5 yards, no play.

leaves.title: Neutral zone infraction
leaves.criterion: Defender in the A gap jumps; the guard next to him flinches: foul on the defense. Same jump; only the far-side tackle (more than 2.5 positions away) flinches: false start on the offense. Defender jumps, nobody moves, he gets back: no foul.

leaves.title: Offside and the free play
leaves.criterion: Defensive end's hand in the neutral zone at the snap, no contact, no flinch, 5:00 left in the second quarter: play runs, flag, offense chooses. Same at 1:30 left: dead ball, neutral zone infraction.

leaves.title: Where the ball is snapped
leaves.criterion: A run ending 3 yards from the left sideline at the 40 is next snapped on the left hash at the 40. A run ending between the hashes is snapped at its own lateral spot.

leaves.title: The snapper and the illegal snap
leaves.criterion: A no-huddle snap before the officials are set is dead with no yardage the first time.

leaves.title: Receiving the snap
leaves.criterion: A shotgun snap over the quarterback's head recovered by the defense at the offense's 20 may be advanced. A direct snap to a guard on the line is whistled dead, 5 yards.

leaves.title: One checker for designer, AI, and engine
leaves.criterion: Every formation and motion in the shipped playbooks passes. A formation saved with a known failure draws the foul with the same rule ID when the engine runs it. A unit test for each acceptance criterion in B4.2 to B4.5 passes in both the designer and the engine with the same rule ID.

leaves.title: Forward pass, backward pass, or fumble
leaves.criterion: A screen pass released at the 30.0 and first touched at the 30.0 is backward and live if dropped. A sack-strip one tick after the hand starts forward is an incomplete pass. A strip during the tuck is a fumble.

leaves.title: Legal and illegal forward passes
leaves.criterion: Quarterback's trailing foot on the line at release: legal. Whole body and ball past the line: loss of down, 5 yards from the release spot. Pass after an interception return: 5 yards from release, no loss of down.

leaves.title: Completing a catch
leaves.criterion: Control, left foot in, right foot heel on the sideline: incomplete. Control, both feet in, hit immediately and ball out on contact with the ground: incomplete. Control, both feet, third step, then stripped: catch and fumble. Control with one knee down inbounds and held through the ground: complete.

leaves.title: Incomplete pass and simultaneous catch
leaves.criterion: A jump ball held by receiver and defender coming down together is a completion to the offense. A defender who has it first with the receiver grabbing on after is an interception.

leaves.title: Eligible and ineligible receivers
leaves.criterion: Pass deflected by a defensive lineman and caught by the left guard: legal. Pass caught by the guard untouched: 5 yards from the previous spot, defense may decline and take the result. Receiver steps out untouched, returns, catches: loss of down.

leaves.title: Ineligible player downfield
leaves.criterion: Guard 3 yards downfield, never touched a defender, pass thrown: foul. Guard driving a defensive tackle 4 yards downfield in contact at the throw: no foul.

leaves.title: Contact inside and beyond five yards (illegal contact)
leaves.criterion: Jam at 3 yards, release at 5: legal. Defender grabs and rides at 8 yards with the quarterback in the pocket: illegal contact. Same contact after the quarterback has scrambled outside the tackle: no illegal contact.

leaves.title: Defensive holding
leaves.criterion: Jersey pull at the top of a route before the throw: 5 yards, first down, enforced from the previous spot.

leaves.title: Illegal cut block on a receiver
leaves.criterion: Linebacker cuts a wide receiver on a crossing route 4 yards downfield before the throw: 15 yards, first down.

leaves.title: Pass interference
leaves.criterion: Defender grabs the receiver's arm 38 yards downfield on a catchable ball: first down at that spot. Same foul in the end zone from the 30: first and goal at the 1. Same from the 1.5-yard line: ball at the 0.75. Receiver pushes off at the top of a route: 10 yards from the previous spot. Ball thrown 10 yards over everyone's head: no foul.

leaves.title: Intentional grounding, the throwaway, and the spike
leaves.criterion: In the pocket, under pressure, ball thrown 15 yards from any receiver: loss of down, 10 yards. Sacked-depth throw from 14 yards behind the line: ball at the spot of the pass. Scrambled outside the tackle box, thrown out of bounds past the line: legal. Same throw landing 2 yards short of the line: grounding. Thrown from the end zone: safety.

leaves.title: Backward pass
leaves.criterion: Swing pass released at the 25 and caught at the 24.5, then dropped: live. Pitch thrown out of bounds at 1:10 of the fourth quarter by the team in possession: loss of down, 5 yards, runoff offered.

leaves.title: Fumble: recovery, advance, and the fourth-down and two-minute limits
leaves.criterion: Fourth and 1, runner fumbles at the 30 short of the line to gain, teammate recovers at the 34: dead, ball at the 30, turnover on downs. Same play on third down: first down at the 34 or wherever the teammate is tackled. Fumble at 1:45 of the second quarter recovered 6 yards behind the fumble spot by a teammate: dead at the recovery spot.

leaves.title: Fumble out of bounds and into the end zone
leaves.criterion: Runner fumbles at the opponent's 2, ball rolls through the end zone and out: touchback, defense's ball. Fumble at the 40 rolls forward out at the 45: offense's ball at the 40. Fumble at the 40 rolls back out at the 36: offense's ball at the 36.

leaves.title: Free kick types, spot, and tee
leaves.criterion: After a touchdown and try with no penalties the kickoff is from the A35. After a safety the kick is from the A20 and a punt is allowed.

leaves.title: Kickoff zones and formation
leaves.criterion: Receiving alignment with nine in the zone, four on the B35: illegal. Ten in the zone with five on the line: illegal. Three players stacked off the line in the middle area: illegal.

leaves.title: Movement, blocking, and live play on a kickoff
leaves.criterion: A coverage player who lifts a foot before the ball lands: 5 yards. Two returners forming a shoulder-to-shoulder wedge: 15 yards without contact.

leaves.title: Kickoff results: touchback spots, short and out of bounds
leaves.criterion: Kick from the A35 lands at the B8 and rolls dead in the end zone, downed: B20. Kick flies out the back of the end zone: B35. Kick lands at the B24: dead, receivers' ball at the B40. Kick out of bounds at the B15: receivers choose the B40.

leaves.title: Declared onside kick
leaves.criterion: Kicking team recovers at 9 yards untouched: illegal touching, receivers' ball at that spot or 5 yards and re-kick. Recovers at 11 yards: kicking team's ball, dead at the spot. Kick sails 30 yards untouched: receivers' ball after 15 yards from the A35.

leaves.title: Legal scrimmage kick and formation limits
leaves.criterion: A punt-team guard 3 yards downfield before the ball is kicked: 5 yards. A nose player aligned head-up on the long snapper on a standard punt: 5 yards.

leaves.title: Touching and recovering a scrimmage kick
leaves.criterion: Gunner bats the punt at the 8, ball rolls to the 3 and is downed: receivers' ball at the 8 by choice. Returner muffs at the 20, kicking team recovers at the 18: kicking team's ball, first and 10 at the 18, no advance. Punt blocked, kicker recovers behind the line on fourth down short of the line to gain and is tackled: turnover on downs.

leaves.title: Punts into the end zone, out of bounds, and off the goal posts
leaves.criterion: Punt bounces at the 3 and into the end zone untouched: receivers' ball at the 20. Coverage player with a foot on the goal line catches the bouncing ball: touchback.

leaves.title: Blocking rules during a scrimmage kick
leaves.criterion: Return-team low block on a punt: foul regardless of location.

leaves.title: Fair catch
leaves.criterion: Signal, muff, ball caught by the signaler before it hits the ground: fair catch. Signal, ball hits the ground, signaler picks it up: dead there, no fair catch kick option.

leaves.title: Interference with the chance to catch a kick
leaves.criterion: Gunner hits the returner as the ball arrives, no signal: 15 yards from that spot, receivers' ball. Same with a signal and a dropped ball: fair catch awarded plus 15 yards.

leaves.title: Fair catch kick
leaves.criterion: Fair catch at the opponent's 48 with 0:00 on the clock: the kick option is offered and the snap option is not.

leaves.title: A successful field goal
leaves.criterion: Ball over the top of the right upright, inside its outer edge: good. Kick takes 6.2 seconds of flight and goes through: 5 seconds run off.

leaves.title: Missed field goal
leaves.criterion: Line of scrimmage at the opponent's 10, held at the 18, miss: opponent's ball at the 20. Line at the 35, held at the 43, miss: opponent's ball at the 43.

leaves.title: Special enforcement on free kicks and scrimmage kicks
leaves.criterion: Punt from the A30 caught at the B25, returned to the B40, block in the back at the B30 by the return team: enforced 10 yards from the B25 (end of kick, worse than the B30), ball at the B15. Kicking team offside on a kickoff returned to the B45: receivers choose re-kick from the A30 or the ball at the 50.

leaves.title: Scores and the winner
leaves.criterion: Touchdown plus a good try kick adds 7. A forfeit adds a win and no points for tiebreakers.

leaves.title: When a touchdown is scored
leaves.criterion: Runner dives, ball tip touches the plane before his knee lands: touchdown. Airborne runner's ball passes outside the pylon before he lands out of bounds: no touchdown, spotted where the ball crossed the sideline. Fumble into the end zone recovered by the offense on third down: touchdown. Same on fourth down by a teammate of the fumbler: no touchdown, ball back to the fumble spot (B5.6.2).

leaves.title: Try setup and the one-or-two choice
leaves.criterion: Kick try: line of scrimmage at the 15. Two-point try: at the 2. Defense calls timeout after the offense lines up to kick: offense may switch to a two-point try from the 2.

leaves.title: Results of a try
leaves.criterion: Interception on a two-point try returned the length of the field: defense 2 points. Kick blocked and recovered by the defense in the field of play, runner tackled: try over, no points.

leaves.title: Fouls on a try
leaves.criterion: Defense offside on a good kick try: offense may keep the point and take 5 yards on the kickoff, or re-try for two from the 1. Offensive holding on a good two-point try: replay from the 12. Illegal forward pass (loss of down) on a try: try fails.

leaves.title: Field goal value and follow-on
leaves.criterion: Good kick: 3 points, then a kickoff by the scoring team.

leaves.title: Safety
leaves.criterion: Quarterback sacked in his end zone: safety. Offensive holding in the end zone on a completed pass: safety if accepted. Runner's forward progress stopped with the ball's tip still on the goal line: safety.

leaves.title: Momentum exception
leaves.criterion: Interception at the 3 running toward his own goal, downed in the end zone: his team's ball at the 3. Same at the half-yard line: ball at the 1.

leaves.title: Touchback
leaves.criterion: Interception 4 yards deep, kneel: ball at the 20. Punt hits the pylon on the fly: touchback.

leaves.title: Who put the ball in the end zone
leaves.criterion: The two muffed-punt cases above return touchback and safety. A defender who bats a fumble into his own end zone, where his team recovers it: safety.

leaves.title: What follows each score
leaves.criterion: After a defensive two-point return on a try, the team that was on defense during the try still receives the kickoff.

leaves.title: The foul record
leaves.criterion: Every foul named in B4 to B8 has a catalogue row. Every record carries all fields.

leaves.title: Foul catalogue
leaves.criterion: The table loads as data with no missing fields. A unit test per row checks yardage and flags against the cited rule.

leaves.title: Legal blocking and offensive holding
leaves.criterion: A tackle hooks an edge rusher at the point of attack before the throw: holding, 10 yards. The same hook on the back side of a run 15 yards from the ball: no foul.

leaves.title: Defensive use of hands and defensive holding
leaves.criterion: A linebacker tackles a back who clearly carried out a fake inside the pocket: legal. The same tackle after the back has left the pocket without the ball: holding.

leaves.title: Low and dangerous blocks
leaves.criterion: Back cuts a blitzing linebacker in the A gap inside the box from the front: legal. Receiver cuts a cornerback on the perimeter on a run: foul. Guard cuts a defensive tackle the center is engaged with high: chop block. Receiver in motion toward the ball blocks a linebacker high and legally within 5 yards: legal.

leaves.title: Defenseless players and prohibited contact
leaves.criterion: Shoulder to the head of a receiver in the act of catching: foul even with arms wrapped. Same hit to the chest: legal.

leaves.title: Roughing the passer
leaves.criterion: Contact on the rusher's first step after release, chest high, rolling to the side: legal. Same contact on the third step: foul. Sack with full body weight landing on the quarterback: foul even though the ball had not been thrown.

leaves.title: Kicker, holder, and tackle-technique fouls
leaves.criterion: Rusher misses the punt and hits the plant leg: 15 yards, first down. Rusher brushes the kicking foot on fourth and 8: 5 yards, fourth and 3, no first down. The same foul on fourth and 4: first down, because 5 yards reaches the line to gain.

leaves.title: Unsportsmanlike conduct by players
leaves.criterion: Defense calls timeout with none left as the kicker lines up: no timeout, kick is live, 15 yards after the down. Linebacker runs from 3 yards deep and leaps over the snapper: foul.

leaves.title: Disqualification
leaves.criterion: A player flagged for taunting in the first quarter and again in the fourth, with the second penalty declined, is ejected.

leaves.title: Palpably unfair acts, fouls to prevent a score, and clock manipulation
leaves.criterion: Team leading by 4 with 0:08 left takes an intentional multi-hold punt that uses all 8 seconds: 15 yards, clock back to 0:08, replay.

leaves.title: Illegal bat and illegal kick
leaves.criterion: Offensive player bats his own team's fumble forward on third down: 10 yards and loss of down.

leaves.title: Coach and sideline conduct
leaves.criterion: The "argue the call" action at its highest intensity carries a visible flag risk. An ejected user loses in-game controls.

leaves.title: The enforcement procedure
leaves.criterion: A test suite of at least 60 scenarios, one per rule item in B8.5.2 to B8.5.7 and B6.6.1, returns the cited result. The suite is the gate for any change to this code.

leaves.title: Enforcement spots and the three-and-one method
leaves.criterion: The two edge cases above return a net of minus 10 and minus 4 yards from the previous spot. A defensive face mask on a 12-yard run adds 15 from the dead-ball spot.

leaves.title: Half the distance and fouls near a goal line
leaves.criterion: Defensive offside at its own 4: ball to the 2. Offensive holding in its own end zone: safety offered.

leaves.title: The down after a penalty
leaves.criterion: Third and 12, defensive holding: first and 10 five yards ahead. Third and 3, defensive offside: first and 10, because 5 yards reaches the line to gain. Third and 8, defensive offside: third and 3. Fourth down grounding: defense's ball after the yardage.

leaves.title: Multiple fouls and double fouls
leaves.criterion: The two edge cases above. Offensive false start and defensive unnecessary roughness after the whistle: 15 yards on the defense from the previous spot, false start ignored.

leaves.title: Dead-ball fouls and fouls between downs
leaves.criterion: Third-down incompletion followed by defensive taunting: the down counts, then 15 yards and an automatic first down.

leaves.title: Fouls on scoring plays
leaves.criterion: Roughing the passer on a touchdown pass: touchdown stands, 15 yards on the try (two-point try from the 1) or on the kickoff. Defensive offside on a made 40-yard field goal on fourth and 3: the user may take a first down instead of the 3 points.

leaves.title: Accept or decline
leaves.criterion: Every option shown produces exactly the state shown when chosen. A declined penalty leaves the play result untouched.

leaves.title: The coach's challenge
leaves.criterion: Two failed challenges: a third flag gets no review and costs a timeout. One won, one lost: a third is available. Challenge with zero timeouts: 15 yards. A flag thrown after the two-minute warning with a timeout left: no coach review, timeout charged (the booth may still review under B9.1.2). The control is live in every case.

leaves.title: Booth-initiated reviews
leaves.criterion: A fumble ruled recovered by the defense triggers a booth look with no challenge. A runner ruled down by contact before fumbling, at 9:00 of the third quarter, is reviewed only if challenged.

leaves.title: The standard and the evidence model
leaves.criterion: Over 10,000 simulated wrong calls with evidence quality 0.6, about 60 percent are reversed. Correct calls are reversed zero times.

leaves.title: Reviewable rulings
leaves.criterion: Each row maps to one or more truth-record fields in B11. On a play with no reviewable aspect the challenge control warns "Not reviewable" and stays live; a flag thrown anyway is charged a timeout (B9.1.1 rule 4a).

leaves.title: What cannot be reviewed
leaves.criterion: A flag thrown on a defensive pass interference call gets no review and costs the throwing team a timeout.

leaves.title: Ball placement and possession after a reversal
leaves.criterion: Pass ruled incomplete, review shows a catch and fumble, defender picked the ball up at once: defense's ball at the recovery spot. Same play with nobody picking it up: offense's ball at the spot of the fumble.

leaves.title: Clock, timeouts, and fouls after a review
leaves.criterion: The edge case above ends the game. With one timeout left the team may spend it and snap with 0:08.

leaves.title: Replay assist and corrections without a challenge
leaves.criterion: A face mask flag thrown when J8 recorded no hand on the mask is picked up at the modeled rate. No uncalled foul is ever added by assist.

leaves.title: Conferences and divisions
leaves.criterion: 1. The default league file loads with 32 clubs, and every club belongs to exactly one division. 2. A file with a 5-club division fails validation with a clear message.

leaves.title: The default league and generated leagues
leaves.criterion: 1. Two fresh Standard-league saves are identical byte for byte before the first user action. 2. A Generated league with seed S is identical across two runs.

leaves.title: Club identity record
leaves.criterion: The build-time name check passes against the A6 list. No two clubs share an abbreviation or a primary colour within a division.

leaves.title: Ownership and organisation record
leaves.criterion: Every club has all fields. Facility grades change the listed systems in a controlled test.

leaves.title: Rivalries
leaves.criterion: Every division pair has strength at least 1.

leaves.title: Stadium record
leaves.criterion: Every club has one home stadium. A dome game logs zero wind in every play record.

leaves.title: Playing surface
leaves.criterion: The same play run 10,000 times on wet grass shows more slips (lost-footing events) than on dry grass.

leaves.title: Location and time zone
leaves.criterion: Matrix is symmetric in distance. Zones crossed from A to B equals minus B to A.

leaves.title: Climate normals and game weather
leaves.criterion: Over 1,000 generated seasons, each stadium's mean kickoff temperature by month is within 1 C of its normals table.

leaves.title: League constants file
leaves.criterion: No number from the table appears as a literal in code. Changing games per club to 16 in a test file produces a 16-game schedule only if a matching formula exists, otherwise a clear error.

leaves.title: The league office as an actor
leaves.criterion: Every league-office action writes an entry to the transactions wire (C10.1) or the user's inbox with its cause.

leaves.title: The daily wire
leaves.criterion: The count of wire items equals the count of committed public transactions for the day. No item appears before its transaction's public time.

leaves.title: Public injury information
leaves.criterion: No screen shows another club's true injury state. The staff note appears only when the opponent coach has at least a starting 10 past filings.

leaves.title: The coaching carousel as news
leaves.criterion: Every head coach change in the world has a public item. An in-season play caller change resets the opponent tendency source in H2.

leaves.title: The rule change process
leaves.criterion: Every adopted change is a valid rule-set diff that passes the B rule-engine tests. The analytics models refit before the first game under the new set. A replay of an old season uses that season's rule set.

leaves.title: The teaching step and the officials' visit
leaves.criterion: In a test, a team that skips the teaching step commits more fouls on the changed rule over the first 4 games than one that takes it, by a margin set in data.

leaves.title: Clip submissions
leaves.criterion: Replies agree with the truth record at the stated rate. The weekly cap is enforced.

leaves.title: Events that change a club's situation
leaves.criterion: Event counts over a 100-year soak match the data rates within sampling error. No event of an excluded type lands on an imported person.

leaves.title: Three channels: official, people you know, media
leaves.criterion: Every inbox item names a source. In a test, a user with a strong edge to a general manager hears of that club's release before the wire at the configured rate. Rumour items are wrong at the configured rate.

leaves.title: Rule records and the check function
leaves.criterion: Every limit in C11.2 exists as a record with a source and a status. No limit is a literal in code.

leaves.title: Offseason program limits
leaves.criterion: Each row is enforced by a checker test. Every row has a class. A blocked act cannot be scheduled. A breakable act can be scheduled after a warning and enters the C11.2.4 detection draw, for the user and for AI coaches alike.

leaves.title: Training camp limits
leaves.criterion: Checker tests for each row. A late-signed player cannot take part in a padded practice until his fifth day.

leaves.title: Regular season and postseason limits
leaves.criterion: A 12th padded practice in the first 11 weeks shows a warning with the rule and the C11.2.4 penalty, can be held after confirmation, and is logged to L8.2.5 (Marlon's ruling of 2026-11-25 22:23 UTC). Unused early padded practices do not carry past week 11.

leaves.title: Violations and penalties
leaves.criterion: A found first violation in the spring deducts $100,000 from the coach's cash and removes the next OTA week from the calendar.

leaves.title: Practice reports and game status
leaves.criterion: Every player who misses a game for injury appeared on that week's report, or a violation event exists.

leaves.title: What a club may fine and how much
leaves.criterion: A fine above the step maximum shows the warning, can be issued, is logged, and is voided with back pay when the player's grievance succeeds.

leaves.title: Required availability
leaves.criterion: Every game week contains at least the required head-coach sessions.

leaves.title: Coach interview and hiring rules
leaves.criterion: Every permission result equals the result of the E2.3.1 state machine for the same candidate, date, and role.

leaves.title: Tampering
leaves.criterion: No user contact action is available for a contracted player before the window without the warning.

leaves.title: Behavioural health clinician and required education
leaves.criterion: Every club's staff has a clinician record.

leaves.title: Concussion protocol authority
leaves.criterion: A player in the protocol returns only by clearance or by the deliberate breakable action, which is always logged and runs the L8.2.5 detection draw.

leaves.title: The 17 opponents
leaves.criterion: 1. For any season, every club has exactly 17 pairings and exactly 6 are division games. 2. Total league games is 272. 3. Over 12 simulated seasons, each club plays every club in its conference's other divisions at least 4 times and every club in the other conference at least 3 times. 4. All clubs of one conference have 9 home games and the other conference 8, alternating by year.

leaves.title: Weeks and byes
leaves.criterion: 1. 1,000 generated schedules all satisfy every hard constraint. 2. Generation takes under 5 s on the target machine (P6). 3. The same seed gives the same schedule.

leaves.title: Week types
leaves.criterion: For a hand-built schedule of 20 cases, every tag matches the table.

leaves.title: Kickoff slots
leaves.criterion: No club plays on fewer than 3 days of rest. No club has more than 2 short-week Thursday games or more than 7 scheduled national games (an eighth only by flex: Pro Football Talk 2026-05-15 reports a per-club maximum of eight prime-time games, seven scheduled plus one flexed, 1 of 3). Over 100 seasons, 2 to 8 clubs a season have no prime-time game.

leaves.title: Body-clock and kickoff time
leaves.criterion: A west-coast club in an eastern 1:00 p.m. game with a Saturday arrival shows a 10:00 a.m. or 11:00 a.m. body time.

leaves.title: Flexible scheduling
leaves.criterion: No flex violates the notice period. In 100 simulated seasons, the final-week national game involves a club whose playoff status is undecided in at least 90%.

leaves.title: International and neutral-site games
leaves.criterion: No club loses more than one home game to a neutral site in a season.

leaves.title: Preseason games
leaves.criterion: Every club has exactly 3 preseason games and none against its Week 1 opponent.

leaves.title: Strength of schedule and rest reports
leaves.criterion: Report values match hand calculation for a sample schedule.

leaves.title: Schedule data contract
leaves.criterion: The schema validates for every generated game. Replaying the event log reproduces the schedule.

leaves.title: Game result record
leaves.criterion: A 20-20 regular-season final produces 0-0-1 for both clubs and a percentage of .500.

leaves.title: Standings tables
leaves.criterion: For a fixture file of one complete real-shaped season entered as fictional clubs, every column matches a hand-checked answer file.

leaves.title: Final division rank
leaves.criterion: No two clubs in a division ever share a rank.

leaves.title: Two clubs in the same division
leaves.criterion: A test file with one case per step, built so that all earlier steps are level, resolves each case at the intended step.

leaves.title: Two clubs in different divisions (wild card and seeding)
leaves.criterion: As C3.2.1, one case per step.

leaves.title: Three or more clubs
leaves.criterion: A property test: for any results set, the output order is a total order, is the same on repeated runs, and never places a club above another club that beat it in a clean two-club tie on step 1.

leaves.title: Seeding
leaves.criterion: For the fixture season, seeds match the answer file.

leaves.title: Clinching and elimination
leaves.criterion: The tool never shows "clinched" for a club that a brute-force check on a small league (8 clubs, 3 weeks left) shows can still miss.

leaves.title: Playoff odds
leaves.criterion: Runs in under 2 s. Calibration: across many simulated seasons, clubs given 30% make it about 30% of the time (within 5 points).

leaves.title: Rounds, byes, and hosting
leaves.criterion: In 1,000 simulated postseasons the top seed never plays in the wild-card round and always faces the lowest surviving seed.

leaves.title: The bye week for the top seed
leaves.criterion: The planner lists every possible divisional opponent with its probability from C3.3.3.

leaves.title: Final order for the next draft
leaves.criterion: The champion always picks 32nd. The list has 32 distinct clubs.

leaves.title: Phases and the league-year clock
leaves.criterion: 1. Advancing day by day and advancing by "next game" reach the same state. 2. No deadline can pass without its check running. 3. A full year can be advanced with all tasks delegated, without a stall.

leaves.title: The task list and delegation
leaves.criterion: Every task in the data file names an owner category that exists in the index.

leaves.title: Season review and exit meetings
leaves.criterion: Every player on the roster has a recorded exit-meeting state (held by head coach, held by assistant, not held).

leaves.title: Staff changes and the hiring cycle
leaves.criterion: Every club has a head coach by the start of Free agency.

leaves.title: All-star games and the combine
leaves.criterion: Events appear on the calendar on the data-file dates.

leaves.title: Tag window, negotiating window, free agency
leaves.criterion: Each deadline stops time if the user's club has an open decision.

leaves.title: The draft on the calendar
leaves.criterion: Dates match the file.

leaves.title: Schedule release and learning time
leaves.criterion: The schedule is visible before the offseason program's third phase.

leaves.title: Program phases
leaves.criterion: The planner warns on a team period in phase two, an 11th OTA, or any contact period in the spring, names the rule and the reference penalty, and schedules it if the user confirms. Each one is logged and runs the C11.2.4 finding draw (L8.2.5).

leaves.title: Voluntary attendance
leaves.criterion: A player with a contract dispute attends less often than a satisfied player in a 1,000-run test.

leaves.title: Install one
leaves.criterion: Knowledge after the spring is lower than after camp for the same concept in a test plan.

leaves.title: Summer break
leaves.criterion: Coach energy is higher at camp after a rested break than after a worked one.

leaves.title: Training camp
leaves.criterion: The planner warns on a padded practice before the acclimation period ends, a 17th padded practice in camp, and a 4th consecutive padded day, using the config values. It names the rule and the reference penalty and schedules the practice if the user confirms (Marlon's ruling of 2026-11-25 22:23 UTC). Each one is logged and runs the C11.2.4 finding draw (L8.2.5).

leaves.title: Preseason weeks
leaves.criterion: Preseason results never change standings.

leaves.title: Cutdown and the days after
leaves.criterion: Time stops at the deadline if the user's roster is over 53.

leaves.title: The weekly loop
leaves.criterion: Each in-week deadline fires at the configured offset for every week type.

leaves.title: In-season dated deadlines
leaves.criterion: A released vested veteran before November 11 is a free agent at once, and on or after it goes through waivers.

leaves.title: Playoff weeks on the calendar
leaves.criterion: An eliminated club's phase changes the next day.

leaves.title: Ending one league year and starting the next
leaves.criterion: A save can be advanced 30 seasons with all tasks delegated, with no stall and no invalid roster.

leaves.title: List types and limits by phase
leaves.criterion: 1. No sequence of legal moves can leave a club with 54 on the Active/Inactive list outside game-day elevations. 2. All limits come from the config file.

leaves.title: Accrued seasons and vested status
leaves.criterion: Generated players' accrued seasons are consistent with their career game logs.

leaves.title: The game-day active list
leaves.criterion: The game refuses to start with 49 active, or with 48 active and 7 linemen.

leaves.title: Emergency third quarterback
leaves.criterion: The emergency quarterback cannot be sent in while an active quarterback is healthy and not disqualified.

leaves.title: Size and eligibility
leaves.criterion: A seventh group C player cannot be signed to the practice squad. An eleventh group B player cannot be signed, even when fewer than 6 group C players are on the squad.

leaves.title: Game-day elevations
leaves.criterion: A fourth elevation of the same player is refused with the rule named.

leaves.title: Signing players off practice squads
leaves.criterion: A protected player cannot be signed by another club before his club's next game.

leaves.title: Injured reserve
leaves.criterion: A player placed after week 3 cannot be activated before the club's week 8 game if the club had no bye, or week 9 if a bye fell in between.

leaves.title: Designated to return
leaves.criterion: A ninth regular-season designation is refused.

leaves.title: PUP, NFI, and suspended lists
leaves.criterion: A player who took part in a camp practice cannot be placed on PUP.

leaves.title: Waivers and claims
leaves.criterion: With two claims, the club with the worse record gets the player.

leaves.title: Trade deadline
leaves.criterion: No trade record is dated after the deadline within a season.

leaves.title: The reduction to 53
leaves.criterion: After the deadline every club has 53 or fewer.

leaves.title: Transaction types and validation
leaves.criterion: 1. A fuzz test of 100,000 random proposed transactions never produces an invalid `RosterState`. 2. Every accepted transaction appears on the wire.

leaves.title: Contract record and money types
leaves.criterion: For any contract the sum of yearly cap charges equals total money paid plus settled incentives. Cash paid by date matches the money types. A contract fails validation if any year is below the minimum salary for the player's credited seasons (C6.4.1).

leaves.title: Team salary, the cap, and cap room
leaves.criterion: Team salary recomputed from contracts equals the stored figure after every transaction in a 30-season run. No club is ever over the cap outside the grace window. The top 51 switch happens on the two dated events.

leaves.title: Signing bonus proration
leaves.criterion: Proration lines sum to the bonus. No bonus is spread over more than 5 years.

leaves.title: Cash, the owner's budget, and the spending floor
leaves.criterion: No AI club ends a floor period below 90 percent in a 30-season run without the shortfall payment being made and logged.

leaves.title: Year-end settlement and carryover
leaves.criterion: Sum of adjustments across clubs equals the incentive differences plus carried room.

leaves.title: Restructure, extension, and pay cut
leaves.criterion: A restructure never changes total money. Total charges before and after are equal across years.

leaves.title: Release, trade, dead money, and June 1
leaves.criterion: For any release the sum of dead money across years equals remaining proration plus remaining guarantees. A third June 1 designation in a year is refused.

leaves.title: Minimum salaries and the veteran benefit
leaves.criterion: No contract year is below the table. The table loads per league year from data.

leaves.title: Rookie contracts and the fifth-year option
leaves.criterion: Every drafted player's contract has the fixed length. Slot values fall strictly with pick number. Option tiers resolve from D14 data only.

leaves.title: Franchise and transition tags
leaves.criterion: Tag values recomputed from world contracts match the stored table. A second tag in one year by one club is refused.

leaves.title: The constraint view
leaves.criterion: Every refusal names one of the four causes. Every number on the panel matches the cap engine. With trust at its floor, intended releases do not appear on the watch list before they happen.

leaves.title: Eligibility and the declared pool
leaves.criterion: No pool member fails the three-season test. In a 30-year run the share of early declarers who go undrafted is a starting 20 to 35 percent (Unverified target, needs a source). No true value changes at the moment of drafting.

leaves.title: The pick ledger and draft order
leaves.criterion: The order built from a saved real season's final standings matches that year's published first-round order before trades. Every pick has exactly one owner at all times.

leaves.title: Compensatory picks
leaves.criterion: Given a saved list of real signings and salaries for one year, the engine reproduces that year's published compensatory awards (test fixture owed by research). No club receives more than 4.

leaves.title: Trading picks
leaves.criterion: Ledger ownership is consistent after every trade. Over a 30-year run the count of draft-day trades per draft falls in a starting band of 20 to 40 (Unverified target).

leaves.title: The clock and making a pick
leaves.criterion: The clock values load from data. A full 7-round draft with 32 AI clubs completes with no pick left unassigned. Every pick made while the user's club is on the clock writes a decision log entry.

leaves.title: Draft rights, signing, and undrafted free agents
leaves.criterion: No club exceeds 90 players or its undrafted bonus pool. Every undrafted signing records the factors of the player's choice for the user to read afterwards.

leaves.title: The pick value chart
leaves.criterion: The chart is strictly falling. Refitting from a new soak run changes no slot by more than a starting 10 percent.

leaves.title: Your players in the draft
leaves.criterion: A coach whose reports run a full grade above outcomes for a starting 5 players has his later reports discounted by the clubs that received them. Draft counts on the program page equal a query over the event log.

leaves.title: Status at contract expiry
leaves.criterion: Status is a pure function of accrued seasons, expiry, and tenders. No restricted player moves without the match window passing.

leaves.title: The negotiating window and opening
leaves.criterion: No contract carries a signing time before the league year opens. In a 30-year run, a starting 60 percent or more of the total guaranteed money of each free agency period is committed in the first 72 hours (Unverified target).

leaves.title: Market value
leaves.criterion: Over a 30-year run each position's share of total cap spending stays within a starting 2 points of its initial share. No expected contract is below the minimum.

leaves.title: How a free agent chooses
leaves.criterion: Every signing stores its top two reasons. With money held equal in a test, a player with a strong relationship edge to a coach picks that club in a starting 70 percent or more of trials.

leaves.title: Trade rules and valuation
leaves.criterion: No trade completes after the deadline or over the cap. In a 30-year run, player trades per league year fall in a starting band of 40 to 90 (Unverified target). Every trade stores each side's valuation for later review.

leaves.title: Deadline week
leaves.criterion: Stance is logged for all 32 clubs each year. A trade made in deadline week sets the arriving player's scheme knowledge to zero for the new system.

leaves.title: Weekly honours
leaves.criterion: One winner per category per conference per week. Over a season, at least 80 percent of weekly offensive winners are quarterbacks, running backs, or receivers (starting check that the public-statistics bias is present).

leaves.title: Season awards and all-league teams
leaves.criterion: Vote totals are stored and sum correctly. In a 30-year run, coach of the year winners' wins above expectation average at least a starting 3. The award never changes any true rating of a person.

leaves.title: Record books as queries
leaves.criterion: Every record shown can be recomputed from the event log. Imported and generated records never appear in one list.

leaves.title: Election and what it reads
leaves.criterion: Class size per year stays in the data range. The user's retirement page shows only facts present in the event log.

leaves.title: Team history and the coaching tree
leaves.criterion: Every tree edge maps to shared seasons in the event log. Tree standing differs by observer in a test with two owners who have different histories against the same coaches.

leaves.title: Identity fields
leaves.criterion: Every person has a unique id for the life of a world. A role change keeps all history reachable from the card.

leaves.title: Experience and eligibility counters
leaves.criterion: Changing the eligibility ruleset changes labels with no code change. Counters never decrease.

leaves.title: Height, weight, length
leaves.criterion: Every player has all fields. Norms shown on the card come from the profile file for his level and position.

leaves.title: Playing weight and body plan
leaves.criterion: A simulated edge rusher who adds 5 percent above frame loses about 2 percent top speed. Body weight never leaves the 92 to 110 percent physical limits, whatever target is set (the limit is the body, not a rule of the game).

leaves.title: Handedness and footedness
leaves.criterion: Flipping a quarterback's hand flips the default blind side in protection calls.

leaves.title: Background fields
leaves.criterion: Every link is two-way and survives role changes. No family field exists on any real person.

leaves.title: Positions a player can play
leaves.criterion: A guard moved to center with zero center reps shows more snap and call errors than after 300 center reps in a controlled test. The injury replacement finder ranks candidates by role grade adjusted for familiarity.

leaves.title: Special teams roles
leaves.criterion: Every special teams role on a depth chart has at least two players with familiarity above 50 or the staff raises a warning.

leaves.title: Freshness between plays and series
leaves.criterion: In a 12-play no-huddle drive test, defensive linemen end with lower freshness than in a 12-play huddle drive, and pressure rate falls late in the drive. A 320 lb player tires faster than a 200 lb player at equal stamina (D2.4.1 criterion).

leaves.title: Conditioning level
leaves.criterion: A player idle for 8 weeks falls to the floor region and regains 90 within 6 weeks of full work.

leaves.title: Load, tolerance, and the accumulated value
leaves.criterion: A test team practising in full pads every day reaches the overreached band by week 3 and shows more soft-tissue injuries and lower fourth-quarter freshness than a control. Thresholds are evaluated on debt only: a single very heavy day followed by rest never triggers the overreached band if debt stays under 35 percent. The planning projection matches the simulated bands.

leaves.title: Wear across a season
leaves.criterion: A back at the 99th percentile of carries shows wear near 1 by the last weeks, and a rotational back shows none.

leaves.title: Heat, altitude, and travel
leaves.criterion: With all three multipliers on, simulated home win rate stays inside the J15 band. Turning them off lowers it by no more than 1 point.

leaves.title: Planned snap shares
leaves.criterion: A simulated league of AI coaches reproduces the reference shares within 5 points for each cell. A user plan is followed within 5 points when no injury or tempo constraint intervenes.

leaves.title: Injury checks in a play
leaves.criterion: After tuning, simulated seasons match each calibration target within 10 percent over 200 simulated team-seasons. Doubling a running back's carries raises his injury count in proportion to his added contact events, with no hidden cap.

leaves.title: Catalog rows and time lost
leaves.criterion: For each row with nflverse data, simulated games-missed distributions match the median exactly and the mean within 0.5 games. The catalog loads from a data file, and a row missing a required field fails the build.

leaves.title: Roles and clearance
leaves.criterion: No user action can set a player to cleared. Placing a player who is not cleared on the game-day active list shows the L8.2.5 warning and writes exactly one `violation_log` row; it is never greyed out (audit Part 17). Limits are enforced by the substitution logic (a snap cap pulls him at the cap unless the user overrides, which counts as pressure under D11.3.3).

leaves.title: The estimate the coach gets
leaves.criterion: Across a simulated season the true return date falls inside the shown range 80 percent of the time (accept 75 to 85).

leaves.title: Pressure and its cost
leaves.criterion: A test world where the user pressures every case shows higher re-injury counts and lower trust than the control, by the configured amounts.

leaves.title: Removal, evaluation, and no-go
leaves.criterion: A player with a no-go sign re-enters only through the rule 8 act: warning shown, one `violation_log` row written, detection drawn. No AI coach with high `ruleRespect` attempts it in a 1,000-game test, and imported AI coaches never do (audit Part 17). The medical timeout stops the clock per B1 and resets a play clock under 10 to 10. The follow-up exam exists for every evaluated player.

leaves.title: Return to participation
leaves.criterion: Simulated concussions reproduce a median near 9 days and about 38 percent playing the following week. No player reaches step 5 in fewer than 4 days after step 1 begins.

leaves.title: Practice report and game status
leaves.criterion: Simulated league play rates by designation fall inside the ranges above over 10 seasons of AI reports. No report can contain "Probable". A report that contradicts logged practice reps is flagged before submission.

leaves.title: Roster lists for injured players
leaves.criterion: The recommendation fires only when the test is true. Values are read from C5 config, not from this file.

leaves.title: Coming back
leaves.criterion: Simulated hamstring recurrence within the same season is 12 to 18 percent. Players held to a snap count in their first game back have measurably fewer re-injuries than those who are not, in a controlled test.

leaves.title: Playing hurt
leaves.criterion: Every catalog row has play-through penalties or is marked "cannot play through". A hidden injury is revealed within 3 weeks in 90 percent of cases.

leaves.title: Shutting a player down and timing surgery
leaves.criterion: Every catalog row with `surgery_optional` offers both paths with dates. A surgery date earlier in the season gives an earlier return the next year by exactly the difference in dates. In a 10-season AI test, contract-year players choose to play through more often than players with guaranteed deals.

leaves.title: Illness and heat events
leaves.criterion: Cramp events per game rise with heat index in simulation and are near zero in domes. An illness cluster never removes more than half a position room at once without the user being warned a day ahead.

leaves.title: The role a player expects
leaves.criterion: Every rostered player has an expected role and usage. A promise in the ledger changes the expectation the day it is made.

leaves.title: The satisfaction value
leaves.criterion: Each driver can be set alone in a test and moves satisfaction by its range. The reasons list always names the two largest negative drivers.

leaves.title: Trust in the head coach
leaves.criterion: A coach who keeps every promise for a season raises mean roster trust by a visible band. One who breaks three promises to starters loses a band across the room, not only with those players.

leaves.title: Buy-in
leaves.criterion: With all caps set to 1, a world's football output is identical whatever buy-in is. With defaults, a team at buy-in 85 commits fewer discipline errors than the same team at 40 by the configured ratio.

leaves.title: Stress accumulation and thresholds
leaves.criterion: A scripted sequence of small stressors that totals 66 fires exactly one breaking-point event, and the same stressors with a relief event in the middle fire none. No band changes on any single stressor unless the total crosses a threshold.

leaves.title: Effects on football
leaves.criterion: With every D12 multiplier set to 1 the engine's output is unchanged. With defaults, the gap in points per game between a league's happiest and unhappiest quartile of teams, holding talent equal, is under 1.0.

leaves.title: Threshold events
leaves.criterion: A benched starter with no conversation reaches the public-complaint step within the stated weeks. The same player given an honest role conversation and a real path back does not.

leaves.title: Morale for real imported people
leaves.criterion: The D13.6.2 fuzz test finds no stress event, quoted complaint, or personal driver on any real person.

leaves.title: Entry points and editing
leaves.criterion: A player made from each entry point loads in a game and produces a valid play record. A designed player in a career world sets the "edited" flag. A blank-sheet player with no fields set is rejected with a list of missing required fields.

leaves.title: Plausibility checks and the sandbox switch
leaves.criterion: The 330 lb, 4.30 player is flagged. Every real combine row in the data passes the single-value check. Sandbox players are excluded from any shared ranking.

leaves.title: Pipeline and determinism
leaves.criterion: Same seed and request give a byte-identical record. Generating a class of 10,000 at one position reproduces the profile's means within 0.05 sd and its correlations within 0.03. No generated person fails D13.1.2.

leaves.title: Position profiles
leaves.criterion: The profile script reproduces the table from the CSV. Each profile's correlation matrix is positive semi-definite. A missing cell fails the build with the cell named.

leaves.title: People built from real profiles for the shipped world
leaves.criterion: Position-by-age counts of the shipped pro population match the real 2025 active rosters within 2 percent per cell. The nearest-neighbour check passes. No shipped full name equals a name in the pack (D13.5.2).

leaves.title: Who is tracked: three tiers of people
leaves.criterion: Opening the same abstract slot in two saves of one world yields the same person. Save size after 40 simulated years is under 1.5 times the size at year 5 (starting target).

leaves.title: High school recruit classes
leaves.criterion: Four classes exist at all times. Position shares of a generated class are within 1 point of config. After a 30-year run every college team fields a full roster every year with no emergency fills. The count of age-22 players at or above the draftable line is within 10 percent of D13.3.4's target each year, averaged over 10 years.

leaves.title: Other player entries: walk-ons, transfers in, and late entrants
leaves.criterion: No team starts a season under its minimum roster. Walk-ons who become starters occur, and at a rate under 2 percent of starters (starting band).

leaves.title: The pro entry pool
leaves.criterion: Over 30 simulated years the mean number of rookies making an opening 53 is within 10 percent of the real figure (target source needed, see open questions). Small-school fills are under 5 percent of a class on average.

leaves.title: Coaches, staff, agents, and officials
leaves.criterion: In a 40-year run no job at any rung stays open more than 30 days for lack of candidates. Mean age by rung stays within 2 years of its starting value. At least one former player of the user's becomes a coach in a typical 20-year career.

leaves.title: The weekly top-up
leaves.criterion: In a 60-year run no pool is ever under its threshold at the start of a week. No top-up person has a ceiling above tier 2. Total top-up volume is under 10 percent of yearly intake.

leaves.title: The yearly census
leaves.criterion: The census runs in under 5 seconds on a full world. Every metric has a target and a tolerance in config, and a missing one fails the build.

leaves.title: Correction rules
leaves.criterion: In a test where development gains are raised 20 percent on purpose, pro-starter ISS stays within 1.5 tolerances for 30 years and the cap alarm fires. In a correct world, total correction stays under 0.15 sd at every position for 50 years.

leaves.title: Era settings
leaves.criterion: With frozen era, the mean 40 of drafted receivers in years 1 to 5 and years 36 to 40 differ by less than 0.01 s.

leaves.title: Soak tests
leaves.criterion: As listed. The test runs in the nightly build.

leaves.title: The class validator
leaves.criterion: Under 5 percent of classes need a regeneration. Two machines given the same world seed, version, config, and pack produce identical classes for 60 years.

leaves.title: Name generation
leaves.criterion: The 50 most common generated surnames in a 10,000-person class match the table's top 50 in at least 45 cases. Name files can be swapped without a rebuild.

leaves.title: The collision guard
leaves.criterion: Zero generated full names equal a pack name in a 60-year soak run, including the common-surname cases that exhaust 10 first-name redraws. The check adds under 1 ms per person.

leaves.title: Background
leaves.criterion: Every generated adult has a team history with no gaps and no overlap. No real high school or college mark appears.

leaves.title: The import tool
leaves.criterion: Importing the project's own pack yields 32 full pro rosters' worth of real players with zero schema errors. The preview's gap counts match the README's gap list. No image is downloaded.

leaves.title: The real-person safety rule
leaves.criterion: A fuzz test that fires every sensitive event 10,000 times in an all-real world produces zero events with a real subject. Every event type in the catalog has the tag set to true or false, and a missing tag fails the build.

leaves.title: Auto-fill and the real-career dial
leaves.criterion: A pack with only name, position, and age per row imports without error and produces valid players. With the dial at 100 in a past-year start, a real player's simulated attribute path matches U3's estimate of each real season within 2 ISS.

leaves.title: From play record to stat lines
leaves.criterion: For any player and statistic, the sum of credit rows equals the aggregate shown. Re-deriving a season's statistics from stored play records gives identical totals. Team totals equal the sum of player credits for every additive statistic.

leaves.title: Box-score statistics
leaves.criterion: Every column in the pack's season table maps to a catalog statistic or is listed as deliberately skipped. A simulated league's totals for completion rate, yards per attempt, interception rate, and sack rate can be computed from the catalog with no extra fields.

leaves.title: Charting and tracking statistics
leaves.criterion: Each charting statistic has a written definition in the catalog and a test play set with a known answer. League pressure rate computed under the "hurries included" and "hurries excluded" definitions differs in the direction the research found.

leaves.title: Logs and split queries
leaves.criterion: Any split's total equals the sum of its parts across a complete partition (for example four quarters plus overtime). A query over one season returns in under 200 ms on the target machine.

leaves.title: Totals, honours, and the career page
leaves.criterion: Career totals equal the sum of season rows by level. No real team mark appears on any career page. Record books update at the end of each game.

leaves.title: Team and unit context
leaves.criterion: Every player-season has a system family and position coach recorded. Coaching-tree queries ("everyone who played for coach X") return from these fields.

leaves.title: Sample size and reliability notes
leaves.criterion: The two worked examples produce the stated standard errors. No rate is displayed without its count.

leaves.title: Level and competition splits
leaves.criterion: Translated bands contain the player's actual higher-level result 80 percent of the time (accept 72 to 88) across a 30-year run. No screen shows a lower-level statistic without its level mark.

leaves.title: Storage and archiving
leaves.criterion: The D13.3.1 save-size criterion holds with default settings over 40 years. Deleting old play records never changes any frozen aggregate.

leaves.title: The test battery
leaves.criterion: Simulated repeat tests of one player scatter with the configured noise. The card never shows the true value in career mode.

leaves.title: Tracking and practice load data
leaves.criterion: Top recorded speed never exceeds the true top speed plus noise. No load screen reads a hidden value (code check as in D6.1.1).

leaves.title: Speed and acceleration
leaves.criterion: J2's test: simulated 10-yard and 40-yard times match the stored times within 0.02 s for 20 sample players.

leaves.title: Change of direction
leaves.criterion: J2's drill reproduction test passes for 3-cone and shuttle.

leaves.title: Play strength
leaves.criterion: Across a position, the correlation between bench reps and play strength is 0.45 to 0.60.

leaves.title: Explosiveness
leaves.criterion: Jump-ball outcomes in J6 tests move with jump reach plus height plus arm length as specified there.

leaves.title: Stamina
leaves.criterion: With equal stamina, a 320 lb player's freshness falls faster per play than a 200 lb player's. In a simulated league season with staff default rotations (M2.3.1), the top defensive lineman's mean snap share is 71% to 81% and the fourth's 39% to 49%, while the top five offensive linemen stay above 85%.

leaves.title: Durability
leaves.criterion: In a long simulation, players in the worst durability decile miss about twice the games of the best decile, and no card shows the trait.
