Calibration target from the evidence above: players injured in season N have a hazard of any injury in season N+1 between 1.8 and 3.5 times that of uninjured players (band around the 2.7 found in soccer, to be narrowed when a football figure is sourced); players with a prior ACL injury have a later ACL injury rate about 2 to 3 times that of matched players (25% against 9% over the study period).

leaves.title: Norm tables and percentiles
leaves.criterion: A 4.47 forty for a corner shows the 50th percentile on the pro profile. Editing a threshold changes only marks, never percentiles. A 4.37 corner shows the 90th percentile and a 4.59 corner the 10th. An RB 40 of 4.68 reads the 10th percentile from the empirical table, not the normal curve. Every real row in the register maps to a percentile between 0 and 100 with no error.

leaves.title: Storage, groups, and universal attributes
leaves.criterion: A build-time check lists, for every attribute, at least one J formula that reads it. Changing one attribute by 10 ISS in a controlled test changes the win rate of its named contest and of no unrelated contest.

leaves.title: Quarterback attributes
leaves.criterion: As D3.1.1, for each row.

leaves.title: Running back and fullback attributes
leaves.criterion: As D3.1.1. A back with high zone vision and low gap vision gains more per carry on inside zone than on power in a controlled test with equal blocking.

leaves.title: Offensive line attributes
leaves.criterion: As D3.1.1. A lineman with high anchor and low mirror wins more against bull rushes than against speed rushes in a controlled test.

leaves.title: Coverage attributes
leaves.criterion: As D3.1.1. A corner with high press and low off-man loses more separation in off alignment than in press against the same receiver.

leaves.title: Specialist attributes
leaves.criterion: As D3.1.1. A league of generated kickers reproduces the J15 field goal targets by distance within tolerance.

leaves.title: Returner and core special teams attributes
Play recognition
leaves.criterion: In a controlled test, linebackers at recognition 70 reach their run fits about 0.1 s sooner than at 50 on the same play, and bite on play action less often by the configured ratio.

leaves.title: Processing speed
leaves.criterion: A quarterback at processing 70 reaches read three about 0.2 s sooner than at 50 in the J7 test harness. Cutting a defense's checks from four to two lowers its average reaction delay.

leaves.title: Assignment discipline
leaves.criterion: The film sheet labels each mental error as knowledge or discipline correctly in a test with forced errors. Raising discipline from 40 to 70 cuts discipline errors by the formula's ratio.

leaves.title: Foul discipline
leaves.criterion: A simulated league's accepted penalties per game fall inside the J15 tolerance. Teams with the highest standards factor commit fewer discipline fouls than those with the lowest, by the configured ratio.

leaves.title: Composure under pressure
leaves.criterion: With the range set to zero, results are identical in every leverage bucket. With defaults, the difference in completion rate between high and low leverage for a league of average players is under 0.5 points.

leaves.title: Learning rate
leaves.criterion: Two players differing only in learning rate (0.8 against 1.2) reach knowledge 80 on a concept in a rep ratio of about 3 to 2.

leaves.title: Football intelligence
leaves.criterion: Teams that practise the two-minute situation show fewer in-bounds errors late in halves than teams that do not, in a controlled comparison.

leaves.title: Quarterback and signal-caller skills
leaves.criterion: A build-time check confirms each skill is read by the J formula named. A quarterback with low blitz recognition is sacked by unblocked rushers more often than one with high recognition against the same pressures.

leaves.title: Traits and their storage
leaves.criterion: Every trait is read by at least one named system (build check, as in D3.1.1). No trait value is displayed in career mode.

leaves.title: Observation and trait lines
leaves.criterion: No trait line exists without a logged observation behind it. After one full season with an average staff, at least 6 of 12 traits have an estimate band under plus or minus 15 for a starter. The engine uses the true trait from the first day regardless of what has been observed.

leaves.title: Bounded effects table
leaves.criterion: A config test sets every range to 1 and confirms identical simulation output to a world with all traits at 50. Each row is verified by a controlled test that varies one trait.

leaves.title: Off-field incident model
leaves.criterion: The D13.6.2 fuzz test covers this leaf: zero incidents with a real subject. In an all-generated pro league, arrests average about 1.5 per team per season (53 roster spots × 2.9 percent), within plus or minus 25 percent.

leaves.title: Neutral traits and the exclusion flag
leaves.criterion: After a 20-year run of an all-real world, no real person has a trait line, a character flag, or a non-50 trait. The exclusion flag cannot be cleared by any command in the log.

leaves.title: The estimate record
leaves.criterion: With unbiased evidence, the mean converges on the true value and 80 percent of true values fall inside the shown band across a test population (accept 76 to 84 percent). No screen in career mode reads a true value: a code check proves that the UI layer cannot import the true-value accessor.

leaves.title: What is never estimated
leaves.criterion: No band is drawn for an exact field. A school-reported test shows a "reported" marker.

leaves.title: Scale options and the default mapping
leaves.criterion: Switching scale changes no stored data. ISS 40, 50, 60 show 6.0, 6.5, 7.0 on the default. A custom scale file loads without a rebuild.

leaves.title: Overall grade for a position and role
leaves.criterion: Every role in F1 has a weight table. Rank correlation target above is met in the calibration report.

leaves.title: Role label
leaves.criterion: Every rostered player has exactly one label per unit he belongs to. A user override is kept until he clears it.

leaves.title: Flags
leaves.criterion: No character flag exists on any real person after a 20-year run. Each flag type has a raise rule and a clear rule in config.

leaves.title: Priors
leaves.criterion: Prior means are unbiased across the population: mean error within 1 ISS at every position.

leaves.title: Evidence sources and their noise
leaves.criterion: The tuning target is met within 20 percent. An attribute with no qualifying snaps keeps its prior variance.

leaves.title: Evaluator bias and the floor
leaves.criterion: With one evaluator of skill 50, band half-width never goes below 1.28 × 3.5 = 4.5 ISS. Adding a second independent evaluator narrows it.

leaves.title: Aging of evidence
leaves.criterion: The 80 percent coverage test in D6.1.1 still passes for players unseen for 1, 2, and 3 years.

leaves.title: One scale for every level, and the competition discount
leaves.criterion: In a 30-year run the simulated draft reproduces the outcome table above within 8 points per cell, with seasons started and honours taken from D14. Fewer than 1 in 5 quarterbacks who start for a college champion ever exceed ISS 60 as pros, and their mean first-year pro role grade is below 6.5 (starting bands, Assumption). No code path changes a true value on a change of level. A player with the same true values shows the same absolute grade whether he is listed on a college or a pro roster.

leaves.title: Projected grade and its band
leaves.criterion: Across a generated recruit class, internal projections at 17 correlate with true peak ISS between 0.45 and 0.65 for an average staff (starting band), and higher for a strong one. Late bloomers exist: at least 3 percent of eventual pro starters were projected below 6.0 internally at 18 (their words read as a modest hunch). No UI screen renders a projected number or range: a code check proves it.

leaves.title: Gain per rep
leaves.criterion: A player with a 20-point gap, full reps, average teaching, age 22 gains about 0.8 ISS in the first week and about 12 points over a 30-week year. Simulated young pro cohorts reproduce the sign and rough size of the measured changes when run through the same delta method.

leaves.title: Which attributes develop and how fast
leaves.criterion: Config holds a class for every attribute, and a missing class fails the build.

leaves.title: Rep sources and weights
leaves.criterion: The weekly rep projection in H3 equals what D7 later credits, within rounding. Moving 10 team reps from a starter to a backup shifts credited reps by 10 × the weight.

leaves.title: Playing time
leaves.criterion: Two identical rookies, one playing 800 snaps and one playing 100, differ in recognition gain by the ratio the formula implies.

leaves.title: The teaching multiplier
leaves.criterion: The best possible coach raises a room's yearly gain by no more than 15 percent over an average one, all else equal. A user who passes every check gets a teaching term of exactly `user_term_ceiling` (75), never 100. A check that would pass against the staff estimate but fails against truth counts as failed. Setting the range to 0 in config removes the effect. The range appears in no Q2 target list.

leaves.title: Coaching points
leaves.criterion: An active point on pass set raises that attribute's gain and no other. A tendency never moves more than 15 points from natural.

leaves.title: Ceilings and the development rate
leaves.criterion: In a generated class, at least 3 percent of eventual pro starters had a projection below 6.0 at 18 (D6.5.1 criterion). No true value exceeds its ceiling.

leaves.title: Plateaus and breakthroughs
leaves.criterion: Year-to-year gain for players of the same age and gap has a coefficient of variation between 0.3 and 0.5, reached without per-player caps (Marlon, 2026-11-26: improvement depends on more than the player). G-20 measured about 0.25 with the earlier caps (form 0.5 to 1.5, development rate 0.6 to 1.5, PR 62) and 0.38 with the uncapped terms and the yearly surroundings multiplier (PR 78), so the target is met and the conflict is resolved by the ruling. The Q1.6.4 30-season stability check still passes. The spreads are Assumptions.

leaves.title: Loss without use
leaves.criterion: A skill left unused for 20 weeks falls about 3 percent and returns to its peak within about 4 weeks of full work.

leaves.title: Changing a player's position
leaves.criterion: A safety moved to linebacker with a matching frame reaches a linebacker role grade within 5 ISS of his safety grade in two seasons when his hidden ceilings allow it, and never when they do not.

leaves.title: Development windows and individual plans
leaves.criterion: Every rostered player has a plan at the start of each window, written by the staff if the user does not. Plan priorities change credited reps by the stated amount.

leaves.title: Body growth curve
leaves.criterion: A generated class aged from 14 to 23 with average programs reaches adult values within 1 percent. Mean weight gain from 18 to 22 by position falls within the 4 to 7 percent range above.

leaves.title: Position curves
leaves.criterion: After tuning, every cell of the calibration table is reproduced within 2 standard errors of the measured value, using the standard errors in `aging_curves_results.csv`. No position's mean roster age drifts more than 0.5 years from D13.4.1's values over 30 simulated years.

leaves.title: Order and split of physical loss
leaves.criterion: A simulated quarterback cohort shows scramble rate falling from age 27 while completion rate over expected is flat to 30. A simulated receiver cohort's average depth of target falls after 30.

leaves.title: Permanent losses from injury
leaves.criterion: Simulated ACL cohorts reproduce a 55 to 65 percent return rate and a multi-season drop in games played.

leaves.title: Exit hazard
leaves.criterion: Simulated exit rates by age band and position fall within 5 points of the table over a 30-year run. Median career length of drafted players is 6 seasons, within 1 (D13.4.1 fact).

leaves.title: Signs of decline and the aging outlook
leaves.criterion: The outlook label is right about direction at least 60 percent of the time for an average staff in a simulated test, and no better than 80 percent for the best staff.

leaves.title: Knowledge items and their structure
leaves.criterion: Every assignment in a called play maps to knowledge items for the player holding it. A play using an uninstalled tag shows zero knowledge for that tag and a warning on the call sheet.

leaves.title: Teaching units and the gain formula
leaves.criterion: The projection shown in planning matches the simulated result within 5 points on average. Doubling new items in a week lowers average knowledge gained per item by the crowding formula.

leaves.title: Decay
leaves.criterion: An item at 90 unused for 8 weeks falls to about 80 and returns to 90 with two full-speed reps and a review.

leaves.title: Carryover between systems
leaves.criterion: A team that keeps its coordinator and system starts camp with family knowledge near last year's floor. A team that changes system starts lower by the similarity table, and its early-season mental errors are higher in simulation.

leaves.title: Knowledge errors on a play
leaves.criterion: The four knowledge levels above produce error rates within 10 percent of the formula in a 100,000-assignment test. Film tags separate knowledge from discipline errors correctly in a forced-error test.

leaves.title: Cohesion from snaps together
leaves.criterion: A line that has played 1,000 snaps together allows fewer free rushers on stunts than the same five with zero snaps together, by the configured cap. Setting all caps to zero removes every cohesion effect.

leaves.title: Readiness report
leaves.criterion: Every call on the sheet has a readiness value. Cutting the lowest-readiness tenth of the sheet lowers simulated mental errors in a controlled comparison.

leaves.title: Coach record schema
leaves.criterion: 1. The user's coach record validates against the same schema as a generated AI coach. 2. Swapping `is_user` to an AI coach in a test save lets the simulation run a full season with the former user coach driven by K3 to K5. 3. No field in the record is a direct modifier on a play contest (J6). A static check of the engine's inputs confirms it.

leaves.title: Playing history
leaves.criterion: Two test coaches that differ only in playing history show the stated opening differences and reach equal player reputation within two simulated seasons of equal results.

leaves.title: Coaching history and the tree
leaves.criterion: After creation, the hireable-assistant list (L4) ranks former colleagues above strangers of equal skill. Every history row has a team that existed and a head coach who held that job in that season of the generated world. Across 1,000 generated first-time college head coaches, mean prior coaching seasons fall between 15 and 19 and the share whose first row is an entry seat is above 0.88.

leaves.title: Education and non-football experience
leaves.criterion: No football system reads the education field. A static check confirms it. Every generated history with a graduate assistant row also has a bachelor's degree and a graduate program row covering those seasons, and none has more than three graduate assistant seasons.

leaves.title: Side of the ball and specialty
leaves.criterion: Two coaches who differ only in stated side produce identical results when the same inputs are played. They receive different job interest. In a 30-season world run, the offensive share of new professional head coach hires falls between 0.50 and 0.65 and of top-subdivision hires between 0.58 and 0.75.

leaves.title: System families and seasons worked in them
leaves.criterion: Install time for a package depends on the players' and assistants' exposure to the family and never on a value stored on the user's coach.

leaves.title: No points: the coach starts as his past
leaves.criterion: 1. The coach record of a newly created user coach contains no numeric ability field. A schema check confirms it. 2. Two user coaches with different backgrounds, given identical inputs in an identical game state, produce identical outcomes. 3. No descriptor appears on a new coach's card until the label engine's minimum sample is met.

leaves.title: Age, name, and appearance
leaves.criterion: The age picker never offers an age below the computed minimum. In a 30-season world run, the mean age of new professional head coach hires falls between 46 and 51, and of top-subdivision hires between 43 and 48, with 10% to 22% of top-subdivision hires under 40.

leaves.title: Household
leaves.criterion: Choosing "no household detail" produces zero family events in a simulated 10-season test.

leaves.title: Personal traits: retired as a choice
leaves.criterion: The creation flow has no trait step. A text search of config finds no user-trait modifier table.

leaves.title: Career start mode
leaves.criterion: Each start mode produces a coach whose age, history, contract, and money are mutually consistent under the rules in E1.2 to E1.5. Each shortcut's written seasons fall inside the table's range, and a head coach start never writes fewer coaching seasons than its age allows minus the playing and work years.

leaves.title: Choosing the first team
leaves.criterion: The situation report's records, money, and contract figures equal the world database values. Its roster grades equal the public D6 estimate, not the true ratings. In "open jobs only" mode the count of vacancies falls inside the verified real range per cycle.

leaves.title: Creation flow
leaves.criterion: The same choices with the same seed produce an identical coach record. Confirm is disabled while any bound is violated. A fuzz test of 10,000 random step orders and back-steps never produces a confirmed record that fails checks 1 to 8.

leaves.title: Archetype presets
leaves.criterion: Every preset passes creation validation unedited (E1.7.1 checks 1 to 8). No preset row holds a field other than the past facts listed in the table, which the schema check confirms.

leaves.title: Statement schema and editor
leaves.criterion: Every commitment maps to a catalogue id with a measure. Saving a statement changes no value outside the `philosophy` object.

leaves.title: The identity sheet
leaves.criterion: With the sheet changed and nothing else, no play result changes. Roster-need output from M1 changes.

leaves.title: Standards that are real instructions
leaves.criterion: Each standard in the catalogue resolves to exactly one owner setting. Removing E10 from the build leaves every setting reachable from its owner screen.

leaves.title: Words against deeds
leaves.criterion: 1. Each ledger row's counts equal the number of linked decision records. 2. One discipline case produces one consistency event in total across L3.3.1 and this ledger. 3. A decision made with a contrary fact hidden from the coach is never recorded as a break. 4. With the ledger disabled, play results with the same seed and inputs are identical.

leaves.title: Replacing the last coach's identity
leaves.criterion: With an empty statement the target equals the coach's measured behaviour. Holdover and new-arrival starting values differ as stated.

leaves.title: Below head coach
leaves.criterion: A rung 5 coach's commitments to his players are tested only on decisions that were his.

leaves.title: The note object and where it can be written
leaves.criterion: 1. From every screen that shows a person, team, crew, play, game, or decision, a note can be created and is attached to that subject without the user choosing it. 2. Creating a note during a live play clock does not stop or slow the clock. 3. A search of the codebase finds no reader of `note.text` other than display, search, and export.

leaves.title: Note kinds and prompts
leaves.criterion: Each prompt appears at its trigger, can be dismissed with one input, and can be disabled in settings.

leaves.title: Notes that come back when the subject does
leaves.criterion: 1. A note written on a coordinator in season 1 appears on the scouting screen when the user faces a team he coaches in season 6, at a different club and level. 2. On game day the notes tab shows only pinned notes for the current opponent and crew. 3. No resurfaced note is altered by the game.

leaves.title: The notebook screen, search, and export
leaves.criterion: All notes survive save, load, job change, and a move between levels. Export of 1,000 notes produces a readable text file with dates and subjects. A shared save without the box ticked contains no note text.

leaves.title: Rungs and titles
leaves.criterion: Every job in a generated world maps to exactly one rung. The distribution of AI coaches' years per rung over a 30-season simulation falls inside the verified real ranges once those are Verified.

leaves.title: Work at each rung
leaves.criterion: 1. At every rung from 1 to 7 at least one assignment per game week opens a real tool with real data from the save. 2. A deliberately wrong report by the user measurably lowers the AI boss's plan quality in a controlled test. 3. A rung 2 season in key-weeks mode completes in under 60 minutes of play.

leaves.title: Rung 0: getting in the door
leaves.criterion: From every rung 0 path a competent user can reach rung 2 within four in-game years in at least 90% of seeded trials.

leaves.title: The levels
leaves.criterion: Every job has a level, and every level has a hiring window in the calendar.

leaves.title: Moving between levels
leaves.criterion: In a 30-season world simulation, cross-level moves occur in both directions and the direct college-to-professional head coach hire is rare, inside the verified real rate.

leaves.title: The hiring calendar
leaves.criterion: 1. For every employed candidate and every day of a simulated cycle, the engine's allowed interview mode matches the state table. 2. No interview with a playoff-team candidate exceeds 180 minutes in total per hiring club under default config. 3. No contract object is created for a coach before the day after his club's final game. 4. A head coach search that interviews fewer than two external qualifying candidates in person is flagged as a violation. Changing `head_coach.external_candidates` to 1 removes the flag with no code change. 5. Loading the college rule record removes all playoff-keyed windows. 6. The cascade fills every job before the offseason program begins.

leaves.title: Who is hiring and what they want
leaves.criterion: With identical candidates, two hiring parties with opposed weights rank them differently. Across 1,000 simulated cycles the share of hires by side and by prior job falls inside verified real ranges.

leaves.title: The open jobs board and applying
leaves.criterion: 1. At any date the board's rows equal the set of unfilled opening objects in the save, at both levels. 2. The user can submit an application to every listed opening. 3. With relationships and record held equal, applying changes the user's chance of an interview only by adding him to the pool: the candidate score for the user is identical with and without the application. 4. A rung 2 coach applying for a professional head job receives no interview in 1,000 seeded trials.

leaves.title: A market that keeps moving: lateral moves, retirements, failures, and new entrants
leaves.criterion: 1. In a 50-season world simulation with no user, at least one opening appears every year at every rung from 2 to 9 at each level. 2. Over the same run, professional head coach openings per year average inside five to ten (firings alone five to nine; an offseason can reach 10). 3. The count of people holding rung 1 to 3 jobs stays within 5 percent of the number of such jobs for the whole run. 4. Each of the reasons (lateral, followed a boss, released, retired, left football, promoted) occurs in the run and appears in the `reason` field. 5. No health, money, or scandal event is recorded for any imported real person.

leaves.title: Search firms and who runs a search
leaves.criterion: 1. Over 200 simulated college cycles the share of openings with a firm is within tolerance of the key. 2. A candidate with a tie to the consultant appears on more lists than an identical candidate without one. 3. The final choice never comes from the firm record.

leaves.title: Market value and the network
leaves.criterion: Removing all relationship edges from a test rung 5 coach cuts interview requests by at least half with results held equal.

leaves.title: Requests, permission, and saying yes
leaves.criterion: A lateral request is blockable and a head coach request is not, under the default rule data. Changing the rule data changes the behaviour without code changes.

leaves.title: The interview
leaves.criterion: A user who answers every board question correctly scores above a user who answers none, with all else equal, in every seeded trial. No term of the interview score reads a stored value of the user's coach: replaying the same answers from two different career histories gives the same interview score.

leaves.title: Interview rules for clubs: the Rooney Rule and the user
leaves.criterion: 1. A search that hires with the counter unmet produces a league finding every time. 2. AI clubs satisfy the rule in at least the share set in config and violators are fined on the same table as the user. 3. Setting the key to `none` removes the counter and all checks with no other change. 4. Compensatory picks appear in the C7 order for the right club and years.

leaves.title: Offers
leaves.criterion: With two live offers, the final terms of the accepted one are never worse than with one.

leaves.title: Judging a situation
leaves.criterion: With a contact inside the organisation the estimate error for owner patience is smaller than without, by the configured factor.

leaves.title: Coach trades: hiring a coach who is under contract
leaves.tag: v1, pro; college uses the buyout in E3.8.1
leaves.criterion: 1. A professional head coach with years left cannot be signed by another professional club unless a compensation agreement exists or the holding club has released him. 2. Agreed picks leave the pursuing club's ledger and enter the holder's on the agreement date. 3. With `coach_trade.mode = contract_buyout`, no picks move and the buyout amount in the contract is paid. 4. Across 200 simulated seasons under default config, coach trades for a head coach occur at a low rate (starting target: fewer than one every three seasons) and none exceeds the configured maximum compensation.

leaves.title: Work grades
leaves.criterion: A perfect report earns full accuracy regardless of the boss's skill. The boss's stated opinion can differ from it.

leaves.title: Promotion from within
leaves.criterion: With equal scores, the internal candidate wins more often than the external one by the configured bonus.

leaves.title: Interim head coach
leaves.criterion: An interim stint appears in career history with its own record line.

leaves.title: Being fired
leaves.criterion: After a firing, salary continues to post to E6 on schedule until the contract ends or offset applies.

leaves.title: The year out and the second act
leaves.criterion: In a long world simulation the share of first-time professional head coaches who later hold a second head job is near 39% and inside 33% to 46% (R32, 1 of 3, so a starting target and not a verified range).

leaves.title: Resigning and walking away
leaves.criterion: A resignation for a new job posts the buyout to E6 on the stated date.

leaves.title: Retirement
leaves.criterion: Retirement writes a complete legacy record and the world continues to simulate.

leaves.title: Work after and between coaching jobs: the media seat
leaves.criterion: 1. A coach in a media seat has a slower market-value decay than an idle coach with the same record. 2. No attribute or skill value changes because of a media job. 3. Offset arithmetic matches E3 for a fired coach with a guarantee.

leaves.title: Contract schema
leaves.criterion: Every employed coach in a generated world has exactly one active contract. The sum of scheduled payments equals the sum of salary fields.

leaves.title: Reading the conflict between the two research files
leaves.criterion: The guarantee default is read from config per level.

leaves.title: Pay bands by rung and level
leaves.tag: v1, both; bands by level via pay_bands.<level>
leaves.criterion: Every generated contract's salary falls inside its band unless a logged leverage event explains it. Every band cell carries a source and status field.

leaves.title: Incentives
leaves.criterion: A triggered bonus posts once, on the event date.

leaves.title: Payment schedule
leaves.criterion: Twelve months of payments sum to the year's salary to the cent.

leaves.title: Termination without cause
leaves.tag: v1, both; defaults by level via contract_defaults.<level>
leaves.criterion: Firing a coach with three full years left at $6M produces an $18M obligation spread over the original schedule. A power four assistant at $350,000 with a 70% guarantee fired with 18 months left is owed $367,500, paid monthly. A Group of Six assistant whose head coach leaves is owed at most two months of salary.

leaves.title: Offset and the duty to mitigate
leaves.tag: v1, both; defaults by level via contract_defaults.<level>
leaves.criterion: A fired coach owed $6M a year who takes a $2M coordinator job receives $4M from the old club and $2M from the new one in that year.

leaves.title: Termination for cause
leaves.tag: v1, both; defaults by level via contract_defaults.<level>
leaves.criterion: No for-cause event can occur without a logged conduct event. A cure-eligible ground with a cure completed in 5 days ends the case with no termination. Losing games alone never produces a for-cause notice.

leaves.title: The coach leaves early
leaves.criterion: A college coach leaving in year 2 owes the year 2 buyout amount exactly. An Oregon-style assistant leaving on September 15 of the first season owes 50% of remaining guaranteed salary, and owes nothing if the new job is a play-calling coordinator job. A resignation inside the season window is possible and is logged as a breach.

leaves.title: Settlements
leaves.criterion: Accepting a settlement stops all scheduled payments and removes the offset.

leaves.title: Roster authority
leaves.criterion: In a test dispute over a roster cut, the outcome follows the authority flag in every case.

leaves.title: Staff authority and budget
leaves.criterion: The user cannot sign assistants whose total salary exceeds the pool. A generated professional staff has 19 to 27 on-field coaches. A generated top-subdivision college staff never lists more than 11 coaches who recruit off campus without a logged violation (L8.2.5).

leaves.title: Other clauses
leaves.criterion: Each clause maps to at least one consuming rule in another category.

leaves.title: The negotiation loop
leaves.criterion: A counter inside the hidden budget is always accepted. Total value conceded never exceeds the budget.

leaves.title: Leverage
leaves.criterion: Adding a competing offer never lowers the multiplier.

leaves.title: Agents as people
leaves.criterion: The fee posts to E6 as an expense each time a salary payment posts, at the agreed percent.

leaves.title: What the agent does
leaves.criterion: With an agent whose network includes the decision maker, interview requests from that club occur more often than without, by the configured term.

leaves.title: Shared representation and package deals
leaves.criterion: In a generated world some clubs show three or more football decision makers with one agency.

leaves.title: Extensions
leaves.criterion: A coach with owner confidence above the threshold never enters the final contract year without an offer.

leaves.title: The final year
leaves.criterion: The flag clears the moment an extension is signed.

leaves.title: How college deals differ
leaves.criterion: College and professional defaults are separate config blocks and a contract reads the block for its level.

leaves.title: Season expectation
leaves.criterion: 1. Two teams with the same roster estimate and schedule but different owners get expectations that differ by the owners' optimism only. 2. League-wide, the mean of `expectation.wins` exceeds the mean of true projected wins by the mean optimism value, and the sum of expectations exceeds the number of games available. This is intended: owners as a group expect more wins than exist. 3. The band word shown matches the cut-point table.

leaves.title: Stated and unstated goals
leaves.criterion: Every season record holds the full goal list with tests that can be evaluated from saved data alone. An unstated goal never appears in any user-facing text before its discovery flag is set.

leaves.title: The preseason meeting
leaves.criterion: The expectation after the meeting differs from the value before it by no more than the configured cap. A promise record exists whenever the stance was "promise more".

leaves.title: The confidence value and its weekly update
leaves.criterion: 1. Replaying a saved season from its logged terms reproduces the weekly confidence values exactly. 2. The displayed word never reflects the current week's game. 3. No term reads any stored ability value of the coach, because none exists (E1.4.1). A static check of the term inputs confirms it.

leaves.title: Inputs and their weights
leaves.criterion: 1. Each term can be switched off in config, and a test season with only that term on moves confidence in the stated direction. 2. Across 500 simulated seasons, the correlation between season-end confidence change and (win share minus expected win share) is at least 0.7. 3. Two coaches with identical results and events but different E6 and E8 states have identical confidence.

leaves.title: What the user can learn about his standing
leaves.criterion: Over 1,000 test queries to an owner with candour 0.6, about 60% of answers match the true word.

leaves.title: Review points and the firing hazard
leaves.criterion: 1. Over 200 simulated professional seasons under default config, the mean number of head coach firings per season is between 5 and 9, and no more than 5% of seasons fall outside 3 to 11. 2. Coaches under a non-hiring general manager are fired at a rate about 1.4 times that of coaches under their hiring general manager, within sampling error. 3. Reloading a save before a review reproduces the same outcome. 4. The college record of `owner_model` yields firings within 6% to 12% of programs per season.

leaves.title: Dead money as a brake
leaves.tag: v1, both; defaults by level via contract_defaults.<level>
leaves.criterion: 1. With all else equal, raising `owner.dead_money_owed` lowers `p_fire` monotonically. 2. A firing adds exactly the contract's remaining guaranteed amounts to `owner.dead_money_owed`. 3. In a 200-season test, clubs in the top quarter for dead money owed fire their coaches at a lower rate than clubs in the bottom quarter at equal confidence.

leaves.title: In-season firings
leaves.criterion: In a 200-season test, in-season firings are between 15% and 40% of all firings. The band is now sourced for the NFL: 16 of 44 head coach firings were in season over 2020 to 2025, 36 percent, season shares 25 to 60 percent (facts/coach-firing-timing.json, PR 112, status 2 of 3, derived by listing coaches, 2025 partial). G-77 measured about 8% with a flat no-fire rule for teams alive for the postseason, so that rule gave way (edge case above); re-measure after the change. No college share is claimed (no readable same-year source).

leaves.title: A new owner or general manager
leaves.criterion: After a general manager change, the firing rate of inherited coaches in simulation exceeds that of non-inherited coaches at equal confidence.

leaves.title: After a firing: no built-in bounce
leaves.criterion: 1. A code search finds no modifier keyed to "games since coach change" or similar in J, K, or L. 2. In a controlled test, a team whose coach is replaced by an identical copy of the same coach record (same system, same staff, same relationships copied) produces the same distribution of results as the control. 3. In the 200-season test, teams that fired a coach improve the next season by no more than teams with a matching prior record that kept their coach, within sampling error.

leaves.title: Signals the coach can read
leaves.criterion: In simulation, coaches who are fired at the main review had at least two signs in the preceding 10 weeks in at least 80% of cases. Coaches with confidence above 70 see a sign in fewer than 5% of seasons.

leaves.title: Situation types and grace
leaves.criterion: In simulation, first-year coaches in a rebuild are fired less than a third as often as first-year coaches in a win-now situation at equal confidence.

leaves.title: Owner meetings, conditions, and commitments
leaves.criterion: Every condition has a test evaluable from saved data and a deadline. Passing all tests lowers the next review's firing probability by the configured factor.

leaves.title: Staff sacrifices and what they cost
leaves.criterion: A second staff sacrifice in one season yields zero confidence. Loyalty changes are written for every remaining assistant.

leaves.title: Job security below head coach
leaves.criterion: An assistant user receives head-coach hot seat signs at a rate that rises with rung.

leaves.title: The college version
leaves.criterion: 1. With the college record loaded, no professional-only term (playoff seeding, general manager factor) is evaluated. 2. Simulated firings per season fall within 6% to 12% of top-division programs, and total changes including departures within 18% to 28%. 3. Raising booster wealth for a program raises its firing rate at equal confidence.

leaves.title: When the owner offers more years
leaves.criterion: No extension offer is generated at confidence below 65. A title season always generates one.

leaves.title: The reputation record
leaves.criterion: 1. A new coach with no playing or coaching past shows "unknown" in all five rows. 2. Deleting the record and replaying the event log reproduces it exactly. 3. A dependency test finds no read of `regard` or `known` in areas J or D.

leaves.title: Reputation events
leaves.criterion: Every row of the reputation log points to a source event id that exists in the save. Events with reach 0 change nothing.

leaves.title: Reputation with players
leaves.criterion: With results held equal, a coach who breaks ten promises in a season starts his next roster at lower trust than one who keeps ten. The lame-duck and removed-authority events each apply once.

leaves.title: Reputation with coaches
leaves.criterion: Blocking an interview and supporting one move the score in opposite directions. A candidate's willingness to join (L4) rises with the score in a controlled test.

leaves.title: Reputation with owners and executives
leaves.criterion: Backing out of an agreed offer lowers interest from other hiring parties in the next cycle in a controlled test.

leaves.title: Reputation with media
leaves.criterion: Two identical fourth-down decisions, one converted and one not, produce opposite media events and identical decision-log grades.

leaves.title: Reputation with fans
leaves.criterion: Fan values are stored per fan base and a coach's value with one base does not change from events seen only by another.

leaves.title: The book on the coach
leaves.criterion: 1. Every label shown opens to at least the minimum sample of evidence records. 2. A coach created one minute ago shows "No book on you yet." 3. No input on the page changes any label.

leaves.title: Lag, error, and correction
leaves.criterion: For a coach whose behaviour changed two seasons ago, the public copy still shows the old label when the full-record copy has dropped it. A reference call from a qualified contact changes that hiring party's copy and no one else's.

leaves.title: The tree object
leaves.criterion: 1. Rebuilding all trees from employment records reproduces the stored edges. 2. A pupil appears on a mentor's counted list only after a full season at the higher rung. 3. No tree edge for an imported person is created from generated history dated before the save began.

leaves.title: What the tree does
leaves.criterion: In a long world simulation, coaches with larger trees receive more post-firing offers from former assistants than coaches with none, with reputation held equal.

leaves.title: The career record
leaves.criterion: Head coach totals equal the sum of game results on the dates he held the job. College and professional lines never mix.

leaves.title: The career summary
leaves.criterion: Every figure on the summary matches its source record. The summary of an imported person contains no family, health, or money text.

leaves.title: Awards
leaves.criterion: Across 200 simulated seasons the award goes to the coach of the team with the best record less than half the time. Starting target, to be replaced by the measured real share.

leaves.title: Records
leaves.criterion: The tables rebuild exactly from career records.

leaves.title: The Hall of Fame case
leaves.tag: v1, pro; college hall via config
leaves.criterion: A coach with zero titles and a losing record is never elected in 1,000 trials. Election occurs only with at least 80 percent yes votes. No imported person carries a conduct penalty.

leaves.title: Reputation below head coach and across levels
leaves.criterion: A rung 2 coach's events never change the media or fans rows. Moving levels applies the transfer weights once.

leaves.title: The balance sheet and the monthly cycle
leaves.criterion: 1. For any month, opening balances plus ledger entries equal closing balances to the cent. 2. A 40-season autopilot career never produces a negative cash balance at month end without a logged shortfall event. 3. The Money screen opens from any hub screen and shows the last closed month.

leaves.title: Opening money by start mode
leaves.criterion: Every start mode yields a sheet that balances and whose first three months of autopilot cash flow do not default.

leaves.title: Income sources and pay timing
leaves.criterion: The 12-month forecast equals the sum of scheduled contract payments, known outside deals, and partner income, and changes on the day a contract changes.

leaves.title: Federal tax engine
leaves.criterion: 1. For a set of 20 test incomes, computed tax matches hand calculation from the loaded table to the dollar. 2. Replacing the table file changes results with no code change. 3. Every salary figure on an offer card shows a take-home estimate.

leaves.title: State and local tax by location
leaves.criterion: 1. The same salary produces a higher take-home at a location with a no-wage-tax profile than at one with a high-rate profile, by the amount the table implies. 2. Every location in a generated world has a `tax_profile_id` that resolves. 3. A row marked placeholder triggers a warning in a release build check.

leaves.title: Road-game income allocation
leaves.tag: v1 as a setting, default off, pro
leaves.criterion: With the flag off, no entry of this type exists in any ledger. With it on, a coach resident in a no-wage-tax profile pays a positive amount to other states.

leaves.title: Lifestyle tiers
leaves.criterion: Monthly cost equals the formula for every tier and location in a test grid. A tier change downward takes effect on the configured delay.

leaves.title: Household costs and obligations
leaves.criterion: Every obligation has an end date or an explicit "ongoing" flag, and its entries stop on that date.

leaves.title: Rent or buy
leaves.criterion: The up-front cash shown equals what leaves the cash account on purchase. A coach whose payment would exceed the qualification share cannot buy at that tier.

leaves.title: Selling after a firing and carrying two homes
leaves.criterion: Proceeds equal price times the market factor, minus selling costs, minus the mortgage balance, in every test case.

leaves.title: The catalogue of outside income
leaves.criterion: Every active deal has a matching time entry in E7 for each week it runs. Total outside income in a season equals the sum of scheduled deal payments less commission.

leaves.title: Approval, conflicts, and the cost in attention
leaves.criterion: With outside hours at zero the story never fires.

leaves.title: Asset classes and yearly returns
leaves.criterion: 1. Over 1,000 simulated years, each class's mean and standard deviation match config within sampling error. 2. Over the same run, the index fund's result is not improved by any user action other than the amount held. 3. Changing the market seed changes no football outcome in a paired test.

leaves.title: Risk level, allocation, and rebalancing
leaves.criterion: After yearly rebalancing, class weights equal the target within 1 percentage point.

leaves.title: Private deals and owning a business
leaves.criterion: Every private holding resolves to an exit, a write-off, or a continuing stake with a current reported value. Hidden fields never appear in user-facing text before resolution.

leaves.title: Debt and default
leaves.criterion: A default event fires on the third consecutive missed payment and never earlier. Two otherwise identical coaches, one bankrupt, receive identical interview scores and owner confidence in a paired test.

leaves.title: Money screen help level (replaces the financial literacy value)
leaves.criterion: The same deal produces the same outcome distribution at all three help levels. No football module imports the setting. The save contains no literacy field for the user.

leaves.title: Advisers: fee, honesty, skill
leaves.criterion: The registration check reveals a dishonest adviser's discipline flag whenever one exists. With an honest fee-only adviser, yearly cost equals fee times average assets.

leaves.title: Pitch events
leaves.criterion: Over a 30-season head coach career, the count of pitches falls inside the configured band. Zero pitches are delivered in game weeks under the default setting.

leaves.title: Bad deals and scams: how they resolve
leaves.criterion: 1. No ledger entry of type investment exists for the user without a matching user confirmation. 2. Every fraud resolves to a collapse date and a recovery schedule.

leaves.title: Due diligence and warning signs
leaves.criterion: For a test set of 200 generated deals, running the accountant's and lawyer's reviews separates fraud and doomed from sound with at least 85% accuracy. Running no checks gives the user no information beyond the document.

leaves.title: Retirement plans and the pension
leaves.tag: v1, both; plan rules via benefits.<level>
leaves.criterion: A coach who leaves an employer before `vesting_years` has zero pension credit from it. Contributions never exceed the table's limit.

leaves.title: The target number and security status
leaves.criterion: Status changes within one month of a change in net worth or tier that crosses a threshold. The status is never read by E2.4, E4, or any J, K3 to K6 module.

leaves.title: Insurance, a will, and protecting the household
leaves.criterion: No cover is bought without a user action or a contract term. A fired coach's employer cover ends on his last day. No football module imports any field of this leaf. No imported real person is ever sued or paid out on a harmful event.

leaves.title: Giving and a foundation
leaves.criterion: Total deductions never exceed the table's limit. The yearly reputation gain from giving never exceeds the cap.

leaves.title: What money looks like at each rung
leaves.criterion: At rung 1 with the default opening sheet and the bare tier, a 12-month autopilot run shows at least one month where cash falls below one month of costs. At rung 9 it never does.

leaves.title: Money never changes football
leaves.criterion: 1. A static dependency check fails the build if a forbidden module imports an E6 type. 2. A paired simulation of 100 seasons with every coach's net worth multiplied by 100 produces identical game results, hires, and firings, given the same seeds, when AI retirement decisions are held fixed.

leaves.title: The net worth line
leaves.criterion: The sum of categories in the summary equals the ledger total for the career. No money field appears in a real person's profile.

leaves.title: The week as 168 hours
leaves.criterion: 1. For every simulated week the six categories (work, sleep, home, travel, fixed needs, free) sum to exactly 168 hours. 2. Scheduling a 2-hour block into a full day forces a visible choice of what loses 2 hours. 3. Two saves with different coach histories and the same weekly choices produce identical `coach_week` records.

leaves.title: The hour ledger and the dry run
leaves.criterion: 1. With no unplanned events injected, the dry run's hours and sleep debt equal the committed week's to the quarter hour. 2. Running the dry run 100 times changes no saved value. 3. Ledger totals per week equal `coach_week` totals.

leaves.title: The task cost table
leaves.criterion: 1. Every timed action in the game resolves to a row of this table (a test walks all action ids). 2. The costs cited in E4 and E6 equal the rows here. 3. Completing a film task in 10 seconds or 10 minutes of real time charges the same in-game hours.

leaves.title: What changes a cost
leaves.criterion: A search of the cost function finds no input that belongs to the user's coach record other than his location and schedule.

leaves.title: Handing work off
leaves.criterion: 1. Delegating a task reduces the coach's hours by its table cost and adds the same to the delegate's load. 2. With staff parameters held fixed, the delegated product is identical whatever the coach's history. 3. No screen shows a delegate's hidden parameter as a number.

leaves.title: Checking delegated work
leaves.criterion: A product seeded with a known error is shown with the error unmarked. Returning it adds hours to the delegate and none to the coach beyond the review.

leaves.title: Sleep debt
leaves.criterion: 1. Seven nights at 7.5 hours leaves the debt unchanged. 2. Seven nights at 5 hours adds 17.5 hours. 3. No function outside E7.4.2, E8.1.1, and the display reads `sleep_debt_hours` (dependency test).

leaves.title: What overwork costs, and what it never costs
leaves.criterion: 1. Two games with the same seed and the same user inputs at the same times, one rested and one exhausted, produce identical play results. 2. In the exhausted game, booth items are stamped 6 seconds later and halftime allows two fewer items. 3. A dependency test shows `sleep_debt_hours` is read by no module in areas J, D, or L.

leaves.title: One thing at a time
leaves.criterion: While a sideline conversation is open no second conversation can be opened. Items not taken are logged with who handled them.

leaves.title: Offseason weeks
leaves.criterion: Every offseason week has a `coach_week` summing to 168.

leaves.title: The break
leaves.tag: v1, pro; college via T calendar
leaves.criterion: A break spent fully away repays up to 14 hours of sleep debt per week and logs the home hours.

leaves.title: The same clock for everyone
leaves.criterion: Two certified records from the same config version have identical cost tables.

leaves.title: The budget below head coach and in college
leaves.criterion: At rung 2 the user cannot remove a required block. He can skip it, and the skip is logged with the boss.

leaves.title: AI coaches' time
leaves.criterion: For every AI head coach, weekly hours by category sum to 168 at both fidelity tiers. A test finds no path by which an AI coach does more self-performed tasks than his hours allow.

leaves.title: Sustained load
leaves.criterion: `load_12w` and `heavy_weeks_52` recompute exactly from ledger rows. No module in areas J, D, I, or N3 reads either.

leaves.title: The yearly check-up
leaves.criterion: In 10,000 simulated coach-years no state reaches serious without a prior delivered warning. A coach with `heavy_weeks_52` of zero for his whole career never leaves well before age 55.

leaves.title: The physician's warning
leaves.criterion: Every at-risk state has a delivered warning dated before any event. Meeting both targets for 12 weeks always moves the state to watch.

leaves.title: Health events
leaves.criterion: 1. In 10,000 coach-careers with every warning followed, zero health events occur. 2. No health event exists in any save for an imported person. 3. Two seasons with the same seed and inputs, one containing a health event during a bye week, have identical play results in games the user coached with identical inputs.

leaves.title: The household object
leaves.criterion: A career with an empty household runs with no household prompts. Children's ages advance one year per calendar year.

leaves.title: Time at home and household satisfaction
leaves.criterion: Holding home hours at target keeps satisfaction steady. A separation without two prior conversation events is rare, not impossible: it occurs at the floor `prob.floor` per week after a single shock event (a sudden discovery), so life can surprise him. The dependency test in rule 7 passes.

leaves.title: Life events
leaves.criterion: Every event in a save traces to a household member and a table row. No event is created for an empty household.

leaves.title: Moving for a job
leaves.criterion: Each mode produces its stated effects and no others. A coach living 1,500 miles apart in season cannot log more home hours than travel allows.

leaves.title: The permitted effects, and the test
leaves.criterion: 1. A dependency test finds reads of E8 state only in the permitted modules. 2. Replaying a season with all E8 state deleted, and with the same user inputs and calendar, gives identical play results and identical decision grades. 3. No E8 record exists for any imported person.

leaves.title: Conduct off the field and its consequences
leaves.criterion: 1. No conduct event ever occurs for the user without an accept action in the log. 2. Over 1,000 simulated careers, AI and user detection rates for the same act class match within tolerance (Q4). 3. No imported person appears in any conduct event. 4. Dismissal for cause removes the remaining guarantee in E3's ledger.

leaves.title: What is measured
leaves.criterion: Every label definition in N2.8 whose subject is a coach names one of the six families as its source. A definition that names anything else fails validation.

leaves.title: The record object
leaves.criterion: 1. The schema for the user's coach has no field named skill, rating, level, competency, experience, or points, and the validator rejects one if added. 2. Deleting every computed summary and reopening the tab reproduces the same numbers from the logs. 3. Two users with identical logs have identical record tabs.

leaves.title: What a formula uses when the coach is the user
leaves.criterion: 1. A static check finds no formula in any area that reads a stored attribute of the user's coach as a multiplier. 2. In a test, the same task performed with the same inputs in a first-year career and a twentieth-year career gives the same result. 3. Each calling leaf states case 1, 2, or 3.

leaves.title: Descriptors and their evidence
leaves.criterion: Every descriptor shows a sample at or above its minimum. No input on the screen changes a descriptor.

leaves.title: How the coach sees his own record
leaves.criterion: The three views can differ and each traces to its observer's evidence. Nothing in the game changes when a self-assessment is written.

leaves.title: Working under a mentor
leaves.criterion: After two seasons on a staff and a move, the user's personal playbook holds exactly the pages his old job had rights to. No value on his coach record changed other than facts and references.

leaves.title: Clinics and conventions
leaves.criterion: Each talk document's plays exist in the speaker's playbook in the save. Attending adds documents, edges, and facts only. Giving a talk makes the chosen pages readable to every attendee.

leaves.title: Visiting another staff
leaves.criterion: A visit adds exactly the pages for the chosen subjects. A refused request leaves the relationship unchanged except for a small note.

leaves.title: Studying film of other systems
leaves.criterion: Studying film changes no field on the coach record except the history fact and the user's own saved material.

leaves.title: The coaching school
leaves.criterion: Completing every school unit changes no value read by any career system.

leaves.title: Offseason study projects
leaves.criterion: 1. A study with every counted claim correct and one with half wrong produce different family 4 events and no difference on the coach record beyond those events. 2. A study adopted by the staff changes only the team's documents named in it.

leaves.title: Teaching evidence
leaves.criterion: The view lists every qualifying player season and no others. Its numbers recompute from D7 and N1 records.

leaves.title: Systems worked in and levels coached
leaves.criterion: The list equals the facts. No formula outside hiring preferences reads it.

leaves.title: Game management evidence
leaves.criterion: The view's counts equal N3's.

leaves.title: Communication evidence
leaves.criterion: Every line opens to its events.

leaves.title: Evaluation evidence
leaves.criterion: Each recommendation is scored exactly once and appears in the view.

leaves.title: What each rung lets a coach demonstrate
leaves.criterion: For a test coach at each rung, only the listed families gain events during a season.

leaves.title: AI coaches: hidden parameters and visible records
leaves.criterion: A search of all user-facing views finds no binding to a K2 field.

leaves.title: Screens
leaves.criterion: The page contains no element bound to a skill value.

leaves.title: Retired, and cleanup owed elsewhere
leaves.criterion: A search of the bible for "competenc", "skill tree", "experience points", and "fluency value" returns only this leaf, the ruling notes, and K2.

leaves.title: The two-digit naming grammar
leaves.criterion: 1. Every legal mix of backs, tight ends, and receivers summing to five yields a unique code. 2. A package with six linemen always shows the plus suffix and requires a reporting player (F1.1.3).

leaves.title: Catalog of offensive groupings
leaves.criterion: 1. Every play in the shipped playbooks references a code present in the catalog. 2. A fast-simulated league season (J14) reproduces the usage shares above within 5 percentage points for 11 and 12 when AI coaches use default profiles.

leaves.title: Extra linemen and reporting eligible
leaves.criterion: 1. A package with an ineligible number in an eligible slot sets the reports flag by default. The user may clear it and save; the package then carries a warning, and the snap is an illegal-substitution or illegal-formation foul when the officials see it (B2.3.3 rule 5, B11.3.1). Nothing is blocked (ruling of 2026-11-25 22:23). 2. A formation that leaves the reporter covered is flagged as "ineligible by alignment" in validation.

leaves.title: Defensive naming grammar
leaves.criterion: Every legal split of 11 across the three levels produces a name by the rules above.

leaves.title: Catalog of defensive groupings
leaves.criterion: No strength or weakness in this table is coded as a direct modifier. A test confirms outcome differences between groups come only from player attributes and alignment.

leaves.title: The package object
leaves.criterion: 1. Resolving any shipped package against any legal game-day roster for the league's level (size from C5 or T5) yields 11 distinct players or a clear error naming the empty role. 2. Removing a starter mid-game changes only the slots he filled.

leaves.title: Situational sub-packages
leaves.criterion: A new save has every package above resolvable from the default depth chart.

leaves.title: Rotation groups within a package
leaves.criterion: Over a simulated game, a 65/35 rotation yields snap shares within 5 points of target when no injury occurs.

leaves.title: Defensive matching rules
leaves.criterion: 1. For every offensive code and bucket the table returns exactly one package. 2. A player-specific override takes precedence over the code row.

leaves.title: Substitution windows and their cost
leaves.criterion: 1. Before the two-minute warning, an offense that substitutes can never snap before the defense's match window ends. After the warning no hold is applied. 2. A no-huddle offense that does not substitute can snap while the defense is changing players, and a 12-man foul results when a defender is still on the field.

leaves.title: Tendency by grouping
leaves.criterion: After a simulated season, a team that calls 90% runs from one grouping faces a higher loaded-box rate from AI defenses in that grouping than a balanced team does, with the same rosters and seeds.

leaves.title: Personnel differences by level
leaves.criterion: Switching a test league's `rule_set_id` from pro to college changes every value in the table with no code change. A search of the F1 implementation finds no literal pro value for the items above.

leaves.title: Coverage data shape
leaves.criterion: Every shipped coverage resolves against every shipped formation with eleven jobs and one force player per side.

leaves.title: Leverage and technique
leaves.criterion: Same corner, same receiver: press raises both the incompletion rate on quick throws and the rate of completions of 20 yd or more, compared with off.

leaves.title: Zone drops, eyes, and breaks
leaves.criterion: Slower hook defenders give larger completion windows on dig routes in a same-seed test.

leaves.title: Run support by coverage
leaves.criterion: For each coverage the fit view names one force player per side for every shipped formation.

leaves.title: Cover 0
leaves.criterion: See F9.6.1.

leaves.title: Cover 1 and its low helpers
leaves.criterion: Removing the rat raises completions on shallow crossers, same seed.

leaves.title: 2-Man
leaves.criterion: Scramble yards against 2-Man exceed scramble yards against Cover 3 for the same quarterback over 3,000 dropbacks each.

leaves.title: Cover 2
leaves.criterion: A corner who fails the reroute on number 1 increases completions in the sideline hole.

leaves.title: Tampa 2
leaves.criterion: Completion rate on deep middle throws against Tampa 2 falls as the middle linebacker's speed rises.

leaves.title: Cover 3: sky, cloud, and buzz
leaves.criterion: Seam completions fall when the curl-flat players are given a "carry number 2" rule and flat completions rise, same seed.

leaves.title: Cover 3 match
leaves.criterion: Four verticals completes less often against Cover 3 match than against spot-drop Cover 3, and switch-release concepts complete more often.

leaves.title: Quarters and its checks
leaves.criterion: With number 2 running a short out, the safety's robber action lowers completions on the dig by number 1.

leaves.title: Match rules and the read penalty
leaves.criterion: Busted coverages per 1,000 snaps are higher for a match coverage with zero practice reps than for the same coverage after a full week of install. Spot-drop coverages show a smaller gap.

leaves.title: Palms, or two-read
leaves.criterion: Interceptions on quick outs by number 2 rise with the check on; completions on wheel routes by number 2 rise too.

leaves.title: Cover 6 and mixed halves
leaves.criterion: A coverage built from two halves validates only when no deep area is unowned.

leaves.title: Brackets and doubles
leaves.criterion: Targets to a bracketed receiver fall and targets to the single-covered receiver on the other side rise, same seed.

leaves.title: Red-zone and goal-line coverage
leaves.criterion: No defender in any test is assigned a landmark beyond the end line.

leaves.title: Pre-snap shell and rotation
leaves.criterion: A two-high show rotating to Cover 3 on the snap produces more wrong pre-snap reads by the quarterback and more open deep-middle windows than the same coverage shown honestly. Both effects appear in a 3,000-dropback same-seed test.

leaves.title: Open and closed: what the offense can learn
leaves.criterion: The offense's panel never shows a defender's real job, only positions and the perceived label.

leaves.title: Coverage shares and results for calibration
leaves.criterion: A ten-season simulated league shows man completion rate at least 8 percentage points below zone and man sack rate above zone (starting bounds).

leaves.title: Coverage rules and usage by level
leaves.criterion: Switching `catch.feet_required` from two to one raises sideline completion rate in a same-seed test with no other change.

leaves.title: Run strength and passing strength
leaves.criterion: For every shipped formation, on either hash, both strengths resolve to exactly one side.

leaves.title: The check object
leaves.criterion: A check whose chain time exceeds the time left before the snap does not apply, and the film tag records "check late".

leaves.title: Lock, bump, and rotate
leaves.criterion: With lock, the offense's man or zone perception after motion is correct more often than with bump, same seed.

leaves.title: Resetting the front after shifts and motion
leaves.criterion: After any shift, the fit view shows every gap owned under each of the three rules, or flags the open gap.

leaves.title: Banjo, lock, and box against bunch and stack
leaves.criterion: Against a rub concept, banjo lowers completions compared with lock at equal depths; against a double out-breaking concept, banjo gives up more than lock.

leaves.title: Trips checks
leaves.criterion: With the push check, targets to the back-side single receiver rise; with stay two-high, targets to number 3 rise.

leaves.title: Empty
leaves.criterion: Against empty with no spy and a mobile quarterback, quarterback run yards rise compared with the spy check on, same seed.

leaves.title: Unbalanced lines and extra linemen
leaves.criterion: Defenses that practiced against the opponent's unbalanced look in the week recognise it more often than those that did not.

leaves.title: The tempo menu
leaves.criterion: At fast tempo the share of snaps played with the tempo call rises and the share with disguise falls to zero in a logged test.

leaves.title: Defending the run-pass option
leaves.criterion: Each answer, same seed, shifts the offense's RPO outcomes: man coverage raises handoff share; slow play raises ineligible-downfield flags when the limit is 1 yd more than when it is 3 yd.

leaves.title: Communication errors and busts
leaves.criterion: Over a simulated season, a defense with twice the installed checks and the same practice time has more tagged busts than its twin. Replacing the caller with a rookie raises "check late" tags.

leaves.title: Checks by level
leaves.criterion: Switching `foul.ineligible_downfield.yards` changes flag rates on slow-played RPOs with no code change.

leaves.title: The units and the special teams depth chart
leaves.criterion: No game starts with an unfilled slot on any unit. Removing a player from the actives updates every unit he was on.

leaves.title: What the specialists do
leaves.criterion: A long snapper with slower snap time raises block rate on punts and place kicks in a same-seed test.

leaves.title: Dynamic kickoff geometry
leaves.criterion: Every row is a config value. Changing the touchback spot from 35 to 30 changes the starting field position in a test with no code change.

leaves.title: Kickoff types and coverage
leaves.criterion: Over a simulated season, average starting field position after landing-zone kicks sits between the two touchback spots for an average kicker and coverage unit (starting check), and moves with coverage quality.

leaves.title: Kickoff return schemes
leaves.criterion: A return alignment with players outside the legal areas saves with a warning and, in play, draws the alignment foul at the B11.3.1 detection rate.

leaves.title: Onside kick and recovery
leaves.criterion: The kicking team cannot legally recover a ball untouched by the receivers before 10 yd; the engine rules it illegal touching.

leaves.title: Punt formation and protection
leaves.criterion: A formation that releases an interior lineman before the kick saves with a warning; in play the engine produces the ineligible-downfield foul, flagged at the B11.3.1 detection rate.

leaves.title: Punt types and coverage
leaves.criterion: For the same punter, lowering hang time at equal distance raises average return yards in a same-seed test.

leaves.title: Return, rush, or safe
leaves.criterion: An eight-man block call against a protector who miscounts produces a free rusher; whether he gets the ball is decided by his arrival time against the operation time.

leaves.title: Fielding the punt
leaves.criterion: A returner with poor catching in strong wind muffs more often than in calm air, same seed otherwise.

leaves.title: The place-kick operation and protection
leaves.criterion: A simulated league's make rates by distance band fall within 3 percentage points of the F12.9.1 rows up to 59 yd (starting tolerance).

leaves.title: Field goal block and safe
leaves.criterion: Low-trajectory kicks are blocked in the middle more often than high ones, same seed.

leaves.title: Fake punts and fake field goals
leaves.criterion: The same fake succeeds more often against a block call than against safe across 1,000 trials each.

leaves.title: Free kicks other than the kickoff
leaves.criterion: With 0:00 on the clock after a fair catch, the engine offers the kick and blocks the option to snap.

leaves.title: Kicking-game targets for calibration
leaves.criterion: Every row in `calibration.pro.kicking` carries a source and status; a row with no source fails the config check.

leaves.title: The kicking game by level
leaves.criterion: Setting `kickoff.format` to traditional removes the setup and landing zones, lets the kicking team run before the kick, and allows an undeclared onside kick, with no code change.

leaves.title: Situations as named filters
leaves.criterion: Changing the red-zone boundary from the 20 to the 25 changes which sheet section appears at the 23, and regroups the self-scout report.

leaves.title: The depth clamp and the shrinking field
leaves.criterion: No route or landmark in any snap finishes beyond the end line. The preview matches what the engine runs.

leaves.title: Red-zone concepts on offense
leaves.criterion: Each tagged concept runs from its listed area with no route clamped by more than 3 yd (starting check), or it is flagged for the user to redraw.

leaves.title: Short-yardage and goal-line offense
leaves.criterion: Over 5,000 fourth-and-1 plays between average units, conversion rate lands within 5 percentage points of 69.4% (starting tolerance).

leaves.title: Goal-line and five-one fronts
leaves.criterion: Against a sneak, the goal-line front lowers average gain compared with a base front; against a play-action flat throw, it gives up a higher completion rate. Same seed.

leaves.title: Two-point plays
leaves.criterion: A ten-season simulated league's two-point success rate falls between 43% and 53% (starting bounds around 47.8%).

leaves.title: Third down by distance
leaves.criterion: In a simulated league, third-down conversion rate falls as distance rises across all four bands.

leaves.title: Fourth-down plays
leaves.criterion: The league-wide attempt rate by distance in a ten-season run falls within 5 percentage points of each A7 figure (starting tolerance).

leaves.title: Offense and defense inside the 5
leaves.criterion: Safeties occur in simulated play only from the listed causes, and punt block rate is higher from inside the 5 than from the 30.

leaves.title: Two-minute offense
leaves.criterion: With no timeouts, a completion in bounds in the middle of the field costs more game-clock time before the next snap than one caught at the sideline and taken out of bounds.

leaves.title: Two-minute and prevent defense
leaves.criterion: Against prevent, completion rate rises, yards per completion fall, and plays of 25 yd or more fall, compared with the base defense, same seed.

leaves.title: Closing the game with the lead
leaves.criterion: A runner with the stay-in-bounds instruction goes out of bounds less often than without it, same seed.

leaves.title: Hail Mary, laterals, and their defense
leaves.criterion: Hail Mary completion rate falls as throw distance rises and falls to a tiny but nonzero floor beyond the quarterback's usual maximum distance (a freak throw and a gust are possible), and no completion is credited when the ball cannot physically reach the field.

leaves.title: Weather plans
leaves.criterion: In strong wind, simulated field goal range differs by direction of kick and the I4.2.1 panel shows it.

leaves.title: Situations by level
leaves.criterion: Switching `clock.first_down_stop` to the college value changes the seconds remaining after an in-bounds first down inside two minutes, with no code change.

leaves.title: System data shape
leaves.criterion: Renaming a system or changing its family label changes no play result in a same-seed test.

leaves.title: Fit between system and players
leaves.criterion: The demands view never shows a single combined fit rating. Every line links to the snaps behind it.

leaves.title: Pro passing families and their languages
leaves.criterion: The same play called through each of the three shipped terminology maps resolves to identical assignments.

leaves.title: Run-first and play-action systems
leaves.criterion: A system whose play-action passes share first steps with its base run draws more linebacker bites than one whose fakes do not match, same players and seed.

leaves.title: Spread, tempo, and air raid
leaves.criterion: A system with half as many pass concepts reaches the same average scheme knowledge in fewer practice weeks.

leaves.title: Option families
leaves.criterion: A defense with zero practice reps against option fits makes more assignment errors against it than one with a week of reps, same seed.

leaves.title: Common defensive families
leaves.criterion: Each shipped defensive system validates: every front has a fit against every shipped run, and every coverage resolves against every shipped formation.

leaves.title: College three-safety and three-down structures
leaves.criterion: Against inside zone from 12 personnel, the three-down structure gives up more yards per carry than a four-down front with the same players' attributes held equal by position, same seed.

leaves.title: The terminology map
leaves.criterion: Replacing every word in a map changes no assignment. Lengthening every call by 50% raises average time used on the play clock.

leaves.title: Who declares what at the line
leaves.criterion: Switching the Mike declarer from a rookie centre to a veteran quarterback lowers wrong-point declarations in a same-seed test.

leaves.title: Install order
leaves.criterion: Installing a play-action pass before its run partner yields lower knowledge after equal reps than the reverse order.

leaves.title: Changing systems and what carries over
leaves.criterion: After a full system change, a team's tagged assignment errors in its first four games exceed those of a twin team that kept its system, same rosters and seed.

leaves.title: Systems by level
leaves.criterion: Generated college coordinators and pro coordinators show different family distributions drawn from `generation_weights[level]`, and changing the weights changes the distributions with no code change.

leaves.title: Formation data shape and alignment grammar
leaves.criterion: 1. Mirroring a formation twice returns the original. 2. Derived labels are recomputed on every edit and match hand-checked values for the shipped library.

leaves.title: Legality validation
leaves.criterion: Each of the five failure reasons can be produced in the designer and is shown. A formation with any failure can still be saved and called, and is flagged at the B11.3.1 detection rate. A fast-simulated season produces illegal formation fouls within 30% of the league rate.

leaves.title: Quarterback sets: under center, shotgun, pistol
leaves.criterion: With the same play and players, time from snap to first available throw is shorter from shotgun than from under center, and the play-fake effect on linebackers (J3) is larger from under center.

leaves.title: Back alignments
leaves.criterion: Each label is produced by the derivation for its spots and for the mirrored version.

leaves.title: Distribution families
leaves.criterion: Labels match hand-checked values for all shipped formations before and after their tagged motions.

leaves.title: Named formation library
leaves.criterion: Every library formation passes F2.1.2 for a default roster.

leaves.title: Attached, wing, flexed, and backfield tight end alignments
leaves.criterion: Surface labels are correct for all shipped formations.

leaves.title: Receiver split rules by landmark
leaves.criterion: For each split rule and each of three ball positions, the resolved spot is inbounds, at least 1 yd from any teammate, and matches a hand-computed value.

leaves.title: Line splits and stances
leaves.criterion: Wide splits increase the distance an edge rusher must travel to the quarterback's launch point, measurable in the engine's geometry.

leaves.title: Offensive strength call
leaves.criterion: A formation called right at the left hash and left at the right hash both resolve legally inbounds.

leaves.title: Defensive strength recognition
leaves.criterion: For every shipped formation the declared strengths match a hand-checked table.

leaves.title: Bunch
leaves.criterion: The cluster tag appears for all shipped bunch sets and disappears if any member is moved 4 yd away.

leaves.title: Stack
leaves.criterion: A press technique assigned to the back receiver of a stack is rejected by defensive validation or converted to off.

leaves.title: Unbalanced line and tackle over
leaves.criterion: Validation accepts tackle-over sets with a legal end man and shows the illegal-formation banner on those without (savable, flagged by officials per F2.1.2).

leaves.title: Empty
leaves.criterion: Any formation with the empty flag refuses six- or seven-man protections in validation.

leaves.title: Formation tendency and tells
leaves.criterion: A team that runs to the back's side 90% of the time from shotgun sees AI linebackers shade that way more often than against a balanced team, same seeds.

leaves.title: Hash width and its effect on formations
leaves.criterion: The same formation resolved at the left hash under each rule set gives a field-side width that differs by the difference in hash inset. No literal hash distance appears in F2 code.

leaves.title: Other formation rules that differ
leaves.criterion: Validation outcomes change with the rule set for a test formation built at each limit.

leaves.title: The shift object and its legality
leaves.criterion: 1. No shipped play can be snapped less than 1 s after a shift ends except through the modelled error hazard. 2. A tight end trade flips the defense's declared run strength.

leaves.title: The motion object and its legality
leaves.criterion: The designer marks motion by an on-line player and motion angled toward the line as illegal motion, still savable, and the engine flags it at the B11.3.1 rate when snapped. Derived formation labels at the snap are correct for every shipped motion.

leaves.title: Catalog of motions
