leaves.criterion: Every catalog motion can be attached to at least one shipped play and passes F3.2.1.

leaves.title: Man or zone indicator
leaves.criterion: Against a defense with no disguise, a recognition-80 quarterback's post-motion belief is correct more often than a recognition-40 quarterback's, and both are more accurate than with no motion.

leaves.title: Leverage, numbers, and eye candy
leaves.criterion: Linebacker lateral displacement at the snap against jet motion falls as the offense's rate of using the jet man falls, across a simulated season.

leaves.title: Motion tendencies
leaves.criterion: Tables populate after one simulated game.

leaves.title: Cadence structure
leaves.criterion: With the same line matchup, sack rate over 10,000 simulated dropbacks is higher against an offense that always snaps on one than against one that mixes counts. False start rate rises under high crowd noise.

leaves.title: Hard count
leaves.criterion: Season totals of offside plus neutral zone infraction fall within 30% of league rates in fast simulation with default profiles.

leaves.title: Procedure at the line
leaves.criterion: For any shipped play, the sequence's total duration is computed before the snap and drives the latest-call marker (I2.1.1).

leaves.title: Tempo as a weapon
leaves.criterion: A defense facing 8 straight no-huddle snaps shows higher line fatigue than the offense's line in the engine's fatigue output.

leaves.title: Live and dummy words
leaves.criterion: A team that never changes its audible words suffers a rising rate of defensive counter-checks over a simulated season; a team that rotates weekly does not.

leaves.title: Communication, signals, and tempo by level
leaves.criterion: Under the college rule set with radio disabled, I2.4.1 offers no radio relay and the call cycle uses signal timings.

leaves.title: Gap, technique, and hole conventions
leaves.criterion: For any formation the engine lists gaps on each side, and the count equals blockers on the line plus one.

leaves.title: The run concept data shape
leaves.criterion: Every run in F4.3 to F4.7 is expressed only with these fields and runs in the engine against every front in F8.

leaves.title: Rule primitives
leaves.criterion: 1. For each shipped run, rules resolve to a legal target for all blockers against each of the fronts in F8.2, and the unblocked defender matches the concept's `unblocked` field. 2. A defensive line slant after the snap changes at least one blocker's target within the reaction delay.

leaves.title: Counting the box and the numbers rule
leaves.criterion: Engine-reported box counts on a simulated season have a distribution within 5 points of the league shares at 6, 7, and 8 (shares derivable from the baseline file).

leaves.title: Identification: setting the point
leaves.criterion: With a forced wrong declaration, the engine shows a free linebacker on a zone run that is otherwise fully blocked.

leaves.title: Perimeter and receiver blocking
leaves.criterion: No shipped rule produces a below-waist crack by design.

leaves.title: Inside zone
leaves.criterion: Against an even front with a 1 technique playside and a 3 technique backside, the resolved blocks match the hand-drawn standard in the test set; the back's cutback rate rises when the backside 3 technique is reached.

leaves.title: Wide zone (outside zone, stretch)
leaves.criterion: Simulated wide zone has higher variance (more losses and more 10-plus runs) than inside zone with the same players. Tested over 10,000 plays.

leaves.title: Split zone
leaves.criterion: Cutback share of carries is higher on split zone than inside zone, same fronts.

leaves.title: Duo
leaves.criterion: Resolved blocks leave the playside corner or force player as the only free defender against a 4-3 over front with a seven-man box.

leaves.title: Power
leaves.criterion: The puller's resolved target is the playside linebacker against even and odd fronts in the test set; he logs when the end man squeezes inside the kick-out.

leaves.title: Counter
leaves.criterion: Linebackers' first-step direction is wrong more often against counter than against power for the same defenders, scaled by their discipline.

leaves.title: Trap and wham
leaves.criterion: Simulated yards per carry on trap are higher against a one-gap penetrating technique than against a two-gap technique, same players otherwise.

leaves.title: Pin and pull
leaves.criterion: The set of pullers changes correctly between a 4-3 over, 4-3 under, and 3-4 front in the test set.

leaves.title: One-puller gap variants: dart, G, and buck sweep
leaves.criterion: Each variant's pullers resolve to the stated targets against the F8.2 test fronts, and its unblocked defender matches the concept field.

leaves.title: Iso and lead
leaves.criterion: The fullback's resolved target is the playside linebacker against all test fronts.

leaves.title: Draw and delay
leaves.criterion: Draw yards per carry rise with the depth of linebacker drops in the defensive call.

leaves.title: Toss, sweep, and crack toss
leaves.criterion: Toss reaches the edge sooner than wide zone in engine timing, with a non-zero pitch fumble rate.

leaves.title: Jet sweep, end-around, reverse
leaves.criterion: Using jet sweep at least 3 times a game raises linebacker displacement against jet motion fakes (F3.3.2).

leaves.title: Zone read
leaves.criterion: A higher option-read attribute raises the share of correct give or keep decisions against a standard end; a scrape exchange lowers keep yardage.

leaves.title: Power read, counter read, quarterback power, quarterback draw, sweep read
leaves.criterion: Quarterback power shows one more blocker than box-minus-one against a seven-man box in the count display.

leaves.title: Quarterback sneak
leaves.criterion: Sneak conversion on one yard to go falls as A-gap defenders rise from 2 to 4.

leaves.title: Speed option and triple option
leaves.criterion: Pitch fumble rate is configurable and non-zero.

leaves.title: Inside veer, midline, and rocket toss
leaves.criterion: Against a defense that assigns the dive and the quarterback but no one to the pitch, the engine gives the pitch back the most yards per play of the three options over 10,000 snaps.

leaves.title: Tracks and footwork
leaves.criterion: A patience-80 back cuts after the press distance on at least 90% of zone runs; a patience-40 back cuts early more often and averages fewer yards behind the same line.

leaves.title: Reads and vision
leaves.criterion: Correct-read share rises monotonically with vision in a 10,000-play test.

leaves.title: Run concept against front and box: what makes a call good
leaves.criterion: In the decision-response battery (Q3): the same run gains more against a 6-man box than a 7-man box; gap runs gain more against a shaded front with good angles than against the same front slanting into the play.

leaves.title: Run checks at the line
leaves.criterion: With a "run away from the 3 technique" check, the run goes away from him on at least 85% of snaps for a recognition-80 quarterback when the defense does not stem.

leaves.title: Run-game rules and usage by level
leaves.criterion: Changing `foul.ineligible_downfield.yards` changes how far linemen climb on RPO plays before the throw with no code change. Changing `deadball.down_without_contact` changes the outcome of a test play where the runner slips untouched.

leaves.title: Protection data shape
leaves.criterion: Every shipped protection resolves to one assignment per blocker against every front and pressure in F8 and F9, and the list of unblocked rushers equals rushers minus blockers when rushers exceed blockers.

leaves.title: The arithmetic of protection
leaves.criterion: In the decision-response battery (Q3), raising protection from 5 to 7 against the same six-man pressure lowers pressure rate and lowers the number of receivers in the pattern.

leaves.title: Setting the Mike
leaves.criterion: Forcing a wrong declaration against a known pressure in a test produces a free rusher that the correct declaration blocks.

leaves.title: Counting threats and the hot side
leaves.criterion: For each shipped protection and each test pressure look, the reported hot defender matches a hand-checked table.

leaves.title: Big on big (man) protection
leaves.criterion: Against a four-down front with one linebacker blitzing through a B gap to the back's side, the back resolves to that linebacker; with a linebacker blitzing from the side away from a five-man version, he is listed as hot.

leaves.title: Full slide
leaves.criterion: Against an interior twist, full slide yields a lower free-rusher rate than man protection in a 5,000-play test with the same players.

leaves.title: Half slide
leaves.criterion: The split point changes correctly between over, under, and odd fronts in the test set.

leaves.title: Five-man and empty protections
leaves.criterion: Against a six-man pressure, a five-man protection always lists one hot rusher, and sack rate is lower when the paired route concept has a hot route than when it has none, same players and seeds.

leaves.title: Scan and dual read
leaves.criterion: Pickup success in a 5,000-rep test rises with the back's protection recognition; a dual read with both rushers coming always yields the outside rusher as hot.

leaves.title: Check-release, chip, and free release
leaves.criterion: A chip lowers the chipped rusher's pressure rate and delays the chipper's route arrival by the configured time.

leaves.title: Hot throws
leaves.criterion: With both players at recognition 80, the hot throw is delivered on at least 85% of hot pressures in test; lowering either attribute lowers it.

leaves.title: Sight adjusts
leaves.criterion: Sight-adjust conversions occur only when the triggering defender rushes.

leaves.title: Built-in answers to all-out pressure
leaves.criterion: With no zero check assigned, sack and pressure rates against all-out pressure are higher than with any of the four options, in test.

leaves.title: Play-action protection
leaves.criterion: Linemen stay within the downfield limit on every play-action snap except through the modelled foul hazard.

leaves.title: Quick-game, sprint-out, bootleg, screen, and max protections
leaves.criterion: Each type's launch point and time goal are honoured by the quarterback model's drop.

leaves.title: Passing off twists and games
leaves.criterion: Free-rusher rate on tackle-end twists against man protection falls as pair cohesion rises, over a 5,000-play test.

leaves.title: Protection checks at the line
leaves.criterion: Crowd noise at maximum raises missed-check rate above zero for the far-side tackle.

leaves.title: The weekly protection plan
leaves.criterion: A pressure answered in the plan and practised yields a lower free-rusher rate in the game than the same pressure unplanned, same players and seeds.

leaves.title: Protection rules and conditions by level
leaves.criterion: Switching rule sets changes the downfield limit used by play-action protection with no code change.

leaves.title: Route data shape
leaves.criterion: Every library route renders, resolves to a path against every coverage in F10, and reports a break time that falls when receiver speed rises in a same-seed test.

leaves.title: The route tree and its numbering
leaves.criterion: Renumbering the tree changes call text only; play results with the same seed are identical.

leaves.title: Library routes beyond the tree
leaves.criterion: Every listed route exists in data and passes the F6.1.1 render and resolve check.

leaves.title: Releases against press and off coverage
leaves.criterion: In a 5,000-rep test, press against a low-release receiver delays breaks more than against a high-release receiver; press-loss by the defender raises yards per target against man coverage with no deep help.

leaves.title: Stem leverage and separation at the break
leaves.criterion: With the same players and seed, an out route gains more separation against an inside-leverage man defender than against an outside-leverage one.

leaves.title: Sit against zone, run against man
leaves.criterion: Conversion fires only on routes that carry the tag; the correct-read rate rises with receiver recognition in test.

leaves.title: Option and choice routes
leaves.criterion: Agreement rate rises with shared practice reps in a same-seed comparison.

leaves.title: Vertical conversions
leaves.criterion: The seam read bends only when two deep safeties stay split at the read point.

leaves.title: Drop catalog
leaves.criterion: League-wide simulated time to throw has a mean within 0.1 s of the measured value once calibrated.

leaves.title: Matching route breaks to the drop
leaves.criterion: Swapping in a receiver 0.2 s slower over 12 yd moves that route's marker on the strip by the matching time.

leaves.title: Quick-game concepts
leaves.criterion: In the decision-response battery, quick game against a six-man pressure has a lower sack rate than a five-step concept against the same pressure, same seed and players.

leaves.title: The pass concept object
leaves.criterion: Every shipped concept attaches to every shipped formation that meets its `requires` and yields one route per eligible.

leaves.title: Horizontal stretches
leaves.criterion: Against three-deep four-under with the curl-flat defender forced wide in a test, the curl is thrown; forced inside, the flat is thrown.

leaves.title: High-low and triangle stretches
leaves.criterion: Against a two-deep zone with a squatting corner the smash throw goes to the corner route; with a sinking corner it goes to the hitch, in forced-defender tests.

leaves.title: Crossers and man-beaters
leaves.criterion: Same-seed test: mesh yields more separation at the catch against Cover 1 than curl-flat does against Cover 1.

leaves.title: Four verticals and its landmarks
leaves.criterion: In forced tests the quarterback throws the seam away from the single-high safety's first movement.

leaves.title: Shot plays: Mills, Yankee, post-wheel, double moves
leaves.criterion: Same-seed test: a sluggo thrown after three completed slants against the same corner gains more separation than a sluggo thrown cold.

leaves.title: Rubs, switches, and the pick rule
leaves.criterion: Rub-tagged routes draw offensive pass interference at a non-zero rate that falls as the rubbing receiver's route-running rises.

leaves.title: Progression types
leaves.criterion: Raising quarterback processing from 50 to 90 raises the share of dropbacks that reach read 3 with the same protection time, in a 5,000-play test.

leaves.title: Pre-snap reads: shell, leverage, and numbers
leaves.criterion: A disguised rotation lowers the pre-snap belief's accuracy compared with a static look, same quarterback, in test.

leaves.title: Using the route-by-coverage data
leaves.criterion: A code search shows no play-resolution path that reads a concept-against-coverage table. The pro calibration report lists each A1 row with simulated value, target, and pass or fail.

leaves.title: Pointer to F13
leaves.criterion: No route in a red-zone snap has a finish point beyond the end line.

leaves.title: Pass-game rules and usage by level
leaves.criterion: Switching the rule set from pro to college changes the sideline catch result in a scripted one-foot-in test and caps a 40-yd interference foul at 15 yd, with no code change.

leaves.title: The play-action object and its run partner
leaves.criterion: Every play-action play resolves to one partner run or to "none", and its first 0.3 s of offensive movement matches the partner run within the position tolerance used by the film comparison tool.

leaves.title: What the fake does to defenders
leaves.criterion: Same-seed pairs: the same routes and protection with and without a full fake against Cover 3 on first and 10 give deeper hook-dropper position error with the fake. On third and 15 the difference is near zero.

leaves.title: Play-action concepts
leaves.criterion: Every play-action concept shipped lists a partner run family it is drawn from.

leaves.title: Bootleg, naked, and keeper
leaves.criterion: With the back-side end set to crash in a forced test the naked quarterback gets outside untouched; set to boot rules he is pressured within 2.5 s.

leaves.title: Sprint out and dash
leaves.criterion: Sprint-out plays record a launch point outside the original tackle position on at least 90% of unpressured snaps.

leaves.title: The screen object
leaves.criterion: Under the college rule set, screens caught behind the line never draw ineligible-downfield or offensive-interference fouls in test, and the same play with the catch forced 1 yd beyond the line does at a non-zero rate. Under the pro rule set, a releaser more than 1 yd downfield before the throw draws the foul at a non-zero rate wherever the catch is made. (Corrected by audit Part 17: the earlier criterion contradicted this leaf's own pro reading.)

leaves.title: Screen families
leaves.criterion: A bubble thrown behind the passer's release point and dropped is ruled a fumble by the rule engine.

leaves.title: Screens against pressure
leaves.criterion: Simulated league screen EPA falls inside the band above after calibration, and screens against five or more rushers do not beat non-screen dropbacks against five or more rushers on average.

leaves.title: The RPO object
leaves.criterion: With the rule set switched from pro to college the computed `legal_throw_window` for the same play grows, and the foul rate on late throws falls, with no code change.

leaves.title: Pre-snap RPO: count and leverage
leaves.criterion: In forced-alignment tests the decision matches the rule line in every case.

leaves.title: Post-snap RPO: the conflict defender
leaves.criterion: In forced tests, a conflict defender who always fits the run yields throws on every RPO snap and one who always drops yields gives.

leaves.title: Building a series: base play, complements, and counters
leaves.criterion: The series view lists the correct members for a test playbook with known shared looks. No resolution code reads call order except through defender state.

leaves.title: Rates and results for calibration
leaves.criterion: The pro calibration report lists each row with simulated value, target or band, and pass or fail.

leaves.title: Play action, screens, and RPO by level
leaves.criterion: The same RPO play shows a longer legal window under the college rule set than under the pro rule set in the designer.

leaves.title: The technique table
leaves.criterion: For every shipped formation the overlay places each technique at the configured offset, and renaming an entry changes labels only, with identical play results on the same seed.

leaves.title: Stance, depth, and tilt
leaves.criterion: Moving a linebacker from 4 yd to 6 yd depth in a same-seed inside zone test raises the time before a climbing guard contacts him.

leaves.title: The front object
leaves.criterion: Every shipped front lines up legally against every shipped formation, and every gap on the offensive front has exactly one assigned defender or is listed as a second-level or third-level fit (F8.4).

leaves.title: Four-down fronts
leaves.criterion: Over and under put the three technique on opposite sides against the same formation.

leaves.title: Odd and five-man fronts
leaves.criterion: In tite, both B gaps resolve to down linemen and the C gaps to second-level or edge players.

leaves.title: Front against personnel and box count
leaves.criterion: In a 5,000-run test with the same teams, simulated yards per carry falls as box count rises from 6 to 8.

leaves.title: One-gap and two-gap techniques
leaves.criterion: Same-seed test: a one-gap three technique is trapped for more yards than a two-gap player at the same spot, and records more tackles for loss against inside zone.

leaves.title: Every gap has an owner
leaves.criterion: For every shipped front and coverage pair against every shipped formation, the table has no unowned gap unless the call is tagged as a pressure.

leaves.title: The extra fitter: safeties and corners in the run fit
leaves.criterion: With the same front, a two-high zone shell gives up more yards before first contact on inside runs than a one-high shell, same seed.

leaves.title: Keys and reads by position
leaves.criterion: A linebacker keyed on the guard follows a false pull more often than one keyed on the back, in a forced-play test.

leaves.title: Spill and box
leaves.criterion: Same-seed power play: with the end set to spill the runner's path bends outside the kick-out block; set to box it stays inside.

leaves.title: Force, alley, cutback, and pursuit
leaves.criterion: Forcing the force player to lose in a toss-play test produces a longer average gain than forcing him to win.

leaves.title: Fitting zone runs, duo, and split zone
leaves.criterion: For each zone run against each shipped front the resolved fit leaves exactly the defender named in the run's `unblocked` field free, matching F4's check.

leaves.title: Fitting gap runs: power, counter, trap, pin and pull
leaves.criterion: As F8.7.1 for each gap run.

leaves.title: Option responsibilities
leaves.criterion: With a scrape exchange forced, a quarterback who reads "end crashed, keep" is met by the scraping linebacker; with default rules the same read gains yards.

leaves.title: Misdirection: boot, reverse, and screen rules
leaves.criterion: As F7.2.1: chase lets the naked out; boot rules pressure it and concede more wide-zone cutback yards in a same-seed comparison.

leaves.title: Slants, angles, pinches, and stems
leaves.criterion: In a 5,000-run test, slants raise both the tackle-for-loss rate and the rate of runs of 10 yd or more compared with the same front without movement.

leaves.title: Fronts and fits by level
leaves.criterion: Changing `field.hash_from_sideline_ft` changes where a field-set front places its overhang, with no code change.

leaves.title: Rush lanes and contain
leaves.criterion: With the same seed, removing the contain flag from one edge raises scramble yards to that side over 2,000 dropbacks.

leaves.title: Rush moves come from the player
leaves.criterion: A rusher with high get-off and low power wins more often outside than through the blocker across 5,000 one-on-ones. No config value is keyed by move name.

leaves.title: Rush plans for the quarterback in front of you
leaves.criterion: Same seed, same players: cage lowers scramble yards and raises average time to throw compared with standard.

leaves.title: The stunt object
leaves.criterion: Against an offensive line with low shared-snap counts the same game produces more free rushers than against a line with high shared-snap counts, same seed, 2,000 dropbacks.

leaves.title: Two-man games
leaves.criterion: Each library entry loads and resolves against every protection in F5 without an unassigned gap.

leaves.title: Three-man games and run stunts
leaves.criterion: The fit view shows every gap owned after any run stunt. A stunt that leaves a gap empty is flagged.

leaves.title: The pressure object
leaves.criterion: Every shipped pressure validates. A pressure with a doubled gap or an unassigned receiver cannot be saved without a warning.

leaves.title: The blitz catalog
leaves.criterion: Each family, run against half slide away from the pressure, produces a free rusher in more than half of 1,000 trials. Run into the slide, it produces one in fewer than a quarter (starting test bounds).

leaves.title: Fire zone: three under, three deep
leaves.criterion: With a dropper placed in the hot window, the interception rate on hot throws rises against quarterbacks with low recognition and stays near baseline against high recognition, same seed.

leaves.title: Zone pressure shells: two-deep and six-man
leaves.criterion: Same seed and rushers: hot throws to the flat complete less often against the two-deep shell than against three-under three-deep. Against the six-man shell, quick inside throws complete more often than against the five-man fire zone.

leaves.title: Simulated pressure
leaves.criterion: Against a protection whose Mike point is set to the shown side, a simulated pressure from the other side yields a faster first pressure than the same four rushers from normal alignments, same seed.

leaves.title: Cover 0 pressure
leaves.criterion: Over 5,000 Cover 0 pressures the share of plays gaining 20 yd or more and the share with a sack or interception are both higher than for a four-man rush with Cover 3, same teams.

leaves.title: Peel and screen recognition
leaves.criterion: Turning peel off on a man pressure raises completions to the back on that side, same seed.

leaves.title: Green dog
leaves.criterion: Against seven-man protection, green dog on raises pressure rate; against check-release backs it raises completions to the back.

leaves.title: Spy
leaves.criterion: Adding a spy lowers quarterback scramble yards and lowers pressure rate in the same test.

leaves.title: Pressure rates for calibration
leaves.criterion: A ten-season simulated league lands inside the tolerance on every listed pressure rate.

leaves.title: Pass rush and pressure by level
leaves.criterion: Switching `foul.grounding.enforcement` changes the enforcement spot with no code change.

leaves.title: Play object schema
leaves.criterion: 1. Every starting-system play loads and saves without loss. 2. A play object with any outcome field fails schema validation. 3. Mirroring a play twice returns the original object byte for byte.

leaves.title: Role slots and position letters
leaves.criterion: For each personnel group in F1 the designer offers exactly the slots that group defines. A play cannot be saved with a missing or duplicate slot.

leaves.title: The play page view
leaves.criterion: The page renders in under 50 ms. Every assignment in the object appears in both the diagram and the text list.

leaves.title: Design flow
leaves.criterion: A user can build a valid shotgun 11-personnel dropback play from installed parts in under 60 s. The guided steps list only parts that are legal for the choices already made. An illegal alignment or assignment is reached by editing a slot by hand (G1.3) and passes through the G1.5 warning.

leaves.title: Formation editing
leaves.criterion: No formation that fails G1.5.1 can reach status valid. A landmark split resolves to the right yard value on left hash, middle, and right hash.

leaves.title: Shifts and motion
leaves.criterion: A play with two players moving at the snap cannot be saved as valid. Displayed pre-snap duration equals the sum used by I2.1.1 for the same play.

leaves.title: Route editor
leaves.criterion: Every route saved compiles to J4 rules without error. The time-to-break shown is within 0.1 s of the engine's result for a test receiver with no defender. With the same players and seed, a route run with "sell vertical" on gives the man defender a longer reaction delay at the break than the same route with it off. A step-count route converts to the same yards in the editor and the engine. A coverage landmark resolves to the midpoint rule in a board test against Cover 3 and Cover 2.

leaves.title: Blocking assignment editor
leaves.criterion: For each library scheme and each front in the preview set, every lineman resolves to exactly one assignment. Protection count plus releasing receivers equals ten for every pass play.

leaves.title: Ball carrier and mesh
leaves.criterion: A play-action pass cannot reach status valid without a partner run or an explicit "no partner" confirmation. Match score is 1.0 when the pass copies the run's formation, motion, and first-second line and back movement exactly.

leaves.title: Quarterback read editor
leaves.criterion: Every pass play has exactly one read type, at least one progression target, and an escape rule. Hot rules reference only releasing receivers.

leaves.title: RPO and option assignment
leaves.criterion: An RPO whose throw is later than the computed limit shows the ineligible-downfield warning with the timing gap in seconds and the lineman who will be past the limit. No foul chance is shown: engine odds appear only in the coaching school (N5). A 10,000-snap engine test of a late-throw RPO produces the foul at a rate above zero.

leaves.title: Tag definition
leaves.criterion: Every play plus every allowed tag, alone and in every non-exclusive pair, passes G1.5.1 and G1.5.2.

leaves.title: Mirror, strength, field and boundary
leaves.criterion: A field-side play called from the left hash aligns its strength to the right, and from the right hash to the left, in 100% of trials.

leaves.title: Packaged play definitions
leaves.criterion: A package cannot be saved if the two plays use different personnel groups. Its trigger evaluates to true or false for every look in the preview set.

leaves.title: Formation and motion legality
leaves.criterion: A test set of 40 formations (20 legal, 20 illegal with known reasons) is classified correctly with the right reason for each. Each of the 20 illegal ones can be saved after one confirmation, and running it in the engine draws the matching foul.

leaves.title: Eligibility and numbering
leaves.criterion: A route assigned to a covered end or an interior lineman is an error unless the play is a screen behind the line where rules allow, which is checked against B5. A reporting player is flagged in 100% of test cases.

leaves.title: Soundness warnings
leaves.criterion: Each warning type fires on a hand-built bad example and stays silent on a library play that is known sound.

leaves.title: Board walk-through
leaves.criterion: The same play and look always produce the same walk-through. Every assignment shown matches the engine's resolved assignment for the same inputs.

leaves.title: Practice-field trial
leaves.criterion: The staff estimate's interval contains the true engine mean for the same matchup in at least 80% of cases with an average staff, and is wider with a weak staff. No screen shows a point estimate without a sample size.

leaves.title: Teaching load of a play
leaves.criterion: A duplicate of an installed play with one new tag shows a load equal to the tag's cost only.

leaves.title: Staff drafting and review
leaves.criterion: A coach with maximum design skill finds every warning the validator finds. A coach with minimum skill finds under half on a 50-play test set.

leaves.title: Special teams play design
leaves.criterion: No kickoff or return design that breaks a B6 alignment rule can be saved as valid.

leaves.title: Trick plays
leaves.criterion: A design with two forward passes cannot be saved as valid. Extra exchanges raise the fumble rate in a 10,000-snap test.

leaves.title: Cadence design
leaves.criterion: A team with three installed counts draws a lower defensive get-off advantage than a team with one, in a 10,000-snap test. A freeze call with no paired play cannot be saved.

leaves.title: Short yardage, goal line, and the quarterback sneak
leaves.criterion: Under a rule set that makes pushing the runner a foul, a play with a pusher assignment is marked "illegal as drawn", can still be saved and called, and draws the foul in an engine test. The sneak has no handoff event in its engine trace.

leaves.title: Call object schema
leaves.criterion: Every starting-system defensive call loads and saves without loss. A call resolves to exactly eleven aligned defenders with one job each against every offensive formation in F2.

leaves.title: Role slots and declarations
leaves.criterion: For every formation in F2 the declaration rules produce exactly one run strength and one passing strength. With the ball on the left hash, a player tagged "field" aligns to the offense's right, and the reverse on the right hash, under both rule sets.

leaves.title: Package builder
leaves.criterion: Every offensive personnel group in F1 maps to a package. A package with twelve players cannot be saved, because a call has eleven slots (too many men on the field comes from substitution, I6, B2). A package with ten is legal (B2: playing with fewer than 11 is legal) and saves with a warning. Under the starting table, a season simulated against a league-average offensive personnel mix puts nickel on most defensive snaps and dime on a large share of third and long, within the calibration bands J15 sets from the facts above.

leaves.title: Front editor
leaves.criterion: For every front in the library and every formation in F2, every gap has an owner. Editing a technique updates the diagram and the gap table together.

leaves.title: Run fit editor
leaves.criterion: For each call and run family, the walk-through shows no unfilled gap when every defender does his job in chalk mode, or the designer has listed the gap as an error. Switching a side from box to spill moves the bounce responsibility to the named outside defender and the walk-through shows it. A spill call with no outside defender draws the error.

leaves.title: Stunt editor
leaves.criterion: Every saved stunt leaves each rusher with exactly one final gap. Raising the looper delay raises his computed arrival time by the same amount. In a calibration run of four-man third-down rushes, stunts raise pressure rate over straight rushes by an amount inside the J15 band set from the 2017 data.

leaves.title: Pressure editor
leaves.criterion: No saved pressure leaves an eligible receiver unassigned against any formation in F2 after checks are applied. Rushers plus droppers equals eleven in every resolved case.

leaves.title: Coverage editor
leaves.criterion: Against every formation in F2, a man coverage assigns each eligible receiver exactly one defender, and a zone coverage assigns every pass defender exactly one zone or match rule.

leaves.title: Match rules
leaves.criterion: The consistency check finds a planted conflict in a hand-built broken rule set and passes the library sets against the F6 concept list. With the ball moved from the near hash to the far hash, a divider rule moves its line by the stated amounts. A blocked "Under" call (forced link failure) leaves the overhang on his first man.

leaves.title: Matchup and help rules
leaves.criterion: With a travel rule on, the named corner aligns over the named receiver in 100% of man-coverage snaps in a test game, wherever the receiver lines up.

leaves.title: Formation checks
leaves.criterion: For each call, the validator lists every formation in F2 for which neither the base call nor a check gives every receiver a defender and every gap an owner.

leaves.title: Motion and shift rules
leaves.criterion: With the lock rule, the man defender follows the motion in every chalk-mode trial. With bump, defender-to-receiver assignments shift by one in the right direction. A switch with its communication link forced to fail leaves both defenders on the same receiver or neither, and the validator's replay names the uncovered receiver. A spin started with less than 1.2 s before the snap ends late, by the remaining time.

leaves.title: Tempo and no-huddle calls
leaves.criterion: A hurry-up snap with no call relayed runs the default tempo call in 100% of trials when one is set. With check-with-me on, an offense that snaps 2 s after setting gets the default call; one that waits 5 s gets the checked call.

leaves.title: Pre-snap picture and rotation
leaves.criterion: A disguise needing a 15-yard rotation in under 1 s is flagged. In an engine test, disguised calls lower a test quarterback's correct pre-snap coverage identification rate against undisguised calls.

leaves.title: Legality and soundness
leaves.criterion: A test set of 30 calls with planted faults reports each fault with the right reason. Each planted rule failure can be saved after one confirmation and draws the matching foul in an engine run.

leaves.title: Board and practice testing
leaves.criterion: Same as G1.6.1 and G1.6.2 for defensive calls. The auto test set for a call contains every formation in the opponent's scouted top list. Changing the scout card of a play changes the walk-through result for that play and no other.

leaves.title: Playbook object and sections
leaves.criterion: A 1,500-play book opens in under 1 s. Editing a shared formation updates every dependent play and re-runs validation on each. Every generated pro offensive book falls in the 600 to 1,000 range at creation.

leaves.title: Families and variants
leaves.criterion: Every play belongs to exactly one family. Filling a grid cell yields a play that passes G1.5.1 or reports why it cannot. Filling a cell under the concept profile costs fewer units than under the digit or descriptive profile, by the G4.2.1 table.

leaves.title: Base, complement, constraint
leaves.criterion: The review lists every base play that has no linked complement. A highlighted answer appears only after the booth reports the linked reaction. A reaction seen on 2 of the last 6 base calls is not reported; on 3 of 6 it is.

leaves.title: Series and looks-alike groups
leaves.criterion: Two identical plays score 1.0. A run and its exact play-action copy score 1.0 until the fake ends.

leaves.title: Playbook size report
leaves.criterion: Retiring a section lowers the upkeep number by that section's units. With upkeep above available time for four simulated weeks, average knowledge falls. With R = 180 team reps the readiness ceiling prints 40 plays. Raising the plan above the ceiling turns the warning amber without changing any knowledge value until the week is simulated.

leaves.title: Starting playbooks and the coordinator's book
leaves.criterion: Adopting a book that shares 60% of parts with the old one produces less relearning work than one sharing 10%. Renaming every word while keeping every concept costs only label-layer units. A departed coordinator's copy does not contain plays added after his departure date.

leaves.title: Versions, import, export, sharing
leaves.criterion: Export then import into an empty save reproduces every play object exactly. A play that fails validation is never imported as valid. A play edited after a game still shows its game-version form in that game's film and self-scout. A departed staff member's view of the team book stops at his departure version.

leaves.title: Edit permissions by job
leaves.criterion: For each job, every control outside its row is locked in every G screen.

leaves.title: Search and filters
leaves.criterion: Every filter combination on a test book returns exactly the plays a brute-force scan returns.

leaves.title: Call parts and order
leaves.criterion: For a 500-play test book every play renders to a unique string, and parsing each string returns the original play and tags. Rendered under each family template, the starting playbook's median single-play word count falls in that family's starting range above (a regression test on the templates, not a claim about real teams).

leaves.title: Huddle procedure
leaves.criterion: Doubling the repeats raises stage 4 time by the spoken length and lowers measured mishear rate in a 10,000-call test.

leaves.title: Call string parser
leaves.criterion: Results in under 100 ms for a 500-play book. Every rendered string parses to itself. On a planted test of 1,000 strings with one misspelled word each, the intended play ranks first in at least 95% (starting value, Assumption). A two-play string with a kill word returns a packaged call. A wristband cell code returns the same play as its full string.

leaves.title: System language families
leaves.criterion: Each family renders the full starting playbook with unique strings. The same play has different spoken lengths in the three families.

leaves.title: Word list editor
leaves.criterion: No two parts of one type share a word. The confusion warning fires on a planted similar pair.

leaves.title: Run and protection numbering
leaves.criterion: Every run in the starting book gets a unique number under both side conventions. Flipping the side convention re-renders every run and charges the rename cost once per changed word. "Six-seven" counts 3 syllables in G4.3.1.

leaves.title: Spoken length computation
leaves.criterion: For 20 hand-counted calls the computed syllable count is exact after user corrections and within 1 syllable before them.

leaves.title: Length limits and warnings
leaves.criterion: The report's latest-call time for a call equals the marker I2.1.1 shows for that call in a huddle-tempo test. A 13-word call draws the word warning; at the starting speech rate (5 syllables a second plus 0.2 s per part boundary) it is at least 5 s long, so it also draws the length penalty above 4 s, and a 13-word call is never "under 4 s" at starting values. Defining an alias drops that call's relay length to one word and adds the alias to the code-word teaching load.

leaves.title: Wristband codes
leaves.criterion: A band call's relay time is independent of call length. With team-wide bands, huddle time for a 5 s call falls below the single-band case.

leaves.title: One-word and no-huddle calls
leaves.criterion: A code word resolves to exactly one call. Calling by code word in no-huddle produces zero huddle time in I2.1.1. A repeat code after a play with no substitution leaves the defense no substitution window (I6). An indicator word cuts pre-snap time to the set value.

leaves.title: Sideline signals and boards
leaves.criterion: A play without an installed signal cannot be sent by signal. Decode chance by watching is zero for a signal set never used in a game, but a signal set can still leak (a staff member moves, a notebook is lost) at the floor `prob.floor` per game, never zero. With three dummy signalers and three signs per call, decode chance per game is at most a quarter of the single-signaler, single-sign case for equal exposure, for up to 11 live showings at any decoding effort E from 0 to 2 (per-showing chance ratio 0.18; the ratio of game chances rises toward 1 as n grows and passes 0.25 at n = 12 for E = 2 and n = 22 for E = 1, so the test is bounded to n of 11 or fewer). A total coach-to-player failure on one side under the pro rule set removes the other side's radio until restored.

leaves.title: Dummy calls
leaves.criterion: In an engine test, a defense's rate of anticipating a repeated audible is lower with dummies on. With r = 0.3 the defense needs about 43% more exposures to reach the same confidence as with r = 0, by the formula above.

leaves.title: Defensive wristbands and call boards
leaves.criterion: With all eleven wearing bands and the relay chain's first link forced to fail, the players with bands still play the sent call. A board call reaches defenders when the speaker-helmet player is off the field.

leaves.title: Defensive call string and relay
leaves.criterion: Every defensive call renders to a unique string. With the chain's first link forced to fail in a test, all eleven defenders play the previous call. At noise 1.0 with mid knowledge, a three-link voice chain delivers the full call to every defender less often than the same chain at noise 0, and less often than a signal chain at noise 1.0.

leaves.title: Defensive naming conventions
leaves.criterion: Every stunt in the starting book has a generated name matching its drawn order. No two declaration words in a pair share a first letter. A plan with 21 coverage words draws the warning.

leaves.title: Checks, alerts, and cadence words
leaves.criterion: Each audible on the list has a unique word. In maximum noise without hand signals, the share of wide receivers who receive a check is below the share at low noise. A kill call leaves formation and motion unchanged and runs the second play's concept in 100% of chalk trials when heard.

leaves.title: Cost of renaming and of a new system
leaves.criterion: Renaming one formation changes only the label layer of plays using it. A full family switch lowers team readiness more than renaming ten words.

leaves.title: Install unit
leaves.criterion: No unit can be placed before its prerequisites. Total units of a play equal G1.7.1's value.

leaves.title: Teaching events and their yield
leaves.criterion: A unit taught by meeting alone reaches a lower knowledge than the same minutes split across meeting, walk-through, and reps. Doubling meeting length gives less than double the gain.

leaves.title: Install schedule builder
leaves.criterion: The planner's own fill never schedules an activity a phase forbids. The user may place one by hand: it warns once with the rule, saves, and logs one violation row through L8.2.5 (H3.1.2, T5.4.1), the same for AI staffs. Every unit in the chosen base system is scheduled at least once or listed as not fitting. The planner's default fill places every base unit at least twice before the first game when the calendar allows, and shows the count of passes per unit.

leaves.title: Weekly install plan
leaves.criterion: With a test staff of perfect accuracy and a fully tested roster, projected readiness is within 5 points of realised readiness on average over a simulated season with no injuries. With an average staff the error is larger and unbiased. A short week projects lower readiness for new items than a normal week. With the default template, no third-down unit is scheduled before the first full practice day and no red zone unit before the second, unless the user moves it.

leaves.title: Carry-over and the standing menu
leaves.criterion: A unit not repped for four weeks shows lower knowledge than one kept in the "always up" set.

leaves.title: Readiness views
leaves.criterion: Replacing one starter with a player of zero knowledge lowers the play's readiness by more than one eleventh of the mean. Shown readiness converges on true knowledge as tests are added. After a written test the shown value for that player is within 8 points of true knowledge in at least 95% of test cases.

leaves.title: New players and backups
leaves.criterion: A catch-up plan raises the player's knowledge of the reduced package faster than no plan, at a measurable cost in the position coach's hours. With the default 5% backup share, the backup's projected readiness on the base sheet at kickoff is below the starter's on at least 80% of calls; raising his share to 30% narrows the gap.

leaves.title: Cadence, operation, and communication install
leaves.criterion: In a 10,000-snap noise test, a team with the silent count installed commits fewer false starts than one without.

leaves.title: Looks board
leaves.criterion: Every number on the board equals the scouting database value for the window. No rate is displayed without its sample size.

leaves.title: Themes of the week
leaves.criterion: Each theme links to at least one evidence row and one call, or is flagged.

leaves.title: Menu selection
leaves.criterion: Balance counts equal a hand count on a sample menu. Every scouted look above a rate threshold with no answering call is listed.

leaves.title: New for this week
leaves.criterion: The meter's total equals the sum of G1.7.1 units for uninstalled items on the menu. A new third-down play added after the second full practice day shows a lower projected readiness at kickoff than the same play added on the first day, with the same total reps available.

leaves.title: Sequences and set-ups
leaves.criterion: A linked later call shows its reminder on the sheet after the earlier one has been called.

leaves.title: Matchup hunting
leaves.criterion: With perfect scouting in a test, the predicted defender matches the engine's alignment in every case.

leaves.title: Protection plan
leaves.criterion: Every menu pass shows, for each listed threat, either an answer or a flag.

leaves.title: Defensive menu and rules of the week
leaves.criterion: Every offensive personnel group the opponent has used this season maps to a package and at least one call.

leaves.title: Emphasis settings
leaves.criterion: With takeaway emphasis high, both forced fumbles and missed tackles rise in a 10,000-play test.

leaves.title: Special teams and possession plan
leaves.criterion: Projected possessions fall as chosen pace slows.

leaves.title: Contingency plans
leaves.criterion: Each contingency resolves to a valid sheet version. Adding a contingency lowers the main plan's reps per call by the reps its unique calls use, and removing it restores them.

leaves.title: Plan size and review
leaves.criterion: Every warning on the screen traces to a rule in G5 or G6 and clears when its cause is fixed.

leaves.title: Sheet object
leaves.criterion: A filled sheet round-trips through save and load unchanged. The game-day console renders the same boxes in the same positions as the designer.

leaves.title: Layout editor
leaves.criterion: No two boxes overlap. Every box and entry has a unique key path of at most 3 presses.

leaves.title: Situation rule editor
leaves.criterion: For any rule set the editor lists every unmatched state in a 5,000-state grid. The focus result for 50 sample states matches I2.2.2's result exactly.

leaves.title: Standard situation catalogue
leaves.criterion: A template sheet with every catalogue box shows zero missing. Deleting a box moves its situation to missing or covered correctly. The missing list is ordered by expected snaps per game for the save's level, highest first. A row whose matching box matches fewer than 80% of its grid states shows as partly covered.

leaves.title: Expected snaps by situation
leaves.criterion: For the pro reference table, expected third-down snaps per team game equals 12.6 within 0.1, and the four third-down buckets sum to the third-down total within 0.1. A box rule of "any down, opponent 20 and in" shows 9.5. Expected snaps for any box are never shown without the source (league or team) and its game count.

leaves.title: Adding and ranking calls
leaves.criterion: Every entry resolves to a valid play or package. Readiness shown equals the staff's current estimate (G5.4.1) for the unit at the time of viewing, never D9's true value.

leaves.title: Sheet size and the reduction
leaves.criterion: The counter equals the number of distinct play-plus-tag entries. The warning fires exactly when the ratio is exceeded.

leaves.title: Script builder
leaves.criterion: Script order on the console equals designer order. Variety counts match a hand count on a sample script.

leaves.title: Second-half openers
leaves.criterion: The second script becomes active only after halftime. Each candidate offered at halftime traces to a first-half mark, result, or link.

leaves.title: Must-calls and touch targets
leaves.criterion: An outstanding must-call is visible on the console until called. Counts match the call log.

leaves.title: Reminders and tendency notes
leaves.criterion: A pinned tendency's numbers equal the scouting database values.

leaves.title: The head coach card
leaves.criterion: Each chart cell traces to a model output and input set. An edited cell is flagged as edited.

leaves.title: Wristband builder
leaves.criterion: Every band number maps to exactly one call. The console sends a band call with the number shown on the proof.

leaves.title: Audible list and quarterback freedom
leaves.criterion: The quarterback never audibles to a play outside the list in 1,000 test snaps at full freedom.

leaves.title: Defensive call sheet
leaves.criterion: For 50 sample states with offensive personnel, the focused box matches the expected box. The stress highlight appears on the first dead ball after the offense's success rate against the set call passes the stress line and never before 4 snaps against it (Assumption).

leaves.title: Special teams sheet
leaves.criterion: Every kicking situation I4 can raise has a focused box or shows as missing in review.

leaves.title: Backup quarterback, injury, and weather versions
leaves.criterion: Switching versions changes entries and leaves every box position and key unchanged.

leaves.title: Pre-lock review
leaves.criterion: Each planted fault in a test sheet appears in the report.

leaves.title: Printing and export
leaves.criterion: The PDF matches the console layout box for box.

leaves.title: Marking the sheet during the game
leaves.criterion: Tally on each entry equals the count in the call log at every dead ball.

leaves.title: Own-call tendency tables
leaves.criterion: Every cell equals a direct count from the call log. No rate appears without its count. A planted 18-of-20 run tendency from one formation over three games shows as strong. A 7-of-10 split shows as watch. A 13-of-20 split shows as lean. A 4-of-4 split shows counts only.

leaves.title: What the opponent probably knows
leaves.criterion: The ranked list changes when the breakdown window changes. Nothing on the screen reads K3's hidden state. A tendency shown only in games outside the assumed window ranks below an equal tendency shown inside it.

leaves.title: Predictability index
leaves.criterion: A caller who always runs on first down scores worse than one who mixes at league rates. A random caller scores near zero gain. In a simulated league season, the reference model's situation-only run-or-pass accuracy for the median AI caller lies inside the band Q2 sets around 67 to 75%.

leaves.title: Structural tells
leaves.criterion: A planted formation used only for runs appears in the list. A formation with a 50 to 50 split does not.

leaves.title: Player tells
leaves.criterion: In an engine test a defender who knows a lineman's run or pass stance tell diagnoses run or pass faster than one who does not. A position coach with skill factor 1.5 finds a planted habit sooner on average over 1,000 test seasons than one with skill factor 0.5. A habit fixed for 3 weeks and kept off heavy fatigue does not return.

leaves.title: Breaker planner
leaves.criterion: Every suggested breaker shares the tendency's formation and personnel and differs in play kind or direction.

leaves.title: Results of breakers
leaves.criterion: Counts match the call log.

leaves.title: Holding calls back and planting tendencies
leaves.criterion: A held call has zero entries in any opponent's charted data until it is first called in a game. A plant mark changes nothing in the engine.

leaves.title: Weekly and bye-week study
leaves.criterion: A high-skill author's report lists the planted strongest tendency first in at least 90% of test seasons. A low-skill author does so in under half.

leaves.title: Week object and block types
leaves.criterion: 1. For every team and week in a generated season, a `Week` record exists with no overlapping blocks per attendee. 2. Day numbering G-n is correct for Sunday, Monday, Thursday, and Saturday games. 3. Every block opens the right owner screen.

leaves.title: Work rules and limits on the players' week
leaves.criterion: 1. A fifteenth padded practice in a regular season can be scheduled only through the L8.2.5 warning, and confirming it writes one `violation_log` row. 2. The same holds for a twelfth padded practice within the first 11 weeks. 3. Changing a value in config changes the panel and the validation with no code change.

leaves.title: Advancing time through the week
leaves.criterion: 1. "Next decision" never passes a league deadline with a required choice. 2. Running a week block by block and running it with "to game day" from the same seed and the same choices produce identical end states.

leaves.title: Default normal-week template
leaves.criterion: 1. The default template validates against H1.1.2 with zero warnings. 2. A full season can be played without editing the template.

leaves.title: Install sequence across the week
leaves.criterion: 1. An item with all three exposures shows full weekly gain in D9. Removing each exposure lowers it by the configured factor. 2. The plan-size warning appears at the configured ratio.

leaves.title: Short week (Thursday game after a Sunday game)
leaves.criterion: 1. A Sunday-then-Thursday schedule produces a four-day week with no day off and no padded practice in the default template. A padded practice added by the user counts against the season total and carries the rule 2 fatigue charge. 2. With the default short-week template, new-item readiness is lower than in a normal week for the same plan.

leaves.title: Long weeks: after a Thursday game, Monday games
leaves.criterion: A Thursday-then-Sunday schedule produces a ten-day week. A Monday-then-Sunday schedule produces a six-day week with one fewer block day.

leaves.title: Bye week
leaves.criterion: 1. The planner accepts fewer days off than the configured rule after showing the rule and the C11.2.4 penalty warning once, and records a violation and a decision log entry. It never refuses. 2. Over 10,000 such violations at neutral trust, the share that produce a finding matches the configured C11.2.4 chance within sampling tolerance. 3. A found violation deducts the configured fine from the coach's cash (E6). 4. Each staff project produces its report.

leaves.title: Late-season and playoff weeks
leaves.criterion: A rested starter records zero snaps and no game injury. Plan work on an eliminated opponent contributes nothing to the actual game.

leaves.title: Scoreboard and clinching scenarios
leaves.criterion: 1. For a fixed standings file, the listed scenarios match a brute-force enumeration. 2. A standing instruction fires at the first dead ball after its condition is certain, never before.

leaves.title: Editing and saving week templates
leaves.criterion: A saved template is applied to the next week of the same shape. An edit that breaks a hard limit shows the rule and the reference penalty and is saved once the user confirms (H1.1.2, C11.2.4). An edit that cannot exist, such as overlapping blocks for one attendee, is refused with the reason.

leaves.title: Delegating blocks to staff
leaves.criterion: A whole week can run with every block delegated. Hours charged to the user equal the sum of blocks he attended.

leaves.title: Week summary and readiness check
leaves.criterion: Every call-sheet play appears with a readiness value. The stored snapshot matches the screen at kickoff.

leaves.title: College game-week template
leaves.criterion: 1. The default template never exceeds the configured weekly or daily hours. 2. A college team's week holds exactly one day with zero countable hours.

leaves.title: College work rules: countable hours
leaves.criterion: 1. A college week with more countable hours than the config values saves only through the L8.2.5 warning, and each confirmed excess writes one `violation_log` row. 2. A game day always charges exactly the configured game-day hours. 3. Changing the rule-set year changes the preseason practice limit.

leaves.title: Class time and academic blocks
leaves.criterion: For every weekday block in term, the absence list equals the set of players whose class pattern overlaps it.

leaves.title: Recruiting blocks in season
leaves.criterion: 1. Off-campus evaluation blocks beyond the configured day pool are placed only through the L8.2.5 warning, each writing one `violation_log` row. 2. A coach's recruiting and game-prep blocks never overlap.

leaves.title: The week by rung
leaves.criterion: 1. A user below coordinator cannot move a fixed block. 2. Every `boss_task` has a deadline and produces one completion record. 3. At graduate-assistant rung the default task hours exceed the default working day.

leaves.title: Breakdown scope
leaves.criterion: 1. Selecting more games than staff hours allow shows a late-finish time. 2. No tendency number is computed from a game that is not in a finished job.

leaves.title: Play tagging and its accuracy
leaves.criterion: 1. Observable tags equal the true record in every case. 2. Over 10,000 test plays the inferred-tag accuracy matches the configured probability within 1 percentage point. 3. A perfect-skill tagger with zero disguise produces fully correct tags.

leaves.title: Cut-ups
leaves.criterion: Every standard cut-up's play count equals the number of `ScoutedPlay` records matching its filter. A custom filter can be saved and reopened in a later week.

leaves.title: Tendency tables
leaves.criterion: 1. For a fixed set of plays the displayed rate, `n_eff`, and interval equal hand-computed values. 2. Thin rows are marked at the configured threshold.

leaves.title: The play caller's history
leaves.criterion: The card for a coach with prior-team games shows those games in his sample. The user's own card, viewed in a debug mode, matches his decision log.

leaves.title: Unscouted looks
leaves.criterion: A concept the opponent has not run this season but ran last season appears on the list.

leaves.title: Opponent personnel report
leaves.criterion: No true attribute appears on the report. Bands narrow as more games are broken down.

leaves.title: Expected lineup
leaves.criterion: The screen shows exactly the fields the policy publishes and nothing from the opponent's private medical state.

leaves.title: Tells
leaves.criterion: A taught tell with true reliability 1.0 always improves the read in test snaps. A taught tell with reliability 0.5 produces wrong reads at about that rate.

leaves.title: Signals and signal security
leaves.criterion: The known chance is zero for an opponent never faced with the current set and no former members.

leaves.title: Inside knowledge
leaves.criterion: The bonus applies only against the former team and decays on the configured schedule.

leaves.title: The staff scouting report
leaves.criterion: Every claim in the report resolves to a filter with a play count.

leaves.title: The head coach's own film study
leaves.criterion: Opponent film never shows the opponent's assignment overlays or call names. Hours charged match the rule.

leaves.title: Film exchange: what film arrives and when
leaves.criterion: 1. No breakdown job can start on a game before its availability time. 2. Tag accuracy for inferred tags is lower on broadcast-only film than on two-angle film in a 10,000-play test.

leaves.title: Limits on gathering information
leaves.criterion: 1. The user can order the recording from the advance-scouting assignments without waiting for a staff proposal, and sees the rule and the reference penalty before confirming. 2. A detected violation always produces a C11 event naming the head coach. 3. In a 100-season run with no user, at least one AI club is detected and penalised, and the detection rate per game of recording matches the user-side rate within sampling tolerance (Q4.3.2).

leaves.title: The user as tagger and report builder
leaves.criterion: 1. Every user-entered tag is stored with the true value linked and hidden. 2. A wrong user tag changes the tendency table that the team's plan reads. 3. "Cannot tell" is never scored as wrong. 4. The tagging screen exposes no field that reveals the true call.

leaves.title: College opponents with thin film
leaves.criterion: An opponent with a new play caller and under half its roster returning never shows "strong" in week 1.

leaves.title: Bought charting data and advance scouts
leaves.criterion: 1. Service tags for a given game are identical for every subscriber. 2. Service tags never overwrite staff or user tags. 3. A college in-person scouting trip writes exactly one violation row and is never blocked.

leaves.title: Practice object
leaves.criterion: Period minutes plus transitions never exceed the block. Setting full pads decrements the season counter when the practice resolves, not when planned.

leaves.title: Period types
leaves.criterion: Each type in config appears in the palette with its profile. A team period without a script runs with the coordinator's draft (H3.2.1 rule 5) and says so.

leaves.title: Tempo and pads
leaves.criterion: The same script at walk, jog, thud, and live gives load in increasing order and knowledge highest at thud and live.

leaves.title: The practice script
leaves.criterion: The rep count equals minutes times rate, rounded down. Each call-sheet play shows its number of scripted reps for the week.

leaves.title: Scout cards
leaves.criterion: Every card links to a tag source or is marked "coach's own". Gains in game follow the three-level match rule.

leaves.title: Scout team
leaves.criterion: Assigning a closer-matching scout player raises the factor.

leaves.title: Rep distribution
leaves.criterion: Sum of rep shares per position per period is 100 percent. A backup given zero reps has only mental-rep gains.

leaves.title: Participation and rest days
leaves.criterion: Unless the user changes it (rule 2), the report label equals the label implied by the rep share. A player set to Did not participate records zero practice load.

leaves.title: Competition and position battles
leaves.criterion: Grades shown equal the resolver's recorded rep outcomes.

leaves.title: Practice environment
leaves.criterion: With noise preparation the road cadence penalty in J12 is reduced by the configured share.

leaves.title: Walkthroughs and the mock game
leaves.criterion: Skipping the mock game raises the simulated substitution error rate in a 1,000-game test.

leaves.title: Resolving a practice
leaves.criterion: 1. Same seed and same plan give identical results. 2. Doubling team-period minutes roughly doubles reps and load. 3. Fast mode and rep-level mode give matching average gains within 5 percent over 1,000 practices.

leaves.title: Practice film and the practice report
leaves.criterion: Every mental error in the true record is visible on film. The report's error list differs from the true list at the rate implied by staff skill.

leaves.title: College practice limits and shape
leaves.criterion: 1. A college practice that pushes the day over the configured daily hours shows the warning, can be saved, and on saving writes exactly one violation row. 2. With the padded-limit value empty, no padded budget is shown or enforced.

leaves.title: Running your part of practice by rung
leaves.criterion: 1. A position-coach user's drill choices change the technique gains of his group and no other group. 2. Scout-team quality for a period changes with the graduate-assistant user's choices.

leaves.title: Meeting types and owners
leaves.criterion: No player or coach is in two overlapping meetings. Each type has a leader at block time.

leaves.title: Agenda and the meeting effect
leaves.criterion: 1. Two 45-minute meetings with a break give more total gain than one 90-minute meeting with the same agenda. 2. Items beyond the daily cap show half gain. 3. Gains scale with the leader's teaching factor.

leaves.title: Team meeting agenda
leaves.criterion: 1. A theme without supporting practice time gives no on-field effect. 2. Situational teaching raises the named situation's awareness value for attendees only. 3. The consistency record shows each theme against the philosophy statement.

leaves.title: Accountability and recognition in front of the team
leaves.criterion: Each framing creates its event with the named players. A four-week pattern of unequal call-outs lowers the consistency value.

leaves.title: The night-before meeting
leaves.criterion: The modifier never exceeds the cap and is zero after halftime.

leaves.title: Staff meeting
leaves.criterion: Each raised item is stored with its outcome. Alignment moves the teaching factor within the configured range.

leaves.title: Game-plan meetings and the head coach's input
leaves.criterion: Hours charged match the level. Credit in N4 follows authorship.

leaves.title: Teaching methods and learning styles
leaves.criterion: The same agenda with a better-matched method gives a higher gain.

leaves.title: Tests
leaves.criterion: After a test the displayed readiness band for the tested sections is narrower than before.

leaves.title: The players' version of the plan and study away from the building
leaves.criterion: Higher work ethic gives more out-of-building gain with the same packet.

leaves.title: New arrivals
leaves.criterion: A new arrival is used only in tagged plays unless the user overrides.

leaves.title: Quarterback meeting with the play caller
leaves.criterion: Marks appear on the game-day sheet. A marked play applies the configured penalty.

leaves.title: Leadership council meeting
leaves.criterion: Skipping the slot suppresses that week's council items.

leaves.title: Goal board
leaves.criterion: Each goal evaluates correctly against the box score.

leaves.title: College meetings
leaves.criterion: Adding 30 minutes of required meetings on a full day forces 30 minutes out of another countable block.

leaves.title: Meetings by rung
leaves.criterion: 1. A position-coach user's agenda changes knowledge gains for his group only. 2. Every proposal is recorded and scored once after the game.

leaves.title: Clearance and use
leaves.criterion: No control changes a clearance. Practising or playing a not-cleared player is possible only through the rule 2 warning, and always writes a log row and an L8.2.2 objection draw. A player removed in a game by the independent consultants never returns in that game. Clearance timing differs between a cautious and an aggressive medical staff on the same injury and seed.

leaves.title: The daily medical report
leaves.criterion: Every player with an active injury record appears. Ranges narrow with higher staff skill in a paired test.

leaves.title: Practice report
leaves.criterion: For any practice, the draft label equals the label implied by the recorded rep share. Reports are produced on exactly three days per game week for each week shape.

leaves.title: Game status
leaves.criterion: Placing a player declared Out on the active list opens the H6.2.1 warning and always raises an H5.2.3 flag. No screen offers "Probable".

leaves.title: Accuracy, gamesmanship, and league discipline
leaves.criterion: A truthful report never triggers an inquiry. A player with no status who is inactive for injury raises a flag every time.

leaves.title: Playing hurt
leaves.criterion: The card never shows a true hazard value. A logged pressure decision followed by aggravation produces the trust event.

leaves.title: Load management
leaves.criterion: Flags appear at the configured ratio. A rep cap is honoured by the practice resolver.

leaves.title: Second opinions and surgery timing
leaves.criterion: The event appears for injuries flagged in D11 as having more than one treatment path.

leaves.title: Concussion protocol during the week
leaves.criterion: No user action changes a protocol player's step. A player cannot be cleared without passing all five steps.

leaves.title: Illness, heat, and cramping
leaves.criterion: Heat bands change the fatigue rate in the configured direction. Illness spread can be switched off in config for tests and calibration only. It is never a player option, since a switch that changes outcomes would be a second difficulty.

leaves.title: The team clinician and mental health
leaves.criterion: No interface path exposes a player's mental health record to the user.

leaves.title: Return to practice and ramp-up
leaves.criterion: A player cannot be activated before four games have passed. The ninth regular-season designation is refused. A window closes on day 22.

leaves.title: College health and availability
leaves.criterion: 1. With the availability-report flag off, no report is filed and no H5.2.3 discipline can occur. 2. No college player can be dressed without medical clearance except through the H5.1.1 rule 2 warning, which always logs the act and draws an L8.2.2 objection.

leaves.title: Health information by rung
leaves.criterion: 1. A position-coach user never sees medical detail for players outside his group. 2. An observation report can only raise, never lower, the chance that a hidden injury is found.

leaves.title: Weekly roster calendar
leaves.criterion: 1. Every regular-season and postseason game week has a full marker set with deadlines that match C5 config. 2. An untouched marker is resolved by K7 at its deadline and logged. 3. Markers move correctly for Thursday, Saturday, and Monday games.

leaves.title: The coach's voice and the general manager's
leaves.criterion: 1. No transaction is filed without passing through the `decider` check, and every `decider` value traces to the job's L5.2.1 arrangement or a contract clause. 2. Over 1,000 simulated requests with negative general-manager value, the approval rate rises with trust (L5.2.4) and with nothing else. 3. Every request and answer appears in the decision log with the reason. 4. The same move renders as "Do it" in a final-say job and as "Ask the general manager" in a job without it.

leaves.title: Building the active list
leaves.criterion: 1. The screen refuses a list that breaks the C5 limit. 2. A list with a red coverage gap cannot be locked without a confirmation that names the gap. 3. Staff recommendations never leave a special teams unit short when 11 healthy candidates exist.

leaves.title: Position flexibility and emergency assignments
leaves.criterion: 1. When the last listed player at a position is injured in a game, I6 inserts the named emergency player. 2. A cross-trained player's readiness at the second position rises with reps and falls without them.

leaves.title: Inactive list planning and the declaration
leaves.criterion: 1. No edit is accepted after the lock time. 2. The inactive count always equals roster count minus actives. 3. A healthy scratch produces a D12 event. A prior talk changes its size.

leaves.title: Elevations as a tactic
leaves.criterion: 1. A third elevation in one game is refused. 2. The per-player season count blocks at the config limit. 3. The roster count for the active list rises by the number of elevations and falls back after the revert.

leaves.title: Practice squad upkeep and protections
leaves.criterion: 1. A fifth protection is refused. 2. A protected player cannot be signed away before the next game ends. 3. A scout-look swap changes scout-card fidelity for one week only.

leaves.title: The emergency list and weekly tryouts
leaves.criterion: 1. Every position shows up to the configured number of available names or "none". 2. A workout changes the confidence band and never the true value. 3. A player signed after a long layoff shows the conditioning penalty in his first games.

leaves.title: Signing from the street, another practice squad, or your own
leaves.criterion: 1. No signing is filed that leaves the roster over its limit. 2. Projected readiness matches the value D9 computes at kickoff within 5 points when the plan is followed. 3. A signing from another practice squad lands on the 53 only.

leaves.title: Waiver claims
leaves.criterion: 1. Claims resolve in priority order with one winner. 2. A lost claim leaves the roster unchanged.

leaves.title: Injured reserve and the return designation in season
leaves.criterion: 1. A placed player cannot play before the minimum number of team games has passed. 2. The 21-day clock closes the window when unused. 3. Designation counts never exceed config.

leaves.title: Depth chart changes during the week
leaves.criterion: 1. A depth change before the first practice of the week changes that week's rep distribution. 2. A late change leaves the new starter's readiness lower than an early change in the same test week. 3. A broken role promise always creates a trust event.

leaves.title: Releasing a player
leaves.criterion: 1. Every release records who told the player. 2. A release of a leadership-council member triggers the L2 check.

leaves.title: College in-season roster management
leaves.criterion: 1. No pro transaction type can be filed for a college team. 2. With `college.redshirt_enabled` true, playing a player past the limit requires confirmation and updates his eligibility. 3. With an empty travel limit the screen applies none and logs it.

leaves.title: Roster work by rung
leaves.criterion: 1. At each rung only the tasks listed for it are editable. 2. Every recommendation is scored once and is written to S4 standing and to the evidence list in E9.4.5.

leaves.title: The head coach's weekly media schedule
leaves.criterion: 1. Every game week holds the configured required sessions unless the user removed one. 2. A skipped required session creates exactly one C11 event and one L6 event. 3. Session counts read from config. Changing the config value changes the validator.

leaves.title: Coordinators, assistants, and the open locker room
leaves.criterion: 1. Coordinators' sessions never fall on a head coach session day when another day is free. 2. Off-message quote frequency rises as trust falls in a 1,000-week test.

leaves.title: Season-ending, pre-draft, and special conferences
leaves.criterion: A public promise broken inside the window always produces one consistency event.

leaves.title: The session: questions and message choices
leaves.criterion: 1. Every answer writes one `Statement` and sends events only to the audiences in its table row. 2. No statement changes any D2, D3, or D4 attribute. 3. The bland default produces no positive or negative relationship events in a single session.

leaves.title: Hot topics and announcements
leaves.criterion: 1. A quarterback change always appears as the top topic of the next session. 2. Leak frequency rises with the number of people who know and with lower trust in a 1,000-week test.

leaves.title: Injury information in public
leaves.criterion: A spoken answer that contradicts the filed status always sets the H5.2.3 conflict flag.

leaves.title: Bulletin-board material
leaves.criterion: With the modifier on, the simulated win rate change over 10,000 games is below 0.5 percentage points (starting bound).

leaves.title: Officials and the league
leaves.criterion: Every public criticism produces exactly one discipline event at the config amount or the default tier.

leaves.title: Broadcast production meeting
leaves.criterion: With the flag off, no such block is ever created.

leaves.title: The opponent's media
leaves.criterion: Declining never creates a C11 event.

leaves.title: The coach's show, sponsors, and community appearances
leaves.criterion: Appearance income appears in E6 only for attended blocks.

leaves.title: The college media week
leaves.criterion: 1. No pro policy value is read for a college team. 2. With `college.recruit_comment_ban` true, an answer naming an unsigned recruit is offered only with the violation mark, and choosing it always writes one `violation_log` row.

leaves.title: Media by rung
leaves.criterion: A user below coordinator never receives a required session block at pro level other than the assistant availability.

leaves.title: Travel plan and departure day
leaves.criterion: 1. Every away game has exactly one `TravelPlan` by G-5, chosen by the user or by default. 2. No block overlaps a travel block for any traveller. 3. Over 10,000 simulated games, the difference in win rate between Standard and Early plans on the same trips is below 1 percentage point (starting bound that keeps the effect inside noise).

leaves.title: The travel day
leaves.criterion: A travel day over a work limit is saved only after the H1.1.2 warning, and always ends in a curfew time.

leaves.title: Hotel, curfew, and bed check
leaves.criterion: 1. Breach frequency falls with bed check on and with higher discipline in a 10,000-night test. 2. Every found breach reaches L3 before kickoff.

leaves.title: The travel party
leaves.criterion: No player off the travel list can be made active for an away game.

leaves.title: Time zones and the body clock
leaves.criterion: 1. The offset is zero for a home game and for a team on site long enough to adapt fully. 2. With the modifier set to zero in config, results are identical with and without travel across a fixed seed set.

leaves.title: Altitude
leaves.criterion: For a game above the threshold, the decision book's field goal range differs from the sea-level table by J12's computed amount.

leaves.title: International and neutral-site games
