leaves.criterion: Both plans produce valid weeks with no overlapping blocks and correct local times.

leaves.title: Staying on the road between away games
leaves.criterion: The offer appears only when both thresholds are met.

leaves.title: Forecast, practice conditions, and the weather plan
leaves.criterion: 1. Forecast error on G-1 is smaller than on G-5 in every simulated week. 2. Truth is unreadable from the UI before kickoff.

leaves.title: Delays and disruptions
leaves.criterion: Event frequency over 10,000 trips matches config within sampling error.

leaves.title: College travel
leaves.criterion: 1. A college travel plan that takes the week past the configured countable hours is saved only through the L8.2.5 warning (H1.5.2 rule 3). 2. Class-missed hours are written for every player on the travel list for every plan that overlaps class days.

leaves.title: Travel work by rung
leaves.criterion: Each rung sees only its listed tasks, and every task writes one completion record.

leaves.title: Team meals and the nutrition staff
leaves.criterion: 1. Moving a meal block moves the earliest start of the next meeting or treatment block. 2. Meal blocks never count toward work-rule hours. 3. The pregame meal effect is zero inside the 3 to 5 hour band.

leaves.title: Document object and lifecycle
leaves.criterion: 1. Every game week creates one record of each weekly type for each team. The self-scout report follows its own cadence. 2. No unpublished document is visible to its recipients. 3. A late document reduces recipients' available study time by exactly the lateness.

leaves.title: Authors, workload, and review
leaves.criterion: 1. An overloaded author's documents show lower quality than the same author's at normal load. 2. When an AI head coach reviews, seeded errors are caught at the rate his hidden parameter gives, within sampling error. When the user reviews, exactly the errors he marks are caught and no roll is made (rule 3, E9.1.3 case 1) (audit Part 17, was: "a rate equal to the user's skill").

leaves.title: Distribution and security
leaves.criterion: A released player's received-document list is available to H2.4.2 at the moment he signs elsewhere.

leaves.title: Install schedule
leaves.criterion: Every plan item appears in exactly one cell.

leaves.title: Practice schedule and script
leaves.criterion: Every scripted rep references an existing play and an existing scout card.

leaves.title: Scout cards
leaves.criterion: A card drawn by the user is scored against engine truth and the score is stored.

leaves.title: Scouting report, players' packet, and tip sheet
leaves.criterion: A tip sheet never exceeds the configured line limit per unit.

leaves.title: Decision book
leaves.criterion: Every cell the user overrode is logged with his note, and the override is what I5 recommends in the game.

leaves.title: Weather sheet
leaves.criterion: Range bands on game morning are narrower than on G-3 in every simulated week with an outdoor game.

leaves.title: Depth card, call sheet, and wristband
leaves.criterion: A player made inactive after the call sheet is published always raises a flag on every play that names him.

leaves.title: Archive and reuse
leaves.criterion: Against a division opponent in the second meeting of a season, document hours are lower than in the first by the configured saving.

leaves.title: College documents
leaves.criterion: With a two-person support staff and a full-size plan, the panel raises the workload warning on G-6.

leaves.title: Producing documents as the user's job
leaves.criterion: 1. Every user-authored document stores an accuracy score that the UI never shows directly. 2. At graduate-assistant rung, the default weekly task list needs more hours than a normal week provides at full depth. 3. A wrong tendency in a user's report can be traced in N1 to the document and its author.

leaves.title: Pregame clock and task list
leaves.criterion: 1. No locked item can be changed after its deadline. 2. Skipping every task produces a legal game with staff defaults and a log entry for each skipped task. 3. The countdown and the J12 weather clock agree at every step. 4. A team that has not taken the field by T minus 10 loses its toss option for both halves and overtime and is charged 15 yards on the opening kickoff (Rule 4-2-1). AI teams never miss it unless a delay event moves them. 5. After T minus 90 the captains list changes only by the coach informing the referee (Rule 18-1-4), and the change is logged.

leaves.title: Carry-over from the night before
leaves.criterion: Every flag shown traces to an H4, H5, or L3 record. A curfew decision left open at T minus 90 defaults to the team rule in L3.

leaves.title: Pregame workout of questionable players
leaves.criterion: Over 1,000 simulated workouts, report accuracy rises with staff skill. A "cannot go" player reaches the active list only after the L8.2.5 warning is confirmed, and each such case writes one violation row.

leaves.title: Inactive list and the active 48
leaves.criterion: 1. The screen cannot produce an active list over 48, or over 47 with fewer than 8 offensive linemen. 2. The thin-spot panel lists every position and unit job below its minimum for a set of 20 test rosters. 3. An inactive player never appears in any snap of the game log.

leaves.title: Emergency third quarterback
leaves.criterion: The emergency quarterback cannot enter while either other quarterback is available. Plays with a direct snap to a non-quarterback are removed from the callable list while the emergency quarterback is in.

leaves.title: Radio helmet designations
leaves.criterion: At no snap do two players of one side on the field have a live radio. With both defensive users out, every defensive call uses the signal relay.

leaves.title: Game-day depth card
leaves.criterion: Removing any single active player from a test roster yields a legal 11 for every unit using only the card.

leaves.title: Weather and field check
leaves.criterion: Reported current values equal J12 values at the report time. Forecast error over 1,000 games has the configured spread and zero mean.

leaves.title: Kicking lines
leaves.criterion: With a perfect-skill coordinator the reported comfortable line equals the J9 75% line within 1 yard. Lines differ by direction when wind along the field is above 10 mph.

leaves.title: Opponent warm-up and inactives
leaves.criterion: Every game plan rule that names an inactive opponent is listed in the prompt.

leaves.title: Call sheet edits
leaves.criterion: Every play on the final sheet is installed. Key positions for unchanged boxes are identical before and after edits.

leaves.title: Decision book
leaves.criterion: With a perfect-skill analyst, every non-close cell equals the model's best choice. Changing a kicking line by 5 yards changes the cells between the old and new line.

leaves.title: Standing instructions and delegation for the day
leaves.criterion: In a delegated test game, no coordinator call breaks an active instruction except at the configured miss rate.

leaves.title: Heads-up to the officials
leaves.criterion: Over 10,000 simulated unusual legal plays, the wrong-flag rate is lower with the alert than without.

leaves.title: Pregame challenge designee
leaves.criterion: 1. No challenge in the game log is started by anyone other than the head coach or the named designee. 2. A designee flag decrements the same challenge and timeout counters as a head-coach flag.

leaves.title: Captains
leaves.criterion: 1. The screen cannot name more than six (four under the college key). 2. The captain list locks at T minus 90 in the pro set and any later change is an in-game event through the referee. 3. Every accepted or declined penalty in the game log names exactly one captain for the choosing team.

leaves.title: Coin toss choices
leaves.criterion: 1. For all toss results and choices, the first-half and second-half kickoff and goals match Rule 4-2-2. 2. Choosing "kick" with a won toss shows the warning. 3. AI coaches in calm conditions (steady wind under 10 mph) defer at a rate inside 80% to 95% across a simulated season (starting band from the playoff rate above, 2 of 3 for direction, the band itself an Assumption for calibration). 4. With a steady wind of 15 mph or more along the field, the advice line names the end that gives the wind in the fourth quarter, and in every half a team has the wind in exactly one of its two quarters (goals change after the first and third quarters).

leaves.title: Pregame talk
leaves.criterion: Over a simulated season, the talk changes mean win probability by less than 0.5 percentage points for any fixed policy. No single theme is best in every context.

leaves.title: Pregame record
leaves.criterion: Replaying the save's event log reproduces an identical pregame record.

leaves.title: Handshake and leaving the field
leaves.criterion: The default choice changes no state. A non-default choice writes one relationship event. A warm word with no existing tie changes nothing. Over 10,000 simulated cold handshakes after a provoking event, the share that becomes a media item is 0.20 plus or minus 0.01.

leaves.title: The postgame talk
leaves.criterion: The talk's morale effect never exceeds the cap. The same talk given three weeks running has a smaller effect the third time (0.49 of the first with the starting values). A poor-fit talk lowers credibility. The talk always ends before the locker room opens to media.

leaves.title: Game balls
leaves.criterion: At most three per game from the head coach. Each writes exactly one recognition event. A second ball to the same player within 4 weeks gives 0.6 of the first gain. A ball from the players to the coach writes a reputation event and changes no number on the coach.

leaves.title: The postgame injury update
leaves.criterion: Every injury event in the game appears on the list. Preliminary category and final category disagree at the configured rate over a season.

leaves.title: The postgame news conference
leaves.criterion: Every game has a postgame session unless the user chooses to skip it, and a skip writes a policy violation event. Every question cites a real event from that game's record.

leaves.title: First notes before the film
leaves.criterion: No field on the notes screen comes from assignment grades. Tagged plays open first in the next film session.

leaves.title: The day after: day off, corrections, and travel home
leaves.criterion: Choosing the day off removes the Monday corrections block, adds the Wednesday 45-minute session, and adds the recovery effect once. A third Victory Monday within 4 weeks gives 0.36 of the first morale gain. No week the game builds has zero player days off in a calendar week. After a Thursday game the next three days are days off. On a short week the day-off choice is not shown.

leaves.title: Plays sent to the league office
leaves.criterion: A tenth play in one week is refused. The Thursday video arrives for every club in every regular-season week. Over 1,000 sent plays, the share of "incorrect" replies matches the share of true missed or wrong calls among sent plays within the office error. No reply changes a result or shows an engine number.

leaves.title: Grading the game film
leaves.criterion: Every player who took a snap has a staff grade for every snap he played, unless grading was dropped for a short week. With a coach of high observation quality the staff grade matches the engine result more often than with a low one, over 10,000 player-snaps. No grade screen shows engine truth outside the coaching school.

leaves.title: Postgame record
leaves.criterion: Replaying the event log reproduces the same postgame record. A revised injury category appears as a new linked row and the first row is unchanged. Internal fields never appear in a media item without a leak event.

leaves.title: Booth and field assignments
leaves.criterion: Every job on the list has an owner or a visible "unfilled" warning before kickoff. Moving a coach from field to booth changes his note delay and removes him from bench meetings.

leaves.title: Headset channels
leaves.criterion: A note sent on the defense channel is not delivered in full to a user listening to offense. Only the link owner can speak to the radio player.

leaves.title: Voices on the channel
leaves.criterion: With five undisciplined test coaches on a channel and no talk rule, median AI call time is later than with a one-helper rule.

leaves.title: The personnel caller
leaves.criterion: Over a simulated season the too-many-men and illegal substitution foul rate falls inside the calibration band. Teams with a low-skill personnel caller have a higher rate than teams with a high-skill one.

leaves.title: Kicking-unit alerts
leaves.criterion: On every fourth down in a test game the alerted unit matches the decision book's default for that situation.

leaves.title: The depth card in use
leaves.criterion: After an injury, a unit's lineup uses the new man only once that unit has been told. With a perfect-skill holder the delay is at the minimum.

leaves.title: Dealing with officials
leaves.criterion: No argument path changes a judgment call. A coach flagged twice for unsportsmanlike conduct is disqualified.

leaves.title: The restricted zone and the get-back coach
leaves.criterion: The bench-area limit in the field model equals the 27-yard lines for the pro rule set. A team with a get-back coach has fewer sideline fouls over 1,000 simulated games.

leaves.title: Talk budgets during stoppages
leaves.criterion: The user can never take more actions in a stoppage than its slots. Slots are identical for the user and AI coaches in the same role.

leaves.title: Weather delays
leaves.criterion: After a delay the game state (down, distance, spot, clock, timeouts) equals the state before it. Fatigue values are lower than before it.

leaves.title: Headset failure on the coaches' channels
leaves.criterion: While the channel is down no booth note is delivered. With a fallback plan the first call after the failure is made by the named field coach.

leaves.title: Operation record
leaves.criterion: Every too-many-men foul and every timeout spent on a personnel problem appears with an owner.

leaves.title: Game-day rule-breaking acts
leaves.criterion: Every act in the table can be taken from its screen. Each off-field act writes exactly one violation row. Over 1,000 simulated seasons, AI acts fall as `rule_respect` rises.

leaves.title: Call cycle timeline
leaves.criterion: 1. With a default huddle call confirmed at 25 s on the play clock, the offense is set with 8 to 14 s left in at least 95% of trials. 2. The latest-call marker moves earlier when a longer call or a substitution is selected. 3. Stage timestamps appear in the play record for every snap.

leaves.title: The decision window is real time
leaves.criterion: 1. No game setting changes the rate at which the play clock runs while the user decides. 2. For any call, play clock used in stage 2 equals wall-clock time between situation shown and call confirmed, within one frame. 3. Slow or paused calling is reachable only from practice tools and the coaching school. (The earlier three-mode acceptance test is retired.)

leaves.title: Late calls and their cost
leaves.criterion: A call confirmed at 2 s on the play clock from a huddle always produces a timeout or a delay foul. The standing instruction "never burn a timeout to save 5 yards" is honoured. In a 20,000-snap test, pass plays snapped with 5 s or less on the play clock have lower average EPA than pass plays snapped with 10 s or more, and run plays show no difference beyond noise.

leaves.title: The situation strip
leaves.criterion: Every field updates within one frame of the dead-ball record. A coach reading it aloud would say the situation correctly.

leaves.title: Automatic jump to the situation box
leaves.criterion: For a table of 50 game states and a sample sheet, the focused box matches the expected box in every case.

leaves.title: What is known about the defense before the call
leaves.criterion: No screen available before the snap exposes the defensive call. The tendency line's numbers equal the scouting database values for the bucket.

leaves.title: Calling from the sheet
leaves.criterion: A sheet call can be selected and confirmed in under 2 s by keyboard. The call object validates against the schema in P3.

leaves.title: Tags and changes at the line of the call
leaves.criterion: Every tag offered produces a play that passes the formation and eligibility checks in B4.

leaves.title: Personnel and substitution with the call
leaves.criterion: A call whose personnel differs from the field produces the right substitutes, and the defense's matching window opens.

leaves.title: The opening script
leaves.criterion: The script advances only when a scripted play is called. Leaving and returning keeps the position.

leaves.title: Calling a play that is not on the sheet
leaves.criterion: Search returns results within 100 ms for a 500-play book.

leaves.title: The next-call queue
leaves.criterion: With entries queued for three second-down boxes, the entry for the box that occurs is preselected within one frame of the dead-ball record, and the other two are cleared. A queued call is never sent without a confirm unless the auto-send option is on.

leaves.title: Setting up third down
leaves.criterion: The three shares for any call equal the stored results table for that play. The strip shows no value derived from the opponent's actual call on this snap.

leaves.title: Relay methods
leaves.criterion: A radio call confirmed after the cutoff time does not arrive by radio. A wristband call takes the same time regardless of call length.

leaves.title: Call length
leaves.criterion: The displayed length equals the sum of token costs for every play on a sample sheet. Calling the same play by wristband number shortens the relay by the difference, less the look-down time.

leaves.title: Tempo
leaves.criterion: Average seconds of game clock used per play differs by tempo in the expected order: hurry-up, no-huddle, huddle, slow.

leaves.title: Radio failure and loss of the radio player
leaves.criterion: While either team's total failure is active, no call by either team uses radio. A team with installed signals has a smaller added delay than a team without. Events replay identically from the seed.

leaves.title: Signal security
leaves.criterion: Against a test opponent with reading skill and no signal changes, the defense's anticipation of signalled calls rises over a game. With a dummy signaller it rises more slowly. No in-game action records opponent signals with a device unless the user confirms the L8.2.5 warning, and each such action writes one violation row.

leaves.title: Packaged calls: kill, alert, can
leaves.criterion: With a perfect-reading test quarterback and no disguise, the correct play runs every time the trigger is unambiguous.

leaves.title: Quarterback freedom
leaves.criterion: With freedom at none, the quarterback never changes the play or protection in 1,000 test snaps.

leaves.title: Snap count and cadence instruction
leaves.criterion: Hard counts raise both defensive offside and own false start rates above their base rates in a 10,000-snap test.

leaves.title: Pairs judged from the sideline (check with me)
leaves.criterion: 1. An `SL` pair with no key press runs play A and logs "no choice". 2. With a test defense that never disguises, the look shown equals the alignment at the snap. 3. The time between "set" and "snap" on `SL` pairs is longer than on single calls by the configured amount, in a 1,000-play log. 4. No quarterback attribute appears in the trigger result for an `SL` pair.

leaves.title: Coordinator and booth suggestions
leaves.criterion: The suggestion is always a legal call from the sheet or the playbook.

leaves.title: Delegating the play calling
leaves.criterion: A full game can be played with zero user play calls, and every call in the log is attributed to the coordinator.

leaves.title: Keyboard layout and speed training
leaves.criterion: Any play on the sheet can be called in at most 3 key presses. The drill reports median time to call by situation.

leaves.title: The head coach who does not call: channels and overrides
leaves.criterion: With the user off the offense channel, no coordinator call text is displayed before the snap. An override confirmed with less time left than its cost produces a late-call result. Ten overrides in a game lower coordinator trust more than one.

leaves.title: Call record
leaves.criterion: Replaying a game from its event log reproduces identical call records.

leaves.title: Defensive call timeline
leaves.criterion: 1. Against a huddle offense, a call confirmed 12 s after the dead ball reaches all defenders before the snap in at least 95% of trials. 2. A call confirmed after the marker produces at least one defender on the default call. 3. Stage timestamps exist for every defensive snap.

leaves.title: Matching personnel
leaves.criterion: 1. For a table of 30 offensive group and situation pairs, the highlighted defensive group equals the matching table row. 2. With the offense substituting, no snap occurs inside the protected window. 3. With the offense not substituting and hurry-up tempo, a defensive substitution produces a foul or a short-handed snap at a measurable rate.

leaves.title: Late and missing calls
leaves.criterion: With no call and no timeout, all eleven play the group's default call. In a forced partial-call test, mixed assignments appear in the play record.

leaves.title: What the defensive caller knows
leaves.criterion: No screen before the snap exposes the offensive call. Tendency numbers equal the scouting database values.

leaves.title: Automatic jump on the defensive sheet
leaves.criterion: For 50 test states the focused box equals the expected box.

leaves.title: The defensive call object
leaves.criterion: Every call on a sample sheet validates against the P3 schema and passes the eleven-man and coverage-completeness checks. A sheet call takes under 2 s by keyboard.

leaves.title: Pressure timing and sequencing
leaves.criterion: In a test where the user blitzes on 100% of third and long, the AI offense's screen and quick-game rate in that bucket rises over the game compared with a 30% blitz rate.

leaves.title: Matchup rules
leaves.criterion: With a travel rule on, corner A aligns on receiver X on every man-call snap where both are on the field. With a bracket on, the vacated zone named in the panel is empty in the play record.

leaves.title: Disguise instruction
leaves.criterion: Over 5,000 snaps, quarterback pre-snap identification accuracy is lower with default shell than with show it, and average defender distance from assignment at the snap is higher.

leaves.title: The check package
leaves.criterion: With a perfect-recognition test unit, every check fires when its condition is met. With low-recognition players, missed checks appear at a rate that falls as knowledge rises.

leaves.title: Defending tempo
leaves.criterion: Against hurry-up, a tempo-menu call reaches all eleven defenders before the snap in at least 95% of trials. A full-length call does not.

leaves.title: Freedom of the signal caller
leaves.criterion: At the lowest level the signal caller never changes a call in 1,000 test snaps beyond its listed checks.

leaves.title: Defensive relay
leaves.criterion: With both radio players out, no defensive call uses radio. A signal call's arrival time does not depend on call length.

leaves.title: Radio failure and both radio players out
leaves.criterion: With both designated defenders out of the game, no defensive call uses radio for the remainder, and no third player is ever given the speaker. During an outage a call with no installed signal and no band number either arrives by messenger timing or falls back to the default call. One failure event sets the radio state for offense and defense together.

leaves.title: Situational defensive menus
leaves.criterion: Every listed situation has a box rule in the default sheet template. An empty box produces a warning in the week and on game day.

leaves.title: Coordinator suggestions and delegating the defense
leaves.criterion: A full game can be played with zero user defensive calls and every call attributed to the coordinator.

leaves.title: Defensive call record
leaves.criterion: Replaying a game from its event log reproduces identical defensive call records. Every defensive snap has all eight time fields or a null with a reason (for example no radio sent because the relay was a signal). A partial-call snap always lists at least one defender not on the call.

leaves.title: Kicking-unit alert and fourth-down handoff
leaves.criterion: With a pre-commit, the kicking unit is set with at least 10 s on a 40 s clock in 95% of trials. A reversal after the unit starts leaves under 8 s or produces a foul or timeout in a measurable share of trials.

leaves.title: Field goal range in today's conditions
leaves.criterion: Over 10,000 simulated kicks, realised make rate inside each displayed band is within the band's stated range for a perfect-skill coordinator.

leaves.title: Field goal operation and the rushed kick
leaves.criterion: With 14 s left, a running clock, and a practised unit, the kick gets off in a minority of trials. With 20 s it gets off in at least 90%.

leaves.title: Field goal defense: block or safe
leaves.criterion: Block rate and kicker-foul rate are both higher under block than under safe in a 10,000-kick test.

leaves.title: Punt type and direction
leaves.criterion: In simulation, average hang time, gross distance, return rate, and touchback rate differ by type in the expected directions.

leaves.title: Punt protection and the gunners
leaves.criterion: Block rate falls and average return yards rise under protect first.

leaves.title: Returner rules
leaves.criterion: A perfect-judgment returner never fields a punt inside the user's "let it go" line. After first touching by the kicking team, a receiving-team recovery and fumble still leaves the receivers with the ball at the first-touch spot.

leaves.title: Rush, return, or punt safe
leaves.criterion: Fake success rate against punt safe is lower than against return or rush in a 5,000-trial test.

leaves.title: Kickoff type under the dynamic format
leaves.criterion: Each row of the result table is reproduced by the rule engine in a scripted test. Aiming deeper raises the touchback share and aiming shorter raises the short-kick share.

leaves.title: Onside kick
leaves.criterion: The onside option is available at every free kick. The receiving team always gets the declaration before aligning.

leaves.title: Kickoff return rules
leaves.criterion: A perfect-judgment returner downs a bounced ball in the end zone whenever the model's expected return is short of the 20.

leaves.title: Hands team
leaves.criterion: Recovery rate for the receiving team is higher with the hands team than with the regular unit.

leaves.title: Safety kick
leaves.criterion: The rule engine offers all three kick types and applies the 20-yard kick line.

leaves.title: Fair catch kick
leaves.criterion: The option appears after every fair catch within range and never otherwise. Kick distance excludes snap depth.

leaves.title: Calling a fake
leaves.criterion: A fake called against punt safe succeeds less often than the same fake against a return call.

leaves.title: The special teams sheet and coordinator rules
leaves.criterion: A full game can be played with every kicking call delegated and each head coach decision still presented to the user.

leaves.title: Kicking-play record
leaves.criterion: Replaying the event log reproduces identical records.

leaves.title: Decision prompts and their clock
leaves.criterion: Every decision type listed in this file produces a prompt in a scripted game. Timer expiry applies the standing instruction, else the default, and logs which.

leaves.title: The advisor line
leaves.criterion: With a perfect-skill analyst the recommended option equals the model's best option in every non-close state of a 500-state test set.

leaves.title: Go, kick, or punt
leaves.criterion: League-wide AI go rate by distance band over 10 simulated seasons is within 3 percentage points of the measured rates. Each option leads to the correct next screen.

leaves.title: One point or two
leaves.criterion: For the four classic cases above with league-average rates, the advisor recommends the option stated. The try never consumes game clock.

leaves.title: Clock state and the arithmetic panel
leaves.criterion: For 40 scripted dead-ball states the display's next-start line matches the rule engine. The burn estimate is within 5 s of simulated kneel-down sequences.

leaves.title: Two-minute offense
leaves.criterion: A practised unit gets a spike off within 18 s of an inbounds tackle in 90% of trials. A spike attempt from shotgun is flagged as grounding by the rule engine.

leaves.title: Four-minute offense
leaves.criterion: Average game clock used per play in four-minute mode is higher than in normal huddle tempo by at least 5 s.

leaves.title: Victory formation
leaves.criterion: For a grid of clock, down, and timeout states, "can kneel it out" appears exactly when a scripted kneel sequence ends the game.

leaves.title: The defense's clock
leaves.criterion: The saved-time figure is within 3 s of the simulated outcome.

leaves.title: The timeout ledger
leaves.criterion: The rule engine refuses a second timeout by the same team in one dead-ball period. The ledger total equals timeouts charged.

leaves.title: Icing the kicker
leaves.criterion: Icing changes make rate by no more than 2 percentage points in a 20,000-kick test.

leaves.title: The coach's challenge
leaves.criterion: The third challenge is available exactly when at least one of the first two succeeded. No challenge is offered in a booth-only situation. Over a season, the share of user challenges won rises with replay assistant skill.

leaves.title: Booth reviews and replay assist
leaves.criterion: Every scoring play and turnover passes through the review check.

leaves.title: Accept or decline
leaves.criterion: For 60 scripted foul situations the options shown equal the rule engine's legal set.

leaves.title: Ten-second runoff choices
leaves.criterion: Each branch of Rule 4-7 in the rules reference has a scripted test that produces the right options.

leaves.title: Deliberate fouls and the intentional safety
leaves.criterion: The intentional safety option appears in a scripted state (leading by 4 to 7, fourth down inside own 3, under 20 s) and not when trailing.

leaves.title: End-of-half sequence
leaves.criterion: The staff line's "plays possible" is within one play of the simulated result in 90% of scripted end-of-half states.

leaves.title: Last-play situations
leaves.criterion: Both sheets always have a call in focus when one play remains, or a warning that the box is empty.

leaves.title: Overtime toss and plan
leaves.criterion: Scripted overtime games reproduce each numbered rule. A tie is recorded when the regular-season period ends level.

leaves.title: Resting starters and pulling the quarterback
leaves.criterion: The prompt appears at the threshold. Rested players take no snaps until re-entered.

leaves.title: Game management record
leaves.criterion: Every prompt shown in a game has exactly one record. Replaying the event log reproduces identical records.

leaves.title: On-field medical emergency and the suspended game
leaves.criterion: 1. A resumed game restores possession, spot, down, distance, period, time, and player eligibility exactly. 2. In 10,000 simulated seasons no imported real person receives a life-threatening event. 3. The college flow offers exactly the four Rule 3-3-3-c outcomes, and a tie after four periods. 4. No screen during the stoppage shows a replay or a close view. 5. The user's answers change trust values and never change the player's medical outcome.

leaves.title: Lineup resolution for each snap
leaves.criterion: 1. For 200 test snaps with random injuries and fatigue, every lineup has eleven distinct, available players. 2. No lineup ever contains an inactive or disqualified player. 3. Every non-first-choice player in a lineup carries a reason code.

leaves.title: Substitution cost and the match window
leaves.criterion: An offensive substitution before the two-minute warning always opens a match window. The same substitution after the two-minute warning in a running-clock series does not. A quick snap that produces twelve defenders results in a replayed down and a logged warning.

leaves.title: Rotation rules and pitch counts
leaves.criterion: With a 25-snap pitch count and no override, the player never takes snap 26. With a "every third series" rule, the second back starts series 3, 6, and 9. Snap counts in the panel equal the play record.

leaves.title: Defensive line waves
leaves.criterion: Over a simulated season with default waves, the ranked defensive line shares fall within 5 points of the I6.2.5 targets for ranks 1 to 6. In a simulated 12-play no-huddle drive without offensive substitution, the same defensive line plays every snap and its fatigue at the end is higher than in a huddle drive of 12 plays with wave changes.

leaves.title: Fatigue-driven substitution
leaves.criterion: A player forced below his floor with a backup available is absent from the next lineup. He returns only after reaching floor plus margin. A "stays in" mark keeps him on the field.

leaves.title: Snap ceilings from the medical staff
leaves.criterion: Playing a player past a medical stop happens only after the L8.2.5 warning is confirmed and writes one violation row. Each request to extend is in the decision log with the answer.

leaves.title: Snap-share targets from real games
leaves.criterion: The calibration run reports each cell's simulated mean beside the table and fails any cell outside its tolerance. The table values are stored as data with their source and status, not typed into code.

leaves.title: Injury replacement by the depth card chain
leaves.criterion: After an injury to a player with N roles, all N roles have a new available first choice or a visible "no backup" flag before the next snap. With no user input the planned chain is applied. No player is placed in two spots of one unit.

leaves.title: The injured player sits one down
leaves.criterion: A test table of 12 injury-timeout cases (before and after the two-minute warning, with and without timeouts left, with and without an opponent's foul) gives the rule's result in every case.

leaves.title: Concussion evaluation removes a player
leaves.criterion: No user input changes an evaluation's length or result. A player with a no-go sign appears in a later lineup that game only after the L8.2.5 warning is confirmed, which writes one violation row and raises the spotter's stop chance.

leaves.title: Disqualified and suspended players
leaves.criterion: A disqualified player is in no later lineup. A suspended player is absent for at least one snap.

leaves.title: The backup quarterback and the reduced sheet
leaves.criterion: Over a simulated league season the share of team games in which a second quarterback plays 10% or more of snaps is between 10% and 17%. On a quarterback change the sheet view changes within one frame. Every dimmed play has readiness below the line. Calling a dimmed play applies its true readiness.

leaves.title: Emergency third quarterback entry
leaves.criterion: With one healthy active quarterback the emergency quarterback cannot be placed in any lineup. While he plays, calls with a direct snap to another player fail validation.

leaves.title: Hot hand and matchup substitutions
leaves.criterion: "Feature" puts the player in every later lineup whose package has his position. No attribute changes when an override is set.

leaves.title: Benching a player during the game
leaves.criterion: A benched player is in no later lineup that game. The reason is stored and shown in the postgame questions.

leaves.title: Substitution record
leaves.criterion: Summing counted rows per player equals the snap counts shown in the box score, and each share uses his unit's counted snaps as the base. Replaying the event log reproduces the same rows.

leaves.title: The live view and its limits
leaves.criterion: No pixel or label in the live view derives from assignment data or the opponent's call object. In every game the view follows the seat, and no setting changes it. In the field seat, no label is drawn between the snap and the whistle, and a safety at 14 yards is drawn at the fixed depth line until his play's picture arrives.

leaves.title: The play-result reveal
leaves.criterion: The result line for 500 sample plays contains no field taken from assignment grades or the opponent's call.

leaves.title: Booth reports and their delay
leaves.criterion: Over 1,000 notes from an assistant with recognition skill at the scale midpoint, the share of true notes falls inside the configured band. No note about play N is shown before play N ends.

leaves.title: Booth pre-snap alerts
leaves.criterion: No alert spoken after the 15-second mark changes the quarterback's behaviour on that snap.

leaves.title: Medical and position-coach reports
leaves.criterion: Every injury produces a first report before the next snap when the trainers saw it, and within one stoppage otherwise. A revised report replaces the earlier one in the panel and both are kept in the record. Over a season about 30% of first words are revised.

leaves.title: Sideline tablets: stills and clips
leaves.criterion: With tablet mode "stills" no moving picture is available on the sideline. No tablet screen contains a recommended call. A picture of play N is never available before play N ends.

leaves.title: Equipment failure and the equity rule
leaves.criterion: While class 2 is active for either team, no call by either team uses the radio relay. Failure events replay identically from the seed.

leaves.title: Stat sheet and in-game charting
leaves.criterion: Our-call counts equal the call records exactly. Opponent counts differ from engine truth at the charter's configured error rate over a season. No percentage is shown for fewer than 3 plays. At a level whose rule set bars analytics on game-day devices (college), the dashboard half is replaced by paper charting with the same errors and a 2-play delay (Assumption (design tuning) (design tuning)).

leaves.title: Replay assistant feed
leaves.criterion: Advice never arrives after the next snap. Over many trials the share of correct advice matches the skill setting.

leaves.title: One conversation at a time
leaves.criterion: With attention on the offense channel, no full defensive booth note is displayed until the user switches. Urgent items always display. During a player conversation no headset note is shown in full.

leaves.title: Information state record
leaves.criterion: For any decision in a saved game, review can list every message shown before it and none shown after.

leaves.title: Unit benches
leaves.criterion: The user can be in at most one bench meeting at any moment. A meeting cut short applies only the fixes completed before the unit went back on.

leaves.title: What can be fixed between series
leaves.criterion: No adjustment creates an object that fails validation in G1 or G2. A third structural change in one series lowers the uptake of all three. Day-only edits are gone from the saved playbook after the game.

leaves.title: Finding the problem
leaves.criterion: With a perfect-skill test staff every listed problem matches an engine-truth cause. With a low-skill staff at least the configured share do not. No truth label is visible during the game. With a diagnostic parameter of 1.0, at least 85 percent of listed items name the true cause in a 1,000-series test; with 0.0, at most 35 percent do (the rule 2 values). No panel ever shows more than 6 items.

leaves.title: How well players carry out a change
leaves.criterion: In a 10,000-snap test the mental error rate on an adjusted rule is higher for an unpracticed re-point than for a practiced contingency, and both exceed the rate for the base rule.

leaves.title: The halftime clock
leaves.criterion: The sum of minutes spent on halftime items never exceeds working minutes. Changing the rule-set halftime length changes working minutes by the same amount.

leaves.title: Staff huddle first, players second
leaves.criterion: The user cannot give full attention to both sides' staff phases. The total cost of chosen items never exceeds the phase length.

leaves.title: Second-half openers
leaves.criterion: The second-half script appears in the script slot on the first offensive snap of the third quarter and advances only when a scripted call is used.

leaves.title: Kicking lines, the decision book, and crossing plays off
leaves.criterion: After a halftime line change, the fourth-down advisor in the second half uses the new line.

leaves.title: Adjustment record
leaves.criterion: Every day-only edit made during a game has exactly one adjustment row. A test adjustment aimed at the true tagged cause and carried out on every later snap grades yes, yes, and 1.0 executed.

leaves.title: Overhead film view
leaves.criterion: At default zoom all 22 markers are inside the frame at the snap for every formation in the test set. Team colours pass the 3:1 contrast check or the game swaps to the alternate pair. Measured on-screen distances match J1 coordinates within one pixel at any zoom.

leaves.title: Marker playback from engine positions
leaves.criterion: For any saved play, marker positions at each displayed tick equal the stored trajectory. No cue appears at a time or place with no matching event in the play's event list. Playback at each speed ends within one frame of trajectory length divided by speed.

leaves.title: Real time across the whole game
leaves.criterion: No game setting or input stops or slows a running play clock or decision timer. A scripted test that confirms each call after exactly 10 s of wall-clock time shows 10 s of play clock used in stage 2 on every snap.

leaves.title: Stoppage compression
leaves.criterion: A player in evaluation for 10 simulated minutes becomes available at the same game-clock point whether or not stoppages are compressed. No stoppage card offers more slots than I11.5.1 gives.

leaves.title: Replay during the game
leaves.criterion: In a game the last play can be replayed once and no earlier play can be replayed. The play clock does not stop during the replay.

leaves.title: Overlays and what they may show
leaves.criterion: An automated check finds no reference to opponent call objects or assignment grades in any overlay available before the final whistle. Every overlay source carries the "user-visible" tag. A booth-label overlay text equals the booth note text exactly.

leaves.title: Delegated possessions and skipping ahead
leaves.criterion: No decision prompt owned by the user is ever auto-resolved by a skip unless a standing instruction covers it (I1.4.3). Every play that meets a stop rule halts the skip before the snap. The game clock and fatigue at the end of a summarised drive equal those of the same drive watched.

leaves.title: Presentation settings record
leaves.criterion: Every saved game has a settings block. No stored item changes whether a game can be certified. For every decision, the seat recorded in its information state (I7.6.1) matches the settings block at that game-clock time.

leaves.title: Field frame
leaves.criterion: 1. Converting any spot to a yard-line name and back returns the same `x` within 0.01 yd. 2. A field goal kicked from the centre of the field straight down the `x` axis passes through the middle of the uprights. 3. No engine module contains a literal field dimension. A search of the code for `53.3`, `23.58`, or `120` finds only tests. 4. The same play run under the pro and college rule sets from a hash spot starts from different `y` values, and the field and boundary widths differ accordingly.

leaves.title: Play frame
leaves.criterion: 1. `toField(toPlay(p))` equals `p` exactly for any representable point. 2. The same play called at the west 20 and the east 20, with the same seed streams and with wind and sun switched off (J12), produces trajectories that are identical in the play frame. With wind on, the two differ only through the wind's effect on the ball (J9).

leaves.title: Field landmarks as data
leaves.criterion: Every landmark name used in any shipped play resolves to a point inside the field. A lint step fails the content build otherwise.

leaves.title: Units
leaves.criterion: Type names or field suffixes carry the unit (`speedYps`, `distYd`, `tSec`). A lint rule rejects a kinematic field without a unit suffix.

leaves.title: Number representation
leaves.criterion: A 1,000-play golden file produces identical record hashes on the desktop build and the browser build.

leaves.title: Ticks and sub-steps
leaves.criterion: 1. Halving the tick to 0.05 s in a test build, with movement parameters refitted by J2.2.1 for the new sub-step, changes league-level calibration outputs (J15) by less than the tolerance bands. This proves results do not hang on the step size. 2. A runner crossing the goal line between two ticks is ruled across at the interpolated time, not the next tick.

leaves.title: Sim time, play clock, and game clock
leaves.criterion: The play simulation's code has no write access to the game clock type. A unit test confirms a play that starts with 0:01 left runs to its natural end.

leaves.title: Player body state
leaves.criterion: The state validates against the P3 schema on every tick in debug builds. Trajectory size for a 6 s play is under 40 kB uncompressed.

leaves.title: Ball state
leaves.criterion: A property test over 100,000 random plays finds no tick with the ball in zero or two states, and no `held` state without exactly one player with `hasBall`.

leaves.title: Officials as observers
leaves.criterion: One official track per crew member exists for every play record (seven under the pro rule set).

leaves.title: Geometry helpers
leaves.criterion: Unit tests cover each function with hand-computed cases, including coincident and collinear points. No function allocates in the per-tick path (verified by a benchmark with allocation counting).

leaves.title: Boundaries and planes
leaves.criterion: For a table of 40 hand-built boundary cases (taken from the approved rulings in the rulebook where they exist), the event order matches the expected order.

leaves.title: Play simulation interface
leaves.criterion: The function has no imports from interface, storage, or time modules (enforced by the module boundary lint in P1). Calling it twice with the same input returns byte-identical results.

leaves.title: Truth record and trajectory record
leaves.criterion: Replaying a stored trajectory draws the same film on any build. The information filter test (K9) confirms scouting code cannot read hidden fields.

leaves.title: The reference resolver
leaves.criterion: A season simulated with the resolver lands inside the J15 tolerance bands for plays per game, completion rate, yards per carry, and points per game. A build flag proves the shipped game's season loop cannot call it.

leaves.title: Committed fouls as events
leaves.criterion: 1. Every `FoulCommitted` event has a trigger that can be shown on the trajectory. 2. With B11's detection model applied, league called-foul rates by type land inside J15 tolerance. 3. Raising every player's foul discipline (D4.2.2) on one team by 10 ISS (1 z) lowers that team's committed fouls in a 500-game test. Setting `team_discipline` to its best bound changes only the hazards L3.4.1 names, and by no more than those bounds allow.

leaves.title: Offensive holding
leaves.criterion: Holding rate per pass block rises sharply as the matchup gap grows beyond 1 z against the blocker. League called rate lands in the J15 band.

leaves.title: Illegal blocks: in the back, below the waist, chop, crackback
leaves.criterion: Illegal block fouls occur mostly on returns and long runs in the simulated distribution, and the league rate lands in its band.

leaves.title: Ineligible downfield and illegal touching
leaves.criterion: With a decision time of 1.5 s on a run-pass option the foul is rare. At 2.5 s it is common. Under the college key the same play draws fewer fouls.

leaves.title: Defensive pass interference, holding, and illegal contact
leaves.criterion: Interference rate per deep target is several times the rate per short target. Defenders who located the ball commit far fewer. League called rates land in J15 bands.

leaves.title: Offensive pass interference and illegal picks
leaves.criterion: Rub concepts thrown into man coverage near the goal line draw this foul at a higher rate than any other concept family.

leaves.title: Roughing the passer and late hits
leaves.criterion: Roughing rate per quarterback hit falls with rusher discipline, and the league called rate lands in the J15 band.

leaves.title: Dangerous contact: helmet contact, defenseless players, face mask, horse collar, targeting
leaves.criterion: Under the college rule set targeting ejections occur at a per-game rate inside the T12 band once sourced. Under the pro set the targeting hazard never fires.

leaves.title: Fouls on kicks: running into or roughing the kicker or holder, and kick catch interference
leaves.criterion: In a controlled punt-rush test, running into the kicker is several times more frequent than roughing, and an all-out block call raises both. League called rates land in J15 bands once those rows are measured.

leaves.title: Unsportsmanlike conduct, taunting, and fighting
leaves.criterion: League rates land in J15 bands. A team whose players have the league's lowest foul discipline and composure draws well above the league rate. With the same players, moving `team_discipline.post_play` from its best to its worst bound raises the team's rate by no more than that ratio (about 16%).

leaves.title: Exposures and the hazard
leaves.criterion: 1. Team-season "Out" episodes average near the target with a realistic spread between teams (some seasons of 8, some of 25). 2. Injuries per snap rise with fatigue above 0.7 and with load excess in controlled tests. 3. Position shares of injuries are plausible against a sourced table once one exists.

leaves.title: Wear without injury
leaves.criterion: Heavy-usage players show more Wednesday practice limitations than light-usage players at the same position across a simulated season.

leaves.title: Play continuation and the stoppage
leaves.criterion: An injury inside the final two minutes with no timeouts applies the rule set's runoff logic in J11 in every test case of a 20-case table.

leaves.title: Concussion evaluation and return within the game
leaves.criterion: No evaluated player re-enters before the evaluation's end tick. Diagnosed players are unavailable for the rest of the game in 100% of cases.

leaves.title: Game state object
leaves.criterion: Replaying a game's event list from the initial state reproduces the final state bit for bit. No field is mutated in place (enforced by frozen objects in debug builds).

leaves.title: Phases and transitions
leaves.criterion: A property test driving random legal events for 10,000 games never reaches an undefined (phase, event) pair. A table of 60 scripted sequences (including untimed downs, safeties, defensive scores on tries, and overtime) ends in the expected states.

leaves.title: Dead-ball detection inside the play
leaves.criterion: Under the college key a runner who slips untouched is down at the slip. Under the pro key he may get up and run.

leaves.title: Spotting, down, and distance
leaves.criterion: For a table of 80 results including penalties, the next down, distance, and spot match hand-worked answers checked against rulebook approved rulings where those exist.

leaves.title: Game clock
leaves.criterion: 1. A 50-case table of clock situations (taken from the rule text's cases) produces the expected clock status and restart trigger. 2. Simulated games average the J15 plays per game and elapsed time per play within tolerance, as an emergent result of tempo choices and these rules.

leaves.title: Play clock
leaves.criterion: In hurry-up after a 20-yard completion in bounds, the earliest possible snap is limited by the spotting delay, not by the offense's readiness.

leaves.title: Recovery, substitution window, and sideline updates
leaves.criterion: A player below his fatigue threshold is replaced at the next dead ball when a substitute exists and the tempo allows substitution. Snap counts in D14 equal the count of plays each player appears in.

leaves.title: Prompting coaches
leaves.criterion: Every request type has a default and a deadline. A game can be completed with the user answering nothing (all defaults and delegations).

leaves.title: Scores and what follows
leaves.criterion: Scripted sequences for each score type, including a defensive two-point return and a penalty carried to the kickoff, end with the correct score and spot.

leaves.title: Period changes and halftime
leaves.criterion: After a quarter change the offense attacks the opposite goal from the mirrored spot with the same down and distance.

leaves.title: Overtime
leaves.criterion: Scripted overtime games under each format (pro regular season, pro postseason, college) end by the correct rule in each of 10 cases per format.

leaves.title: Play-by-play, drives, and statistics
leaves.criterion: The project's calibration scripts (`research/nflverse_baselines.py` and `nflverse_gaps.py`) run unchanged against a simulated season's play-by-play export. Box score totals equal the sum of play-by-play credits.

leaves.title: Environment snapshot
leaves.criterion: 1. Every play input contains a valid snapshot. Indoor games show zero wind and dry conditions in 100% of cases. 2. A retractable roof's state never changes between T minus 90 and halftime, and changes at halftime only from closed to open under the policy key. 3. Every derived multiplier is a pure function of the snapshot fields (same snapshot, same multipliers), so replays reproduce them.

leaves.title: Pre-game weather draw
leaves.criterion: Over 1,000 simulated seasons, each venue's game-day temperature and wind distributions match its input normals. The forecast error shrinks monotonically toward game day.

leaves.title: In-game weather change
leaves.criterion: Changes occur only at quarter boundaries and are reproducible from the seed.

leaves.title: Wind field for a play
leaves.criterion: 1. Gust draws come from the `gust` stream, so changing the play call does not change the gust on that play (J13 counterfactual rule). 2. League calibration, outdoor games: completion over 15 mph is 1.5 to 4 points below games under 10 mph, and completion on passes of 20 or more air yards falls 2.5 to 6.5 points; extra point rate over 15 mph is 1.5 to 4.5 points below calm games. 3. With wind direction pooled as in the public data, the fitted field goal wind term lands between 0.3 and 1.0 yard of equivalent distance per 5 mph. With direction known, the simulated make rate into the wind is lower than with it at every distance over 40 yards.

leaves.title: Wet ball and grip
leaves.criterion: 1. In a controlled test, completion rate and drop rate move down from dry to heavy rain. 2. League calibration over outdoor games: completion in rain 2 to 4 points below dry, in snow 3.5 to 7.5 points below dry; interception rate within 0.4 points of dry; fumbles lost within 0.15 per 100 plays of dry (bands bracket both measured windows). 3. AI play callers raise the run share in rain by 1 to 4 points and in snow by 3 to 8 points without any direct rule forcing it (decision-driven).

leaves.title: Cold and heat
leaves.criterion: 1. Long field goal make rate is lower at 20 F than at 70 F with all else equal, and the drop is fully explained by the shorter carry in J9 (removing the distance term removes the drop). 2. League calibration: outdoor gross punt average at 32 F or colder is 2.5 to 4 yards below games above 69 F; outdoor completion at 32 F or colder is 1.5 to 4 points below games above 69 F; total points per game vary by less than 2 across the four temperature bins. 3. Fourth-quarter fatigue is higher at a 95 F heat index than at 60 F.

leaves.title: Surface type and condition
leaves.criterion: In a controlled test, separation on hard-breaking routes and pass-rush speed-move win rates fall on a muddy field, and power-run efficiency falls less than outside-zone efficiency.

leaves.title: Noise level by situation
leaves.criterion: 1. With noise as the main home effect, the simulated league home margin and home win rate land in the J15 band (J12.8.1 states the full composition). 2. Visiting offenses commit 20% to 50% more delay-of-game fouls per snap than home offenses; visiting defenses commit 10% to 30% more offside, neutral-zone, and encroachment fouls; offensive false starts differ by less than 8% between home and road (bands bracket the measured 36%, 19%, and 3% home excess). 3. With `noiseBase` set to 0 for every venue (an empty-stadium test like 2020), the delay-of-game and defensive pre-snap gaps fall to within 5% of even. 4. The home and road pre-snap split matches J5.7.1 with noise and the venue term together.

leaves.title: Thin air
leaves.criterion: 1. Mean kickoff distance and 50-plus field goal make rate are higher at 5,000 ft than at sea level with identical kickers. 2. Under the 2016 to 2023 kickoff rule set, the simulated touchback rate at a 5,280 ft outdoor venue is 15 to 30 points above the league outdoor rate (measured gap 22 points). 3. Simulated gross punt average at 5,280 ft is 1 to 3 yards above sea-level outdoor venues (measured 2.0). 4. Over 2,000 seasons, the second-half margin of a 5,280 ft home team exceeds its first-half margin by more than the league's home teams do (sign test only; size is a calibration report item, not a target, at 1 of 3).

leaves.title: Composition of home advantage
leaves.criterion: 1. Simulated home margin and home win rate land inside J15 bands for the pro set (and T12 bands for college). The residual term is below 50% of the total effect, or the calibration report flags it. 2. Empty-stadium test: with `noiseBase` 0 at every venue and everything else unchanged, the simulated home margin falls to within 0 to 1 point (the 2020 season measured 0.14 points and 50.4%). 3. Indoor home teams do not out-gain outdoor home teams at home by more than 0.5 points over a 2,000-season run.

leaves.title: Travel and rest
leaves.criterion: 1. In a 2,000-season test, the simulated margin effect of a short week when both teams are short is small (under 0.5 points against equal-rest Sunday games), consistent with the measured Thursday split. 2. A rest gap of 3 or more days moves the simulated margin by 0.5 to 2 points toward the rested team, produced only through D9 and D10 (measured raw swing about 1 to 1.5 points). 3. Pacific teams playing 1 p.m. Eastern road games show a margin within 1 point of their other road games (measured: no penalty). 4. No J or K module reads `tzCrossed` or `bodyClockKickoff` as a direct performance input (a lint or test checks it).

leaves.title: Algorithm and interface
leaves.criterion: Published test vectors for the chosen algorithm pass on all builds. A statistical test battery (uniformity, serial correlation on 10 million draws) passes. `normal()` over 10 million draws has mean within 0.001 of 0 and variance within 0.002 of 1.

leaves.title: Stream keys
leaves.criterion: 1. Changing only the offensive play call leaves the `weather`, `gust`, and opponent `coachAI` draws for that play identical (tested by logging raw draws). 2. Two contests between different pairs never share a key in 1 million generated keys (collision test on the catalogue's scope space). 3. Adding a new stream to the catalogue does not change any existing stream's output (keys include the stream name). 4. No key from the `resolver` stream equals any key of the full-engine play streams for the same game (tested on 1 million generated keys). (`distant` is retired and reserved.) 5. Decision-support estimates (I4 and K5 make chances, any shown or AI-used estimate) never draw from a live stream; they are computed without draws or from their own throwaway key, so asking for an estimate changes no game result.

leaves.title: Decision-time draws for AI and for players' choices
leaves.criterion: In certified mode the attempt index is always 0 and the option is disabled. Replaying a full game from the event log reproduces every AI call.

leaves.title: Math library
leaves.criterion: A file of 100,000 input values per function produces byte-identical outputs on every supported platform and build. Accuracy against a high-precision reference is within 1e-12 relative error.

leaves.title: Fixed step order
leaves.criterion: Simulating a league week with 1, 4, and 16 workers yields identical results for every game. A user game replayed from its event log on a machine ten times slower gives identical clocks and results.

leaves.title: Seed hierarchy
leaves.criterion: Two machines creating a world from the same seed and data pack produce identical teams, rosters, and schedules. Simulating season 3 before season 2's off-field events are fully processed is impossible by construction, and each season's generated class is identical whether reached by playing or by fast simulation with the same decisions.

leaves.title: Engine version and what is replayed against what
leaves.criterion: After an engine update, a save from the previous version loads, its past box scores are unchanged, and film of a past game plays identically. A certified game re-simulated on a second machine with matching hashes reproduces every play record.

leaves.title: Mid-play and mid-game saves
leaves.criterion: Save, quit, load, and continue produces the same game as continuing without saving, for 100 random save points.

leaves.title: Separating luck from decisions
leaves.criterion: For a fixed play input, the distribution from 200 attempts is stable (two independent sets of 200 differ in mean yards by less than sampling error allows). The simulated spread of game margins around expectation lands within the J15 band.

leaves.title: Running a game without display
leaves.criterion: 1. A game simulated headless and the same game stepped through the interface with AI answering every prompt produce identical event logs. 2. No code path in the engine checks whether a display is attached.

leaves.title: No level-of-detail shortcut
leaves.criterion: A build-time check proves the season loop cannot import the reference resolver at all. The calibration report shows the same league rates for headless and watched games. Every saved game, near or distant, is a full-engine game, and any distant game re-simulated from its stored inputs reproduces its saved result exactly.

leaves.title: Workers and ordering
leaves.criterion: A league week simulated with 1, 4, and 16 workers gives identical results and identical world state after commit (same test as J13.3.2). No ticker item appears before its scheduled kickoff time in the user's game clock mapping.

leaves.title: Spreading the work over the real week
leaves.criterion: In a scripted normal week (20 minutes of user activity between games), the user never sees a progress screen on the reference machine.

leaves.title: Retention tiers
leaves.criterion: Storage per season stays under the P6 budget on a world with both levels. Opening a tier D game from the current season produces full film whose event log matches the stored summary exactly.

leaves.title: Delegated and simulated user games
leaves.criterion: A fully simulated user game logs every decision with the acting staff member's id. With the same seed and inputs, "simulate to end" and "watch with everything delegated" give identical results.

leaves.title: Simulating weeks and seasons
leaves.criterion: Advancing a season in one request and advancing it week by week with the same policies produce identical world states.

leaves.title: One engine, two rule sets
leaves.criterion: With a talent gap of 2 z across the roster, the stronger team's win rate and average margin land inside the T12 bands once sourced, and no contest produces out-of-range values in 10,000 such games.

leaves.title: How much of the college world is simulated
leaves.criterion: The world-creation benchmark predicts weekly simulation time within 25% of the measured time in the first simulated week.

leaves.title: The batch harness
leaves.criterion: The project's analysis scripts run unchanged on a league-mode export. Any row of a batch result can be reproduced in full detail from its recorded seed.

leaves.title: Targets the engine must meet
leaves.criterion: The benchmark meets each target on the reference machine. Profiling shows no single J category above 40% of play time.

leaves.title: Target file format and status rules
leaves.criterion: Every number in this category appears in the pro file with status and definition. The loader rejects a `certify` target whose status is not Verified.

leaves.title: Tolerances and sample sizes
leaves.criterion: The harness computes every tolerance from the file with no hand-entered thresholds in code.

leaves.title: Order of tuning
leaves.criterion: The tuning log shows each stage's targets passing at the time it was frozen and at the end.

leaves.title: Scoring, margins, and results
leaves.criterion: All rows inside tolerance in a 10,000-game league run. The re-simulation SD is between 12.0 and 13.5 (widened from 13.2 because outside sources put the real value near 13.0. Assumption until the conflict is resolved).

leaves.title: Drives
leaves.criterion: All rows inside tolerance.

leaves.title: Down, distance, and field position
leaves.criterion: Anchor cells inside tolerance. Conversion rate decreases monotonically with distance in each down.

leaves.title: Passing efficiency and distribution
leaves.criterion: All rows inside tolerance. Interception rate rises monotonically with depth from 1 to 5 yards upward.

leaves.title: Pressure and rushers
leaves.criterion: Pressure rate strictly rises from 3 to 7 rushers. Sack rate rises from 3 to 5 rushers and is not lower at 6 than at 4. At 7 or more the sack rate is not required to rise: both sources show it falling (quick throws and hot routes), so a simulated rise at 7 is a fault to examine, not a pass. Levels inside tolerance of the primary definition.

leaves.title: Rushing efficiency and distribution
leaves.criterion: Quantiles and rates inside tolerance. Yards per carry falls monotonically as the box grows from 6 to 8.

leaves.title: Kicking game
leaves.criterion: All rows inside tolerance under the matching rule set.

leaves.title: Fouls
leaves.criterion: Each type inside tolerance (rare types at `watch` tier). The venue split's sign and approximate size reproduce.

leaves.title: Turnovers and injuries
leaves.criterion: Rows inside tolerance over 100 simulated seasons.

leaves.title: Personnel, formation, and coverage splits
leaves.criterion: Signs and ordering reproduce in league mode (man lower completion than zone, play action higher yards per attempt, Cover 1 lowest completion among the main shells). Levels inside `tune` tolerance.

leaves.title: Decision-response battery
leaves.criterion: Every direction holds at p < 0.001 in 20,000 trials per arm. No tested decision is free: each has a measurable cost somewhere.

leaves.title: AI behavior match
leaves.criterion: League means inside tolerance. No AI coach's fourth-down go rate falls outside the real observed team range once sourced.

leaves.title: Team-level spread and noise
leaves.criterion: Each row inside its band. A test swaps every team's head-coach profile between seasons and confirms the pre-snap foul year-to-year correlation changes by less than 0.03.

leaves.title: Report contents and release gate
leaves.criterion: The report regenerates byte-identically from the same build, parameters, and seeds. Certified mode (N4) refuses to start on a build without a passing report.

leaves.title: State update
leaves.criterion: 1. A player told to run a straight 40 yards from rest, with the pads factor set to 1.0, no start reaction, and dry footing, covers it in his true forty time within 0.03 s (J2.2.1). The recorded time on his card can differ by the D2.1.1 day noise. 2. No player ever exceeds his fresh top speed in any tick of a 10,000-play test.

leaves.title: Forward acceleration curve
leaves.criterion: For 20 sample players, simulated 10-yard and 40-yard times both match the times the conversion was fitted to, within 0.02 s.

leaves.title: Turning at speed
leaves.criterion: 1. Simulated three-cone and short-shuttle drill times for sample players match their listed times within 0.08 s (J2.7.1). 2. A pursuing defender with equal speed never catches a carrier who is running directly away from him. He does catch him when he has an angle that geometry says is sufficient.

leaves.title: Speed and acceleration from timed drills
leaves.criterion: For forty times from 4.25 to 5.40 s and realistic splits, the solver converges and the simulated straight-line sprint reproduces both inputs within 0.02 s.

leaves.title: Change of direction from drills and grades
leaves.criterion: Simulated drill times match listed times within 0.08 s for 95% of a 500-player test set.

leaves.title: Sprint and run
leaves.criterion: Covered by J2.1 tests.

leaves.title: Backpedal and transition
leaves.criterion: In a test with equal players, a receiver running a go route against off coverage with a 7-yard cushion is in phase with the corner (within 1 yd) at 30 yards. With a 3-yard cushion and a late transition the receiver is past him.

leaves.title: Shuffle, slide, and lateral flow
leaves.criterion: A tackle with average feet cannot reach the set point against an elite speed rusher's track without help in a scripted test. That gap is what the pass block contest (J6.2) then resolves.

leaves.title: Braking, stopping, and arriving
leaves.criterion: A player told to stop on a point from full speed stops within 0.3 yd of it.

leaves.title: In-play energy and its effect
leaves.criterion: A defensive tackle left on the field for 12 straight plays at hurry-up tempo shows a measurably lower pass-rush win rate on plays 10 to 12 than on plays 1 to 3 in a 5,000-drive test.

leaves.title: Seek, arrive, and path following
leaves.criterion: With no defenders, a receiver's break point on a 12-yard dig is within 0.5 yd of the drawn depth for all speed grades.

leaves.title: Pursue and intercept
leaves.criterion: In a scripted sideline run, a safety with a pursuit grade of 70 makes contact at least 3 yards sooner on average than an otherwise identical safety with a grade of 30.

leaves.title: Traffic and spacing
leaves.criterion: In 10,000 plays no two upright non-engaged players have centres closer than half the sum of their radii. Mesh against man coverage creates more separation than mesh against zone in a controlled test.

leaves.title: Momentum at contact
leaves.criterion: In a controlled test, average yards after contact rise with carrier weight and speed at contact, holding grades equal.

leaves.title: Drill reproduction tests
leaves.criterion: The suite passes for 100% of shipped players.

leaves.title: Game-speed comparison
leaves.criterion: Each compared figure falls inside the tolerance band set in J15 once the reference figures are sourced. Until then the comparison is reported, not enforced.

leaves.title: Perceived-state buffer
leaves.criterion: 1. With all delays forced to zero and full attention, perceived equals true for every entity (test mode). 2. With a 0.3 s delay, a defender's reaction to a scripted cut begins exactly 3 ticks after the cut. 3. The rule compiler rejects a rule that references a true-state field.

leaves.title: Field of view and attention
leaves.criterion: A zone defender facing the quarterback does not react to a receiver crossing behind him until a teammate's call arrives (J3.6) or the receiver enters his peripheral range.

leaves.title: Base reaction delay
leaves.criterion: In a 5,000-trial test, mean delay falls monotonically with play recognition and rises with fatigue above 0.7.

leaves.title: Run-pass key reading
leaves.criterion: 1. Against a plain inside zone run, league-average linebackers read run at a mean of 0.45 to 0.65 s after the snap (starting target, Assumption). 2. Against plain dropback pass, the same linebackers read pass and reach their zone landmarks on time in at least 90% of trials. 3. Raising `z_rec` by 1 lowers the false-read rate against play action (J3.3.1).

leaves.title: Anticipation
leaves.criterion: In a test where the offense runs the same route from the same look on 90% of snaps, interception and breakup rates rise against a defense given that tendency. They do not rise against a defense without it.

leaves.title: Play action
leaves.criterion: 1. League-wide, play action raises yards per attempt over non-play-action by an amount inside the J15 band, as an emergent result. 2. Linebacker depth at 1.0 s after the snap is shallower against play action than against straight dropback, and the difference shrinks as down and distance become more pass-obvious.

leaves.title: Misdirection and motion at the snap
leaves.criterion: A counter run gains more against defenders with low assignment discipline than high, holding other grades equal, in a 2,000-trial test.

leaves.title: What disguise does to the offense's perception
leaves.criterion: With disguise quality at maximum and a quarterback post-snap coverage reading of 30, the wrong-side-of-progression rate is at least three times the rate at 70.

leaves.title: Gaze control
leaves.criterion: Every player has a defined gaze target on every tick.

leaves.title: The quarterback's eyes as a signal
leaves.criterion: Interception rate on throws into a zone defender's lean side is higher than on throws away from it, and a quarterback who stares down his first read on every snap in a test throws more interceptions against zone than against man.

leaves.title: Ball in the air
leaves.criterion: In a test of deep throws against trailing man coverage, defenders with head turned and ball located produce more breakups and fewer interference fouls than defenders who never locate it.

leaves.title: Finding the ball carrier and a loose ball
leaves.criterion: On a scripted read-option where the end crashes, the end's believed carrier is the back for at least 0.3 s after the quarterback keeps.

leaves.title: Calls and their limits
leaves.criterion: Protection bust rate and false start rate rise with noise for the offense in a 10,000-snap test. Zone pass-off errors fall as the secondary's communication grades rise.

leaves.title: Structure of an assignment
leaves.criterion: Every shipped play validates against the assignment schema. The readable form round-trips to the stored form without loss.

leaves.title: Conditions vocabulary
leaves.criterion: The vocabulary is a data file. Adding a condition requires an implementation, a unit test, and a glossary entry. The rule compiler rejects unknown names.

leaves.title: Actions vocabulary
leaves.criterion: Each action has a scripted test showing a single player carrying it out on an empty field.

leaves.title: Behavior catalogue
leaves.criterion: Every behavior has defined transitions for every universal event (checked by a table-completeness test).

leaves.title: Universal rules
leaves.criterion: With an assignment containing zero rules, a player still completes the play without leaving the behavior's defined states.

leaves.title: Offensive binding
leaves.criterion: For every shipped play and every legal personnel package, binding yields 11 assignments and a legal formation (B4), or a named validation error.

leaves.title: Defensive binding and rule-based adjustment
leaves.criterion: For every shipped coverage against every shipped formation family, every eligible receiver is accounted for by some defender's rule, or the validation report names the hole (it is allowed to exist, because real coverages have holes, but it must be reported).

leaves.title: Conversions and options
leaves.criterion: In a test with option routes, quarterback-receiver disagreement falls as pair familiarity rises from 0 to 1, and each disagreement appears in the truth record as a named event.

leaves.title: Decide stage
leaves.criterion: Shuffling the order in which the Decide stage evaluates players (in a test build, with slots, stream keys, and every slot-index tie-break left unchanged) does not change any outcome, proving that no player's decision reads another's same-tick decision. Slot order itself stays fixed (J13.3.2), because the tie-breaks in J1.3.1 and J2.5.3 use it.

leaves.title: Hesitation
leaves.criterion: A unit installed at knowledge 0.5 produces measurably worse contest results than the same unit at 0.9 in a 5,000-play test, with no mental errors enabled.

leaves.title: Mental error draw
leaves.criterion: 1. Error rate rises as knowledge falls, in every position group. 2. A week in which the user installs twice the normal number of new plays produces more errors in the following game than a normal week (the over-install cost, G5). 3. Raising assignment discipline from 40 to 70 cuts discipline errors by D4.2.1's ratio and leaves knowledge errors unchanged.

leaves.title: Error catalogue
leaves.criterion: Every behavior has at least three error forms. Each form has a scripted test showing the changed behaviour.

leaves.title: Static validation of plays
leaves.criterion: All shipped content has zero errors and no illegal-formation warning. A set of 30 deliberately broken plays each produces the expected error or warning.

leaves.title: Explain record
leaves.criterion: For any player and play in the user's own game, the explanation names a rule that exists in that player's bound assignment.

leaves.title: Substitution run-on and run-off
leaves.criterion: 1. Substitution fouls per game across a simulated league season fall inside the J15 band (defensive too many men 0.15 per game in 2022 to 2024, 1 of 3). 2. Hurry-up with a personnel change produces at least 3 times the error rate of a huddle change.

leaves.title: Defensive matching and the substitution hold
leaves.criterion: With offense substitution on every play and hurry-up selected, the snap never occurs before the hold window ends. With no offensive substitution, a defensive substitution begun late can be caught with too many men.

leaves.title: The huddle and the break
leaves.criterion: Call-delivery failures per game are below 0.5 for a huddle offense at home and rise on the road in loud stadiums at no-huddle.

leaves.title: Offensive alignment
leaves.criterion: Every shipped formation aligns legally from both hashes and the middle, under both rule sets, at every yard line from the 1 to the 99.

leaves.title: Defensive alignment
leaves.criterion: For each shipped front against each shipped formation, every gap is assigned to exactly one defender, or the validation report from J4.6.1 lists the uncovered gap.

leaves.title: Executing shifts and motion
leaves.criterion: Every shipped motion is legal when run with full time. Illegal shift and illegal motion fouls per game land in the J15 band (illegal shift 0.15 per game, 1 of 3).

leaves.title: What motion reveals and how the defense adjusts
