leaves.criterion: In a test of motion against a man call with no bluff, a defender follows on 100% of trials. Against zone with bluff enabled, the quarterback's pre-snap man or zone read is worse than without bluff.

leaves.title: Reading the shell and counting the box
leaves.criterion: Pre-snap read accuracy rises with the coverage reading grade and falls with disguise quality in a 10,000-snap test.

leaves.title: Setting the protection
leaves.criterion: 1. Against a five-man pressure with a six-man protection correctly set, no rusher is unblocked at the snap in 100% of trials with errors disabled. 2. Unblocked-rusher rate rises with disguise quality and crowd noise, and falls with the centre's and quarterback's protection grades.

leaves.title: Checks, audibles, and packaged calls at the line
leaves.criterion: Matches I2.5.1 and I2.5.2 acceptance criteria when run inside the engine.

leaves.title: Disguise and stemming
leaves.criterion: Holding a two-high shell until the snap and rotating to a single-high coverage produces a measurably later arrival of the deep-middle safety at his landmark than showing it honestly.

leaves.title: Defensive checks by rule
leaves.criterion: A defense with an "empty" check installed plays it on every empty look given enough time. A defense without one stays in the huddle call.

leaves.title: Get-off
leaves.criterion: Pass-rush win rate in the first 2.5 s is higher against silent count than against a voiced, varied count, with players held equal.

leaves.title: The snap exchange
leaves.criterion: Bad-snap loose balls per team per season fall in a band set once measured. Rate rises in rain.

leaves.title: Pre-snap foul hazards
leaves.criterion: League rates for each pre-snap foul type land inside the J15 tolerance band. Home and road pre-snap foul rates differ by about 5% on offense and 12% on defense. Simulated team-season standard deviation of pre-snap fouls per 100 snaps is near 0.30.

leaves.title: Scheduling pre-snap actions against the clock
leaves.criterion: 1. At hurry-up, the share of snaps on which the defense has completed all checks is lower than at huddle tempo. 2. No action executes after the snap tick. Dropped actions appear in the log. 3. The distribution of play-clock time at the snap by tempo matches reference data once sourced (same open item as I2.1.1).

leaves.title: Effective z
leaves.criterion: For a fresh, healthy, fully prepared player with neutral technique and leverage, `zEff` equals `zAttr`. Each penalty term alone moves a 5,000-trial contest win rate in the expected direction.

leaves.title: Engagement contests
leaves.criterion: With `dz = 0` the win split over 100,000 trials is 50 to 50 within 0.5 points. With `dz = +1` the offensive win share at 2.5 s matches the closed-form or Monte Carlo reference to within 1 point.

leaves.title: Event contests
leaves.criterion: Each event contest reproduces its `beta0` rate within sampling error in a neutral 100,000-draw test.

leaves.title: One-on-one pass block
leaves.criterion: 1. League-average four-man rush against five-man protection yields pressure and sack rates inside the J15 bands. 2. Pressure rate rises with time held: the curve of cumulative pressure by seconds since the snap is monotone and steepens after 2.5 s. 3. A +1 z rusher against an average tackle wins meaningfully more often. The slope matches the Q3 rating-response band.

leaves.title: Stunts, twists, and pickups
leaves.criterion: Against lines with stunt recognition 30, stunts raise pressure rate over a straight rush. Against lines at 70 with slide protection, they do not.

leaves.title: Help: double teams, chips, and slides
leaves.criterion: Doubling a +2 z rusher brings his pressure rate down to about that of an average rusher in a 5,000-trial test (tunable target).

leaves.title: Blitz pickup and the free rusher
leaves.criterion: The league-wide curve of pressure, sack rate, and expected points by rusher count matches J15 in shape: pressure and sacks rise with each rusher, expected points stay within a band of neutral.

leaves.title: Pressure, hits, and sacks
leaves.criterion: Share of pressures that become sacks lands near the J15 figure (16.4%, 1 of 3). Mean sack yardage is within its band.

leaves.title: One-on-one run block
leaves.criterion: With league-average units and typical calls, stuff rate, yards-before-contact proxy, and 10-plus run rate fall in the J15 bands. Adding an eighth defender to the box lowers yards per carry.

leaves.title: Double teams and combination blocks
leaves.criterion: Raising the nose tackle's double-team anchor from 40 to 70 measurably raises the share of inside runs on which the playside linebacker is unblocked at the line.

leaves.title: Pullers, lead blockers, and blocks in space
leaves.criterion: A scripted power play against a boxing end goes inside the kick-out. Against a spilling end it bounces. Both show on the trajectory.

leaves.title: Defensive line movement against run blocks
leaves.criterion: 1. In scenario mode, slanting into the play's direction raises the stuff rate of outside zone and lowers its 10-plus yard rate, while slanting away raises the 10-plus yard rate (cutback). Direction must hold at p < 0.001 over 20,000 plays. 2. Over a league season, the net expected-points effect of run-defense movement stays within a band around zero once offenses' calls are mixed, so movement is a trade, not a free gain.

leaves.title: Release against press
leaves.criterion: Against press, average time for outside receivers to reach 10 yards downfield is later than against off coverage, and the delay shrinks as the release grade rises.

leaves.title: Separation at the break
leaves.criterion: Mean separation at arrival rises with the receiver's route grade and falls with the defender's coverage grade. Completion rate by depth against man coverage approaches the J15 by-depth table once the throw and catch contests are fitted.

leaves.title: Zone coverage breaks
leaves.criterion: With league-typical calls, the completion and yards-per-attempt gap between zone and man has the direction in the fact above.

leaves.title: Catch, drop, breakup, interception
leaves.criterion: With league-average players and typical calls, completion and interception rates by depth land within the J15 tolerance for every depth band at once, without per-band output adjustment. Drop rate lands in its band.

leaves.title: Tackle attempt
leaves.criterion: League yards after catch and the rushing yardage quantiles (5th to 99th percentiles: -2, 0, 1, 3, 6, 11, 14, 29 for the pro set, 1 of 3) are matched within tolerance. Missed tackle rate lands in its band once sourced.

leaves.title: Piles, forward progress, and short yardage
leaves.criterion: Simulated conversion rate on runs with 1 yard to go lands within the J15 band, and it responds to line quality (a +1 z line converts noticeably more).

leaves.title: Fumbles and strips
leaves.criterion: Fumbles per carry and per sack land inside J15 bands. Wet-weather games show a higher rate (size to be set from data). Across simulated seasons, the odd-week against even-week split-half reliability of team offensive fumble rate is near zero (target 0.05, band 0 to 0.15). If player ball-security grades alone push it higher, the grade slope is too steep.

leaves.title: Recovery
leaves.criterion: Aggregate offensive recovery share lands in the band set once measured.

leaves.title: Contest parameter file
leaves.criterion: A script lists every parameter with its constraining test and fails the build on an orphan. Loading the file with any value outside its range fails validation.

leaves.title: Drops and the launch point
leaves.criterion: In a no-rush test, the quarterback reaches each drop's launch point within 0.1 s and 0.5 yd of the table.

leaves.title: Route timing against the drop
leaves.criterion: For shipped timing concepts with average players and no jam, the first read's break falls within 0.2 s of `tSet`. Anticipation grade 70 produces more separation at arrival than grade 30 on the same route and coverage.

leaves.title: Working the reads
leaves.criterion: With throwing disabled, a grade-50 quarterback reaches read 3 at about `tSet + 1.1 s`. A grade-80 reaches it about 0.5 s sooner.

leaves.title: Judging open
leaves.criterion: Across 50,000 simulated throws, the grade-80 quarterback's `pHat` has lower mean absolute error against the true completion probability (or a lower Brier score against realised completion) than the grade-30 quarterback's. Error against the binary caught-or-not outcome does not work: in expectation it is insensitive to estimate noise.

leaves.title: Throw threshold and risk
leaves.criterion: Raising the risk grade raises both yards per attempt and interception rate in a 20,000-dropback test. League interception rate lands in the J15 band with league-typical quarterbacks.

leaves.title: Checkdowns, hot throws, and sight adjustments
leaves.criterion: Against an unblocked sixth rusher with hot rules installed and recognised, the ball is out in under 1.8 s on at least 90% of trials.

leaves.title: Feeling pressure
leaves.criterion: Strip-sack share of sacks is higher from the blind side than the front side. Quarterbacks with pocket movement 70 take fewer sacks at equal pressure than those at 30.

leaves.title: Response to pressure
leaves.criterion: League sack, scramble, and throwaway rates land inside J15 bands simultaneously.

leaves.title: Scramble
leaves.criterion: Scramble rate is higher against man coverage without a spy than against zone in a controlled test, and the league rate lands in its J15 band.

leaves.title: Throwing the ball away and intentional grounding
leaves.criterion: Grounding fouls per game land in the J15 band. No legal throwaway by the rule keys is ever flagged as committed.

leaves.title: Extending the play and designed movement
leaves.criterion: Completion rate on out-of-pocket throws is below in-pocket rate by a margin in the direction of the fact above.

leaves.title: Release, ball speed, and trajectory choice
leaves.criterion: A grade-70 arm completes a higher share of 15-yard outs to the far sideline than a grade-40 arm against the same coverage in a 5,000-trial test.

leaves.title: Accuracy
leaves.criterion: With the catch-point model fixed, completion by depth for a grade-50 quarterback against league-average coverage matches the J15 by-depth table within tolerance.

leaves.title: Mesh reads
leaves.criterion: With a correct read every time (test quarterback), the option's unblocked defender never makes the tackle for a loss. With a grade-30 read, he does at a visible rate.

leaves.title: Spike, kneel, and sneak
leaves.criterion: A kneel consumes the play's live time and is spotted 1 yd back. A legal spike never draws a grounding foul.

leaves.title: The free play and the Hail Mary
leaves.criterion: On a recognised free play the mean air yards of the throw are at least twice his normal mean.

leaves.title: The look-ahead
leaves.criterion: With a single unblocked defender placed in the designed hole and an open cutback lane, a vision-70 back takes the cutback at least twice as often as a vision-30 back in 2,000 trials.

leaves.title: The track and the read
leaves.criterion: 1. On a scripted inside zone with the playside defensive tackle reached, the back hits the playside A or B gap. With the tackle crossing the centre's face, he cuts back. Both in at least 85% of trials at vision 60. 2. League rushing direction shares approximate left 38%, middle 26%, right 36% (pro, 2022 to 2024, 1 of 3) when AI teams call league-typical run mixes.

leaves.title: Getting what is blocked, and bouncing
leaves.criterion: A back set to maximum bounce bias has a higher stuff rate and a higher 10-plus rate than the same back set to minimum, in a 5,000-carry test.

leaves.title: Moves
leaves.criterion: Missed-tackle rate forced by a carrier rises with his elusiveness in the open field and with his power in head-on contact, in separate controlled tests.

leaves.title: Using blockers downfield
leaves.criterion: Mean screen gain is higher for patience-70 carriers than patience-30 carriers behind the same blockers.

leaves.title: Contact, falling forward, and protecting the ball
leaves.criterion: With the ball-security instruction on, fumbles per carry fall and yards per carry fall slightly in a 10,000-carry test. The effect is a late-game situational instruction, small enough that team season fumble rates keep near-zero split-half reliability (J6.7.1). The game never tells the user his standards reduced fumbles.

leaves.title: Clock and boundary awareness
leaves.criterion: With the "stay in bounds" rule set and practiced, carriers within 3 yd of the sideline end the play in bounds on at least 85% of such plays. Unpracticed, the share is clearly lower.

leaves.title: Quarterback slides and giving himself up
leaves.criterion: Quarterback hits taken per scramble fall by at least half with protection on.

leaves.title: Team pursuit and leverage
leaves.criterion: With every defender on his rule and average talent, runs of 20 or more yards stay near the J15 rate. Removing the force rule from the playside defender in a test multiplies that rate several times on outside runs.

leaves.title: After the catch
leaves.criterion: Yards after catch are higher on in-stride placements than on adjusted catches at the same depth, and the league mean lands in the J15 band.

leaves.title: Returns: kicks, punts, interceptions, and fumbles
leaves.criterion: Fair catch share, return average, and touchback share for punts and kickoffs land in J15 bands once those targets are sourced for the modelled season.

leaves.title: Trajectory of a thrown ball
leaves.criterion: 1. With no wind and no error, the ball lands within 0.05 yd of the aim point for all depths within range. 2. Flight time rises with distance and falls with arm strength. A touch throw has a longer flight than a drive throw to the same point. 3. The solver is deterministic across platforms (golden test in Q1).

leaves.title: Snaps, handoffs, pitches, and laterals
leaves.criterion: Every exchange in shipped plays completes on its designed tick with average players and no defense.

leaves.title: Batted and tipped passes
leaves.criterion: Batted-pass rate lands in its band once measured, and it is higher for drive trajectories than touch trajectories.

leaves.title: Bounces and rolls
leaves.criterion: No loose ball remains live longer than 12 s. Punt touchback share lands in its J15 band with league-typical punters.

leaves.title: The operation: snap, hold, kick
leaves.criterion: Non-clean operations occur on a small share of kicks (starting target 2%) and lower make rate when they occur.

leaves.title: Kick flight and the make model
leaves.criterion: 1. A league of grade-distributed kickers reproduces the make-rate table within tolerance in neutral-weighted conditions. Long attempts in the real table are selected (coaches try 50-plus yard kicks mostly with strong legs and good conditions, which is why 45 to 49 and 50 to 54 yd read alike), so the test runs with K5 and I4 choosing which attempts to take, not on a uniform mix of attempts. 2. Make rate falls with crosswind and headwind, with cold, and from a hash relative to the middle at short range. 3. The same kick under the college rule set from the hash is harder than under the pro set, by geometry alone.

leaves.title: Blocks and rush on kicks
leaves.criterion: Block rates land in J15 bands. Slowing the operation by 0.15 s at least doubles the block rate.

leaves.title: Punt distance and hang time
leaves.criterion: League gross average, touchback share, and (once sourced) net average and return rate land in J15 bands. Hang time and distance are negatively correlated for a given punter across 5,000 punts.

leaves.title: Coverage timing against the ball
leaves.criterion: Mean distance from the nearest coverage player to the returner at the catch falls as hang time rises, across simulated punts.

leaves.title: Kickoff placement under the rule set
leaves.criterion: For each kickoff type the share of each rule result (landing zone, end zone, short, out of bounds) is stable and plausible, and league touchback and return rates land in J15 bands for the modelled season's rule set. Switching the rule-set file switches behaviour with no code change.

leaves.title: Onside kicks
leaves.criterion: Recovery rate lands in its band once measured.

leaves.title: Wind effects on the ball
leaves.criterion: Field goal make rate from 45 to 54 yd falls monotonically across wind bins of 0, 10, and 20 mph crosswind. Simulated total points by wind bin move in the direction of the fact above.

leaves.title: What J owns and what K1 adds
leaves.criterion: No K1 module writes to contest results. Each K1 output has exactly one J reader named in its leaf.

leaves.title: Effort on a snap
leaves.criterion: In scripted plays run 1,000 times, a low-motor fatigued backside defender reaches the ball later than a high-motor one, and the point-of-attack contest distribution differs by no more than the X1.4.2 bound. Loaf tags per game per team are recorded for tuning.

leaves.title: Defensive gambles: jumping routes, undercutting, going for the strip
leaves.criterion: Players at high `risk_tolerance` have both more interceptions and more receptions of 20 or more yards allowed per target than otherwise identical players, over 20,000 scripted dropbacks. League interception rate stays inside its J15 tolerance.

leaves.title: Offensive improvisation
leaves.criterion: In scripted scrambles, receivers with the rule installed move by rule in at least 95% of cases they perceive. Without it, under 20%.

leaves.title: Deliberate fouls by a beaten player
leaves.criterion: In scripted beaten-deep plays, deliberate interference is more frequent under the college rule set than the pro one, and more frequent for low-`discipline` players. League interference and holding rates stay inside their J15 bands.

leaves.title: Matchup learning within a game
leaves.criterion: In scripted one-on-one series where a rusher uses one move every rep, his win rate falls across reps for high-intelligence blockers and stays flat for a rusher who alternates two moves.

leaves.title: Getting people lined up
leaves.criterion: Replacing a high-quality communicator with a low one in a scripted unit raises that unit's mental error count by a measurable amount at 95% confidence, with all other players unchanged.

leaves.title: Players use perceived state only
leaves.criterion: The static check runs in continuous integration. The paired test covers every behavior in the J4.2.1 catalogue and every K1 trigger type, with zero early divergences.

leaves.title: The four kinds of deviation and the one record
leaves.criterion: Every truth-record deviation has exactly one kind and one motive from the content list. A test that forces two producers on the same player and play records only the first by rule 3. No career screen reads `kind` or `motive` (static check, same mechanism as K9.3.1).

leaves.title: Accidents: he knew it and could not do it
leaves.criterion: Over 10,000 scripted dig routes, accident rate rises with fatigue and falls with route-running grade in the stated directions. With every multiplier at 1, average accident rate per check point equals the base 2% within sampling error. No accident ever changes the rule index in the explain record (J4.6.2).

leaves.title: He did not know better: situational lapses
leaves.criterion: In scripted late-game plays, situational misses fall as installed situational knowledge rises and as years at the level rise. A sideline reminder lowers misses on that snap only.

leaves.title: Intentional, for himself: freelancing
leaves.criterion: Two generated players identical except for `ego` and team orientation produce the same number of discipline errors over 20,000 snaps, and the high-ego player's errors have a larger share of `stats` and `touches` forms. A contract-year flag raises the `forSelf` share. A real imported player never has a `forSelf` deviation with motive `stats` caused by traits alone (test with neutral block).

leaves.title: On purpose, for the team: the veteran's adjustment
leaves.criterion: No player below the gate ever records a `forTeam` deviation from this leaf. In scripted tell plays, a gated veteran who studied the tell deviates more often and gains more expected points per deviation than one who did not study it. When the teammate dependent on him has cohesion under 0.3 and no call is delivered, the play allows more explosive gains than when cohesion is above 0.7.

leaves.title: How each kind shows on film and what the staff says
leaves.criterion: Over a season of forced deviations, staff tag accuracy per kind matches rule 1 within sampling error, and a selfish player's explanations are dishonest more often than a candid one's. No career screen displays `kind` or `motive`.

leaves.title: How coaches respond: teaching, benching, freedom and trust
leaves.criterion: In a scripted season, benching players for true accidents lowers their trust more than benching them for true `forSelf` deviations. Praising a successful `forSelf` deviation raises that player's later `forSelf` share. Each label in rule 4 appears only after its evidence threshold.

leaves.title: Real rates and how the four kinds are calibrated
leaves.criterion: Every constant in K1.7.2 to K1.7.7 is listed in config with status Assumption, and Q2 reports the four calibration totals above each run.

leaves.title: Record structure and storage
leaves.criterion: Schema validation rejects a profile with a label, archetype, or point field. No interface module imports `CoachProfile.behavior` (static check, K9.3.1). Loading and saving a profile is lossless.

leaves.title: The system block
leaves.criterion: A coach with `playAction` 0.30 against scripted neutral opponents with no plan adjustments calls play action on 27% to 33% of neutral early-down dropbacks over 2,000 plays.

leaves.title: The tendency block
leaves.criterion: Two coaches identical except for `fourthDownOffset` differ in go rate in the expected direction over 5,000 scripted fourth downs. Changing a tendency changes no play outcome distribution when the calls are held fixed.

leaves.title: Hidden behavior parameters
leaves.criterion: For each parameter, a test changes only that parameter between two identical coaches and shows a different distribution of the named decision over 1,000 seeded trials, and no change in any other logged decision type. A search of J, B, and D finds no read of any `behavior` field.

leaves.title: The memory block
leaves.criterion: After two games in which a scripted caller runs the same concept on every third and medium, the AI coach's starting belief for that bucket in the third game puts at least 60% on that concept (starting value). Notes contain no field absent from the film filter.

leaves.title: Generating a coach by level and role
leaves.criterion: Generating 1,000 head coaches twice with one seed gives identical profiles. No two profiles in 1,000 are equal. Every template appears. No person record contains a template name.

leaves.title: Imported real coaches
leaves.criterion: An imported coach's profile has neutral X1 facets and median `behavior` unless the pack row carries a sourced estimate. The game starts and runs with no pack.

leaves.title: Calibrating tendency and system distributions
leaves.criterion: League means inside tolerance for every J15.8.3 row over 20 simulated seasons. No AI coach's fourth-down go rate falls outside the real team range once that range is sourced.

leaves.title: Calibrating the size of the coach effect
leaves.criterion: The measured pro effect is inside the band. The weak-roster effect is larger than the average-roster effect at 95% confidence.

leaves.title: Computed descriptions and their error
leaves.criterion: Deleting labels and recomputing reproduces them. With the label engine off, every AI decision in a season is unchanged for the same seed. In a 200-season run, the "disciplined" label's year-to-year persistence for a coach who changes teams is no higher than chance.

leaves.title: Between-season change
leaves.criterion: Over 30 simulated seasons the population means of every `behavior` parameter stay within 0.1 z of their starting values (no inflation). A coach who never held a play-calling job has an unchanged `callFit`.

leaves.title: Lineage: what a coach takes from the people he worked under
leaves.criterion: In a 40-season world, assistants of one head coach share his offense family at more than twice the base rate when they become play callers.

leaves.title: One schema for every coaching role
leaves.criterion: Every decision type in J11.6.1 maps to exactly one person on every AI team in every week of a simulated season.

leaves.title: Forbidden parameters
leaves.criterion: A profile file with a `teamDiscipline` or `penaltyModifier` field fails the build. (The X1 person facet named `discipline`, read by K2.8.1, sits on the person record, is not a coach profile field, and changes no foul rate.) The J15.9.1 swap test passes: swapping every team's head-coach profile changes the year-to-year pre-snap foul correlation by less than 0.03.

leaves.title: The rule-respect disposition
leaves.criterion: Exactly one function returns the value, and every violation leaf's code imports it (static check). No interface module imports it. With imported people in a world, a 50-season run logs zero violation events with an imported person as actor.

leaves.title: The violation decision
leaves.criterion: Across a 50-season world, violation counts fall with `ruleRespect` and rise with pressure, each at 95% confidence. Every `violation_committed` event names a content row. A world with every person at `ruleRespect` z of +3 logs zero violations by AI people.

leaves.title: The AI scouting report
leaves.criterion: With charter error at zero and maximum `preparation`, the AI report's counts equal the G8.1.2 view of the same team. A new play the user installs but has never run in a game appears in no AI report. Report build time per team is inside the P6 weekly budget.

leaves.title: The AI staff's player grades
leaves.criterion: Estimated grades differ from true grades with an error whose SD falls as `evaluation` rises. A test that changes a player's true attribute without changing any film leaves the AI's estimate unchanged.

leaves.title: Three sources: concept priors, matchup adjustment, planning reps
leaves.criterion: With perfect grades, zero noise, and many reps, `A` converges to the engine's true expected points within 0.03 per cell. Planning reps never read true attributes of opposing players (static check, K9.3.1).

leaves.title: The matrix per situation bucket
leaves.criterion: Every non-empty box on every AI sheet has a matrix and a stored mix at lock.

leaves.title: Building the plan
leaves.criterion: Every AI plan validates against the G6 schema the user's plans use. Plans of high-`preparation` staffs contain more opponent-specific calls than low ones.

leaves.title: Building the sheet
leaves.criterion: Every AI sheet validates against the G7 schema. Catalogue coverage rises with `preparation` across the league.

leaves.title: Allocating practice
leaves.criterion: For identical rosters, plans, and staff parameters, an AI team and a user team that enter the same practice plan get identical readiness. No AI practice week exceeds the level's limits unless a `violation_committed` event exists for it.

leaves.title: Order, timing, and fidelity
leaves.criterion: Running a week's preparation with 1 and 16 workers gives identical sheets. A team's sheet is unchanged when another team's profile is edited in a test.

leaves.title: Installing a system and planning a season
leaves.criterion: Teams with a new system show lower early-season readiness than the same teams in a control run with the old system kept, and the gap closes over the season.

leaves.title: Situation bucket and candidate list
leaves.criterion: For 10,000 random legal game states every AI sheet returns a bucket and at least 2 candidates. No candidate is illegal or uninstalled.

leaves.title: Thinking time and the play clock
leaves.criterion: In league-mode simulation the share of AI offensive snaps taken with 5 s or less on the play clock, and the delay-of-game rate, fall inside their J15 target rows where those rows exist. An AI call is never produced in zero simulated time.

leaves.title: Starting belief
leaves.criterion: With the opponent's charted share at 80% over 40 plays, the starting belief is between 70% and 80%. Changing the opponent's plan for this week without changing his past games does not change the belief.

leaves.title: Updating belief during the game
leaves.criterion: A scripted opponent who shows one look every play shifts a z = +3 caller's belief past the half-way point by the 3rd repeat and a z = -3 caller's by the 12th, within one play. Belief never changes on a play the caller's staff did not observe.

leaves.title: The matrix game and stored mixes
leaves.criterion: For 1,000 random matrices the stored mix's worst-case payoff equals the game value within 0.001. Total live call computation for a game stays under 5 ms on the reference machine.

leaves.title: Tilt toward the read, and call fit
leaves.criterion: Against a scripted opponent who always shows one look, the caller's share of the best counter rises with plays observed and is higher for higher `callFit`. Against a scripted opponent playing the equilibrium mix, expected payoff does not fall as `tau` rises by more than the matrix's uncertainty.

leaves.title: Self-scout penalty
leaves.criterion: Over a simulated season, the count of "strong" tendency rows (N2.3.1 rule 3) per AI caller falls as `selfScout` rises, with rank correlation below -0.5 across the league.

leaves.title: Sequencing: base, complement, constraint
leaves.criterion: In scripted tests where the defense shows the trigger reaction, the constraint's call share in the next 3 matching snaps is at least 1.3 times its share without the trigger.

leaves.title: Readiness check
leaves.criterion: Calls with estimated readiness under 0.4 make up less than 1% of AI calls in league simulation.

leaves.title: The draw and the call record
leaves.criterion: Replaying a full game from its event log reproduces every AI call. Changing only the user's call on a snap leaves the opposing AI call on that snap identical.

leaves.title: System habits and game-state lean
leaves.criterion: With population means set by K2.3.1, simulated neutral pass rate, play action share, and 11 personnel share fall inside their J15 tolerances. Two callers identical except `offenseRates.playAction` 0.15 and 0.30 differ in neutral play action share in that direction over 2,000 plays. League pass rate rises with deficit band in the second half.

leaves.title: The defensive call and when it is committed
leaves.criterion: A static test confirms the defensive call function's inputs contain no field of the offensive call object. Changing the offensive formation while holding personnel fixed does not change the defensive call drawn, only the checks that follow.

leaves.title: The opening script
leaves.criterion: On opening drives, at least 80% of first-and-10 and second-and-medium calls come from the script.

leaves.title: Tempo choice
leaves.criterion: League no-huddle share inside the J15 tolerance.

leaves.title: Series-break and halftime adjustments
leaves.criterion: In league simulation, high-`adjustment` staffs' second-half expected points against first-half looks they were losing to improve more than low-`adjustment` staffs' at 95% confidence.

leaves.title: Kicking-game calls
leaves.criterion: League fake rate and onside rate inside J15 tolerance where rows exist.

leaves.title: The exploit boundary
leaves.criterion: Q4.1.1 finds no dominant call against any shipped profile. A scripted "scout and attack" caller beats low-`selfScout` profiles by more than high-`selfScout` profiles.

leaves.title: Fouls on purpose, feigned injuries, and the edges of the rules
leaves.criterion: In scripted end-of-half states where a delay of game gives a better punt result, AI coaches at `clockManagement` z of 0 or more take it in at least 80% of cases. No rule 2 act happens without a `violation_committed` event. In mirrored worlds, a feign ordered by the user and one ordered by an AI coach have the same detection chance.

leaves.title: Estimate, offset, advice, choice
leaves.criterion: A coach with zero offsets, full `analyticsTrust`, perfect estimates, and no errors chooses the model's best option in every non-close state of the I5.1.2 500-state test set. Every AI game-management decision in a simulated season has a log row with both estimated and true win probabilities.

leaves.title: Go, kick, or punt
leaves.criterion: League mix inside J15 tolerance for the default era and for the 1999 to 2005 era population. Across AI coaches, go rate on fourth and 2 or less is monotonic in `fourthDownOffset`.

leaves.title: One point or two
leaves.criterion: In scripted late-game states where the model margin for going for two exceeds 5 win-probability points, at least 90% of AI coaches go.

leaves.title: Clock mode
leaves.criterion: In scripted states with a lead and the ball where kneeling wins by arithmetic, every AI coach kneels (K5.4.3). League-wide run share when leading by two scores in the final 5 minutes is above the neutral run share.

leaves.title: End of half
leaves.criterion: With the ball, 1:30 left in the half, three timeouts, at midfield, at least 95% of AI coaches attack. With 0:20, no timeouts, own 20, at least 90% kneel or run a safe play.

leaves.title: Kneel and spike
leaves.criterion: No AI team spikes on fourth down in 1,000 simulated seasons. No AI team runs a risky play in a state where kneeling wins with the safety margin.

leaves.title: Timeouts
leaves.criterion: AI coaches never call a timeout the rule set forbids. League timeouts used per game falls inside the J15 tolerance around 7.7. Timeouts remaining at the two-minute mark of each half is recorded for comparison once sourced.

leaves.title: Challenges
leaves.criterion: No AI challenge is made on a non-reviewable or automatically reviewed play. Simulated league challenge success rate is recorded for comparison once the real rate is sourced.

leaves.title: The error list
leaves.criterion: Error frequency across coaches falls with `clockManagement` for every row. With the error list disabled in a test build, no AI decision differs from the sound decision. Every error in a simulated season is tagged in the log.

leaves.title: Accept or decline
leaves.criterion: In a 300-case table of foul situations, coaches at z of 0 or more choose the higher win-probability option in every case where the options differ by more than 1 point.

leaves.title: Coin toss and overtime choices
leaves.criterion: Every election is legal under the active rule set in a test that cycles all shipped rule sets.

leaves.title: Resting starters and pulling players
leaves.criterion: No AI team rests starters in a game that can change its seeding. Starters return in scripted comeback tests.

leaves.title: College switches
leaves.criterion: A search of K5 code finds no numeric rule value. Running the K5 test suite under the college rule set passes with college-specific expected results.

leaves.title: Delegated decisions use the staff member's own profile
leaves.criterion: With all duties delegated, a user game completes with every decision logged to a staff member. Swapping in a coordinator with higher `callFit` raises the delegated side's expected points per play over 200 simulated games with everything else fixed.

leaves.title: Standing instructions and reserved decisions
leaves.criterion: A forbidden call never appears from a delegated caller in 100 simulated games. Every reserved decision either reaches the user or is logged as timed out.

leaves.title: Suggestions and reports from the staff
leaves.criterion: In a logged season, the share of recognition reports that match the true look rises with the reporter's `evaluation`. No advice message is time-stamped earlier than its inputs became observable.

leaves.title: Delegated game management and the advisor
leaves.criterion: With a perfect analyst the line equals the model's best option in the I5.1.2 test set. A delegated game-management season logs error tags at the rate implied by the staff member's parameter.

leaves.title: Staff work products and their quality
leaves.criterion: Tag accuracy of delivered breakdowns rises with the producing assistant's `evaluation`. Late or thin deliveries rise with hours over the L4.3.5 limit.

leaves.title: Candor and disagreement
leaves.criterion: Over a simulated season, voiced disagreements per staff member rise with `candor` and fall after scripted punishments of candor.

leaves.title: Staff stand in when the user simulates
leaves.criterion: "Simulate to end" and "watch with everything delegated" give identical results for the same seed (J14.4.1). Advancing a week with a better staff yields better preparation outputs than with a worse staff, all else fixed.

leaves.title: Decisions the user does not own
leaves.criterion: In a scripted season at rung 3, replacing the user's tendency reports with deliberately wrong ones lowers the boss's team's expected points on the affected situations, with all else fixed. The boss's decisions never read a field of the user's product that a real boss could not see.

leaves.title: How the boss judges and uses people
leaves.criterion: In paired simulations where the user's work scripts are replaced by an AI assistant producing identical outputs, the boss's trust path is identical.

leaves.title: Violations by the user's staff, with or without him
leaves.criterion: A scripted staff of low-`ruleRespect` assistants under job pressure produces violation events without any user request. A scripted request to a high-`ruleRespect` assistant is refused at a rate above 90%.

leaves.title: General manager record
leaves.criterion: Schema validation as K2.1.1. Two general managers with opposite `draftVsVeteran` values produce measurably different roster age profiles over 10 simulated seasons with the same starting roster.

leaves.title: College roster-builder record
leaves.criterion: Schema validation as K2.1.1. Two programs with opposite `highSchoolVsTransfer` values and the same starting roster and budget show measurably different shares of transfers on the roster after 6 simulated seasons.

leaves.title: Team needs and the coach's voice
leaves.criterion: With `w` at 0 the list ignores the coach. With `w` at 1 it equals the coach's ranking for positions he listed. Trust changes follow logged outcomes of coach-pushed moves.

leaves.title: Player value as the front office sees it
leaves.criterion: Two teams with different systems value the same player differently in the direction of fit. Changing a player's true attribute without new evidence leaves every team's value unchanged.

leaves.title: Waivers, the practice squad, signings, and injury replacements
leaves.criterion: No AI roster is illegal at any weekly lock in 50 simulated seasons. Every transaction passes C5.7.1 validation.

leaves.title: Contracts and the cap
leaves.criterion: No AI team is over the cap at a date the rules require compliance, across 50 seasons. League-wide share of cap by position stays within a band of the starting distribution (no drift into absurd markets).

leaves.title: Free agency
leaves.criterion: Contract size by position and age in the simulated market is checked against the C6 starting tables each season and stays within tolerance over 30 seasons.

leaves.title: The draft
leaves.criterion: Over 30 simulated drafts, the correlation between pick number and career value is positive and well short of perfect. The acceptance band is set by Q2 from the project's draft history data (`data/people/nfl_draft_history.csv`), which must be analysed before a number is written. Status of that target: missing.

leaves.title: Trades
leaves.criterion: Simulated trade counts per season are recorded for comparison with a real count once sourced. No accepted trade has a negative estimated surplus for either side by that side's own valuation.

leaves.title: The offseason roster, undrafted players, and the cutdown
leaves.criterion: Every AI club is at or under each roster limit at each deadline in 50 simulated seasons. Some undrafted players make rosters every year. With the user holding `final_say_roster`, no cut is made on his club without his decision or logged delegation.

leaves.title: Recruiting boards, offers, and visits
leaves.criterion: No AI program is over the roster limit on the declaration date (the governing body refuses the roster, T5.1.1). No AI program exceeds a signing or visit limit, or contacts outside allowed periods, without a matching `violation_committed` event. Class quality correlates with program reputation, with year-to-year variation.

leaves.title: The transfer market, retention, and the roster budget
leaves.criterion: Yearly roster turnover per program is recorded for comparison with the T6 target once that target is sourced. No budget exceeds its cap without a violation event.

leaves.title: AI head coaches and coordinators building staffs
leaves.criterion: Every staff position required by X8 is filled before the season on every team. In paired tests the user and an AI candidate with identical records and views receive identical scores.

leaves.title: Tampering, cap circumvention, and recruiting violations by AI
leaves.criterion: In a 50-season world, AI violations occur, some are detected, and every detected one produces the tabled penalty. The same scripted violation by the user and by an AI team yields the same detection probability and penalty.

leaves.title: Fixed order after each commit, by tier
leaves.criterion: The same world advanced with different worker counts has identical transaction logs. An offseason day for the whole world fits the P6 budget.

leaves.title: Decision-maker record and goals
leaves.criterion: Schema validation as K2.1.1. Two decision-makers with opposite `patience` and identical team histories differ in mean coach tenure over a 60-season test.

leaves.title: Expectations that rise with success
leaves.criterion: In a scripted program with five straight seasons at 10 wins, expectation exceeds 9 by year six, and a 9-win season then lowers confidence. The same 9 wins at a scripted 4-win program raises it.

leaves.title: Reactions to results, including noise
leaves.criterion: In paired scripted games identical except for the outcome of one fourth-down try, the losing version yields a lower reaction from every observer, and the gap is smaller for process-minded observers. No K8 module imports the truth decision log.

leaves.title: One confidence procedure for the user and for AI
leaves.criterion: In a paired test, the user's coach and an AI coach with identical histories under the same decision-maker have identical confidence paths. A code search finds one confidence update function.

leaves.title: The firing decision, with no built-in bounce
leaves.criterion: E4.3.5's three tests pass for AI teams: no modifier keyed to coach change exists in code. Replacing a coach with an identical copy changes nothing. In a 200-season run, teams that fired a coach improve no more than teams that did not, matched on record and on the preseason public estimate, within sampling error. Matching on record alone is wrong: firing selects on record against expectation, so record-matched fired teams still gain about 0.04 win share by regression alone (G-77). Simulated firings per season are recorded against the real count once sourced.

leaves.title: The search: whom a decision-maker hires
leaves.criterion: Two decision-makers with different culture records rank the same three candidates differently, each traceable to labels and impressions (the X2.3.1 test). In a 60-season world the correlation between a hired coach's hidden quality and his hiring score is positive and well below 1.

leaves.title: The college chain of pressure
leaves.criterion: In scripted programs, sustained losing lowers giving and next year's budget. A funded buyout raises firing probability for the same confidence value.

leaves.title: Agent behavior
leaves.criterion: More aggressive agents produce higher signed values and more failed talks over 30 simulated offseasons.

leaves.title: Stories from labels and notable events
leaves.criterion: Every generated story links to at least one public event. With an imported pack loaded, a 30-season run produces no story of an excluded type about an imported person.

leaves.title: Fan mood
leaves.criterion: Mood falls through a scripted losing streak and recovers on a winning one. Changing mood alone changes home noise and nothing else in a game.

leaves.title: The knowledge rule
leaves.criterion: Every AI decision function takes a `PersonView` or `TeamView` argument and no world-state argument. The K9.3 audits pass.

leaves.title: The AI commits without seeing the user's call
leaves.criterion: J13.2.1 criterion 1 passes: changing only the user's call leaves the opposing AI call for that snap identical. A randomized test over 100,000 snaps finds zero cases where the AI call differs between two runs that differ only in the user's unrevealed input or response time.

leaves.title: Static audit: what AI code can import
leaves.criterion: A deliberately added import of a truth module into a K4 file fails the build. The list of view builders is under a fixed count (starting 25) and each has a field whitelist test.

leaves.title: Dynamic audit: decisions change only when available information changes
leaves.criterion: Zero divergences across the full fact list in the nightly run. The reverse test shows at least one changed decision per visible-fact type.

leaves.title: No difficulty setting, no handicap, no rubber band
leaves.criterion: The settings schema contains no field read by J, K, D, or E outcome code (static check). A search for the user flag in J and K finds only the allowed uses. Two careers from the same seed and pack with different settings produce identical AI decisions when the user's inputs are identical.

leaves.title: Detection and penalties, the same for the user and for AI
leaves.criterion: 1. A scripted violation committed by the user and by an AI coach in mirrored worlds has the same detection probability each week and the same penalty on detection. 2. Over a 50-season world, a share of AI violations is detected and a share is not, and every detection produces a tabled penalty. 3. No penalty is ever applied without a `violation_detected` event. False-accusation inquiries impose none. 4. With an imported pack, no imported person appears in any enforcement event. 5. A code search finds one detection function, called from L8.2.5's pipeline only.

leaves.title: Exploit search, behavior match, and the release gate for AI
leaves.criterion: The report lists every check with status. A build with a failing check cannot be tagged for release.

leaves.title: Relationship record
leaves.criterion: A record exists for every coach and player pair on a roster within one tick of the player joining. Values stay in 0 to 100 under a random event storm test of 10,000 events. Moving a player between teams and back restores the record minus decay.

leaves.title: Memory ledger
leaves.criterion: Given a fixed seed and event list, the ledger and resulting trust are identical on replay. A memory at one half-life shows half its strength within rounding. The 40-entry cap holds.

leaves.title: Knowing the player
leaves.criterion: No D5 field is shown as exact before its threshold. Noise width at familiarity 100 is under 5 points.

leaves.title: Needs
leaves.criterion: Every shown need names its basis (a statement or a staff guess) and the measurable fact behind it. Changing a facet in data changes the need weights with no code change. No weight or satisfaction value appears on any career screen. No need is shown that the player has not voiced and the staff have not guessed.

leaves.title: Stress and breakpoints
leaves.criterion: A single loss or single bad event cannot raise any player above a breakpoint from below 60. No more than two unqueued breakpoint events fire per team per week in a 1,000-season test outside the room-lost state. Every facet change is logged with its touchstone.

leaves.title: Conversation system
leaves.criterion: Adding a new conversation type needs a data row and text only. Every conversation writes a decision log entry with the information shown at the time. The same inputs and seed give the same outcome.

leaves.title: Role definition talk
leaves.criterion: Every rostered player has a dated stated role after the first camp week. A stated starter who plays under 30 percent of snaps in two straight healthy games raises a broken-promise check.

leaves.title: Playing-time talks
leaves.criterion: Every role-step drop raises exactly one prompt. Skipping it writes the "found out elsewhere" memory when the depth chart posts.

leaves.title: Correction and praise
leaves.criterion: Praise decay is applied. Suggested list never exceeds six.

leaves.title: Personal matters and the open door
leaves.criterion: No harmful personal event is ever generated for a person flagged real. With open-door hours at zero, request count falls to zero within three weeks.

leaves.title: Promise ledger
leaves.criterion: Every promise has a machine-checkable test. The pre-break warning fires before the action commits. Void conditions are covered by tests.

leaves.title: Honesty and consistency of word
leaves.criterion: coach_word changes only through logged events, each traceable in N3.

leaves.title: The quarterback
leaves.criterion: shared_language is tracked per pair and survives a quarterback's benching and return. Its game effect is capped by the L1.6.1 table.

leaves.title: Injured players
leaves.criterion: report_propensity responds to each listed input in the stated direction. Returning a player the concussion protocol has not cleared is offered with a warning naming the rule, logged once as a violation, and sent to L8.2.5 for detection and penalty, the same for AI clubs (Marlon's ruling of 2026-11-25 22:23 UTC; matches H3.3.2 after audit FRd-9).

leaves.title: Release and cut day
leaves.criterion: Every release produces exactly one delivery record. The memory persists on the person record after he leaves the team.

leaves.title: Contract incentives late in the year
leaves.criterion: Flags appear only when the gap is reachable within remaining games at the player's season rate times 1.5.

leaves.title: The college player
leaves.criterion: With league level college, the incentive leaf (L1.4.4) is off and the college conversation types are on. An outside-money promise is always offered, always warns, and always writes one violation row.

leaves.title: Relationships below head coach
leaves.criterion: Conversation types offered match the table for each rung. An out-of-authority promise is logged with the rung at the time.

leaves.title: Bounded effects table
leaves.criterion: Each multiplier is clamped to its bound in a property test. A season simulated with all buy_in at 100 against all at 0, same seed and rosters, differs in win total by no more than the tolerance set in Q2 (starting target: under 1.0 win per 17 games before "losing the room" is counted).

leaves.title: Player-to-player ties
leaves.criterion: Graph build for a 105-man roster takes under 50 ms. Same seed gives the same graph. Sparse storage stays under 3,500 stored ties per team (raised from 1,500: the storage rule, store only above 30 or below 20 with same class +10, same region +5, fit up to +15, keeps about 3,300 on a 105-man roster with realistic fit, per G-24's measurement). The storage band is kept because realism comes first; the budget is a performance limit. Assumption, pending a performance check (coordinator ruling 2026-11-26).

leaves.title: Groups and position rooms
leaves.criterion: Every rostered player belongs to exactly one room. Clique detection is deterministic for a seed.

leaves.title: Status and influence
leaves.criterion: Influence sums and ranks are reproducible. Removing a player updates all dependents within one tick.

leaves.title: Captains
leaves.criterion: The vote is reproducible for a seed. Veto and appointment costs are applied once.

leaves.title: Leadership council
leaves.criterion: Surfacing probability matches the formula over 10,000 trials within 1 percent. An item deferred twice is closed.

leaves.title: Position-room leaders
leaves.criterion: Leader does not change more than once in four weeks without a roster move.

leaves.title: Mentors and the rookie program
leaves.criterion: Modifier applies only in the rookie's first season and within L1.6.1 bounds.

leaves.title: Kickers and specialists
leaves.criterion: With the switch at 0, kick accuracy is independent of prior makes and misses in a statistical test.

leaves.title: Culture strength
leaves.criterion: Culture cannot move more than 8 points in a week outside a logged L9 crisis event. No career screen shows the culture value, a band of it, or its term weights. Every reason line shown names a visible fact or a named source.

leaves.title: How messages travel
leaves.criterion: Reception factor stays in 0.5 to 1.3.

leaves.title: Where culture shows on the field
leaves.criterion: A code search finds no read of `culture` in contest resolution outside L3.4.1.

leaves.title: The culture file
leaves.criterion: The file is a data document that validates against a schema and can be edited without code. Two worlds from the same seed have the same files.

leaves.title: Player-only meetings and public complaints
leaves.criterion: Trigger conditions are data. Each event carries the reason shown to the user.

leaves.title: Losing the room
leaves.criterion: The flag cannot set without at least four weeks of visible signs logged first (effort flags on film, L2.5.1 events, or leaks), whether or not any insider passed a warning. The flag itself never appears on a career screen. Modifiers match the list exactly and are removed when the flag clears. In 1,000 simulated AI seasons the state occurs at a rate inside the tuning band set in Q2.

leaves.title: The college locker room
leaves.criterion: All college differences are read from rule and level data keys, none hard-coded. Roster size comes from `league_rules.roster_limit`.

leaves.title: The room as seen from a lower rung
leaves.criterion: Visibility by rung matches the rule in a UI test for each rung.

leaves.title: The rule list set in camp
leaves.criterion: A pro rule row with a fine above its schedule maximum, or for an offence outside the permitted list, can be published only after a warning naming the CBA limit, and each fine issued under it writes one `violation_log` row (L8.2.5). The list has a publish date and a change history. Presets load from data.

leaves.title: The fine schedule
leaves.criterion: The loader reads all schedule years and fails loudly on a malformed cell. A unit test checks the 2026 row against the values above.

leaves.title: Violations and the decision
leaves.criterion: Hazard responds to each input in the stated direction. Every violation that reaches the user has a decision record or an auto-rule record.

leaves.title: Fines and the ladder
leaves.criterion: The amount filled in never exceeds the step maximum, schedule maximum, or daily cap. A fine the user raises past any of them shows the warning, is allowed, and writes one `violation_log` row and a grievance draw (L3.2.5). Offence counts reset at the league year. Tests cover first, second, third, warning-then-second, and an over-limit fine.

leaves.title: Playing time, sending home, and deactivation
leaves.criterion: The football cost of each discipline benching is logged with the replacement's grade. Pro "inactive as punishment" without the predicate or a qualifying single act shows the warning, is allowed, and writes one `violation_log` row. Conduct deactivation weeks plus suspension weeks for one case pass four only through that same warned and logged path. Every deactivation record carries a reason of conduct or ability.

leaves.title: Conduct detrimental and suspension
leaves.criterion: When neither route applies the action stays available behind a warning that states the reason, and using it writes one `violation_log` row (L8.2.5). The same holds for a length past four weeks or a fine past one week's salary.

leaves.title: Grievance and appeal
leaves.criterion: A penalty that passes both tests draws a grievance in under 10 percent of cases in simulation. Results post inside the stated clocks. A stayed suspension leaves the player eligible that week. No salary is deducted for a suspension while its appeal is open. Remedies are drawn only from the closed list.

leaves.title: The consistency value
leaves.criterion: Given a scripted list of cases, the value is reproducible. The pre-decision panel shows the three comparison cases.

leaves.title: The star-player problem
leaves.criterion: The screen always shows both costs with their sources. The +4 event fires at most once per star per season.

leaves.title: Team discipline modifier
leaves.criterion: The multipliers are read only by the four named foul hazards and by no fumble code. off_presnap never leaves 0.95 to 1.05. Clamps hold. Simulated team-season standard deviation of pre-snap fouls per 100 snaps is near 0.30 (observed 0.30, of which noise is 0.25). With every team's coach-controlled part forced to 1.0, that figure falls by less than half.

leaves.title: College discipline
leaves.criterion: With the college model on, no fine UI appears and the pro-only leaves are inert. All switches are data keys. Every case shows its deciding authority. A mandatory-minimum offence closed with less than the school's minimum shows the warning, is allowed, and writes one `violation_log` row (L8.2.5). No mandatory-list offence is ever generated for a real-imported person.

leaves.title: Enforcing someone else's rules
leaves.criterion: Rule editing is locked below head coach. Room consistency exists per position room and appears in the user's evaluation record.

leaves.title: Role list and position chart
leaves.criterion: Every delegable task in H1 has exactly one owner at all times. Removing any role leaves no orphan task. The role set loads from data and differs between pro and college files.

leaves.title: Who calls plays, and changing it
leaves.criterion: Exactly one caller per side at every snap. Overrides are counted and the delay applies only past the threshold. A mid-season change always produces the memory and the news event.

leaves.title: Booth or field
leaves.criterion: Location changes what I7 delivers from that coach. A booth coach never appears in a between-series teaching action.

leaves.title: Staff size and budget
leaves.criterion: Total salaries never exceed budget. Removing a role visibly moves its hours to someone or leaves the task short.

leaves.title: The hiring cycle
leaves.criterion: No timing or count literal for league policy appears in staff code. Lateral blocking is a rules key.

leaves.title: Interviews
leaves.criterion: No interview screen shows a numeric overall for a coach. Every statement about a candidate links to the record rows behind it.

leaves.title: Coaching tree and network graph
leaves.criterion: Ties derive only from shared history. Two coaches with no shared staff have no tie. The network view shows the years behind every tie.

leaves.title: Scheme compatibility
leaves.criterion: The panel's weeks and knowledge loss equal what G4 and G5 then apply.

leaves.title: Assistant contracts
leaves.criterion: Contract terms are data. A flag in the UI marks assistant contract rules as unverified until research closes it.

leaves.title: Staff record and needs
leaves.criterion: Staff use the L1 record type with no extra fields except need types. No staff member has a charisma, motivation skill, or rating number.

leaves.title: Autonomy
leaves.criterion: Autonomy is computed from settings and edits, never set directly. Both room conditions fire only on their stated thresholds.

leaves.title: Disagreement
leaves.criterion: Every objection carries its evidence. Every objection has an outcome row in N3. Public disagreement cannot fire above the trust floor.

leaves.title: Developing assistants
leaves.criterion: The development factor is clamped and is a config value flagged Assumption. Development acts write career rows.

leaves.title: Hours and burnout
leaves.criterion: Diminishing returns apply past the threshold. No task completes without hours.

leaves.title: Delegation has a cost
leaves.criterion: For a fully delegated area, I7 shows only the summary tier. Reviewing a delegated plan raises coach_prep by the reviewed share.

leaves.title: Losing assistants
leaves.criterion: For a promotion the refuse choice is present, marked with the rule, and writes one violation row when used. Departure always triggers succession within the same day.

leaves.title: Firing and interims
leaves.criterion: A test confirms no outcome variable reads "recently fired a coach" directly.

leaves.title: Leaks and loyalty
leaves.criterion: No stored "loyalty" field exists. Labels cite incidents.

leaves.title: College staff
leaves.criterion: The four limits are data keys with status fields. Naming more off-campus recruiters than the cap, or letting a staff member without a slot recruit off campus, is allowed with the L8.2.5 warning and writes one violation row (L8.4.2, T9.5). It is never blocked (audit Part 16b).

leaves.title: The user as an assistant among peers
leaves.criterion: At every rung the user has at least one peer or superior with a relationship record toward him. Head-coach-only decisions (authority acts in the S3 matrix) are locked below that rung. Rule-breaking acts a person can physically do himself are not locked at any rung (L8.2.5).

leaves.title: The team chaplain and faith life
leaves.criterion: 1. No formula for play outcomes, practice gains, or depth chart reads chapel attendance. 2. The user can never view an individual's attendance list or private disposition. 3. Removing the role changes only the outputs named in rules 2 and 3.

leaves.title: Owner profile and needs
leaves.criterion: The page shows no numeric trait. Every label links to incidents. Two owners with different weights produce measurably different event streams in a 20-season test.

leaves.title: Regular and season-review meetings
leaves.criterion: Every raised item links to a real logged decision or result. Promises made appear in the ledger with a test.

leaves.title: Interference
leaves.criterion: Each interference event names the owner interest that produced it in the debug record.

leaves.title: Resource asks
leaves.criterion: Every granted ask changes a real budget or facility value. Conditions appear in the ledger.

leaves.title: Hot-seat signs and dead money
leaves.criterion: Signs never appear without the E4 band that produces them. The dead-money term is a config value flagged Assumption.

leaves.title: Power arrangement and reporting lines
leaves.criterion: Every roster, draft, and contract action checks `power` and renders as a decision or a request. With coach final say, no draft pick, signing, trade, or cut is made for the user's club without the user's own decision or his logged delegation. The offer screen shows the arrangement before the user accepts a job.

leaves.title: Daily requests and the contract word
leaves.criterion: No promise of a contract outcome can be created without the warning. Every refusal carries a reason tied to K7's valuation.

leaves.title: Roster meetings
leaves.criterion: Every evaluation the user states is stored with a date and later outcome.

leaves.title: The trust value
leaves.criterion: Tolerance is a function of trust only. No hidden bonus by coach reputation.

leaves.title: A coach can be traded for
leaves.criterion: A traded coach moves only with pick compensation recorded in the transaction log. Over 100 simulated seasons the number of coach trades falls between 15 and 35, and no trade price exceeds two firsts and two seconds without a logged reason.

leaves.title: Late-season aims that pull apart
leaves.criterion: No late-season request appears before a C3.3.2 flag is set. Every request names the interest that produced it in the debug record. A refused request and its outcome both appear in the season review.

leaves.title: Obligations
leaves.criterion: Every obligation has an hours cost and a decline path.

leaves.title: Team president and other executives
leaves.criterion: Executives are data rows. Clubs can have zero.

leaves.title: Standing upstairs
leaves.criterion: No numeric "capital" is stored or shown anywhere. The read is reproducible from the record.

leaves.title: Athletic director
leaves.criterion: College jobs use this leaf in place of L5.1 with no pro-only fields shown.

leaves.title: President and board
leaves.criterion: The body acts only through events, never as a weekly meeting.

leaves.title: Boosters and donor groups
leaves.criterion: Booster mood changes only through the listed inputs. Rivalry weight is a config value.

leaves.title: Outside payment groups
leaves.criterion: No payment rule literal appears in this module. No forbidden payment action is unavailable in the UI, and each one writes a log row L8.2.5 can read.

leaves.title: Compliance office
leaves.criterion: No rule-breaking action is unavailable in the UI. Every warning cites a rule row. Every clear-rule and grey action is logged and can be detected by L8.2.5.

leaves.title: Public contracts and buyouts
leaves.criterion: Buyout fields are contract data. Values come from `contract_defaults.college` (E3.8.1). A public school's coach contract shows exact figures in the market view; a private school's shows an estimate marked as such.

leaves.title: The chain above you
leaves.criterion: Screens above the user's rung are hidden, not greyed. Interim promotion opens them immediately.

leaves.title: Reporters as people with ties
leaves.criterion: Every team in the user's league window has a beat list from data. No tie is displayed without a logged evidence event. No real-imported person holds a tie.

leaves.title: Goodwill and access
leaves.criterion: A test that sets goodwill to 0 and to 100 for the same seeded season shows identical game results and identical story facts. Only tone tags, narrative build rate, and advance warnings differ.

leaves.title: The coach's public answer and who hears it
leaves.criterion: For a scripted statement the set of people who receive a memory equals the relevance rule exactly. A public and private contradiction always writes one consistency event. No statement writes to D2, D3, or D4.

leaves.title: Background talk and off the record
leaves.criterion: A slanted background talk is checked against the truth record whenever a contradicting public event occurs. The coach's own leaks pass through the same detection code as staff leaks.

leaves.title: Leak propensity and what leaks
leaves.criterion: No leak event exists whose source was not on the item's holder list. With all holder trust at 80 and no ties, a 1,000-season test shows fewer than one small-holder leak a season per team. No leak concerns a non-football item about a real-imported person.

leaves.title: Finding a leaker needs evidence
leaves.criterion: The UI never reveals `source_id` directly. A label about leaking requires at least one confirmed incident. Wrong-suspect punishment is possible in test and writes the stated costs.

leaves.title: Narratives
leaves.criterion: Every narrative lists at least two source events. With identical results, the highest and lowest goodwill bands differ in negative narrative strength by no more than the stated factors. No "hot seat" narrative exists while E4's gap is non-negative unless an owner-side leak event exists.

leaves.title: Pressure reaching the boss
leaves.criterion: With owner sensitivity at its floor, a full-strength negative narrative changes E4 confidence by less than a tenth of what it does at the ceiling. No firing event cites public pressure as its only cause.

leaves.title: Fan mood
leaves.criterion: A single game result changes fan_mood by less than 2 points. No code path reads fan_mood inside a play resolution.

leaves.title: The coach's show and paid media
leaves.criterion: Show income posts only for attended weeks. Show statements create the same routing records as podium statements.

leaves.title: College media, message boards, and booster talk
leaves.criterion: Informal talk has no input from reporter goodwill. Beat size comes from school data. No personal-life story template can select a person flagged under 18.

leaves.title: Media below head coach
leaves.criterion: Session frequency by rung is read from rule data. An off-message statement always produces one head-coach memory event.

leaves.title: Players, coaches, and recruits online
leaves.criterion: 1. Every flagged post has an author, an audience result, and at most one narrative seed. 2. A team game-week ban lowers post volume and raises friction only for people whose disposition values a public voice. 3. No imported person has generated post text. 4. A window breach by an AI club's player is fined on the same table as the user's.

leaves.title: Player agents as people
leaves.criterion: Every pro player has an agent or a self-represented flag. A hopeful statement to an agent creates a promise ledger entry. No more than one agent call a week reaches a head-coach user.

leaves.title: The coach's reputation with agents
leaves.criterion: No stored reputation value exists. The user's view never shows agent_stance or its band. In a test of 1,000 free-agent choices with equal offers, favourable-stance teams win more than half and never more than a starting 65 percent.

leaves.title: Agencies and package deals
leaves.criterion: Shared agency changes interview selection only. The evaluation score of a candidate is identical with and without the shared-agency flag.

leaves.title: Contract-year players
leaves.criterion: No D2, D3, or D4 value and no contest input differs because of contract-year status. The need multipliers are data keys.

leaves.title: Holdouts
leaves.criterion: Daily fines post from league data for the player's contract class. Veteran and free-agent-signee fines carry `waivable = false`: a club waiver or reimbursement of one is allowed with a warning and writes one L8.2.5 violation row. Rookie-contract and option-year fines carry `waivable = true`: the club may reduce or waive them with no violation. Forfeiture never exceeds 25 percent before the first regular-season game. A held-out season with a missed reporting date records no accrued season. Unit tests cover each of the four contract classes for the 2026 values.

leaves.title: Hold-ins
leaves.criterion: No camp-absence fine posts for a player who is present. The user's view never shows the hold-in flag, only participation and the medical read.

leaves.title: Trade requests
leaves.criterion: A trade request changes no attribute. Public requests always create one public `trade_request_public` event, which L6 turns into one story and L2.5.1 reads as one event (one record, two readers; G-49). A request never fires for a player below the stress breakpoint.

leaves.title: Families
leaves.criterion: No person flagged as imported has any family record after generation or import. A recruiting promise broken to a college player writes a full-strength copy to each parent witness. Medical detail is never shown as an option to share when the player's flag is off.

leaves.title: High school coaches
leaves.criterion: hs_coach_stance is derived, not stored, and never shown to the user. The evaluation band change is a data key. A late pulled offer writes the stated memory and its quarter-strength copies.

leaves.title: Representatives for college players
leaves.criterion: With `player_representation` off, no representative objects exist. A role promise with a money term the user's rung does not hold is allowed, warned ("you do not hold this budget"), and logged as an unfunded promise that breaks at full strength if T7 does not fund it.

leaves.title: Agents and families below head coach
leaves.criterion: Agent and high school coach records exist for a user at position-coach rung and persist across a job change. An assistant's role statement creates a ledger entry in his own name.

leaves.title: Community events
leaves.criterion: No community event writes to any attribute or contest input. Every attended event charges its hours.

leaves.title: Injury report inquiry
leaves.criterion: No inquiry exists without a detected H5.2.3 flag. The coach's fine is deducted from his own cash. Blaming staff for the coach's own edit always writes the staff memory and never reduces the fine.

leaves.title: The medical staff's written objection
leaves.criterion: No input can reduce the objection chance for a not-cleared player below the configured floor. Pressing on a concussion case always creates a written objection. Playing a not-cleared player passes through L8.2.5 and is never blocked. Objection records cannot be deleted by any game action.

leaves.title: Public conduct, fines, and the coach's league record
leaves.criterion: No fine text shows a dollar figure for an empty config key. Every finding appears in the coach's league record and persists across job changes. The signal-recording violation, when chosen, passes through L8.2.5 and is punished from this key.

leaves.title: The union representative and work-rule complaints
leaves.criterion: No complaint is filed without a logged violation. A dismissed private word followed by a second violation inside four weeks always files.

leaves.title: Breaking a rule: warn, allow, log, detect, punish
leaves.criterion: No action that breaks a rule is unavailable or greyed out for a person whose job could do it. Every such action writes exactly one `violation_log` row. A violation with an empty `knew` list and no trace has zero detection chance from people sources. No imported AI person appears as an actor. AI and user violations pass through identical code.

leaves.title: Clip submissions to officiating
leaves.criterion: Clip answers never alter any officiating parameter. Each answer is consistent with the truth record at the stated rate.

leaves.title: Rule changes, points of emphasis, and officials in camp
leaves.criterion: With awareness at 100 the foul multiplier is exactly 1. The awareness term is read only by the hazards of the changed or stressed fouls.

leaves.title: League assignments: documentary and international games
leaves.criterion: The camera flag changes only routing and reach. A build with the flag on and off produces identical practice and game results for the same seed.

leaves.title: The conference office
leaves.criterion: No pro config key is read when `body = conference`. Empty values fall back to the default tier.

leaves.title: Compliance cases and head coach responsibility
leaves.criterion: Every detected major staff violation opens a case with the head coach as a party (T9.5.1). No compliance case names a real-imported person. A coach restriction persists across a job change and is readable by E2.

leaves.title: Clinics and the coaching community
leaves.criterion: Every tie created here has a dated source event. No clinic changes an attribute.

leaves.title: League and community below head coach
leaves.criterion: A lower-rung user can be a party to a case only through his own logged act or a contradicted interview answer. League record entries persist across promotions.

leaves.title: Event object and pacing
leaves.criterion: Every crisis outside the two outside classes has a non-empty `cause_events`. In a 1,000-season test no team has more than two open crises without `room_lost`. Hazard functions take no input from win-loss record except where a catalogue leaf names results as the cause.

leaves.title: The real-person guard
leaves.criterion: A fuzz test of one million generated events on a fully imported league produces zero personal-class events and zero quoted text for imported people. The same test finds zero personal-class events with a subject flagged minor. No build setting changes these counts. Every event type in data fails validation if it lacks a guard class.

leaves.title: Early warning
leaves.criterion: With every trust value at 20 and no council, fewer than a starting 10 percent of triggers produce a warning through the trust-based channels (council, open door); position coaches' `report_up` (L4.4.3), medical staff and reporters do not depend on trust, so the case is set with those channels removed or at their minimum. With trust at 80 and a meeting council, more than half do. No warning exists without a pending trigger or a logged false-alarm draw.

leaves.title: Off-field incident
leaves.criterion: No off-field incident has an imported or minor subject. First-report error occurs at the configured rate.

leaves.title: League suspension
leaves.criterion: The game never opens a club discipline case on its own for an act the league has taken up, and closes an open one when the league acts (L3.2.4). One the user opens anyway after the warning is logged through L8.2.5 and open to grievance. Roster handling reads C5 keys.

leaves.title: Injury to a star
leaves.criterion: No contest input other than the lineup changes because of this crisis. Story text for an imported subject contains only injury and timeline facts.

leaves.title: Losing streak
leaves.criterion: A team's play during a streak is identical to its play outside one for the same lineup and the same relationship and morale state (a streak has no effect of its own). Feedback text never attributes a win after a change to the change.

leaves.title: Public dispute
leaves.criterion: Every public dispute creates one L2.5.1 event. No generated quote is attached to an imported person.

leaves.title: Hazing
leaves.criterion: No hazing event has an imported or minor subject. A concealed serious case always carries a later discovery hazard.

leaves.title: Holdout
leaves.criterion: Exactly one crisis exists per holdout record.

leaves.title: Family emergency
leaves.criterion: No performance modifier is read from this crisis. No family emergency exists for a person without a family object.

leaves.title: Team illness
leaves.criterion: Spread uses room membership only. Every player out for illness appears on the report or raises an H5.2.3 flag.

leaves.title: Staff crisis
leaves.criterion: Every task of the absent person has an owner or an "uncovered" mark within the crisis screen. No personal-class cause is assigned to an imported staff member.

leaves.title: Response choices
leaves.criterion: No stored or displayed crisis score or currency exists. Every act in a response maps to an event in exactly one owning system.

leaves.title: Aftermath and the record
leaves.criterion: Every closed crisis has a history entry listing acts and linked outcomes. No label about crisis handling exists without at least one cited incident.

leaves.title: Portal exodus
leaves.criterion: Window dates come from rule data for the year. No more than a configured share of entries is announced on one day.

leaves.title: Academic ineligibility
leaves.criterion: No imported player is ever ruled academically ineligible. The standard is read from rule data.
