leaves.title: Investigation
leaves.criterion: Exactly one crisis per major case. No imported person is an actor.

leaves.title: Booster revolt
leaves.criterion: The crisis opens only from the stated mood condition. A granted demand always writes the precedent memory.

leaves.title: The boss is fired
leaves.criterion: A boss-fired event always opens this crisis for a lower-rung user: it is queued ahead of every other crisis, so it opens in the first week with room under L9.1.1's limit of two open crises (G-50, PR 98). An interim stint writes results to his record and no automatic promotion.

leaves.title: Something you witnessed
leaves.criterion: The item is visible to the user only. Silence about a logged boss violation makes the user a party in any later case on it. No witnessed violation has an imported actor.

leaves.title: Position priority ranking
leaves.criterion: Every job in the installed systems appears exactly once. The side-panel numbers match the play log.

leaves.title: Job profile editor
leaves.criterion: Changing a weight reorders the preview at once. No engine module imports the fit score.

leaves.title: Versatility and role stacking
leaves.criterion: A player with no reps at a second job never carries the tag, whatever his attributes.

leaves.title: Target counts by position
leaves.criterion: The warnings fire for each listed case in a test roster.

leaves.title: Current need by position
leaves.criterion: Removing the best player at a job raises that job's need score.

leaves.title: Depth risk: the next-man-up test
leaves.criterion: The cascade shown equals what the depth chart does when the player is marked out.

leaves.title: Future need: age, contracts, and eligibility
leaves.criterion: A college senior starter always raises a future-need flag at his job.

leaves.title: The needs memo
leaves.criterion: With influence at 100%, the general manager's first move in a test offseason addresses the memo's first item when a legal move exists.

leaves.title: Jobs, slots, and ordering
leaves.criterion: For every personnel group in the week's plan, the chart yields 11 distinct players. Validation lists every group that fails.

leaves.title: Sides, hashes, and travel rules
leaves.criterion: With "field and boundary", the listed field corner aligns to the wide side on every snap of a test drive from each hash. With the ball in the middle, the pair follows the formation-strength rule. Under the college rule set the wide-side width at a hash is 33.3 yd and under the pro rule set 29.75 yd, read from B1 and T10. A motion that crosses the formation after the swap cut-off leaves a travelling pair unswapped and logs it as a late-motion bust risk.

leaves.title: Injury cascade and emergency roles
leaves.criterion: Marking any single active player out mid-game yields a legal 11 for every personnel group without user input. Marking the centre and the backup centre out leaves a guard with centre reps at centre and logs it. A specialist with no practised emergency backup produces a pre-game warning in I1. An emergency holder with fewer than 5 reps in 4 weeks shows a wider operation-time spread in a 1,000-kick test than one with the reps.

leaves.title: Building the game-day 48 from the chart
leaves.criterion: The draft never leaves a core unit unable to field 11 with a named backup when a legal list that does so exists. With 7 healthy offensive linemen the limit shown is 47. Across a simulated season, the mean count of players with at least one snap per team-game is between 45.5 and 47.5 and the median offensive linemen dressed is 8. A healthy veteran inactive three weeks running generates a role-expectation event.

leaves.title: Package depth charts
leaves.criterion: Every package in the week's plan resolves to 11 players. Across a simulated league season with staff default triggers, the fifth defensive back's mean snap share is 59% to 69% and the sixth's 23% to 33%. A coordinator call overrides a personnel trigger on the same snap.

leaves.title: Situational specialists
leaves.criterion: A victory-formation call uses the kneel-down group when it is set. An expected onside kick brings on the hands team when it is set. With no third-down back named, third and long uses the first back on the base chart and I1 listed the gap.

leaves.title: Rotation rules
leaves.criterion: Over a simulated game at normal tempo, actual snap shares are within 8 points of targets. Over a simulated league season with staff default rules, the mean share at each depth rank in rule 1 is reproduced within 5 points for running backs, receivers, tight ends, defensive linemen and defensive backs. Against a no-huddle offense that does not substitute, missed swaps are logged and never forced through illegally.

leaves.title: Snap limits and pitch counts
leaves.criterion: A player with a limit of 30 never logs a 31st snap without an override record. A college player with four appearances triggers a warning before any snap in a fifth regular-season game. A minimum of 10 snaps is met in a game with a margin above 14 points.

leaves.title: Unit charts
leaves.criterion: Every unit resolves to 11 active players in a validation run. Over a simulated season the median number of special-teams-only players per team-game is 7 to 11. No starter is first on more than 2 core units in the staff draft.

leaves.title: Specialists and returners
leaves.criterion: Changing the holder in game week raises the mean of the practice operation times recorded that week. No screen shows the hidden timing value. With an unchanged trio, the recorded field goal operation mean over a season is within 0.05 s of 1.30 s at grade 50 (J9). Three weeks after a change, the penalty has decayed to zero.

leaves.title: Declaring and running a competition
leaves.criterion: The card's weighted grade changes when the same reps are relabelled as against third-team opponents.

leaves.title: Role statements and role talks
leaves.criterion: A starter moved to second on the chart always generates a role-change event with a delivery choice before the next practice. A planned share drop from 70% to 40% labels the player a rotation player. A role change published on the public chart before any talk is costed as learned from the media. A stated condition creates an L1 promise with a review date.

leaves.title: The pro evaluation record and coverage plan
leaves.criterion: - With one scout removed, the average age of looks on his clubs rises and bands widen. - A user request moves a named player to the front of the queue and delays a visible scheduled item. - No field on the board reads a true rating. A test changes a hidden rating with evidence frozen, and the board does not change.

leaves.title: Grade display: the configurable scale and the colour-tier view
leaves.criterion: Switching the view changes no stored data. A player whose band crosses a cut point is drawn hatched.

leaves.title: The ready list by position
leaves.criterion: - Signing a listed player elsewhere removes him from every club's list the same day. - A column never shows a player who is ineligible to sign (suspended, protected practice squad player during the protection window). - The coach's reorder is logged and visible to K7.

leaves.title: Running a workout
leaves.criterion: - After a workout the player's conditioning and speed bands are narrower and his in-pads traits are not. - The workout appears on the wire the same day. - Attending is charged to the coach's time budget.

leaves.title: The daily wire and the claim recommendation
leaves.criterion: - No claim recommendation is shown for a player the cap check rejects. - When two clubs claim, the one higher in the order receives the player. - A vested veteran released before the deadline never appears on the waiver list.

leaves.title: Other clubs' practice squads, and guarding your own
leaves.criterion: No protected player appears as a target during his protection window. A player with a high poach risk who is left unprotected is signed away in a measurable share of test weeks.

leaves.title: The pro report format
leaves.criterion: Every report shows scale grade, role, band, flags, snaps watched, evaluator, and date. Every cited play opens.

leaves.title: What the coach asks for and how his voice is weighed
leaves.criterion: With final say in the contract, an insisted signing that is legal always happens. Without it, the same insistence succeeds at a rate that rises with the L5 relationship value.

leaves.title: Medical records, background, and character checks on veterans
leaves.criterion: No medical detail beyond public history appears before an examination. Every conduct line names a source. No conduct number appears on any screen.

leaves.title: What college programs share with this category
leaves.criterion: At college level the M3.2 to M3.5 screens do not appear. The report format renders for a portal player.

leaves.title: Who looks at whom, and when the coaches join
leaves.criterion: Hours spent on draft work reduce hours available elsewhere in E7. A prospect graded only from games against opponents 20 points weaker carries a wider band than one graded from games against equals.

leaves.title: The draft board and the short board
leaves.criterion: Board and short board sizes load from data. Every user proposal writes a log entry with its reason. Absolute grades on the board never change when the "relative to level" view is toggled.

leaves.title: All-star games
leaves.criterion: A lower-division prospect's band after an all-star week is narrower than before by at least the amount the opponent-strength rule implies.

leaves.title: The combine and pro days
leaves.criterion: After the combine, attendees' measured attributes show bands at the test-noise width. No technique attribute's band narrows from a timed test alone.

leaves.title: Interviews and visits
leaves.criterion: No interview output shows a personality number. Slot limits load from data. Interview slots past the limit cannot be booked. A visit past the limit is allowed after a warning and enters the L8.2.5 detection draw, for AI clubs too.

leaves.title: Background checks, the medical recheck, and private workouts
leaves.criterion: Every recheck writes a second, separate medical evidence entry. No background line lacks a source. No character number appears.

leaves.title: The fit report
leaves.criterion: Every report has an author and a conviction level. The competition note is forced when rule 1 applies. Insist weight falls with the number of insists in one draft. There is no hard cap.

leaves.title: The evaluation record
leaves.criterion: No label appears below the minimum sample. Every label links to the reports behind it. The page holds no numeric skill rating for the evaluator.

leaves.title: The coach in the room
leaves.criterion: Every pick by the user's club has a log entry of his stance, including silence. With final say, no AI choice replaces the user's pick unless his clock expires (C7.3.1 rule 2).

leaves.title: Undrafted calls and the rookie class plan
leaves.criterion: Calls are limited only by the running clock and rival signings. Every promise made is stored with the camp check that will test it.

leaves.title: Knowing the players already
leaves.criterion: The history strip matches a query over the event log. The user's estimates persist across a job change in a save and reload test.

leaves.title: The free agency target list
leaves.criterion: Each entry has a conviction level. Weight falls with list length and insist count, with no hard cap. Every insist gets a pursued-or-refused answer with a cause. Each named target is scored after a starting 2 seasons.

leaves.title: The call and the visit
leaves.criterion: A pitch whose emphasis matches the player's top value moves his choice score. One that does not match moves nothing. Every specific promise is stored with the depth chart check that will test it.

leaves.title: Keep, extend, tag, or let go
leaves.criterion: Must-keep weight falls as marks rise above the threshold. Every view is logged and later compared with the player's next two seasons.

leaves.title: The cap casualty fight
leaves.criterion: Each of the four choices produces a distinct logged outcome. Going over the general manager's head always lowers trust with him.

leaves.title: Asking for a trade, and blocking one
leaves.criterion: Without final say every request receives one of the three answers. The readiness estimate shown equals the D9 projection for that player in the user's system.

leaves.title: What changes at a college job
leaves.criterion: The same list and call screens load with the college rule file and show no contract or cap fields.

leaves.title: The camp calendar and padded-day budget
leaves.criterion: Each rule in C11.2.2 has a test that the grid marks a violating layout, warns once, keeps the day if the coach confirms, and writes one L8.2.5 violation row. A plan with no marked day writes no row. The staff's starting calendar passes every rule in rule 4 with 15 padded practices and at least 8 days off in a three-preseason-game year (the starting calendar has 9: the mandatory day after acclimation, two more to keep one in every 7 days before game 1, one after each of games 1 and 2, and four after the last game, three in a row; G-57 built it). A padded practice cancelled by weather within 60 minutes does not count toward 16. A meeting block that pushes a player's facility day past 11 hours (10 after the second preseason game) is marked. Under the college rule file the counter reads 29 practices and marks a fourth live-contact day inside 7.

leaves.title: The camp install schedule
leaves.criterion: Every concept on the opening-day call sheet has at least one install day and one review day in the plan, or the planner lists it as missing. A run-fit concept installed only in acclimation shows "taught, not trained" until a padded rep is logged. A day with 9 new concepts for a returning staff shows the overload warning.

leaves.title: Camp rep allocation and evaluation reps
leaves.criterion: A player who took only third-team reps has a wider grade band at cutdown than one with the same count of first-team reps.

leaves.title: Position battles in camp
leaves.criterion: A quarterback battle that ends a week later leaves lower unit timing on opening day in a paired test. A competitor with fewer than 150 weighted reps on the decision date shows "thin evidence" on the card. Acclimation reps add nothing to a tackling or run-fit grade.

leaves.title: Live periods, tempo, and injury exposure
leaves.criterion: Across 1,000 simulated camps, the "physical" style produces more camp injuries and higher opening-day tackling grades than the "light" style. A league of 32 clubs on staff default camp plans produces between 35 and 60 preseason concussions a year in practices and preseason games combined (centred on the 2024 figure of 44, starting band, Assumption until the practice-and-game split is sourced).

leaves.title: Joint practices
leaves.criterion: A third joint day in one preseason week is marked, allowed after a warning, and written as an L8.2.5 violation with near-certain detection (joint practices are public).

leaves.title: The preseason snap plan
leaves.criterion: A player with a plan of zero snaps logs none. Every bubble player under the staff draft logs at least 20 scrimmage snaps over three preseason games unless injured. Across AI clubs on default styles, the league-wide share of Week 1 starters with zero preseason snaps falls between 20% and 50% (Assumption band around the 2019 figure, to be refined when a post-2021 figure is sourced).

leaves.title: What to show and what to hide
leaves.criterion: A held play never appears in any opponent's scouting database before it is first called. A play run only in a joint practice appears in exactly one opponent's database. A held play's first regular-season call shows the timing multiplier in the play record.

leaves.title: Evaluating preseason film
leaves.criterion: The report's opposition-level shares sum to 100% for every player. The same snaps relabelled as against third-unit opponents lower the weighted grade's evidence and widen the band. A player's special teams grade appears separately from his scrimmage grade.

leaves.title: The roster-building board
leaves.criterion: The board cannot be submitted with 54, or with a practice squad target who is ineligible. A seventh practice squad target with unlimited experience is marked ineligible. A board with 7 offensive linemen shows that only 47 can dress (M2.1.4).

leaves.title: The cutdown meetings
leaves.criterion: Each bubble player has at least one recorded staff opinion before the deadline. Across many simulated meetings, assistants' grades of their own players average higher than the true grade by the configured bias, and the head coach never sees the bias as a number.

leaves.title: Releasing players
leaves.criterion: Every release has a delivery method recorded. Across many cutdowns, invited players told in person accept practice squad offers more often than those told by message, all else equal.

leaves.title: Claims and the practice squad, the day after
leaves.criterion: Claim risk shown as high is realised more often than low across 1,000 simulated cutdowns. No practice squad signing of another club's waived player happens before the claim deadline. A claim filed without naming a player to release is rejected by C5.

leaves.title: Reporting tests, weigh-ins, and camp setting
leaves.criterion: A player below the conditioning line who is let through can be put in padded practice, with higher fatigue and soft-tissue exposure (D10, D11). One who is held out stays out of padded work until he passes.

leaves.title: The mock game
leaves.criterion: Teams with no mock game and no preseason snaps for the operation commit more pre-snap administrative fouls in weeks 1 and 2 across a 1,000-season test. A new staff with no mock game starts week 1 at readiness 0.1 plus its preseason games called, and its week-1 administrative error multiplier is above 1.3.

leaves.title: Playback of a play record
leaves.criterion: Playback of a stored play is identical on two machines. Stepping backward and forward returns the same frame. In the All-22 view all 22 markers are inside the frame on every tick from snap to whistle for at least 99% of plays in a season of film (the rest are long breakaways, where the ball carrier and the nearest pursuer stay in frame). Switching views on a paused frame keeps the same tick.

leaves.title: Overlays
leaves.criterion: No screen shows an opponent's true assignment or call, in any mode outside the developer build.

leaves.title: The play database and filters
leaves.criterion: Every play row holds all 16 base-set fields. The filter "own team, concept X, against coverage Y" returns exactly the plays whose call record is X and whose charted coverage is Y. The opponent's true coverage is used only in the coaching school and the developer build (audit Part 17, was: matched against the truth record).

leaves.title: Building and sharing a cut-up
leaves.criterion: A cut-up keeps working after the season it came from is archived. Each standard template, run on a season of film with known breakdown rows, returns exactly the plays its filter names. A reel with uncharted plays shows the count of uncharted plays.

leaves.title: Tags, notes, and telestration
leaves.criterion: Deleting an annotation leaves the play record's checksum unchanged.

leaves.title: The play breakdown
leaves.criterion: Over a season, the mean of the variance component is within a small tolerance of zero for each team. A known bust (forced mental error in a test) is always flagged.

leaves.title: Busts and responsibility
leaves.criterion: In the coaching school's truth mode every play with a truth-record error shows exactly that error. No career screen offers truth mode.

leaves.title: The play-by-play grading sheet
leaves.criterion: A coach with perfect skill and no bias produces a sheet equal to the truth record. Lower skill produces more disagreements, in proportion. Each of the four loaf patterns, forced in a scripted play, produces a candidate loaf; a player knocked down who rises within 2 s and pursues produces none. The assignment percentage on a sheet equals correct-assignment snaps divided by snaps played, to one decimal.

leaves.title: The grade scale and what goes beside it
leaves.criterion: Switching the scale changes every grade display and no stored data. A sheet of known marks shows the same assignment percentage and the same 0 to 4 mean in every view.

leaves.title: Production against grade
leaves.criterion: A scripted game with two unblocked sacks produces the note.

leaves.title: Showing grades to players
leaves.criterion: The policy is recorded and each effect is traceable to it in the player's log.

leaves.title: From film to the correction list
leaves.criterion: In a paired test, a corrected error repeats less often over the next four games than the same error left uncorrected.

leaves.title: What film exists, when, and what it costs to watch
leaves.criterion: Hours spent on film appear in the weekly time ledger. With every film job kept by the user and no delegation, a full game week's film (own game graded for one position room, 4 opponent games charted, standard reels built) costs more hours than an E7 week leaves after meetings and practice, so delegation is needed.

leaves.title: Stat definitions and the box score
leaves.criterion: - The sum of player rushing yards equals team rushing yards in every game of a 1,000-game test. - Changing a stat definition file and recomputing a saved season changes only that stat. - Every box score number opens a play list whose count matches the number.

leaves.title: Charted statistics
leaves.criterion: Own-team charted pressure totals match engine truth exactly. Opponent charted totals differ from truth by a rate that falls as charter skill rises.

leaves.title: The expected points model
leaves.criterion: - First and 10 expected points rise monotonically from the offense's own 1 to the opponent's 1. - On held-out simulated games, predicted class shares match observed shares within 1 percentage point in every yard-line decile. - Changing a kickoff rule in the rule set and refitting changes the value of the kickoff state.

leaves.title: The win probability model
leaves.criterion: - Calibration: across held-out games, states predicted at 70 to 75 percent are won 70 to 75 percent of the time, and likewise for every 5-point band. - A kneel-down state with a lead and no opponent timeouts returns at least 0.99.

leaves.title: Success rate, explosive plays, and the per-play measures
leaves.criterion: Switching the success definition changes success columns everywhere and nothing else.

leaves.title: The shared tendency store
leaves.criterion: The same query on the user's own team from G8 and from an opponent's AI returns identical counts when charter error is set to zero.

leaves.title: Building the decision chart during the week
leaves.criterion: - With a kicker whose range is cut by 5 yards, the field goal cells at the edge of range flip. - Every cell marked "go" has a computed `wp` for go at least as high as the other options. - Each user edit appears in the decision log with its reason.

leaves.title: Variance strategy for underdogs and favourites
leaves.criterion: In a 10,000-game test with a 10-point underdog, the "shorten the game" lever raises the underdog's win share by a measurable amount. With staff estimates set equal to the true ratings (a test setting only), the brief's estimate lies within two standard errors of it.

leaves.title: Speed, distance, and load from practice and games
leaves.criterion: A player's game distance equals the path length of his stored positions within 1 percent. Doubling a practice period's reps doubles its load contribution.

leaves.title: The team-strength estimate
leaves.criterion: - Across 200 simulated seasons, predicted margins have a mean error near zero and beat a "last season's record" baseline in mean absolute error. - Removing a starting quarterback changes the team's offense term the same week.

leaves.title: Who produces the numbers, by rung and level
leaves.criterion: Removing the analytics staff from a pro club removes the weekly chart from the Friday schedule and leaves N3 scoring unchanged.

leaves.title: The limits-of-the-model note
leaves.criterion: A fourth-down decision with a 0.4-point modelled edge and a 1.0-point error band is recorded as "coach's call" in the decision log whichever way the user goes.

leaves.title: Label definitions and the evaluation function
leaves.criterion: - Deleting every label record and recomputing from the logs reproduces them exactly. - Running a season with the label engine switched off produces identical game results and AI decisions with the same seed. - A generated coach whose profile is aggressive holds no "aggressive" label before he has the minimum sample of decisions. - A coach whose fourth-down rate moves to league average loses the label within two half-lives. - A public observer and a former colleague can hold different label sets for the same person, and each set traces to the events that observer saw.

leaves.title: Record schema
leaves.criterion: Every record validates against the schema. Replaying a save reproduces identical records.

leaves.title: Capturing the information set
leaves.criterion: A test that changes scouting data after a game leaves all earlier records' information fields unchanged.

leaves.title: Game-day decision catalogue
leaves.criterion: A full game produces at least one record for every snap on the side of the ball the user calls, and a record for every fourth down and every try.

leaves.title: Weekly and program decision catalogue
leaves.criterion: Each listed owner emits a record in an integration test week.

leaves.title: Scoring game-management decisions
leaves.criterion: For a table of 200 situations with hand-checked option values, the class matches. No decision inside the range is ever classed clearly wrong.

leaves.title: Scoring play calls
leaves.criterion: Foresight value never uses the truth record. A unit test that swaps the opponent's actual call leaves it unchanged.

leaves.title: Decisions with no model
leaves.criterion: Every roster cut of a player who later plays elsewhere gets a follow-up entry.

leaves.title: The game decision report
leaves.criterion: The report's totals equal the sums of its listed records.

leaves.title: Season and career patterns
leaves.criterion: No pattern statement is generated from fewer than the minimum count.

leaves.title: Append-only storage and tamper evidence
leaves.criterion: Changing any stored record breaks verification of the chain.

leaves.title: The decision components
leaves.criterion: Every component lists its inputs, and each input is a logged record that can be opened from the decision record page.

leaves.title: Decision-based scoring
leaves.criterion: Replaying the same decisions with different random outcomes (different engine seeds for play results) leaves every component score unchanged. The EP and WP models pass the 0.01 calibration check on three held-out simulated seasons. A fourth down whose WP edge is 1.4 points is logged as a close call and scores zero whichever option is taken; one whose edge is 3 points with an interval above zero scores a loss of 3 points if the worse option is taken.

leaves.title: Adjusting for roster and opponent
leaves.criterion: Giving the user's roster to the reference coach for the same schedule yields a median percentile near 50 across many runs (between 45 and 55 over 100 test seasons). A season of 6 games under one coach shows "too few games to say".

leaves.title: The reference coach
leaves.criterion: The reference coach's own decisions, scored against itself, score 50 on every component within its range. An AI coach set to follow the model on every clear fourth down scores above 50 on game management against the reference coach over a season of fourth downs.

leaves.title: Certified conditions
leaves.criterion: With the badge on, none of the locked settings can be changed. Every voiding condition has a test.

leaves.title: Certified scenario packs (the combine for coaches)
leaves.criterion: Two runs with the same inputs give the same score. The reference coach's score on each pack is published with the pack. A second attempt is displayed as attempt 2 and leaves the attempt 1 score as the certified one. No pack part offers pause in a timed game situation.

leaves.title: The coaching record file
leaves.criterion: The data file's chain verifies with the published verification tool. Altering one record makes verification fail. Removing one of the 5 largest losses from the evidence pages is not possible in the export screen. The export holds no personal data beyond the typed name.

leaves.title: Work samples
leaves.criterion: Each listed object exports to a page that prints on one or two sheets.

leaves.title: What the decision record score does not show
leaves.criterion: The note appears on the decision record page and on page one of every export. Each of the five limits shows the record's own numbers. A component with 30 scored decisions carries the "mostly prior" flag.

leaves.title: Curriculum structure
leaves.criterion: - Every lesson's listed terms exist in the glossary, and every listed F, G, or B id resolves. - Passing every lesson in a course marks the course passed. - A save with all lessons mastered and a save with none produce identical career outcomes from identical inputs.

leaves.title: Lesson format and the graded scenario
leaves.criterion: - Every graded scenario has a stored best answer with a margin and seed count. - Two attempts at the same lesson draw different situations at least 80 percent of the time. - A timed answer given after the clock expires is recorded as a delay of game, as it would be in a game.

leaves.title: Term links, hover cards, and "teach me this"
leaves.criterion: A scan of every screen string in the build finds no glossary term without a link. Every "Teach me this" button opens an existing lesson or is hidden.

leaves.title: Call-speed drill
leaves.criterion: A call made after the cut-off time is marked late. Session results persist and chart.

leaves.title: Coverage and front recognition on film
leaves.criterion: Every clip's truth label matches the call record that generated it. Weak-area weighting changes the next session's mix.

leaves.title: Clock and situation problems
leaves.criterion: For 1,000 generated kneel-down problems, the stored answer equals the result of simulating the kneel-downs on the engine.

leaves.title: Protection identification
leaves.criterion: Each stored answer leaves no rusher unaccounted for when run through the J4 assignment rules, or is marked "hot".

leaves.title: The personal lesson picker
leaves.criterion: A seeded log with one large repeated error produces that pattern as the top card with the right lesson. A log with no pattern outside the band produces no card.

leaves.title: One difficulty, and how the ladder teaches
leaves.criterion: - The build contains no difficulty option. A search of settings data finds none. - Gaining a duty in a test career produces its lesson offer exactly once. - Two saves at different rungs with the same seed and the same matchup produce the same game result when the same calls are made.

leaves.title: Watching the coaches above you
leaves.criterion: Every "why" answer maps to reason codes stored at the time of the call. Changing the AI coach's profile changes the reasons given in the same situation.

leaves.title: Hubs
leaves.criterion: 1. Every screen in the registry belongs to exactly one hub. 2. Each hub opens with its number key from any non-modal screen in under 100 ms. 3. No hub is ever removed from the bar during a save's life.

leaves.title: Screen registry
leaves.criterion: 1. Removing a screen record removes it from the hub bar, palette, and help with no code change. 2. The validation catches a duplicated route in a test file. 3. Every v1 screen named in O2, O3, and O4 has a registry record.

leaves.title: Routes, parameters, and deep links
leaves.criterion: 1. Reloading the browser build on any route restores the same screen, tab, sort, and filter. 2. An automated crawl opens every registered route with sample IDs and finds no error.

leaves.title: Today view
leaves.criterion: 1. For a sample week, the blocks shown equal the H1 schedule for that day in order and hours. 2. Hours left equals the E7 budget minus spent hours to the minute.

leaves.title: Inbox and decision queue
leaves.criterion: 1. Time cannot advance past a must item's deadline until it is answered. 2. A should item left unanswered resolves to its stated default and is logged as "defaulted". 3. Every item's sender is a real entity with a card.

leaves.title: Advancing time
leaves.criterion: 1. An advance from Monday to game day with full delegation completes with no user input and files a digest. 2. The stop button halts within one schedule block. 3. Two advances with the same seed and choices produce identical world state (P1 determinism).

leaves.title: Global keys and the hub bar
leaves.criterion: 1. Any screen is reachable in two key presses from any other non-modal screen. 2. `?` lists every active key on the current screen and nothing inactive.

leaves.title: Command palette and search
leaves.criterion: 1. Results appear within 50 ms of a keystroke with a full league loaded (about 1,700 active players plus staff, starting estimate). 2. Typing a jersey number and a position finds the player.

leaves.title: History, back, and breadcrumbs
leaves.criterion: Following ten links and pressing back ten times returns to the start with every view state intact.

leaves.title: Entity links and hover cards
leaves.criterion: 1. No plain-text player name appears on any screen in an automated scan. Every one is a link. 2. No hover card field reads a true (hidden) attribute. A test asserts the data source of each field.

leaves.title: Calendar phase and what is open
leaves.criterion: For each phase in a test table, every screen's actions are enabled or disabled as the table says.

leaves.title: Game-day mode
leaves.criterion: 1. No route outside the Game hub can be opened between kickoff and the end of the game. 2. Killing the process mid-play and restarting resumes at the previous dead ball with identical state.

leaves.title: Alerts
leaves.criterion: No alert moves focus or blocks input in an automated input test.

leaves.title: Window layout and panels
leaves.criterion: 1. Every registered screen renders without clipping or horizontal scroll at 1280 by 720. 2. Column and panel choices survive a restart.

leaves.title: Start screen, saves, and new career
leaves.criterion: 1. A new career with all defaults reaches the office screen in under 60 s of user time. 2. Two new careers from the same seed string and choices have identical opening world state hashes.

leaves.title: Help overlay and glossary access
leaves.criterion: Every screen in the registry has help text. Every glossary term found in UI text is linked.

leaves.title: Regions
leaves.criterion: 1. No region changes position or size between snaps in a recorded full game. 2. At 1280 by 720 every region is readable with no scrolling inside the situation strip or hint bar.

leaves.title: Sideline panel
leaves.criterion: An automated check finds no field in this panel sourced from the truth layer or from the opponent's call object.

leaves.title: Booth line and messages
leaves.criterion: Message text never exceeds one line at the minimum window. Each message in the log records whether it was on screen before the call was confirmed.

leaves.title: Sheet rendering and box focus
leaves.criterion: 1. The on-screen grid equals the G7 layout cell for cell for three sample sheets. 2. Focus lands on the expected box within one frame of the dead-ball record for the 50-state table used in I2.2.2.

leaves.title: Key hints and call chords
leaves.criterion: Any entry on a 20-box, 200-entry sheet is selected in at most 2 key presses and confirmed with 1 more (matches I2.6.3).

leaves.title: Call builder line and confirm
leaves.criterion: 1. Time from the confirm key to the "sent" state is under 50 ms. 2. The call string shown equals the G4 string for 100 sample calls.

leaves.title: Defensive and special teams sheets
leaves.criterion: A full game can be called on offense, defense, and special teams with the keyboard only.

leaves.title: Field geometry and orientation
leaves.criterion: 1. Measured on screen, the hash-to-hash distance is 18.5 feet at the drawn scale within one pixel (160 feet minus two times 70 feet 9 inches). 2. A marker placed at a known world coordinate lands on the correct yard line and lateral position in all three orientations.

leaves.title: Player and ball markers
leaves.criterion: 1. All 22 numbers are readable in a screenshot at the minimum window with the default camera. 2. With colour removed (greyscale test) offense and defense are still told apart by shape or outline.

leaves.title: The pre-snap look
leaves.criterion: A scan of the pre-snap render data finds positions and facings only. No assignment, coverage, or call data is present in the message from the worker before the snap.

leaves.title: Play playback
leaves.criterion: 1. Marker positions at each tick boundary equal the engine's positions exactly (compared by test hook). 2. Playback holds 60 frames per second with 22 markers and all cues on the minimum hardware target in P6. 3. With playback skipped, the game result and clock are identical to the watched version for the same seed.

leaves.title: Result line and flags
leaves.criterion: For a 500-play sample the line's down, distance, and spot equal the dead-ball record in every case.

leaves.title: Timeout and challenge controls
leaves.criterion: Across a rule test table of 40 game states, each control is enabled exactly when the rule engine says the action is legal.

leaves.title: Fourth down, try, and kick decisions
leaves.criterion: Every fourth down, try, and kickoff in a logged game has a decision record naming who decided (user, standing rule, or delegate).

leaves.title: Penalty choices
leaves.criterion: For each case in the B8 enforcement test set, the prompt's options equal the engine's options in number and resulting situation.

leaves.title: Coin toss, halftime, and end-of-game prompts
leaves.criterion: Every legal toss option in B1 can be chosen and leads to the correct kickoff setup.

leaves.title: Latency budgets
leaves.criterion: An automated input test over 500 simulated calls records no response over budget at the 99th percentile.

leaves.title: Hint bar
leaves.criterion: After remapping any console key the hint bar shows the new key.

leaves.title: Mistake guards
leaves.criterion: With guards on, a single tap of the challenge key throws no flag. A held key does.

leaves.title: Viewer layout and transport
leaves.criterion: Stepping forward N ticks then back N ticks returns to the same frame. A re-simulated play equals the stored trajectory bit for bit.

leaves.title: Overlays
leaves.criterion: With all overlays on, 60 frames per second holds on the minimum target. Opponent truth-layer data is absent from the viewer's data for opponent plays.

leaves.title: Layout
leaves.criterion: 1. Every field of the play schema (P3) can be set from this screen. 2. A play built here and reopened renders identically.

leaves.title: Drawing and dragging
leaves.criterion: 1. Each of the standard routes in F6 can be drawn in three pointer actions or fewer and is recognised by name. 2. A play can be built from scratch with the keyboard alone. 3. The alignment readout equals the stored alignment values for 50 sampled drags.

leaves.title: Validator panel
leaves.criterion: For the G1 validation test set, the panel shows exactly the expected messages for every case. Results appear within 300 ms of an edit.

leaves.title: Test bench tab
leaves.criterion: 1. 500 runs complete within the P6 batch budget. 2. Re-running the same batch with the same seed gives identical results. 3. No bench output field exposes an opponent's true attribute.

leaves.title: Layout and call assembly
leaves.criterion: For each formation in the switcher set, every gap and every eligible receiver has a named responsible defender or a validator message.

leaves.title: Playbook library
leaves.criterion: Filtering to "3rd down, 11 personnel, installed" on a 1,000-play book returns in under 100 ms.

leaves.title: Install board
leaves.criterion: The load total per day equals G5's formula for a sample week.

leaves.title: Game plan builder screen
leaves.criterion: Plan totals equal the sums of the listed entries. A delegated draft arrives as a proposal and changes nothing until accepted.

leaves.title: Call sheet editor
leaves.criterion: 1. The coverage map classifies every cell of a 4 downs by 6 distance buckets by 5 zones table. 2. The sheet shown in the game (O2.2.1) is identical to the editor's layout.

leaves.title: Print and export view
leaves.criterion: A printed sheet matches the on-screen grid in box positions and entry order.

leaves.title: Week calendar and period blocks
leaves.criterion: A plan that breaks an H3 limit saves after one warning and produces exactly one violation row. Period times never overlap.

leaves.title: Projection panel
leaves.criterion: With a perfect-accuracy test staff, projected readiness equals the realised mean readiness over 200 simulated weeks within the model's stated tolerance.

leaves.title: Tendency table
leaves.criterion: Counts in any cell equal a direct query of the charted records. No opponent truth-layer field is reachable from this screen.

leaves.title: Drafts, undo, and publishing
leaves.criterion: Undo returns the draft to a byte-identical earlier state. A crash during editing loses no more than the last edit.

leaves.title: Hours and delegation shown on every planning screen
leaves.criterion: The ledger total equals the sum of charged actions for a scripted week.

leaves.title: Card layout
leaves.criterion: 1. A test asserts that the card's read model schema has no field from the true-attribute schema. 2. Opening a card takes under 100 ms.

leaves.title: Grades tab
leaves.criterion: For a test player with known true values, the displayed grade differs from truth by the D6 error model, and the band covers the truth at the D6 stated rate over 1,000 generated players.

leaves.title: Performance and knowledge tabs
leaves.criterion: Every statistic equals a direct query of the play records. Every mental error link opens the right play.

leaves.title: Health and load tab
leaves.criterion: No control on this tab changes clearance. Return range always shows two bounds.

leaves.title: Person tab
leaves.criterion: Every morale reason shown maps to a real event or state in the save. Imported players have no off-field fields in their read model.

leaves.title: Roster table
leaves.criterion: Counters equal direct counts of the roster lists.

leaves.title: Depth chart editor
leaves.criterion: Every package has 11 named players or a flag. The chart used by the engine equals the published chart.

leaves.title: Staff list and coach card
leaves.criterion: The coach card read model has no binding to a K2 field and no skill value, true or estimated.

leaves.title: Delegation settings
leaves.criterion: The projected hours equal E7's computation for three preset tables.

leaves.title: Locker room view
leaves.criterion: Every issue shown has a source entity. Issues not yet reported to the coach are absent from the read model.

leaves.title: Meeting and conversation screen
leaves.criterion: Every conversation in the data files renders with at least two responses. Every promise made appears in the promise tracker.

leaves.title: Owner and general manager view
leaves.criterion: No hot-seat numeric value exists in the read model.

leaves.title: Media screen
leaves.criterion: Each required session appears in the Office agenda (O1.2.1). A story marked as caused by the coach links to the answer that caused it.

leaves.title: Career and reputation
leaves.criterion: The record equals league standings data. The export validates against the N4 format. The page contains no element bound to a skill value.

leaves.title: Personal finance
leaves.criterion: Net worth equals assets minus debts from the E6 ledger at every date. Changing any finance choice changes no football state (asserted by a state-diff test).

leaves.title: Time, energy, health, and family
leaves.criterion: Every active effect of the coach's state is listed on the screen, and a test confirms no unlisted effect exists in the effect table.

leaves.title: Keyboard-first rule
leaves.criterion: An automated run completes a new career, a game week, and a full game using only synthetic key events.

leaves.title: Mouse, controller, and touch
leaves.tag: v1 mouse, v2 controller and touch
leaves.criterion: A full game can be called with the mouse only. Median mouse call time in the drill is reported beside the keyboard time.

leaves.title: Key map data and contexts
leaves.criterion: A validation test finds no collisions in the default map for any context. Every action in the registry of commands has a binding or is marked "no default".

leaves.title: Remapping and profiles
leaves.criterion: After remapping, the hint bar, help overlay, and sheet hints all show the new key.

leaves.title: Store, scopes, and groups
leaves.criterion: Every setting in the schema appears once on the screen. Changing a save-scope setting writes to the save header and to the decision log if mid-season.

leaves.title: Display and audio settings
leaves.criterion: The same seed produces identical game results on all three performance tiers.

leaves.title: Playback and stoppage settings
leaves.criterion: With the same seed and the same calls confirmed at the same simulated times, all playback options produce the same final score. No setting or key pauses the play clock during a game.

leaves.title: Vision
leaves.criterion: An automated contrast check passes on all registered screens in all themes. A greyscale screenshot test passes on the field view (O2.3.2).

leaves.title: Motion, hearing, and motor
leaves.criterion: Every interactive control has a label. Every audio cue has a visual cue listed in a data table.

leaves.title: Local data and export
leaves.criterion: A network monitor records zero requests during a full v1 session after the initial page load of the browser build.

leaves.title: Diagnostics and bug bundle
leaves.criterion: Replaying a bundle in the headless runner reaches the same state hash as the session that wrote it.

leaves.title: Presentation priority rule
leaves.criterion: Every interface task in the roadmap carries its rank from this list.

leaves.title: Screen density and layout grid
leaves.criterion: A 53-row roster table shows at least 25 rows without scrolling at 1280 by 720 and 100% scale.

leaves.title: Token file
leaves.criterion: Switching theme changes every screen with no restart. The lint check passes.

leaves.title: Marker table
leaves.criterion: Every position in D1 maps to a marker row. The greyscale test in O2.3.2 passes.

leaves.title: Diagram line symbols
leaves.criterion: Every assignment type in J4 has a symbol. A diagram printed in black and white loses no information.

leaves.title: What may move
leaves.criterion: A test compares rendered marker positions at tick boundaries with engine positions and finds no difference. No transition in the interface exceeds 120 ms.

leaves.title: Number display rules
leaves.criterion: An automated scan of every screen finds no rate without a sample size and no estimate without a band.

leaves.title: Wording rules and templates
leaves.criterion: A scan finds no user-facing string literal in component code. Switching a save's level swaps every level-keyed term.

leaves.title: Adopted practices
leaves.criterion: Each row's owner leaf exists and covers the practice.

leaves.title: Screen permission states
leaves.criterion: 1. For each rung in a test table, every registered screen resolves to exactly one state. 2. No command for a task the user does not own is accepted by the core, even if sent directly.

leaves.title: The assignment list
leaves.criterion: For a scripted graduate assistant week, every assignment appears with a due time, can be submitted, and returns a grade.

leaves.title: Hub contents by rung
leaves.criterion: Each rung in the default route table opens ten valid routes.

leaves.title: Film tagging screen
leaves.criterion: With a scripted perfect tagger the grade is 100%. Tag time per play is recorded. No truth field is in the screen's data before or after submission in a career.

leaves.title: Scout card and report builders
leaves.criterion: A card that matches the true play scores 100%. A deliberately wrong card lowers the modelled readiness against that play in a test.

leaves.title: Position room screens
leaves.criterion: Grading a 60-snap game for five players can be done with the keyboard alone. The evaluation score responds to deliberately wrong grades in a test.

leaves.title: Seat layouts
leaves.criterion: A full game can be played from each seat. Each seat produces a graded record. The game's pace is unchanged by a user who does nothing in a non-calling seat.

leaves.title: Attention limit and weather delay
leaves.criterion: Messages from unselected channels never appear on the booth line. A delay event pauses the game clock and opens the prompt.

leaves.title: Recruiting screens
leaves.criterion: An action outside its contact period warns with the rule named, is allowed, and produces exactly one violation row.

leaves.title: Eligibility, transfers, and program screens
leaves.criterion: Switching a test save between level keys swaps the limit set and the program screen with no code path specific to a level.

leaves.title: Field and rule differences on screen
leaves.criterion: A scan finds no hard-coded field landmark in interface code. A college save draws hashes at the T1 value.

leaves.title: Job market and career screens
leaves.criterion: A scripted career moves through at least four rungs and two levels using only these screens for job changes.

leaves.title: People import and world setup screens
leaves.criterion: A pack with an image field fails validation. Every imported person has the origin flag in his record.

leaves.title: Long-run simulation controls
leaves.criterion: A 20-season advance completes within the P6 budget for long runs and stops at every must event.

leaves.title: The core is pure
leaves.criterion: 1. A lint rule fails the build when a core package references a banned global (clock, random, file, network, transcendental math). 2. Every core package's test suite runs in a bare JavaScript runtime with no browser or desktop APIs present.

leaves.title: Football knowledge is data
leaves.criterion: 1. Swapping the pro rule-set file for the college file changes rulings in the rule-case tests with no code change. 2. A search of core code for the words "college", "pro", "NFL", or "NCAA" in a conditional returns nothing.

leaves.title: One direction of flow
leaves.criterion: 1. The interface package cannot import `store` or any core package's internals (P1.2.2). 2. Replaying the command log of any test save from its starting state gives a state hash equal to the saved one.

leaves.title: Hidden truth stays in the core
leaves.criterion: 1. An automated scan of every read-model type finds no field of class `truth`. 2. A recording of all worker-to-main messages over a full simulated game contains no value equal to a true attribute of an opposing player beyond chance.

leaves.title: Everything is reproducible
leaves.criterion: 1. The golden-seed set (Q1.3.1) gives byte-identical trajectories on Windows, Linux, and the browser build. macOS is recorded as not tested until a Mac is available, because the only test machines are Marlon's Windows PC and the Linux cloud sandbox (audit Part 17 PQRA, P17-1). 2. A full simulated season run twice on one machine, once with 1 worker and once with 8, gives the same final state hash.

leaves.title: Package table
leaves.criterion: The workspace has exactly the packages in this table, and each has a one-paragraph readme naming its bible categories.

leaves.title: Dependency lint
leaves.criterion: A deliberately banned import in a test branch fails continuous integration with a message naming the rule.

leaves.title: Command contract
leaves.criterion: 1. Every command type has a schema, a permission row, and at least one accept and one reject test. 2. A fuzz test sends 100,000 random payloads and the state invariant checks (Q1.2.2) never fail.

leaves.title: Read-model contract
leaves.criterion: 1. The truth-field scan in P1.1.4 passes. 2. Every screen in the registry (O1.1.2) lists the read-model keys it uses, and no screen imports anything else from the core. 3. Changing the observer from head coach to position coach on one test save changes `permission` values and nothing in the screen code.

leaves.title: Level and rule keys
leaves.criterion: 1. The rule-case suite (Q1.1.1) runs against both files, and every case names the keys it exercises. 2. A game can be started with the college rule set between two pro rosters and completes with no error.

leaves.title: Stack table
leaves.criterion: Phase 0 gate (R1.2.1): a seeded dummy game replays byte-identically in every shell and the browser, and a save written on one opens on the others.

leaves.title: Main thread: interface only
leaves.criterion: With a league week simulating in the pool, a recorded input trace shows no main-thread task over 50 ms.

leaves.title: World worker
leaves.criterion: Killing the world worker mid-game in a test and restarting loses no acknowledged command.

leaves.title: Simulation pool
leaves.criterion: The same week simulated with pool sizes 1, 2, and 8 gives identical state hashes.

leaves.title: Message envelope and types
leaves.criterion: The message recorder used by P1.1.4's acceptance test can capture and replay a full session.

leaves.title: Trajectory format
leaves.criterion: 1. Encode then decode returns positions within 0.005 yd of the rounded engine values. 2. Re-simulating a stored play from its seed gives a buffer byte-identical to the stored one (same engine version).

leaves.title: Desktop shell
leaves.criterion: Phase 0 gate. Install, new career, save, quit, relaunch, load works on Windows and Linux. macOS is recorded as not tested until a Mac is available (R1.2.1 gate 1).

leaves.title: Browser build
leaves.criterion: The determinism tests and the full keyboard-only game test (Q1.5.2) pass in the current releases of the three major browser engines.

leaves.title: Second window
leaves.criterion: A play called in the main window updates the film viewer in the second window with no extra command.

leaves.title: Headless runner
leaves.criterion: `replay` of a bug bundle made in the desktop shell reproduces the same state hash.

leaves.title: Three kinds of data
leaves.criterion: For any stored game, statistics recomputed from play rows equal the cached ones. After archiving, summary rows equal a recomputation made just before thinning.

leaves.title: IDs, references, visibility, units
leaves.criterion: Schema lint: every field has a visibility class and, where numeric, a unit or scale name.

leaves.title: World, competition, team
leaves.criterion: A generated world validates, and a scan of team identity fields against the blocked-terms list (A6.2.2) finds nothing.

leaves.title: Person
leaves.criterion: 1. A 30-season headless run with an imported pack produces zero protected events on imported people (Q1.6.2). 2. A player retiring and taking a coaching job keeps one ID, and his page shows both histories. 3. Schema validation fails for a person with `origin: user` that has `coaching.hidden`, `scouting.evaluationSkill`, or any `coaching` field named skill, rating, level, competency, experience, or points.

leaves.title: PersonView and knowledge of people
leaves.criterion: Two organisations' views of the same prospect differ, and both differ from truth, in a generated draft class. Mean error shrinks as evidence count rises.

leaves.title: Jobs, rosters, depth, contracts, knowledge
leaves.criterion: Roster-limit validators run on every roster command and at each calendar deadline, using league-rules keys only.

leaves.title: Game, drive, play
leaves.criterion: Statistics recomputed from play rows of the 2022 to 2024 style test league match the league report totals exactly (internal consistency, Q1.2.2).

leaves.title: Trajectories, tendencies, grades
leaves.criterion: Deleting the tendency cache and rebuilding gives identical cells.

leaves.title: Content entity list
leaves.criterion: Every F and G leaf that defines content maps to exactly one entity here.

leaves.title: Career, relationships, reputation, money, inbox
leaves.criterion: An inbox item with a deadline that passes moves to `expired` and its default outcome is applied by a logged command.

leaves.title: Screen registry, settings, key map
leaves.criterion: Every setting in the schema appears once in the settings screen, and every screen record's keys resolve.

leaves.title: Packs and folders
leaves.criterion: Loading the same pack set twice in different folder scan orders gives the same content hash (P4.3.1).

leaves.title: Schema validation
leaves.criterion: A corpus of deliberately broken files (one per rule) each produces exactly its expected error.

leaves.title: Football validation
leaves.criterion: Every shipped play and call validates with zero errors under at least one rule set. Each validator rule has a positive and a negative test.

leaves.title: Content hashing and the manifest
leaves.criterion: The same pack hashed on every platform gives the same hash.

leaves.title: Reload in development and in editors
leaves.criterion: Editing a route depth in the designer changes the next bench run and no earlier record.

leaves.title: The ui folder
leaves.criterion: The build-time checks above run in continuous integration.

leaves.title: Templates by level and rung
leaves.criterion: A test renders every template with sample parameters for every level and rung with no missing parameter.

leaves.title: File structure and fact links
leaves.criterion: The build prints a count of rule values by status for each rule set, and the count of values with no register row is zero.

leaves.title: One file and its header
leaves.criterion: The load screen fills from headers alone in under 200 ms for 20 saves (starting value).

leaves.title: Content copies in the save
leaves.criterion: Uninstalling every user pack does not change the behaviour of a save that used them.

leaves.title: The log
leaves.criterion: Replay of one stored season from its season-start snapshot and its log gives the stored end-of-season state hash.

leaves.title: Undo
leaves.criterion: After any undo, state equals the state before the undone command, by hash.

leaves.title: Snapshots
leaves.criterion: Restoring a week-boundary snapshot and replaying that week's log gives the live state hash.

leaves.title: State hash chain
leaves.criterion: Editing any world-state value with an outside tool is detected at the next load by a chain check against the latest snapshot.

leaves.title: What is kept and for how long
leaves.criterion: 1. A 30-season headless career on `standard` ends under the size target (measured at phase 6). 2. Any play from the current or previous season opens in the film viewer within the game budget plus 1 s. 3. Regenerated film is byte-identical to film captured at the time (same engine version).

leaves.title: Season archive step
leaves.criterion: Summary totals equal totals recomputed from play rows immediately before thinning, for every player in a test season.

leaves.title: Save migrations
leaves.criterion: Every fixture save from every released version loads in the current build and passes the invariant checks (Q1.2.2).

leaves.title: Storage, quota, and eviction
leaves.criterion: A career exported from the browser build loads in the desktop build with the same state hash, and the reverse.

leaves.title: Bug bundle
leaves.criterion: A bundle made at a random point of a test career replays to the same state hash on a different operating system.

leaves.title: Export formats
leaves.criterion: Export then import of a playbook gives identical content hashes.

leaves.title: Autosave, copies, corruption
leaves.criterion: A test that kills the process at 1,000 random points during a simulated season always reloads to a state whose hash matches a clean run to the same log position.

leaves.title: Simulation time budgets
leaves.criterion: Each row has a benchmark. A regression of more than 10% against the stored baseline fails the build.

leaves.title: The target machine
leaves.criterion: The benchmark suite is run on a machine at or below this target before each release, and its results are published with the release notes.

leaves.title: Tick loop design rules
leaves.criterion: The allocation counter for a play's tick loop reads zero in the benchmark build.

leaves.title: Tiers of the same engine
leaves.criterion: One game run at tier A and at tier B from the same input gives identical play rows. A distant game re-simulated from its stored inputs reproduces its saved result exactly. No code path resolves a saved game with anything but the full engine.

leaves.title: The benchmark suite
leaves.criterion: A test change that adds a 20% delay to the tick loop fails continuous integration.

leaves.title: Memory budgets
leaves.criterion: Peak memory during a simulated season at the default world size stays under the totals.

leaves.title: Folder and loading
leaves.criterion: Dropping a valid playbook pack in the folder makes it selectable at the next career creation with no restart.

leaves.title: Data-only content and limits
leaves.criterion: A corpus of hostile packs (oversized, deep nesting, path escape, zip bomb, markup in names, embedded images) is rejected or neutralised, each with the expected message.

leaves.title: People pack format
leaves.criterion: The schema has no image, medical, legal, or family column, and a test pack containing them imports with those columns dropped and reported.

leaves.title: The import tool
leaves.criterion: 1. A release build scan finds no people pack and no table of real names in the shipped files. 2. The same pack and seed imported twice give identical worlds by state hash. 3. After import, every imported person has `origin: imported`, no image field, and passes `mayReceiveEvent` denial for every protected event type. 4. A network monitor shows zero requests during import.

leaves.title: Exporting and sharing people
leaves.criterion: A share code made from a world with imported people recreates the generated world without them and says so.

leaves.title: Official signatures
leaves.criterion: Changing one byte of a signed pack makes it "community" and unavailable to certified careers. A certified career started with a people pack shows the pack checksum in its header and on its exported record, and any edit to an imported person is refused.

leaves.title: Editors as content writers
leaves.criterion: Each editor's output passes the pack validator with no hand editing.

leaves.title: The certified flag
leaves.criterion: Each breaking condition has a test that performs it and checks the flag and reason.

leaves.title: Copies and reloads
leaves.criterion: Restoring a week-old copy of a certified career and loading it yields `certified: false` with the reason shown.

leaves.title: What v1 must not block
leaves.criterion: A test harness drives both sidelines of one game with two scripted actors through the command interface, and neither actor's read models contain the other's call before the snap.

leaves.title: Rule-case suite
leaves.criterion: 1. Every case passes for both shipped rule sets. 2. The coverage table shows no non-exempt article without a case. 3. Deleting a rule key from a rule-set file fails at least one case.

leaves.title: Enforcement property tests
leaves.criterion: All properties hold over the starting volume. A deliberately broken enforcement (full 15 yards from the 10) is caught.

leaves.title: Legality generators
leaves.criterion: Zero wrong accepts and zero wrong refusals over 50,000 generated alignments per rule set (starting value). Every shipped play validates.

leaves.title: Schema and content tests
leaves.criterion: Adding a `difficulty` field to any schema fails the build. Removing a `factId` from a rule value fails the build.

leaves.title: State invariant checks
leaves.criterion: Each invariant has a test that breaks it by direct state edit and sees the failure reported.

leaves.title: Migration fixtures
leaves.criterion: Every released version has a fixture. A migration step removed on purpose fails the suite.

leaves.title: Golden-seed determinism on every platform
leaves.criterion: All platforms match. Running the season with 1 pool worker and with 8 gives the same final hash.

leaves.title: Diff runner
leaves.criterion: A one-parameter change to pass-rush speed reports changes only in plays with a pass rush.

leaves.title: AI no-hidden-information test
leaves.criterion: Zero divergences in the swap test over 500 games (starting value). A test AI that reads the user's call is caught.

leaves.title: No truth field in read models
leaves.criterion: Adding a true rating to PersonView fails the test.

leaves.title: Contrast and greyscale checks
leaves.criterion: No screen fails. A test theme with grey-on-grey text fails.

leaves.title: Keyboard-only full game
leaves.criterion: The trace finishes the game with no delay-of-game foul caused by interface reach. A pause command injected during a live game is refused by the core.

leaves.title: Route crawl
leaves.criterion: Every route passes at every rung. A route with a missing data binding fails.

leaves.title: 30-season career run
leaves.criterion: All 5 seeds finish with zero invariant failures and inside both budgets.

leaves.title: Imported-people protection run
leaves.criterion: Zero protected events. A test build with `mayReceiveEvent` forced to true is caught.

leaves.title: Distant-tier equivalence
leaves.criterion: All rows match. A tier C build with scoring raised 5% fails.

leaves.title: Long-run stability of the world
leaves.criterion: No series drifts beyond tolerance. A test parameter set with aging decline removed fails on the age series.

leaves.title: Contest tests
leaves.criterion: Every contest is monotonic and inside its band, or its band is marked provisional (Q6.3.1).

leaves.title: Play, game, and season runs
leaves.criterion: Every Verified row passes at its tolerance.

leaves.title: Rating-response sweeps
leaves.criterion: All curves have the listed direction. A test build where speed alone decides separation fails the dominance cap.

leaves.title: What runs when
leaves.criterion: Each suite in this file appears in the table.

leaves.title: Target rows
leaves.criterion: Every row has a `factId` that exists. No college row shares a `factId` with a pro row.

leaves.title: The five steps
leaves.criterion: A release parameter set has a stored report showing all five steps and their results.

leaves.title: Parameter search and bounds
leaves.criterion: The search recovers known parameters from data produced by the engine itself, within tolerance.

leaves.title: Tolerance rules
leaves.criterion: Each row's pass or fail can be recomputed from the report alone.

leaves.title: Parameter-set versioning
leaves.criterion: A game from season 3 re-simulates identically after the career moves to a new set in season 5.

leaves.title: The coach-effect validation band
leaves.criterion: The measured share is reported per level with its interval. Removing all coach differences drives the share to about zero. A hidden per-coach bonus added on purpose is caught by a code lint for coach identity inside contest models.

leaves.title: Tuning tools
leaves.criterion: The league report regenerates from a parameter-set ID and a seed list alone.

leaves.title: Paired-policy test form
leaves.criterion: An item whose two policies are identical reports a difference whose interval includes zero.

leaves.title: Admission rule
leaves.criterion: Every item in Q3.2 has a basis, a basis status, and a kind.

leaves.title: Pass game items
leaves.criterion: Each row passes or is listed as suspended with a reason.

leaves.title: Pressure and protection items
leaves.criterion: Each row passes.

leaves.title: Run game items
leaves.criterion: Each row passes.

leaves.title: Game management items
leaves.criterion: Each row passes under both rule sets or names the rule set it covers.

leaves.title: Preparation and tendency items
leaves.criterion: Each row passes.

leaves.title: Career-scale items
leaves.criterion: Each row passes, reported with its provisional mark.

leaves.title: Battery report
leaves.criterion: The report regenerates from a parameter-set ID.

leaves.title: Dominant-call search
leaves.criterion: No unexplained exploit in the report. A planted exploit (a route the coverage rules ignore) is found by the search.

leaves.title: Defensive and special teams search
leaves.criterion: No unexplained exploit. Blitzing every down loses to the standard AI offense over a season relative to a mixed plan.

leaves.title: Clock, substitution, and penalty abuse
leaves.criterion: No sequence stops the play clock in a live game. Every illegal gain is answered by the rule engine as the rule set states.

leaves.title: Information exploits
leaves.criterion: No leak beyond D6's learning rates. A bench that used true opponent ratings is caught.

leaves.title: Career loop search
leaves.criterion: No greedy agent outperforms the standard AI coach's career outcomes by more than the starting margin of 25% over 30 seasons (Assumption).

leaves.title: Rule-breaking parity: AI clubs break rules and are caught at the user's rates
leaves.criterion: 1. A test build in which the user's finding chance is half the AI's fails rule 3. 2. A test build in which no AI coach ever breaks a rule fails rule 2. 3. A test build that refuses the user a choosable violation fails rule 5.

leaves.title: What happens when an exploit is found
leaves.criterion: Each closed exploit has a test that fails on the old build and passes on the new one.

leaves.title: Review of content and film by coaches
leaves.criterion: Every written F and G4 file has at least one completed review round before release, or is marked "not reviewed" in the release notes.

leaves.title: Reading simulated film with assignments hidden
leaves.criterion: Once reviewers exist, the test is run with at least 3 reviewers per level before a release and its results are published in the release notes, pass or fail. While deferred, the release notes state that it was not run.

leaves.title: Does the game rank people by coaching knowledge
leaves.criterion: The study plan, sample, and results are written up whether or not the ordering appears.

leaves.title: Do newcomers learn football
leaves.criterion: Both forms exist before the study starts, and every question traces to a rule-book section or a fact-register row. Coach review of the forms is recorded when a reviewer exists, and its absence is stated in the write-up.

leaves.title: Wording of the transfer claim by evidence level
leaves.criterion: The wording shipped in a release matches the level its evidence supports.

leaves.title: Finding and working with reviewers
leaves.criterion: The reviewer need is listed as an open risk in R2 until three reviewers per level have completed one round. While deferred, no build gate and no release wording depends on a coach review, and every stand-in finding is labelled as not from a coach.

leaves.title: Register row format
leaves.criterion: Every row validates against the schema. No two rows share an `id`.

leaves.title: Status words and how a row moves
leaves.criterion: A script recomputes every status from sources and matches the stored value. Two citations of one study yield 1 of 3.

leaves.title: Every football value points at a row
leaves.criterion: Changing a play clock value in a rule-set file without changing the register fails the lint.

leaves.title: Provisional values in tests and reports
leaves.criterion: Setting a Verified row to 1 of 3 makes the mark appear on every test that reads it.

leaves.title: Loading, audit, and yearly refresh
leaves.criterion: After first load, the number of distinct facts cited in bible files equals the number of register rows or the difference is listed.

leaves.title: Order rules
leaves.criterion: Every phase in R1.2 names at least one Q suite by ID. No phase lists a category that depends on a later phase's output.

leaves.title: No calendar dates
leaves.criterion: A search of the bible finds no release date.

leaves.title: Phase 0: foundations and its gate
leaves.criterion: Every suite and measurement named in the gate passes on the same commit, on every platform in P2.3, under both rule sets where the suite is level-tagged both.

leaves.title: Phase 1: a complete game with the reference resolver
leaves.criterion: Every suite and measurement named in the gate passes on the same commit, on every platform in P2.3, under both rule sets where the suite is level-tagged both.

leaves.title: Phase 2: football language and the field
leaves.criterion: Every suite and measurement named in the gate passes on the same commit, on every platform in P2.3, under both rule sets where the suite is level-tagged both.

leaves.title: Phase 3: assignment-level engine, pass game
