leaves.title: Job record
leaves.criterion: Every staff in a generated world validates against the catalogue with no seat lacking a rung, side, or duty set.

leaves.title: College job titles
leaves.criterion: A generated top-subdivision staff has exactly 4 graduate assistants and no more than 11 seats flagged `recruits_off_campus`.

leaves.title: Professional job titles
leaves.criterion: Every pro team has exactly one seat for each coordinator and one quality control seat per side.

leaves.title: Reporting lines
leaves.criterion: Every seat except the head coach has exactly one evaluating boss.

leaves.title: Staff rules by league
leaves.criterion: A college head coach who flags a twelfth off-campus recruiter under the 2026 values is warned once, may proceed, and the act writes one violation row through L8.2.5 (T9.5.1). Nothing is blocked. A generated AI staff obeys the limit unless its head coach's `rule_respect` leads him to break it, through the same pipeline.

leaves.title: Typical paths and their clocks
leaves.criterion: Over a 30-season world simulation, the mean age of first-time top-subdivision head coaches is within 3 years of the target, and fewer than 10% of people who start at rung 2 ever reach rung 9.

leaves.title: Week modes
leaves.criterion: 1. A rung 2 season in key-weeks mode completes in under 60 minutes of play (same bar as E2.1.2). 2. A season-summary season completes in under 10 minutes. 3. Every simulated grade record carries the simulated flag.

leaves.title: The offseason at speed
leaves.criterion: Simulation never passes an offer, a release, or a boss sit-down without stopping.

leaves.title: Starting above the bottom
leaves.criterion: Each start produces a valid save in which the user's seat, contract, and boss exist on day one.

leaves.title: Climb length targets
leaves.criterion: Scripted "perfect work" careers reach rung 7 in 8 to 14 game years across seeds. Scripted "average work" careers usually do not reach rung 9.

leaves.title: Record structure
leaves.criterion: Every job in the history has at least one measure with a non-zero event count, or is marked fully simulated.

leaves.title: Former assistants and former players
leaves.criterion: A former assistant's head coach hire creates a tree entry and a news item in the same week. An assistant with one full season joins the tree; one with half a season does not. In a test where two generation 1 members are head coaches and the user is out of work, both staff searches show the reverse hiring term in their logs.

leaves.title: Ways a career ends
leaves.criterion: Ending a career at any rung produces a summary and leaves a loadable world.

leaves.title: A new career in the same world
leaves.criterion: A second career can begin in a 30-season-old world without regenerating it. A former self with fewer than 50 logged decisions in a family gets the seat median for it. The gap seasons produce the same world for the same seed and the same gap length.

leaves.title: Origin list
leaves.criterion: Each origin produces a different first-year job set and a different first-year assignment mix in seeded tests. Two users with different origins who do the same task with the same inputs get the same grade.

leaves.title: Where you start
leaves.criterion: The starting school list always contains at least one program from each tier in the chosen region. A power four starting school generates a staff of 70 to 100; a Group of Six school 45 to 70.

leaves.title: The playing years
leaves.criterion: Four playing seasons can be completed in under 15 minutes.

leaves.title: The student years
leaves.criterion: A student who completes every task on time for two seasons has a relationship strength with his supervisor above the hiring threshold in S2.3.1 in at least 90% of trials.

leaves.title: The high school and small-college years
leaves.criterion: A high school season completes in one screen with no game played. A second-subdivision season can be completed in under 45 minutes with three coached games.

leaves.title: The first job offer
leaves.criterion: In seeded trials, more than 80% of the user's first seats are on a staff where he had a prior relationship.

leaves.title: Duty record and ownership
leaves.criterion: For every rung, the week screen lists at least three duties in a game week, each opening a working tool.

leaves.title: Practice charting
leaves.criterion: A perfect chart scores 100 and matches the script export. In a tempo period at 15 seconds a rep, a user entering six fields per rep cannot finish every field, and the scoring rewards keeping the result and bust fields over the rest.

leaves.title: Holding cards and signalling
leaves.criterion: Signal delay over 4 seconds shows up as lost play-clock time in the play record. With three signalers on the sideline, the opponent's signal-stealing in I7 can read the live one only after it has been identified as live.

leaves.title: Video and equipment support
leaves.criterion: Unfilmed periods cannot be graded by anyone that day.

leaves.title: Opponent film breakdown
leaves.criterion: 1. Tagging a game perfectly scores 100 on every field. 2. Seeding his tags with 30% wrong coverage calls changes the AI coordinator's coverage beliefs for that opponent in a measurable way. 3. The accuracy report breaks out at least six fields.

leaves.title: Scout cards
leaves.criterion: A card set copied exactly from film grades at or above 95 on the truth part.

leaves.title: Running the scout team
leaves.criterion: Halving look quality halves the readiness gain from that period.

leaves.title: Assisting a position and staying enrolled
leaves.criterion: A graduate assistant with zero coursework hours for a term loses the seat at term's end. A graduate assistant who takes 5 credit hours every term keeps the seat for two years and cannot take a third year; one who takes 6 a term can. A user whose degree is eight years old cannot be hired into the seat without a logged violation.

leaves.title: Opponent tendency report
leaves.criterion: 1. A report listing only the three largest true tendencies in its section scores above 85 on the truth part. 2. A finding with n under 8 that contradicts the true tendency is flagged as overreach. 3. The post-game grade is produced within the same save week.

leaves.title: Self-scout report
leaves.criterion: Every tendency above the G8 alert threshold that he omits lowers the grade.

leaves.title: Cut-ups and teaching tape
leaves.criterion: A reel with one mislabeled clip in ten grades below a clean reel.

leaves.title: Game-management charts and live advice
leaves.criterion: A recommendation costing more than 2 percentage points of win probability against the model's best is marked an error in the log.

leaves.title: Playbook drawings, install sheets, and practice scripts
leaves.criterion: A page with one wrong assignment produces a higher rate of that error in the next practice than a correct page. A script that calls an uninstalled play is flagged by the coordinator, never by the tool before printing.

leaves.title: Individual periods and drill design
leaves.criterion: Two position coaches with equal players and different drill choices produce measurably different attribute growth over a simulated season, in the direction the formula predicts. The same drill choices for the same players give the same gains whoever the user is and however long his career has been.

leaves.title: The position meeting
leaves.criterion: Doubling the number of new calls in a fixed-length meeting lowers per-call knowledge gain.

leaves.title: Grading every snap
leaves.criterion: Random grades score near 50% agreement. Truthful grades score above 90%.

leaves.title: Depth chart, substitution, and his players
leaves.criterion: With boss trust at maximum, the user's depth order is used unchanged.

leaves.title: Recruiting area
leaves.criterion: Recruiting hours reduce the hours available for S3.5.1 to S3.5.3 in the same week.

leaves.title: His players off the field
leaves.criterion: Hours spent on checks lower the hours left for S3.5.1 to S3.5.5 that week. A player whose slide the coach never checked becomes ineligible with no earlier warning on the coach's screen.

leaves.title: Personnel reports for the front office
leaves.criterion: Every report is stored with its date and scored once against the player's later record. No screen shows the assistant the player's true value.

leaves.title: Owning a slice of the plan
leaves.criterion: The user's slice appears on the printed call sheet under his name in the plan record.

leaves.title: Running a side of the ball
leaves.criterion: A coordinator user can complete a full game week touching only his side's tools, with the other side and all head coach decisions run by AI.

leaves.title: The coordinator's duties outside the plan
leaves.criterion: A coordinator user in a pro job has a media session on his week screen every game week. An interview taken in a game week lowers the hours left for G6 and G7 that week.

leaves.title: Pointer
leaves.criterion: Every duty family in S3.1.1 is O in the last column or is delegated by the user's own choice (K6).

leaves.title: System, standards, and preferences
leaves.criterion: Two bosses with opposite `detail_focus` give the same report different grades in the expected direction.

leaves.title: Assignments
leaves.criterion: Total assigned hours scale with the boss's `hours_culture` across seeded trials.

leaves.title: The trust score
leaves.criterion: A user with perfect on-time work at grade 80 or above reaches the 75 threshold within one season under a boss with average `delegation`.

leaves.title: Grade record
leaves.criterion: Every completed duty writes exactly one grade record.

leaves.title: The season evaluation
leaves.criterion: The evaluation's area ratings can be reproduced from the grade records and the boss's weights.

leaves.title: Disagreeing with the boss
leaves.criterion: Each option produces a distinct, logged outcome in a scripted test.

leaves.title: Credit and blame
leaves.criterion: Under a boss with `loyalty_to_staff` above 80, the user's outside reputation rises faster for the same work than under one below 20.

leaves.title: The boss's decision each offseason
leaves.criterion: In world simulations, at least a third of rung 4 to 7 hires on new head coaches' staffs come from the head coach's previous staff.

leaves.title: Seat assignment
leaves.criterion: Every seat on the game-day sheet has exactly one role, and the headset count is within the league limit.

leaves.title: Signals, substitution, and the bench area
leaves.criterion: A late substitution by the user produces a visible consequence: a timeout, a foul, or ten men.

leaves.title: The position coach between series
leaves.criterion: 1. A correct diagnosis reduces the repeat rate of that failure in the rest of the game in controlled tests. 2. The between-series window closes when the unit must return.

leaves.title: Booth eyes: naming what the opponent is in
leaves.criterion: 1. Over a game, his accuracy by family and variant and his mean answer time are written to the record. 2. An AI caller given 90% accurate booth reports calls measurably better against the defense's tendencies than one given 50% accurate reports.

leaves.title: Charting and tendencies in game
leaves.criterion: The halftime screen shows his chart, with its errors, when he holds this role. A flag raised after 3 snaps of a situation is graded "too early". A flag after 8 snaps where the report predicted 50% blitz and none came is graded real.

leaves.title: Game-management advice
leaves.criterion: Advice arrives on the channel only if confirmed before the timer ends.

leaves.title: Calling for someone else
leaves.criterion: A coordinator user can play a full game in which every game-management decision is made by the AI head coach and every play call on his side is his own.

leaves.title: Role log
leaves.criterion: Every graded game-day event appears in the role report with what the opponent really played, visible on film. No hidden attribute or probability is shown. A family with fewer than 10 graded events shows "not enough yet" in place of a percentage.

leaves.title: Who thinks what of you
leaves.criterion: Two assistants with equal unit results and different recruiting results have different college market values and equal pro market values.

leaves.title: The relationship graph
leaves.criterion: In world simulations, more than half of rung 4 to 7 hires share a prior edge with the hiring coach.

leaves.title: Clinics and the convention
leaves.criterion: Convention-only contacts produce a first job in fewer than 5% of trials.

leaves.title: How assistant seats open
leaves.criterion: Yearly counts of head coach changes and assistant hires in a 30-season simulation fall within 25% of the targets.

leaves.title: The working interview
leaves.criterion: The practical portion of each interview opens the same tool the job uses.

leaves.title: Choosing among offers as an assistant
leaves.criterion: The offer card shows every factor listed, and each changes the AI's choice in isolation tests.

leaves.title: Crossing between college and the pros
leaves.criterion: Cross-level moves in both directions occur every simulated year.

leaves.title: When the head coach is fired
leaves.criterion: After a simulated head coach change, at least 60% of rung 5 to 7 seats on that staff change hands within one offseason.

leaves.title: What a released assistant is owed
leaves.criterion: Offset contracts stop paying the overlap when a new football salary starts.

leaves.title: Finding a seat before the music stops
leaves.criterion: A released coordinator with average reputation finds some football seat within one cycle in at least 85% of trials, at his own rung in fewer than 40%.

leaves.title: The year out
leaves.criterion: A year out with zero activity lowers market value. A year with visits and study does not.

leaves.title: Duty-to-evidence map
leaves.criterion: 1. For a test coach at each rung, only the families listed for that rung gain events during a season. 2. After a full season, no field on the user's coach record changed except event references, counts, dates, and history facts. The schema validator confirms it (E9.1.2 acceptance 1). 3. The same duty done with the same inputs in a first-year career and a twentieth-year career gives the same grade and the same downstream result (E9.1.3 acceptance 2).

leaves.title: What working under a boss and study give
leaves.criterion: 1. After three seasons on a staff, the user's history holds `worked_in_system` with 3 seasons for the family that staff ran, and `worked_under` for the boss. 2. No numeric field on his coach record other than counts and dates changed over those seasons. 3. His tagging in a new terminology is graded by the same rule in his first week as in his third season.

leaves.title: Gaps by path
leaves.criterion: 1. The "new to you" list equals the set of duty families in the new seat's duty set that are absent from the user's history. 2. A duty done for the first time and the same duty done with the same inputs after five seasons in the seat give the same result.

leaves.title: Pay by rung and level
leaves.criterion: Every seat in a generated world has a salary inside its band for its program tier.

leaves.title: Hours by rung and season
leaves.criterion: At rung 2 under a high-hours boss, discretionary time in a game week is at most 15 hours (168 less the 90-hour maximum, less 52.5 hours of sleep need and 10.5 hours of fixed needs; the earlier "under 10" was unreachable from the leaf's own maximum, so the acceptance is corrected here; counting game-week travel as work would lower it further; G-53).

leaves.title: Relocation by career stage
leaves.criterion: Simulated careers that reach rung 9 show a median of at least five relocations.

leaves.title: Candidate list from the index, resolved
leaves.criterion: Every candidate named in the index entry for T1 has a row.

leaves.title: The five pressures
leaves.criterion: Running the engine with college rules and college players, with no scheme priors applied, already moves plays per game and fourth-down behaviour toward the college targets. Priors close the rest.

leaves.title: College offensive families and their shares
leaves.criterion: A generated world's pass rate and yards per rush land in the T12 bands with these shares.

leaves.title: College defensive families
leaves.criterion: Simulated sack and interception rates land in T12 bands.

leaves.title: College special teams differences
leaves.criterion: With college kicker distributions the simulated field goal rate lands in the T12 band without any change to kick physics.

leaves.title: The priors the F files read
leaves.criterion: Every F leaf that names T10 as owner finds its key in this file. No F leaf contains a college literal.

leaves.title: Nothing rescales at the draft
leaves.criterion: A test that diffs every attribute of every drafted player the day before and the day after the draft finds zero changes. No function takes an honour, a title, or a level percentile and returns an attribute.

leaves.title: Pro scouts at a college program
leaves.criterion: A coach with a long honest record measurably reduces grade error on his players in simulation.

leaves.title: All-star games, the combine, pro day, and the draft
leaves.criterion: Pick count per draft follows the pro league's rules (C7), not a constant here.

leaves.title: The level discount on production and film
leaves.criterion: In simulation, grade error at the draft is larger for players from lower levels. Late-round hits come disproportionately from wide-band players.

leaves.title: Draft outcome targets by position and round
leaves.criterion: A 20-season world simulation lands every by-round row within tolerance. The first-round quarterback Starter 5 rate lands between 43% and 67%. This closes the acceptance test left open in T4.7.1.

leaves.title: A coach's standing with pro teams
leaves.criterion: Movement between levels in simulation lands within 50% of the starting targets.

leaves.title: Scoring and volume
leaves.criterion: A 10-season simulation lands each row inside tolerance, and the scoring standard deviation within 8%.

leaves.title: Margins and the spread of team strength
leaves.criterion: Simulated rating standard deviation between 8.5 and 10.0. Close-game and blowout shares within 6% relative.

leaves.title: Upset rates by strength gap
leaves.criterion: Each enforced bin within 5 percentage points. Single-game spread around the gap between 12 and 15.5 points. Prior-season table within 6 points, which tests year-to-year roster turnover.

leaves.title: Efficiency
leaves.criterion: League rows inside tolerance in a 10-season simulation with T10.5.1 priors active.

leaves.title: Fourth down, punts, and field goals
leaves.criterion: AI go rates by distance bin inside tolerance. Simulated field goal share inside tolerance with no change to kick physics between levels.

leaves.title: Drives
leaves.criterion: Drive outcome shares within 6% to 12% relative as set in the target file.

leaves.title: Fouls and fumbles
leaves.criterion: Accepted fouls within 8%.

leaves.title: Open rows and how the engine runs without them
leaves.criterion: Every row above exists in the target file or the priors file with a non-certify tier and a status.

leaves.title: The level table
leaves.criterion: Every team has exactly one level. Changing the league file's year changes counts with no code change. A stat line always stores the level it was earned at.

leaves.title: Conference record and tiers
leaves.criterion: A generated world reproduces the starting sizes. In a 20-season simulation the power tier's win share over the other tier lands in the T12 band.

leaves.title: What a program is
leaves.criterion: Standing changes only through logged results. Two programs with identical histories and resources have identical standing.

leaves.title: World generation for college
leaves.criterion: Same seed, same world. Conference sizes match T2.2.1. Every program has at least one rival and 30 seasons of history.

leaves.title: Conference movement
leaves.criterion: Over 30 simulated seasons the count of moves per season stays in the starting band and no conference exceeds 20 members.

leaves.title: Regular-season shape
leaves.criterion: Every team has 12 games, the right conference count, and no two games in one week. Protected games appear every season.

leaves.title: Non-conference scheduling
leaves.criterion: No schedule breaks the 12-game count. The lower-subdivision game rate lands within 0.8 to 1.1 per team-season in simulation.

leaves.title: College calendar file
leaves.criterion: Loading year 2026 and year 2027 produces the two columns above with no code change.

leaves.title: Conference standings and the champion
leaves.criterion: Every conference has exactly one champion. The tiebreak log names the deciding step.

leaves.title: Polls and the committee ranking
leaves.criterion: With noise off, the ranking is a pure function of results. No record guarantees a place: an unbeaten power champion with a weak resume can rank outside the top 4 (2023: 13-0 ACC champion Florida State ranked fifth and was left out).

leaves.title: Field, seeding, and bracket
leaves.criterion: Format switches on the save year. Bracket has the right count and hosts.

leaves.title: Bowl eligibility and selection
leaves.criterion: No team under 5 wins is invited. Berth count matches the year's data.

leaves.title: Homecoming and senior day
leaves.criterion: 1. Both dates appear on every college schedule with a home game available. 2. Delegating an obligation gives a smaller relations change than attending. 3. Setting the rule 6 values to zero removes every on-field effect of the day.

leaves.title: Prospect generation and the class year
leaves.criterion: The share of drafted players who were rated 2 or 3 stars is non-trivial in 20-season simulations (target to be set from data). Depth pass addition: each generated national class at real-world size carries about 32 five-star and about 370 four-star public ratings (plus or minus 20 percent), and by August before the senior season at least 85 percent of the top 400 have a commitment in world simulations.

leaves.title: Junior college prospects
leaves.criterion: 1. Every generated world has junior college prospects each year, and some share of them (starting target 5 to 15 percent of a top-subdivision signing class, Assumption) sign with four-year schools. 2. A junior college signee who has not met the transfer rule for the year is not added to the roster. 3. His remaining seasons equal the T5.2.1 value for the rule year, never a fresh four.

leaves.title: Periods and what each allows
leaves.criterion: 1. An off-campus visit to a prospect in a dead or quiet period can be scheduled. Scheduling it shows the L8.2.5 warning first, and confirming it writes exactly one `violation_log` row and produces the contact's normal effect. 2. No recruiting action is disabled or hidden in any period for a person whose job could take it. 3. With the same act, witnesses, and enforcing body, a user and an AI recruiter get the same detection chance. 4. A seventh off-campus contact with the same prospect, or a second in one week, can be scheduled, shows the warning, and writes one `violation_log` row. 5. On 2026-11-30 the year view turns dead for every FBS program, and on 2026-09-01 the fall evaluation pool resets to 33 days.

leaves.title: The 2027 recruiting model switch
leaves.criterion: 1. On 2027-01-01 the budget panel switches without user action, and the marks in T4.2.1 change with it. 2. Under "opps_2027", a fifth opportunity with one prospect between January and May, or a second in one week, can be taken, warns, and writes one `violation_log` row. 3. Under "opps_2027", an off-campus contact by the head coach in the spring contact period warns and writes one row; under "days_2025" his days count against the pool.

leaves.title: Judging a prospect
leaves.criterion: A prospect seen on film, live, and in camp has a narrower grade band than one seen on film only, on the attributes each look covers. Depth pass additions: a second film look narrows the band by half as much as the first; a prospect below the head coach's board line never reaches the position coach's queue unless someone moves him there by hand.

leaves.title: Interest, relationships, and offers
leaves.criterion: 1. Removing a prospect's main recruiter lowers his true interest in that school in the same week (checked in the truth data, not on screen). 2. A static check finds no user-facing field bound to the prospect's true interest or commitment threshold. 3. Every line of a staff read names its basis and date. With no new evidence, the read does not change when true interest changes. 4. In test worlds the staff read disagrees with the truth in a measurable share of cases (starting target: the standing word is off by one step or more for at least 20 percent of pursued prospects, Assumption).

leaves.title: The people around the prospect
leaves.criterion: 1. Raising a circle member's true influence weight makes that person's preferences change the signing outcome more often in seeded trials. 2. No screen shows a true influence weight. Every line in the circle record has a basis. 3. A prospect's circle is unknown to a staff that has made no contact.

leaves.title: Negative recruiting
leaves.criterion: 1. A false claim that is later contradicted by a logged world event lowers the speaker's standing with that prospect and his high school coach. 2. The user is told of a rival's negative recruiting only through a person who heard it. 3. The action writes no `violation_log` row.

leaves.title: Pulling an offer
leaves.criterion: 1. An offer can be withdrawn at any time before signing with no warning dialog about rules. 2. Withdrawing from a committed player lowers the school's standing with his high school coach, and a later prospect from that school starts with a lower relationship in seeded trials. 3. AI programs withdraw offers at a measurable rate in world simulations. 4. With the starting values, school-driven drops end 2 to 6 percent of power-program commitments per cycle in 20-season world simulations. 5. Once a prospect has signed with one school, a withdraw-offer action is not offered for him by that school in this leaf, and another school's contact with him warns as a recruiting violation.

leaves.title: Offer volume and the committable offer
leaves.criterion: 1. In world simulations AI power programs average 6 to 10 offers per signee. 2. No screen shows the `committable` field of another school's offer. 3. A commitment attempt on a non-committable offer is accepted or refused by the head coach, and a refusal writes a memory entry for the prospect and his high school coach.

leaves.title: Visits
leaves.criterion: 1. A second official visit by the same prospect to the same school can be scheduled. Unless the head coach has changed since the first, it shows the L8.2.5 warning and, if confirmed, writes one `violation_log` row and has a visit's normal effect. 2. After a head coach change the second visit shows no warning (2 of 3, see Football facts used). 3. No visit action is disabled for a person whose job could take it. 4. A visit planned past 48 hours, or with more paid companions than `visits.paid_companions`, can be confirmed, warns, and writes one `violation_log` row. 5. With `visits.school_cap` = none, no warning appears at any visit count; under a 2023-24 rule set the 71st visit warns.

leaves.title: Commitment, flips, and signing
leaves.criterion: 1. In world simulations a measurable share of commitments flip before signing, higher at schools that change head coach. 2. No user-facing field is bound to true firmness. The class list shows words, basis, and date only. 3. The AI decision to recruit a committed player reads no `ruleRespect`, ethics, or integrity value (static check). 4. With the starting values, 15 to 23 percent of power-program commitments end in a decommitment per cycle in world simulations. 5. A head coach firing in October multiplies that program's decommitments over the next six weeks by at least 3. 6. At least 85 percent of power-program high school signees sign in the early period.

leaves.title: Recruits who do not qualify
leaves.criterion: 1. A signee below the rule year's core grade value on the ruling date is not added to the roster. 2. The staff's academic read can differ from the truth when no transcript has been shared. 3. No imported real player fails to qualify.

leaves.title: Recruiting roles by rung
leaves.criterion: Each rung from 1 to 9 on a college staff has at least one recruiting duty in the offseason, and the table has a row for every rung from 1 to 9 and for the general manager. Depth pass additions: generated top-tier programs carry 8 to 10 personnel staff; the off-campus seat count reads `recruiting.offcampus_max` for the date (11 before the fall 2026 waiver, 17 during it and under the 2027 model).

leaves.title: High school players as a pool, with a hook for a coaching rung
leaves.criterion: In a 20-season world simulation, the share of first-round quarterbacks who become top-ten pro starters stays inside the researched real band once that band exists (register row owed by T12). No code path maps a college percentile to a pro attribute.

leaves.title: Signing numbers by position against the roster limit
leaves.criterion: 1. The board total equals the roster count used by T5.1.1 on every date. 2. The game accepts a commitment when no place is open and shows the count over the target. 3. A roster over the limit on the binding date writes a `violation_log` row only if the user chose to stay over after the warning.

leaves.title: The split between high school, transfer, and junior college players
leaves.criterion: 1. AI programs in one world show a spread of mixes, not one value. 2. A place held in December and not filled in the transfer window stays empty or goes to a late signee, and the roster count shows it.

leaves.title: Walk-ons
leaves.criterion: 1. Under the 2026 values, aid players plus walk-ons never pass the limit unless the user confirms a violation (T4.8.1). 2. Under a 2024 rule set a program can carry more than 105 players. 3. Awarding aid to a walk-on writes a locker-room event.

leaves.title: Roster size and aid
leaves.criterion: Under the 2026 values a roster with 106 non-exempt players is refused at the declaration date. This is blocked, not offered as a violation, because the governing body does not accept the roster (Marlon's ruling: an act is blocked only where the league itself rejects it). Before that date the count may run over, and T5.1.2 is how it comes down. Whether a school can in practice carry an extra player and be caught later is Unverified.

leaves.title: Getting down to the limit: cuts, walk-ons, and medical retirement
leaves.criterion: On the declaration date no program has more non-exempt players than the limit. Every cut writes an event with the date and the way the player was told. A medical retirement of a player whose medical report says he can play writes one violation row and is not blocked.

leaves.title: Seasons, years, and the redshirt
leaves.criterion: A 2026 enrollee who plays 4 regular-season games and 2 playoff games keeps the season. A fifth regular-season game uses it.

leaves.title: The player's say in his own season
leaves.criterion: In a seasons-model world some players stop at exactly four games each year, and none do in an age-model world. No imported person is the subject of the event.

leaves.title: Grades and availability
leaves.criterion: A player with zero study hours for a term and low aptitude becomes at risk. A player who passes 8 hours in the fall misses exactly the first 4 games of the next season. A team with a multi-year rate of 929 cannot enter the postseason.

leaves.title: Academic shortcuts and playing an ineligible player
leaves.criterion: Both actions are available to a head coach whenever a generated player on his roster is at risk or ineligible. Each writes exactly one violation row. Neither is ever offered for an imported player.

leaves.title: Required-activity hours and practice counts
leaves.criterion: An in-season week plan totalling 21 required hours shows the warning, can still be saved, and on saving writes exactly one violation row.

leaves.title: Window dates and exceptions
leaves.criterion: Outside a window the association's transfer database does not accept an entry, so the act is refused (the governing body rejects it, which is the one case where the game blocks an action). The exceptions are a head coaching change and a team still in the postseason when the window closed. Contact with a player who has not entered is never blocked. It is T6.4.1.

leaves.title: Retention
leaves.criterion: World simulations produce yearly entries per team within 30% of the target.

leaves.title: Evaluating and signing transfers
leaves.criterion: A transfer's evaluation band is narrower than a high school prospect's at equal scouting effort.

leaves.title: Junior college players and players moving up a level
leaves.criterion: The market board can be filtered by source. A two-year college signee's evaluation band is wider than a same-level transfer's at equal scouting effort.

leaves.title: Contact outside the window
leaves.criterion: With the people pack loaded, no tampering event names a real person.

leaves.title: Revenue-sharing cap and football's share
leaves.criterion: Football budgets across a generated top subdivision span at least a tenfold range. Depth pass additions: an AI athletic director at a top-tier school gives football 60 to 70 percent of the pool; the 2026-27 cap reads 21.3 million and scholarship cost does not count against it from that year.

leaves.title: Third-party deals and the clearinghouse
leaves.criterion: Raising a program's outside-money strength raises its total spend without raising its school pool. Depth pass additions: in a world at real size with the starting values, 3 to 7 percent of outside deals by count and 12 to 25 percent by value are not cleared each year; the not-cleared share rises with amount over market value; an associated deal at twice market value is not cleared at least 30 percent of the time in seeded trials.

leaves.title: The roster budget
leaves.criterion: Depth pass additions: with the starting formula a top-tier program's starting quarterback is valued between 1 and 5 million dollars and its long snapper below 50,000; a top-tier roster's pay bands match the calibration targets above. School payments never exceed the football budget, because the athletic department issues the payments and refuses the excess (the institution rejects the act). Money promised beyond that, through a deal that was not reported or not cleared, is not blocked. It writes a violation row (T7.2.1, T9.5.1).

leaves.title: Agreement terms, agents, and demands for more
leaves.criterion: Every agreement has length, schedule, and exit terms. Over a 20-season world some demands are made, some are met, some are refused, and some refused players leave. No imported person appears in any of these events.

leaves.title: What the coach may and may not do
leaves.criterion: The option to state or promise an outside-deal amount is always present for a coach in a recruiting or retention talk, shows the warning once, and writes one violation row when used. It is never greyed. Depth pass additions: describing opportunities, introducing a player to the collective, and attending a collective fundraiser carry no warning and write no row; a personal donation to an NIL entity by a staff member warns and writes one row.

leaves.title: Growth curves from 18 to 23
leaves.criterion: Across a generated world, four-year strength and mass gains by position group match the bands above within 20%. The mean change in 40-yard time across a college career is under 0.05 seconds.

leaves.title: Technique and mental growth by year
leaves.criterion: Two identical players, one starting and one not, diverge in technique over a season by a measurable margin. Cutting practice hours lowers growth.

leaves.title: Class load and time
leaves.criterion: A team given no tutoring and maximum football time shows more ineligible players the next term than a matched team with support.

leaves.title: Depth by class and attrition
leaves.criterion: The grid's two-year projection matches actual departures within a stated error in simulation.

leaves.title: Position changes
leaves.criterion: A move never changes physical attributes at once.

leaves.title: Early entry
leaves.criterion: Early-entrant count per simulated year lands in 50 to 90. No player with fewer than three seasons since high school is drafted.

leaves.title: Opt-outs and the end of a college career
leaves.criterion: The share of departing top-subdivision seniors who are drafted sits in a band set from the T11 pick counts.

leaves.title: Athletic director and president
leaves.criterion: Every grant or refusal is logged with a reason code. A head coach cannot set his own budget.

leaves.title: Budget lines
leaves.criterion: The sum of lines never exceeds the total. Changing a line changes the consuming system's input.

leaves.title: Facilities
leaves.criterion: A completed project changes the named input the following season.

leaves.title: Booster groups
leaves.criterion: Booster-initiated violations occur in simulation at programs whose coaches never asked for them.

leaves.title: College staff structure and limits
leaves.criterion: Limits are read from data, never hard-coded. Exceeding a seat limit warns once and writes one violation row, never blocks. Salaries cannot exceed the staff pool.

leaves.title: Violations and exposure
leaves.criterion: No action in the game is blocked for being a violation. Every violation writes a ledger row. The user and an AI coach committing the same violation produce rows of the same shape.

leaves.title: Detection and the inquiry
leaves.criterion: In a 30-season world, clean programs are almost never penalised (false findings under 1% of program-seasons) and some cheating programs are never caught. Detection is not certain and not rare.

leaves.title: Penalties
leaves.criterion: A show-cause order makes the person's hire rate fall to near zero for its term. A penalised program's recruiting inputs change on the stated dates. User and AI penalties come from one table.

leaves.title: College pay bands
leaves.criterion: Generated head coach pay in a 138-team world has between 80 and 105 coaches at or above 1 million dollars in 2025 values.

leaves.title: Coverage by group
leaves.criterion: The preview's counts equal row counts of the pack's tables. The project build's preview shows the four gap groups at 0 and "filled by generator". A pack with no people of a group never blocks import.

leaves.title: Source register
leaves.criterion: Every `source statement` in a project-built pack names only register rows. The builder fails if any output column name contains `headshot`, `photo`, `image`, or `logo`. Each row has a read date within one year of the build.

leaves.title: Pack builds and the yearly refresh
leaves.criterion: Two runs of the builder on the same cache give byte-identical pack hashes. Each manifest lists every season it covers and every season it skips. No build output carries an image column.

leaves.title: Row to person
leaves.criterion: Importing the project build yields zero records with an image field, a jersey, or a real contract value. Every imported record has `externalRef` and `origin: imported`. The dropped-column list in the report equals the set difference between the file's columns and U7.1.1.

leaves.title: Identity keys and matching across sources
leaves.criterion: No two pro rows with different `gsis_id` are ever merged. On a synthetic pack with planted name twins, zero false merges. Running the match twice gives the same result.

leaves.title: Real history as plain facts
leaves.criterion: No X2 event is written from the block. With `team_names: omitted`, no real organisation name appears on any screen. Hidden later seasons never appear before their date.

leaves.title: Real links between people
leaves.criterion: Every derived edge names two imported people present in the world. No `family` edge exists unless a pack row states it. Edge count for the project build stays under a config limit (starting value 2 million) after rule 2.

leaves.title: Method, determinism, and confidence
leaves.criterion: Same pack, same seed, same values, byte for byte. Changing the world seed changes only the draws, not any `measured` value. No imported player has a hidden trait away from neutral.

leaves.title: Physical layer from body and tests
leaves.criterion: A player with a full test battery has every D2 attribute `measured` or `inferred`. No imported player's durability differs from the position median. Ageing a 4.40 test by ten years lowers speed by exactly what D8 gives for that span.

leaves.title: Technique and mental from production and usage
leaves.criterion: Across all imported starters (snap share over 0.7 last season), the mean main-role value is within 3 ISS of 50. A player with one game of data has every technique attribute within 1 prior width of the position mean. No mental attribute differs between two players with identical football records.

leaves.title: College players and recruits
leaves.criterion: The value distribution of imported college players by position and class matches that of generated college players within the D13.4.1 census tolerance. Knowing a player's draft slot never changes his college values.

leaves.title: Coach profiles from the public record
leaves.criterion: In 200 simulated seasons, an imported coach's pass rate over expected lies within the shrunk estimate plus or minus 3 points. A coach with no play-by-play has every tendency at the median. No `behavior` field differs from the median without a sourced pack value.

leaves.title: Officials
leaves.criterion: Every imported official starts with median crew parameters.

leaves.title: Back-test and fit
leaves.criterion: The report exists for each pack build, lists each position group's correlation, and fails the build below the pass mark.

leaves.title: Teams, schools, and places
leaves.criterion: The A6.2.2 scan on 1,000 generated worlds finds zero hits. Every city has every field above. Average travel distance between pro teams lies within the real league's range (C1 or H8 target).

leaves.title: Placement modes for players
leaves.criterion: Every roster meets C5 or T5 after placement. Balanced mode's team strength spread is within the set value. Kept-together mode puts every player of one real organisation-season on one team. Same seed, same placement.

leaves.title: Placing coaches and staff
leaves.criterion: No imported coach holds a job above his last real rung at career start. The user's starting job holds the user. Every team has exactly one head coach.

leaves.title: Seeds and sharing a world
leaves.criterion: Two worlds with the same seed, pack hash, and mode are identical at career start. A share code contains no person name.

leaves.title: Which groups are real and which generated
leaves.criterion: Each group's people count equals world need after the fill. A group set to "Generated only" has zero imported people. The `mix` record is in the save header.

leaves.title: Same quality, pack or no pack
leaves.criterion: Over 500 seeds, the value distribution of each generated cohort is the same with and without the project pack (two-sample test passes at the census tolerance). No generator reads any imported person's values.

leaves.title: Real people leaving and new real entrants
leaves.criterion: A delta pack never changes a placed person's team, job, or values. The cohort window's total entrants equal the D13 size rule with or without real entrants. A certified career rejects delta packs.

leaves.title: Displaced people and the pools
leaves.criterion: The count of people in the world after placement equals generated plus imported. Every displaced person has a `released` event at the placement date.

leaves.title: What each scheduled run does in a mixed world
leaves.criterion: A 60-season soak with the project pack loaded creates zero people with `origin: imported` after placement except through delta packs. Zero generated people share a full name with a pack person. Zero family edges touch an imported person.

leaves.title: What a pack may hold, and the distance rule for the shipped world
leaves.criterion: A test pack carrying every forbidden column imports with all of them dropped and listed. The shipped build fails if the distance check fails. No shipped file contains a name from the project's people tables (A6.4.1 rule 4 scan).

leaves.title: Tables and columns
leaves.criterion: A pack with only the bold columns imports. The project build converts to this schema with zero dropped required fields. The schema file lists every column above.

leaves.title: File encoding
leaves.criterion: A pack made by hand in a spreadsheet and zipped imports. A zip bomb past the expansion ratio is rejected before extraction completes. A cell `=HYPERLINK(...)` round-trips as text.

leaves.title: The people editor
leaves.criterion: No editor path sets a sensitive field or changes `origin` to `generated`. Every edited person has `origin: imported_edited`. The edit log replays to the same result.

leaves.title: Base packs, update packs, and community packs
leaves.criterion: Base plus deltas gives the same people set as a single base built from the final data. A delta with a wrong base hash is refused. No in-game sharing path accepts `contains: real` or `mixed`.

leaves.title: Checksums and the certified-career lock
leaves.criterion: Reordering rows, columns, or files leaves the checksum unchanged. Changing one value changes it. A certified career rejects every edit path for imported people.

leaves.title: Validation and the import report
leaves.criterion: Each fail, reject, drop, and warn case has a test pack and gives the stated result. A failed pack leaves no person in the world.

leaves.title: Bosses, colleagues, players, and rivals who are real
leaves.criterion: In a 30-season soak with the user's coach run by the test bot, zero events with `imported_allowed: false` name an imported person. Every user action available on a generated assistant is available on an imported one. No generated quote is attributed to an imported person.

leaves.title: Real careers diverge from day one
leaves.criterion: With the dial at 100, an imported player's team, job, and retirement date still follow the world. A retired imported player who enters coaching keeps `origin: imported`.

leaves.title: Block structure and storage
leaves.criterion: A static check finds no import of the traits block from any interface module. Two worlds built from the same seed and content hold identical blocks for every person. The user's person has empty facet and value maps in every save. Loading a save with one facet added to content fills it identically on two machines.

leaves.title: Facet definitions and the reader rule
leaves.criterion: Every facet file lists at least one reader, and each named reader ID exists in the module map (P1). Removing the last reader of a facet makes the content build fail. For each row above, a test changes only that facet between two otherwise identical generated people and shows a different distribution of the named decision over 1,000 seeded trials.

leaves.title: Value definitions
leaves.criterion: For two generated recruits differing only in `family_and_home` (low against high), over 1,000 seeded trials the high one picks the in-region school more often by a margin the test states in advance. Each value has at least one reader.

leaves.title: Goals
leaves.criterion: A generated position coach with the goal "become a coordinator" and a passed date applies for open coordinator jobs more often than an identical coach without it, over 1,000 seeded off-seasons. A stated goal appears on the person's page with the date it was said. No goal is evaluated outside an event hook.

leaves.title: Population groups and distributions
leaves.criterion: For each group, a generation of 10,000 people lands within 2 percentage points of the target band shares. The same seed gives the same person the same block whether he is generated first or last. Every shifted median has a reason comment or the content lint fails.

leaves.title: Content validator: nothing unread, nothing prescribed
leaves.criterion: Six seeded bad content sets, one per rule, each fail with the right message. The shipped content passes.

leaves.title: Words from observed behavior, never numbers
leaves.criterion: A scripted search of every screen and export in a career build finds no facet or value number. A generated player with `coachability` 5 shows no wording about it on the day he is signed and shows it after the threshold number of logged coaching interactions. Two staff reports on one player differ when the reporters witnessed different events.

leaves.title: Imported real people get neutral blocks
leaves.criterion: In a world built from a test pack, every imported person has all stored facets at 50, no `faith` entry, and all values at 0 after 30 simulated seasons.

leaves.title: Bounds on effects
leaves.criterion: A test sets every facet of every player on one team to the favorable extreme and the other team to the unfavorable extreme with equal football attributes, simulates 2,000 games, and the win share stays inside a band the test states in advance from the caps.

leaves.title: Setup options
leaves.criterion: A static check of the setup screen definition finds no difficulty, slider, or modifier field. The time estimate is within 25 percent of actual on the reference machine. At the default 30 seasons, no active head coach or player in a soak world is a founding person (X10.2.2), and at least one coaching tree of depth 3 exists (also X10.3.2).

leaves.title: Sharing a world
leaves.criterion: Two machines given one code produce identical world hashes.

leaves.title: Competitions and teams
leaves.criterion: Every team has a venue, a place, and a resource band. Changing the place step's seed changes no team count or conference, and two runs of one seed produce identical structures.

leaves.title: Founding people and cultures
leaves.criterion: Every roster and staff is legal for its level on day one. Founding pro rosters have a median age of 26 (plus or minus 1). No founding person has an event dated before the first season.

leaves.title: Running the past
leaves.criterion: The log from a history run contains no event with an imported actor. A world stopped at season 12 loads and plays.

leaves.title: What the run must produce, and the validator
leaves.criterion: 100 seeded 30-season runs: at least 95 pass on the first try (starting target).

leaves.title: Time budget
leaves.criterion: Measured time is reported by the size job each build.

leaves.title: Placing imported people
leaves.criterion: The X14.4.2 scan passes. No generated person shares a full name with an imported one. Every team is roster-legal after placement, and the count of `released` events with `source: import` equals the count of displaced generated people.

leaves.title: Placing the user
leaves.criterion: A new user holds no labels on day one. His stated college teammates exist in the log.

leaves.title: Calendar windows
leaves.criterion: Each season of a soak has exactly one `cohort_entered` per cohort kind. In every season the undrafted pool forms on the same day as the last draft pick, and no recruit class enters before the exits of the same date are processed.

leaves.title: What every new person carries
leaves.criterion: Every person created in a soak has a valid traits block and zero labels at creation. The age distribution of each soak season's pro entry pool has a median of 22 (plus or minus 1) and at least 70 percent between 21 and 24.

leaves.title: The entry-level coach and staff cohort
leaves.criterion: Over 60 seasons no bottom-rung chair is unfilled for lack of candidates, and the count of unemployed young coaches stays inside a stated band. The soak reports the ladder speed check of rule 5 and the yearly count of unplaced entrants; the unplaced count stays between 10 and 40 percent of the cohort (starting band).

leaves.title: Bosses, executives, and reporters over the decades
leaves.criterion: In a 60-season soak every boss and reporter chair is held by someone at every season start, no person holds a top boss chair past age 85 (starting bound), and the share of chairs filled from inside the world is reported.

leaves.title: Target distributions and their status
leaves.criterion: Every target row has a status and a source or the word Assumption.

leaves.title: Validate and reseed
leaves.criterion: A seeded bad cohort is caught and regenerated deterministically. A cohort generated 15 percent too large fails, regenerates, and passes; the same seed always reaches the same attempt number.

leaves.title: Stock balance: entries against exits
leaves.criterion: In a 60-season soak each population stays within 5 percent of its season-10 size, and rows 2 to 4 fall inside their bands.

leaves.title: Weekly top-up
leaves.criterion: No top-up person has an event dated before his creation. In a pro season soak, at least 80 percent of in-season signings are people who existed before the week of the signing (starting band).

leaves.title: Never copy a retired person
leaves.criterion: A static check finds no generator reading another person's attribute record. No `family` edge touches a protected person.

leaves.title: Name collisions with a loaded pack
leaves.criterion: After 60 seasons with a pack loaded, no generated person shares a full name with a pack person. A test pack containing "Michael Smith Jr." blocks generation of "Mike Smith" and of "Michael Smith III".

leaves.title: The loop by tier
leaves.criterion: Two runs of one seed give identical logs over 10 seasons. Reordering steps in a test changes the hash, proving order is part of state.

leaves.title: AI careers move
leaves.criterion: In a 40-season soak each exit path occurs, and head coach tenure stays inside the D13.4.1 band.

leaves.title: Leaving the world: retirement, the inactive record, and death of generated people
leaves.criterion: In a 60-season soak no imported person, active person, or user has a `died` event, and the world's stored person count levels off rather than rising every season. Every deceased person's page loads with his full career. No `died` event carries a cause field.

leaves.title: News reaches the user through people and media
leaves.criterion: A scripted room-only event reaches the user only when a chain of warm edges exists, and no sooner than the hop delay.

leaves.title: Rumor against fact
leaves.criterion: No label's evidence list contains a rumor. A false rumor is marked "Did not happen" within one cycle.

leaves.title: The simulation stops only for the user's decisions
leaves.criterion: A career advanced by day and one advanced by week with the same inputs have identical logs. No stop is caused by an event with no duty or addressee link to the user.

leaves.title: World-watching pages
leaves.criterion: A static check finds no truth-data read in these page definitions.

leaves.title: Tier membership
leaves.criterion: For a scripted career with three job changes, the tier of 50 sampled people matches a hand-written expected table at each change. No person is in two tiers. Recompute at a week boundary finishes inside the P6 budget for it.

leaves.title: What each tier stores and updates
leaves.criterion: For each cell, a test confirms the system ran at the stated frequency for a sampled person over one season. No person record is missing a stored field at any tier.

leaves.title: Promotion with a seeded fill-in
leaves.criterion: Promoting a person changes no stored field (compared field by field). Promoting the same person on the same date in two runs gives identical filled state. Promoting 2,000 people in a different order gives each the same result.

leaves.title: Demotion
leaves.criterion: After demotion, the person's permanent memories and edges are intact. No demotion occurs inside a game week for a person involved in that week's tier 1 game.

leaves.title: The measurement protocol
leaves.criterion: The repository holds a report for the shipping configuration with three agreeing measurements per number. Changing a line in config and rerunning produces a new report with a diff against the last.

leaves.title: Tier 3 game method
leaves.criterion: Every tier 3 game is resolved by the full engine (J14.1.2), and re-simulating one from its stored inputs reproduces its saved result.

leaves.title: Consistency across tiers
leaves.criterion: The per-tier rate report shows every tracked rate inside tolerance. The paired-world watch test shows no detectable difference in the watched person's five-season outcomes over 500 seeded pairs.

leaves.title: Origin field and neutral hidden state
leaves.criterion: Every person created by the import path has `protected: true` and a neutral block. No code path sets `origin` from an imported value to `generated`. After 30 simulated seasons in a test-pack world, no imported person has a stored off-field risk value or a non-neutral facet.

leaves.title: The event-exclusion rule
leaves.criterion: In a 50-season soak of a world that is 100 percent imported people at the start, the log contains zero events of an excluded type with a protected actor or subject, and the emit-refusal counter is zero. A unit test that calls emit directly with an excluded type and a protected actor is refused. No generated quote is attributed to a protected person anywhere in the soak's text output.

leaves.title: The audited list and its test
leaves.criterion: Removing one audit row fails the build. Editing a type's template without re-review fails the build. The release checklist has the soak report and the signed reading sample attached.

leaves.title: The prior career block
leaves.criterion: No row of any prior career block appears in the X2 log. The page shows the two sections separately with the imported heading. In a pack without team names, two teammates show the same "Prior club" letter.

leaves.title: Separate lists for imported and generated records
leaves.criterion: A test world with one imported player holding large prior totals shows him atop the combined list and absent from the world list until he earns a place.

leaves.title: The career-curve dial
leaves.criterion: At dial 100, an imported player's attributes at each pack season match the U3 target within rounding. At dial 0, his development distribution over 500 seeds matches that of a generated player with the same starting state. The dial cannot be changed after world creation.

leaves.title: No images or marks
leaves.criterion: The pack schema has no binary or image-reference field. An import file with an image field is rejected with a clear message.

leaves.title: The history run writes nothing onto imported people
leaves.criterion: For three seeds with a test pack, a scan of all events dated before the career start finds no imported person ID. World creation fails loudly if the scan finds one.

leaves.title: Event record
leaves.criterion: Two runs of one seeded season produce byte-identical logs. Every event in a 10-season test world validates against its type schema. No event payload contains a label ID or a traits field.

leaves.title: Event types as content
leaves.criterion: The build fails for a type with no consumer, and for a `harmful` type marked `imported_allowed: true`. Every shipped type has a line template that renders with test data.

leaves.title: Append-only rule and corrections
leaves.criterion: No code path updates or deletes an event outside the compaction job. A vacated win shows as both lines on the team page and is excluded from the coach's win total. A one-byte edit to a saved season log is detected.

leaves.title: Label definitions as queries
leaves.criterion: Every shipped label lists a consumer and passes the no-truth-data check. For each label, a scripted person who performs the behavior past the threshold gets it, and a scripted person who does not, does not. The same script run with the user as actor yields the same label on the same date.

leaves.title: Evidence thresholds, appearance, and fading
leaves.criterion: In a 20-season world where a scripted coach behaves at baseline, he holds a given label in no more than the stated false-positive share of seasons. A scripted coach who changes behavior in season 6 loses the label within the window and no sooner than `threshold_off` allows. Label state after loading a save equals label state recomputed from the log.

leaves.title: Who says it, and how old it is
leaves.criterion: 1. Every label shown on any screen has a source, a sample, and a last-evidence date. 2. A frozen label's weight falls with time and never rises without new evidence. 3. A test consumer that reads a label without weight fails the build check.

leaves.title: Each observer's view
leaves.criterion: Two AI owners with different culture records rank the same three candidate coaches differently, and each ranking can be traced to labels and impressions. An owner who watched a coach's team lose to his own cites that game in the interview text. Deleting an observer's memory rows about a subject in a test changes his view and nothing else.

leaves.title: Log volume, tiers, and compaction
leaves.criterion: After compaction, every held label in a test world recomputes to the same state as before compaction. A 40-season world's log size is reported by the size job and compared with the P6 budget. No event referenced by a memory row is ever missing.

leaves.title: Page model
leaves.criterion: A crawl of every link in a 10-season test world finds no dead link. Every line on a test page maps to one event ID. Deleting the page cache changes nothing shown. A static check finds no authored prose about a person in page content files.

leaves.title: Public record against what the viewer knows
leaves.criterion: A room-only event on a team the user never worked for appears on no page he can open. After a scripted leak reaches him it appears, marked with its source.

leaves.title: Season chronicle
leaves.criterion: The champion, every head coach change, and every record set in a test season appear in its chronicle.

leaves.title: Era and decade views
leaves.criterion: Decade totals equal the sum of season pages. A team with 3 titles in one block carries the dynasty flag on that block and no other.

leaves.title: Coaching trees
leaves.criterion: Every tree node traces to `hired` and season events on a shared staff. A head coach whose two former assistants became head coaches, one of whom produced another, shows depth 2 and 3 head coaches produced.

leaves.title: Rivalry pages
leaves.criterion: Series totals equal the count of game events. The longest streak shown equals the longest run of consecutive wins by one side in the game events.

leaves.title: Record book
leaves.criterion: A scripted season that breaks a record emits one event and updates both tabs correctly. A quarterback with 13 attempts per team game and the best rating in a season does not appear on the season rating list; the same player with 14 does.

leaves.title: Search and filters
leaves.criterion: No filter key maps to a truth-data field (static check). In a 60-season soak world, a two-letter prefix search returns its first page within the target on the reference machine, and a misspelling by one letter of a 6-letter surname finds the person.

leaves.title: Export as data
leaves.criterion: A scan of an export finds no truth-data field. Two exports of the same save are byte-identical.

leaves.title: No reveal setting
leaves.criterion: A new career can open the champion of every history-run season. A history-run event with a room witness rule is absent from every page a new user can open.

leaves.title: Score definition per event type
leaves.criterion: In a scripted season, a 20-point underdog's win outscores a favorite's win in the same week. Score is identical across two runs of one seed.

leaves.title: Expectation source
leaves.criterion: The stored expectation for a game equals N2's value at kickoff in a replay.

leaves.title: The keep line and score tiers
leaves.criterion: After a 40-season run every event scoring 60 or more is still present in full. Over a 40-season soak the band shares fall within the rule 2 targets, or the tuning log records why not. Over the same soak the share of generated players with at least one `historic` season is within a factor of two of the 4.1 percent first-team All-Pro anchor (tolerance is an Assumption).

leaves.title: Season and career rollups
leaves.criterion: Rebuilding rollups from the log reproduces the stored rows. The career rollup equals the sum of season rollups for every counter. The top 10 list is identical across two runs of one seed, including on tied scores.

leaves.title: Rarity anchors from real honours
leaves.criterion: The calibration report is produced by the standard soak and lists every anchor in rule 1 and rule 2. In a 30-season soak every class size is inside the rule set's bounds, and the enshrined share of generated draftees is within tolerance of 1.1 percent.

leaves.title: Consumers and their thresholds
leaves.criterion: An interviewer in a scripted test cites the candidate's highest-scoring event.

leaves.title: Inbox pacing
leaves.criterion: Over a 10-season soak, no week delivers more than 15 single items (starting bound).

leaves.title: Scoring protected people
leaves.criterion: In a pack test world no scored event with a protected actor has a type outside the audited allow list. No pack honour fact appears as a scored event. In the same test world, no protected person's event reaches 80 when its score without the relationship and first-or-last terms is under 80.

leaves.title: Needs derived from traits, role, and career stage
leaves.criterion: Two generated backups differing only in `ego` hold different `role_and_respect` weights. One `career_stage_changed` event is written per change. An override at one team changes class weights for its people only.

leaves.title: Need definitions
leaves.criterion: Each shipped need has a reader and at least one relief source the user or an AI boss can act on.

leaves.title: One accumulated stress value
leaves.criterion: With every need met, stress falls to 0 from 500 within one calendar year. One fully unmet need at weight 1 takes at least 13 weeks to cross a 250-point band. One maximal event moves stress by no more than 60.

leaves.title: Outcomes at each band
leaves.criterion: Every formal act in a soak is preceded in the log by at least one warning event or staff observation unless the person's `candor` is in a low band. In a 30-season soak no person crosses a breakpoint in a week containing only one stress event and met needs. Outside legal windows, no team has more than 2 formal acts in a week.

leaves.title: Release, repeat spacing, and coping (generated people)
leaves.criterion: In a 30-season soak no person takes the same formal act twice inside the spacing window. Every `coping_started` event names a generated person. With coping disabled in a test build, off-field incident counts fall by an amount the test states in advance, proving the risk path is wired and bounded. The user's coach never holds a coping record.

leaves.title: Group view in words, causes underneath
leaves.criterion: No stress number appears on any screen. A scripted hidden-strain player shows as settled until an observation event exists.

leaves.title: Update frequency and protected people
leaves.criterion: No `effort_dropped` event names a protected person in a pack test world.

leaves.title: Memory row
leaves.criterion: Every row's `event_id` resolves. No row exists for a non-witness without a news delivery record.

leaves.title: The short layer
leaves.criterion: No holder exceeds the slot limit in a soak.

leaves.title: Memory kinds: hold, fade, and repeats
leaves.criterion: A scripted coach who praises one player ten times in a month moves that player's impression by no more than `1 / (1 - stack_factor)` times one praise. A scripted benching is felt at full strength through 70 percent of its life and is gone at the end. A scripted pair of equal and opposite role events leaves a net negative impression.

leaves.title: Promotion to permanent
leaves.criterion: Permanent rows never exceed the cap. Every permanent row's event survives a 40-season compaction test.

leaves.title: Re-feeling and softening
leaves.criterion: A scripted rematch triggers the row once per meeting, not weekly.

leaves.title: Rare permanent facet change
leaves.criterion: No `outlook_changed` event names a protected person or the user. No person has more than 2.

leaves.title: How memory changes later dealings
leaves.criterion: A scripted owner who witnessed a blowout loss to a candidate's team cites that game in the interview and ranks him differently from an identical owner without the row.

leaves.title: Limits by tier and for protected people
leaves.criterion: Memory size per person stays under the X13.3.1 budget in the size job.

leaves.title: Edge record and kinds
leaves.criterion: Every non-family, non-prior edge lists at least one basis event that names both parties. Edge count per person stays under the X13.3.1 budget in a 40-season world.

leaves.title: Trait fit
leaves.criterion: Over 1,000 seeded pairs, low-fit staff pairs end seasons with lower edge strength than high-fit pairs with identical events.

leaves.title: Growth and decay
leaves.criterion: An untouched edge reaches its floor and stops. A scripted broken promise turns a warm edge cold.

leaves.title: Promises
leaves.criterion: A broken promise changes the views (X2.3.1) of people who witnessed or heard it and no one else's.

leaves.title: Cohesion from snaps together
leaves.criterion: Pair counts equal the sum of shared snaps in the play log for a test season.

leaves.title: Cohesion as a contest input, capped
leaves.criterion: With the cap at its starting value, two otherwise equal lines differ in pressure rate allowed by no more than the band the test states in advance.

leaves.title: Relationship view
leaves.criterion: No screen shows an edge strength number.

leaves.title: Vouching
leaves.criterion: An unknown candidate with a strong voucher outranks an identical one without, in a scripted hire.

leaves.title: Position definition file
leaves.criterion: Every game-required position in shipped content has a succession rule that resolves on a test staff. A test staff in which every step but the last is empty still resolves. Two runs of the same seed resolve every tie the same way.

leaves.title: Staff chart built from definitions
leaves.criterion: The chart for a generated small-college staff and a pro staff both render with no orphan chair. A staff whose holders are all interim or acting still renders with every chair labeled. The open-chair count on the team page equals the number of open boxes.

leaves.title: Scope comes from the task list, never an unlock
leaves.criterion: A static check finds no action gated by anything except a duty. A scripted graduate assistant given the scout-team duty gains its screen that week.

leaves.title: Interim head coach
leaves.criterion: In a soak no team plays a game with an empty head chair. Over a 30-season soak the share of interims who become the permanent head coach at the same team falls inside the X8.4.3 band. No interim makes a permanent staff hire unless the appointer lifted the limit by a logged event.

leaves.title: Absent play caller on game day
leaves.criterion: A scripted mid-game loss of a coordinator produces a caller before the next snap.

leaves.title: Firing cascades
leaves.criterion: After every head coach change in a soak, each staff member has exactly one of the three outcome events within 30 days. Over a 30-season soak the per-team yearly count of on-field staff changes at the top college level falls inside the X8.4.3 band, and the professional coordinator change rate falls inside its band.

leaves.title: Vacancy filling
leaves.criterion: No chair stays empty more than 60 days in a soak (starting bound).

leaves.title: Turnover reference bands
leaves.criterion: The calibration report prints every band with its measured value. A 30-season reference soak passes every row with status 2 of 3 or better; rows at 1 of 3 are reported but warn only.

leaves.title: Culture record per program and club
leaves.criterion: Two AI owners with opposite preference for one label rank a coach holding it differently, traceably. In a 30-season soak the per-franchise head coach counts meet the rule 5 targets.

leaves.title: Expectations by size and history, rising with success
leaves.criterion: A scripted run of three over-target seasons raises the target each year; one bad season after lowers it less than one good season raised it.

leaves.title: Drift with the people in charge
leaves.criterion: A scripted head coach who suspends for every violation for 8 seasons lowers `conduct_tolerance` measurably; one season does not. A culture at `tradition_strength` 100 moves no faster than one fifth of the rate of a culture at 0 under the same leaders. No field moves more than 5 percent of its range in one season.

leaves.title: How consumers read the record
leaves.criterion: Removing the last reader of a field fails the build. A K7 candidate's job choice log cites only public culture facts and interview statements.

leaves.title: Generating a culture with its team
leaves.criterion: Same seed, same records. After a 30-season history run, team expectations correlate with their run results.

gates.text: Q1.3.1 passes for plays and games on the dummy game: same seed, same content hash, byte-identical state hash chain (P5.3.2) on Windows, Linux, and the browser build. macOS is recorded as not tested until a Mac is available, because the only test machines are Marlon's Windows PC and the Linux cloud sandbox (audit Part 17 PQRA, P17-1).

gates.title: Phase 0: foundations and its gate
gates.text: A save written on one platform opens on the others (P1.4.1 acceptance).

gates.title: Phase 0: foundations and its gate
gates.text: Q1.2.1 schema tests pass. P1.2.2 lint passes with zero forbidden imports.

gates.title: Phase 0: foundations and its gate
gates.text: Every rule value in the two rule-set files points at a register row (Q6.2.1), and no rule row is below "Rulebook only" (Q6.3.1).

gates.title: Phase 0: foundations and its gate
gates.text: A schema scan finds no field for coach points, experience, skill trees, perks, or difficulty in any entity (A3.1.1 rows 8 to 10, A3.1.2). Q1.2.1's forbidden-key lint is this scan.

gates.title: Phase 0: foundations and its gate
gates.text: If the gate fails on cross-engine math or on SQLite access in the desktop shell, the fallback in P1.4.1 is taken (Electron) and the gate is re-run.

gates.title: Phase 1: a complete game with the reference resolver

gates.title: Phase 1: a complete game with the reference resolver

gates.title: Phase 2: football language and the field

gates.title: Phase 2: football language and the field

gates.title: Phase 2: football language and the field

gates.title: Phase 3: assignment-level engine, pass game
gates.text: Q3.2.1 pass game items and Q3.2.2 pressure and protection items pass in direction and ordering.

gates.title: Phase 3: assignment-level engine, pass game
gates.text: Q1.7.3 rating-response sweeps are monotonic for pass contests.

gates.title: Phase 3: assignment-level engine, pass game
gates.text: P6.1.1 play budget met.

gates.title: Phase 3: assignment-level engine, pass game
gates.text: Q5.1.1 football review has started on this build if reviewers exist (R2.2.2). If none exist, the gate records evidence level 0 (Q5.5.1) and does not block.

gates.title: Phase 4: assignment-level engine, run game and the rest

gates.title: Phase 4: assignment-level engine, run game and the rest
gates.text: Foul and injury rates from play meet their J10 and J15 rows.

gates.title: Phase 4: assignment-level engine, run game and the rest

gates.text: Q4.1.1, Q4.1.2, Q4.2.1, Q4.2.2: the exploit search finds no dominant strategy and no information leak.

gates.title: Phase 5: coach AI and game day

gates.text: Q1.2.3 migration fixtures pass.

gates.text: A scripted user policy completes a career from rung 0 at a college to pro head coach in a headless run, and a second policy is fired and rehired. Both replay identically (Q1.3.1).
